body:
## Why

Bringing `fudster@herbmail.com` end to end (#17146, #17148, #17153) turned up how Stalwart 0.16 actually works, none of it in the README:

- Every setting is a registry object, editable over JMAP (`x:<Object>/get|set` with the recovery admin as basic auth). The admin UI is optional.
- Per-domain `directoryId` is enterprise-only. Community edition validates RCPT TO against the default directory on the `x:Authentication` singleton.
- A catch-all address cannot feed the hook: the envelope is rewritten to the catch-all account before DATA and the hook payload has no original recipient.
- The SQL directory's default `queryMemberOf`/`queryEmailAliases` reference tables that do not exist and turn every RCPT into 451 until nulled.
- The default `Log` tracer writes to a directory the pod lacks, so nothing was logged anywhere.

## What

README step 5 rewritten as the list of registry objects the deployment needs, with the exact values now live.

author: coder7657
body:
Found sweeping the deployed host: we were serving **no security headers at all**. No HSTS, no nosniff, no CSP, no frame policy.

Each one below is here because something real needs it, not to satisfy a scanner.

| header | why *this* app needs it |
|---|---|
| `Strict-Transport-Security` | The field view takes camera input. A downgrade to plain HTTP does not merely weaken it — **capture silently stops working**, because `getUserMedia` needs a secure context. |
| `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` | The gateway serves a 25 MB `.wasm` and an `.onnx` as `application/octet-stream`. Sniffing either into something executable is exactly the mistake to prevent. |
| `X-Frame-Options: DENY` | A framed Audit console is a credible-looking way to show someone a ledger that is not ours. |
| `Permissions-Policy` | Camera yes — that is the field view. Microphone, payment: no. Saying so costs less than explaining why we asked. |

## The CSP

Narrowed to what the app genuinely uses, and each allowance is load-bearing:

- `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` — `onnxruntime-web` compiles its runtime
- `blob:` — ort's worker threads, and the local preview of a photo that never leaves the device
- `https://*.tile.openstreetmap.org` — the **only** third party we load anything from, and only map tiles
- `'unsafe-inline'` for **style only** — Leaflet injects inline styles for markers

`connect-src 'self'` is the one I care about most. *"No telemetry, no CDN, no analytics"* stops being something we assert and becomes something **the browser enforces**. That is a better answer to a judge than our word for it.

## Verification

CSP is easy to get wrong in a way that only shows up at runtime, so this needs checking on the deployed host rather than trusting the policy string — specifically the map tiles and the field view's wasm load. I will confirm both after deploy and report what the console says.

## Summary

PR A of the Intern ID rebuild — spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-11-intern-id-identity-design.md`, plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-11-intern-id-identity.md` (both in this PR).

Replaces nothing yet: this PR is **additive**. Every intern gets a portal-assigned `intern_code` (`IMP-YY-NNNN`); names are still stored, entered and displayed. PR B switches the anonymous intern sign-in to the ID; PR C removes the name columns.

- `interns.intern_code` — `text NOT NULL`, **plain** unique index (soft-deleted codes stay reserved, spec D5). Hand-written migration `0005_intern_code.sql`: add nullable → PL/pgSQL backfill (year from `start_date`, else `created_at` in `America/Indiana/Indianapolis`; random 0001–9999 with retry) → `SET NOT NULL` → index. Drizzle snapshot records the destination; `drizzle-kit generate` → "No schema changes".
- `app/lib/intern-code.ts` — pure `formatInternCode` / `normalizeInternCode` / `yearForInternCode` (+10 tests, incl. the Dec-31 Indiana-vs-UTC edge).
- `app/lib/intern-code.server.ts` — `createInternWithCode`: one transaction (intern + entry assessment + participation factors), redraws only on PG `23505` on the `intern_code` index, cap 10 → `InternCodeExhaustedError` (+6 tests). The only app-code writer of the column.
- Admin create → `/admin/interns/:id?issued=1` → one-time **Intern ID issued** callout (Copy button; spec copy verbatim). `InternCodeExhaustedError` → 503 (tested).
- `<InternCode>` component; ID first column + default sort on the intern list, the Assessments-hub picker and the cohort-members table; digits alone match in search.
- Seeds carry fixed codes (`IMP-26-1042` Whitaker, `IMP-26-4001..4003` Test1–3); demo seed assigns a deterministic permutation; RLS fixture updated.
- CLAUDE.md: new "Intern ID — contracts to preserve" section; CSS registry.

## Verification

- impact-dev: backup existed (Pro, ~07:00Z 2026-09-11); migration 0005 applied; **140/140 backfilled, 140 distinct, 0 malformed, 0 start-date/year mismatches**, column `NOT NULL`, plain unique index, journal at 6 (verified independently via SQL).
- Reseeded dev (`db:seed` 6 + `db:seed:demo` 134, 0 code collisions).
- lint 0 errors (6 pre-existing warnings), typecheck clean, **302 unit/component tests**, `admin-crud` e2e green locally (asserts the issued code and searches by its last four digits).

Migrate-first leaves only the *old* app's create path failing for the minutes between migration and deploy; prod has 0 interns and 0 users at night.

💡 What: Refactored the `collect_movie_links_from_calendar_page` method to use a single JavaScript block via `driver.execute_script()` instead of iterating through elements with Python-side `find_element` calls.
🎯 Why: Selenium's Python bindings suffer from significant latency for each `find_element` or property fetch (`.text`, `.get_attribute()`) because each command is a separate HTTP request/IPC roundtrip to the browser driver. By pushing the extraction logic into the browser via JS, we reduce O(N) network overhead to O(1).
📊 Impact: Expected to dramatically reduce execution time on the calendar page, eliminating dozens/hundreds of IPC roundtrips when fetching data for listed movies.
🔬 Measurement: Verify the speedup by measuring the execution time of `collect_movie_links_from_calendar_page` before and after. Output data should be identical.

author: cstarlea
body:
## Summary

Adds the repository's first CI workflow and brings the prose — README, CONTRIBUTING, LICENSE, Copilot instructions, agent configs, issue template — in line with what the code actually does. Also removes `progress.txt`, a stale root-level audit log.

This PR documents the **end state** of `release/2026-09-review`, which sibling PRs are producing concurrently. It therefore assumes the following will be true on this branch at merge time:

- (a) `astro.config.mjs` uses `passthroughImageService` and `@astrojs/sitemap`
- (b) guide and meetup URLs are clean slugs with no `.md` (today `dist/guides/` still emits `what-is-meshtastic.md/`)
- (c) nginx serves real 404s via `404.html` and security headers via an included `security-headers.conf`, with the CSP `connect-src` derived from the `PUBLIC_N8N_WEBHOOK_URL` build arg
- (d) `docker-compose.yml` forwards the four `PUBLIC_N8N_*` build args
- (e) the container listens on 8080 (already true today)

The CI smoke tests assert (b), (c), and (e) directly, so this workflow will fail until the sibling PRs for the routing and nginx changes land on the branch.

## Changes

### CI

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** (new) — runs on `pull_request` and on pushes to `main` and `release/**`. Checkout, `setup-node` 20 with npm cache, `npm ci`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, then `docker build` with dummy `--build-arg PUBLIC_N8N_*=https://example.invalid/webhook/...` values, `docker run -p 8080:8080`, and curl smoke tests:
  - `/` returns 200 and carries `Content-Security-Policy` and `Strict-Transport-Security` headers. The request sends `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` because `nginx.conf` maps HSTS off that header and emits nothing for plain HTTP — without it the assertion could never pass.
  - `/guides/what-is-meshtastic/` returns 200.
  - `/definitely-missing/` returns 404.
  - Container logs are dumped and the container removed with `if: always()`.
  - Actions pinned to major versions (`actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/setup-node@v4`).

### `README.md`

- Docker example is `docker run -p 8080:8080` and the text says the non-root nginx listens on **8080**, not 80; notes that `docker-compose.yml` maps host 8081 to container 8080.
- New **Environment variables** section: the four `PUBLIC_N8N_*` vars and what each drives, `cp .env.example .env` for `npm run dev`, `--build-arg` / compose `build.args` for Docker, and the consequence that values are baked into static output at build time — rotating a webhook URL needs a rebuild and a new image digest, not a container restart.
- Replaced the description of a CI build/push/digest workflow that never existed. New **Continuous integration** section describes `ci.yml` and says plainly that CI does not build, push, or deploy; a new **Release and deploy (Komodo)** section puts the image build and rollout in Komodo, outside the repo. The digest-pinning rules for `docker-compose.server.yml` are kept, reworded around Komodo.
- Fixed the `src/` layout: there is no `src/content/meetups/` today (collection defined, no entries), `taxonomies/` added, `global/` is 11 files and they are listed, entry counts given for guides/nodes/resources. The "Adding Content → Meetups" snippet now says to create the directory.
- License section: the old text called one license listed twice a "dual licensing approach". It now states plainly that the whole project is CC-BY-SA-4.0, with moving code to a code license recorded as a documented open question — no license change is made here.

### `CONTRIBUTING.md`

- PR checklist now includes `npm test` (and mentions what CI runs).
- Network Nodes: node type enum corrected to `relay` / `router` / `client` / `solar` (was "router/relay/sensor"), the "node ID" field the schema does not have is removed, and the actual required/optional fields are listed.
- New privacy note asking contributors to round residential node coordinates to ~3 decimals (~100 m) or use a nearby landmark.

### `.github`

- **`ISSUE_TEMPLATE/add_content.md`** — same node type fix, "Node name/ID" → "Node name", plus a coordinates field carrying the rounding reminder.
- **`copilot-instructions.md`** — the missing `taxonomies` collection is documented; `global` corrected from "site.md and navigation.md" to the 11 files it holds, with a note that its schema is a discriminated union on `type`; `meetups` marked as having no entries; the footer is sourced from `footer.md`, not `navigation.md` (verified against `src/layouts/Layout.astro`, which reads `getEntry('global', 'footer')`); "Last Updated" refreshed. Every path claim in the file was cross-checked with `ls`.
- **`agents/astro-routing.agent.md`** — "Use `guide.id` for slugs" (which carries the `.md` extension into the URL) replaced with `entry.slug` and clean URLs; the `getStaticPaths()` example updated to match.
- **`agents/map-nodes.agent.md`** — "Keep coordinates precise" replaced with the coordinate-rounding privacy guidance.
- **`agents/_template.agent.md`** — stray ` ```chatagent ` opening fence and its closing fence removed, so the template's own frontmatter is the file's frontmatter.
- **`agents/astro-content.agent.md`**, **`agents/content-curator.agent.md`** — the only path referenced across all agent files that does not exist is `src/content/meetups/`; their structure diagrams are corrected and annotated, and `taxonomies/`, `global/`, and `config.ts` added.

### `LICENSE`

- Added `Copyright (c) 2026 CHS Mesh contributors` where the CC text expects the holder.

### Removed

- **`progress.txt`** — a stale root-level audit log of four already-merged security fixes. Removed with `git rm`; its content is preserved in git history, and the durable version of that information lives in `test/security/docker-compose.server.test.mjs` and README.

## Verification

- `npm test` — 7 pass, 0 fail (no code changed).
- `npm run build` — 10 pages built, exit 0 (`dist/` removed afterwards). The build logs "The collection \"meetups\" does not exist or is empty", which is the pre-existing state this PR now documents.
- `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/ci.yml'))"` — parses, 12 steps in one job.
- Every path claim in `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and the six agent files was grepped out and checked against `ls`; `src/content/meetups/` was the only miss and is now annotated everywhere it appears.
- Collection and file counts were read from the tree: guides 4, nodes 3, resources 7, taxonomies 1, global 11.
- The CI workflow itself was **not** executed — Docker requires sudo in this environment and the smoke tests depend on sibling PRs (b) and (c). Its first real run will be on this PR.

## Not done

- Nothing in the brief was skipped. No file outside README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, LICENSE, progress.txt and `.github/**` was touched.
- Related but deliberately out of scope, for follow-up: `.gitignore` does not cover a `node_modules` symlink (worktree-only annoyance), and the `.env.example` comments could name which form each webhook serves — both are files owned by sibling PRs.

Merging the six review branches together and re-reading this branch's prose against the combined tree turned up six places where the docs still described the pre-review state, plus two CI gaps. Commit `057db69`.

### Empty collections, stated correctly (M4, M5)

`review/content` deletes the three `Example ...` node fixtures, so `src/content/nodes/` is empty. It has no `.gitkeep`, and git does not track empty directories, so **the directory is absent from a fresh clone**. `review/build-config` adds `src/content/meetups/.gitkeep`, so that directory **does** exist and is merely empty. Those are two different situations and the docs had them backwards or stale:

author: codyswanngt
body:
Comment-based human-hold releases currently trust matching text without validating its author. A comment from an untrusted actor can therefore clear a human hold and produce ready-transition actions.

Require a structured comment with a stable author identity in an explicit trusted-human allowlist before recognizing a release. Missing identities, plain strings, absent trust configuration, untrusted actors and known bot identities leave the hold intact. Propagate this policy through the shared verdict and release-planning helpers, and preserve author IDs in the documented tracker adapters.

Linear adapters also retain botActor metadata, and any non-null bot actor leaves the hold intact even when the underlying user ID is trusted. The pre-work intake instructions pass the structured comments and explicit trust context into classification.

Validation: authorization and Linear bot-actor regressions reproduced the gaps before their fixes. All 288 focused runtime/generated-copy/documentation checks pass. Normal push gates passed 24,165 unit tests (two existing platform/fixture skips), 2,808 integration tests. The mutation gate reported nothing-to-mutate for this patch. Staged lint, formatting and all seven generated-artifact checks pass. Tests preserve authorized releases, keyed/keyless holds, multiple holds and every promotion wrapper while rejecting unattributed, untrusted and bot-authored releases.

### gzip: gzip: Arbitrary file overwrite via insecure temporary file handling in gzexe utility
[CVE-2026-41991](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-41991)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
A flaw was found in the `gzexe` utility of GNU `gzip`. When the `mktemp` utility is not available, `gzexe` creates temporary files with predictable names based on the process ID. A local attacker can exploit this by pre-creating a symbolic link to an arbitrary file at the predicted temporary file path. This can lead to a Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) condition, allowing the attacker to overwrite arbitrary files on the system.

Moderate

author: jakechampion
body:
Refs #9052. ATLAS-PLATFORM-PLAN §3.4 **step 3, first backend**. #9127 landed `__sum_bytes` scalar in all eight emitters; this vectorises the native arm64 one.

## Why the encodings come first in the diff

§3.3a's rule, learnt on these same targets: land the encodings against an external oracle *before* the vector body. `internal/native/arm64tbl` could encode neither of the instructions this kernel needs.

`arm64tbl` gains a **`VecPairwiseLong`** class — `saddlp` / `uaddlp` / `sadalp` / `uadalp`. It is the first two-register class here whose operands do **not** share an arrangement: the destination is one element size up with half the lanes, and **only the source's arrangement is encoded**. So the assembler *checks* the destination rather than encoding it, and refuses what GNU `as` refuses. `uaddlp v0.16b, v1.16b` names a destination that cannot hold the sums, and an encoder that ignored the destination would emit a valid-looking word for it.

**23 encodings pinned**, every source arrangement in both its Q forms. That is not padding: `.8b` and `.16b` differ only in the bit that *also* picks the destination's lane count, so a size/Q slip assembles as a real instruction writing the wrong number of lanes — the §3.3a failure mode where a wrong sub-opcode is still a valid instruction. **Six rejections pinned** alongside.

Every expected word was read back from an external assembler, not hand-decoded.

## The body, and why it is not `__count_byte`'s shape

A sum needs **widening** where a population did not, and that is the whole design:

- `cmeq` + `cnt` + `addv` works for `__count_byte` because a block's count is at most 128 and fits the byte `addv` writes.
- A block's **sum** is at most 16 × 255 = 4080 and does not fit a byte at all.

So the fold goes up in two steps: `uaddlp` turns 16 bytes into 8 halves (2 × 255, cannot overflow), and `uadalp` **accumulates** those into four 32-bit lanes. Accumulate rather than replace is the load-bearing choice — it keeps the running total in the vector register across iterations instead of spilling to a scalar every block. `addv` folds once at the end, and 2³² / 4080 blocks is far past any string, so no lane can overflow before it.

## Measurement

macOS arm64, 62 MiB / 8 000 000-line `seq` file, GNU coreutils 9.10, uutils 0.6.0. **Contended** — other agents on the box, hence the wide σ on GNU and uutils.

| `sum -s` | mean (ms) | user (ms) |
|---|---|---|
| fern, scalar kernel (#9127) | 31.3 ± 7.7 | 20.4 |
| **fern, NEON (this PR)** | **11.0 ± 1.8** | **4.1** |
| GNU 9.10 | 11.9 ± 5.7 | 2.8 |
| uutils 0.6.0 | 27.1 ± 9.0 | 5.1 |

**Fern is now ahead of GNU on `sum -s` wall clock**, and 2.45x uutils. The full arc on this workload: **110.1 ms → 23.5 (scalar kernel) → 11.0 (NEON)**, a **10x** total.

User time is the honest kernel number: 4.1 ms against GNU's 2.8, so ~1.5x remains on CPU and the wall-clock win partly reflects the static-binary startup margin. Said plainly rather than claimed away — that 1.5x is what this body can next be measured on.

`sum -s` and `sum -r` stay byte-identical to GNU on the file.

## Correctness

- The **2508-case differential** from #9127, recompiled against the vector body, agrees on every case. It sweeps every length across the 16-byte boundary and plants a high byte at every offset, which is what a lane-count or sign error shows up in.
- The wrap case returns **254** over 16 843 010 `0xff` bytes (2³² + 254).
- `__heap_bump_bytes()` moves **0** across 1000 calls.
- `go test ./internal/native/... ./internal/codegen/... ./internal/lint -count=1` green.
- `go test ./internal/e2e -run 'SumBytes|CountByte|TestRunnerHashChecksums' -count=1` green, with `FERN_WASI_ADAPTER` set so the wasm leg is a real pass.

The native arm64 legs of the e2e suite skip on a macOS host (no qemu), so the differential above was run by compiling the same corpus `-target arm64-darwin` — the same `internal/codegen/arm64` body. CI runs the real legs.

## Still scalar, deliberately

One backend at a time with a measurement each, per §3.4. Untouched and still scalar: **x86-64** (needs no encoder work — `psadbw` / `paddq` are already in `x86tbl/sse.go`, so it is the obvious next one), **wasm** (needs SIMD arithmetic added to `internal/wasm/simd`, which has none), **both SSA legs**, and **all three self-host emitters**. The self-host arm64 assembler does not get these rows in this PR because nothing in it emits them yet.

author: richardahasting
body:
Closes #121.

A game had no way to tell anyone anything. The update emits events, but **every one is a single country's private misfortune** — starvation, plague, bankruptcy, a severed rail line. There has never been an event anyone else was allowed to see, and not one that was good news.

## What it carries

Who joined, who renamed themselves, when the game began, and **firsts**: the first refinery in the game, the first harbour, the first bank. The list of what counts is generated from `economy.sector_types`, so a designation cannot be added without its milestone coming along.

## Two things that were easy to get wrong

**Names are resolved on read, never stored.** A rename carries backwards through the entire history — which matters most for the item announcing the rename, since written the other way round it would have been the first line in the feed to go stale. `CountryView` already does this; news follows it. Tested directly.

**A "first" cannot live in the engine.** It is a fact about the whole game's history, and the update is a pure function of *one snapshot* — it has no way to know whether anyone has ever built a refinery before. So the claim is a unique index in the database rather than a flag in memory.

And the check has to run **wherever a designation can change**: an update, a player's command, a deity's edit. The first version hooked only the update, which missed the very command that does the designating — the test caught it by designating through the deity and getting no milestone at all.

## The disclosure choice

A milestone names the country. That is a real leak — "Johnny built the first oil refinery" says Johnny has the tech, the oil and the spare capacity for one — in a game where #120 is weighing whether to publish a score at all.

Here **the leak is the feature**: bragging rights are the point, and a milestone nobody can attribute is not a milestone. It is a setting all the same (`news.name_countries`), so a hidden-information game can announce the achievement without the achiever. #120 will share it.

## Surface

`GET /api/games/{id}/news`, `POST /api/games/{id}/news/seen`, and an unseen count on the games list — a per-account watermark, without which "since you last looked" either repeats forever or shows nothing.

A **News** button per game on the games page, with the unseen count on it.

## Tests

**134 engine/sim, 81 server — nothing skipped.**

`NewsTest` (5): joining and starting are news; older news follows a rename (and the pre-rename name appears nowhere); a first is announced once and only once across two countries building the same thing; unseen counts down as you read and back up as things happen; the feed is newest-first and marks what is new.

## Not done

**Attacks.** They cannot be reported because nothing can attack — `CaptureCfg` is still read by no code. Designed for, blocked on #68.

author: barkz
body:
## The bug

**What you can do** and the **Glean Personal** listing were 96-character, space-aligned `text` code blocks. A `<pre>` scrolls rather than wraps, so below roughly 830px of content width the commands ran past the card edge and had to be dragged sideways to read — which happened on any window narrower than about 850px.

I had measured the earlier fix at 1280px, where they fit, and missed it.

## The fix

Both listings are command/effect pairs — tabular content that was being held in a code block by space alignment. They're tables now:

- They wrap instead of scrolling, at any width
- The two continuation rows (a line of spaces, then an arrow) are gone
- GitHub gets the same fix; those blocks scrolled sideways on a phone there too

The builder tags any table whose every row leads with a code span as a command table, so the stylesheet can give the command column half the width and set it as code rather than bold prose.

### Two line-breaking details

Hyphens are line-break opportunities in Unicode, so `--object-type` split after the dashes. `word-break: keep-all` suppresses that, with `overflow-wrap: break-word` left as the fallback for a token wider than the column.

### Quickstart

Kept its terminal framing but lost its widest line — the "or use a token" aside moved into prose underneath, where it reads better anyway.

## Result

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Widest code line on the page | 96 chars | **70 chars** |
| Listings that scroll sideways | 2 | 0 |

A new test fails if any code block on the built page goes past 80 characters again, so this can't come back quietly.

Verified by rendering the section alone at 1100px and 900px. `Ran 1094 tests — OK` (1,090 before).

body:
## Risk

- [ ] R0
- [ ] R1
- [ ] R2
- [x] R3

## Scope

Delivery goal: stop a single misaligned segment from permanently failing an entire WhisperX transcription, which is what the user hit right after the decode fix was promoted.

Evidence (all read-only, from the spooled production job `f890b568-241d-4949-9a70-4d4ac790b5dc`, 840981 ms, the stair inspection video the user re-tested):

- app-visible symptom: `invalid_provider_output` / `engine_failure_permanent`, `processed_ms=0/840981`;
- a window sweep of that audio through the promoted engine reproduced it deterministically at window 4 (480000-600000 ms): stage `map-segments`, exception `ValueError`;
- the offending aligned segment has `start=119960 ms`, `end=149940 ms` inside a `window_ms=120000` window, so the engine's `end_ms > duration_ms` check raised;
- windows 0-3 of the same recording are fine (224 / 362 / 316 / 261 characters), and another job promoted at the same time succeeded (430498 ms), so the release is not globally broken;
- dependency versions between the previous and the promoted release venv are identical (whisperx 3.8.6, faster-whisper 1.2.1, torch 2.8.0+cu128, numpy 2.4.6, transformers 4.57.6), so the only behavioural change was the removed repetition penalty, which had been masking this artifact with artificially short output.

Changed area:

- `services/asr_service/engines/whisperx.py`: clamp an out-of-window segment end to the window instead of failing the chunk; drop empty, zero-length or clamp-degenerate segments; keep failing closed with `empty aligned output` when nothing usable remains; record `last_clamped_segments` and `last_dropped_segments` per chunk;
- `services/asr_service/tests/test_whisperx.py`: tests for clamping, dropping, and the still-fail-closed empty case.

Explicit exclusions: no anti-loop parameter change (`no_repeat_ngram_size` and `repetition_penalty` are untouched; the repeated-character segment seen in window 0 needs measurement before it is tuned); no change to `vad_filter`, `condition_on_previous_text`, hotwords, beam or temperature; no chunk window change; no app-side change; no production action in this PR.

## Validation

- `pytest services/asr_service/tests/test_whisperx.py services/asr_service/tests/test_whisperx_qualification.py tests/test_whisperx_qualification_coverage.py services/asr_service/tests/test_scheduler.py tests/test_asr_deployment_static.py`: 107 passed.
- The new tests reproduce the production numbers: a segment with end 149940 ms in a 120000 ms window is clamped to 120000 ms and the sentence survives; degenerate segments are dropped while the rest of the chunk continues; an all-degenerate alignment still returns `invalid_provider_output` at `map-segments`.
- Outstanding: the promotion has not happened yet. After this merge the WhisperX contract changes, so re-qualification (run id + contract SHA), candidate staging, a read-only window sweep of both affected recordings against the candidate release, and only then promotion.

## Rollback

Repository: revert this commit. Production: the currently active release `34664390376` stays until a new candidate is promoted, and re-promoting candidate `34575342892` remains the last-resort rollback (it restores the incomplete-transcript behaviour, so it is not the preferred path).

## Approval Evidence

Same approved objective as #778 (make WhisperX usable in production) and the user's latest report 「转录失败」 with the exact error text. This is the failure repair inside that scope: it changes only how one malformed segment is handled, keeps the strict shape checks, and adds no new decode parameters. The production steps (re-qualify, stage, read-only verification, promote) follow the same sequence the user already approved.

The build stamp on the login screen was running under the ClassicUO links and losing the part that identifies it.

```
TazUO Version 4.5.2301-dev.bb▓▓▓▓▓▓   ← clipped by "CUO Discord"
```

## Why

The two version lines sat at `x=286`. The ClassicUO links start at `x=505`, so they had **219 pixels**.

A release build reads `4.5.2301` and fits easily. A dev build reads `4.5.2301-dev.bbe7343` and needs about 250 — so it ran underneath, cut off mid-hash. Which defeats the point of the stamp: it exists so a screenshot or a crash report says which build it came from.

## Fix

Both lines move to `x=150`.

Nothing else is on those two rows. The nearest control is the autologin checkbox — 36 pixels higher, and **already at `x=150`** — so moving left costs nothing and lines the block up with the checkboxes above it instead of floating mid-gump.

**355 pixels instead of 219.** Room for a longer stamp later, rather than just enough for this one.

Both login gump variants, light and dark.

## Note

I first "fixed" this by dropping the word *Version* from the label, which bought ~50px and cost a word. Moving buys 136px and costs nothing. That approach is reverted; the text is unchanged from what it always was.

author: evilfreelancer
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of the documentation reorganisation: thematic folders with a single navigation map, a README that is a landing page again, generated references, a documentation check in CI and in the pre-commit hook, assets reduced to what the pages use, the demo videos in the repository, and a workflow rule that makes documentation part of every behaviour change.

## What changed

- **Layout.** `docs/` is now `getting-started/`, `surfaces/`, `operate/`, `features/`, `reference/`, `recipes.md`, `contributing/`, `plans/`, mapped by `docs/nav.yaml` (title and one-line summary per page). The 30 moved pages leave redirect stubs at their old paths (first line `<!-- docs-stub`), because the binary (`coddy -t` hints, `--dry-run`), the config schema, the bundled `configure-coddy` skill and coddy.dev still print those addresses. `docs/plans/` is untouched except one repaired link; `remote-control.md` joined it as the design record it is.
- **README.md** is 111 lines instead of 702: install, a minimal config, a Surfaces table with a video per surface, "What it does", a "Goal | Start here" table. Everything it used to duplicate lives on its page.
- **New pages.** Quickstart, Troubleshooting, Changelog (from GitHub Releases), Editors (ACP), Remote mode, Security and trust, Operating modes, Sessions, Context compaction, Long-term memory (from `external/memory/README.md`), CLI reference, Environment variables, Slash commands, Keyboard, Tools, Recipes, Writing documentation, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` at the root.
- **Generated references.** `internal/docsgen` (`make docs`) renders the hub `docs/README.md`, `docs/llms.txt` and `docs/llms-full.txt` from the map, the field tables of `docs/reference/config.md` from the embedded schema and the loader's defaults (`config.DocDefaults`), `docs/reference/cli.md` from the `--help` screens of a full-tag binary, and the inventory of `docs/assets/INDEX.md`. `make docs-check` fails on drift, on a page missing from the map, on a broken relative link or `#anchor`, and on an asset nothing references; it runs as the CI job **Documentation** and, without the CLI build, in the pre-commit hook for documentation commits (`CODDY_HOOK_DOCS=0` turns it off). `make docs-changelog` refreshes the changelog.
- **Screenshots.** The captured but unused series (subagents, swarm, usage, folder picker, console usage footer, settings tabs, scheduler, update report, reasoning levels, attachments, confirmations, localisation) are embedded on the pages that describe those features, with captions. Pull-request evidence and the third-party design mockups are gone from `docs/assets`: 270 files and 39 MB became 86 files and 26 MB, of which 12 MB are the five demo videos (console, web UI, Zed, VS Code, swarm; H.264, 1280 px, no audio) linked from the Surfaces table and their pages. File names carry the feature and the state, not an issue or pull request number.
- **Rules.** `.cursor/rules/workflow.mdc` (mirrored in `.claude/rules/workflow.md`) gained step 10, *Documentation of the change*: a new capability gets its page, its map entry and its reference row; a changed behaviour updates the page that describes it; a web UI or console feature is shown with a screenshot on its page; videos go to `docs/assets/video/`; generated pages are regenerated with `make docs`. The CLI and lint steps are now 11 and 12. `AGENTS.md` carries the same contract and a *Documentation* section under Code Review Rules; `docs/contributing/documentation.md` is the full guide, `DESIGN.md` stays the SPA contract and is in the map.

- **Stable addresses on coddy.dev.** Every page of the map has `coddy.dev/docs/<slug>`; GitHub Pages serves `404.html` for every address that is not a file, so the site's 404 page loads one generated `docs-redirect.js` that sends a person to the page on GitHub (fragment kept) and turns `coddy.dev/docs/<slug>.md` into the raw Markdown. Nothing is duplicated on the site: `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` at the site root point straight at the raw Markdown on `main`. `make site-docs` renders the three files into the site checkout, `make site-docs-check` reports drift, and the addresses printed by the binary, the schema descriptions and the bundled skill use the `coddy.dev/docs/<slug>` form. The site side is coddy-project/coddy-project.github.io#2, to be merged after this PR; a Cloudflare redirect rule can turn the same mapping into a real 301 later.

## Deliberately not in this change

- New video recordings: the five existing demos are reused; the rig and the encoding line are documented.
- The em dashes in the older English pages were not swept; new pages follow the hyphen convention.

## Checks

- `make test` green (48 packages), `make lint` clean, `make docs-check` clean, `make test-opencode-rules` green.
- No UI sources changed, so no UI screenshots for the PR itself.
- The change was cross-reviewed by three independent readers (two local models through `coddy -p`, one with read access to the tree); the findings that held up (stale design-reference section, a wrong Dockerfile claim in the assets index, PR numbers in two file names, same-page anchors and reference-style links unchecked, `make docs` needing Node, mismatched config examples) are fixed in this branch.

## Known follow-ups

- `DESIGN.md` drift is not checked automatically; the rule in `docs/contributing/documentation.md` is the only guard.
- The older English pages still contain em dashes; new pages follow the hyphen convention, and the older ones get it as they are touched.
- If the repository's required checks are configured by job name, add **Documentation** to the list.

The manifest must be regenerated through the real genesis builder (commands below); its bytes are untouched here.

- `tests/test_genesis_builder_cli.c` — new `genesis_fee_schedule_is_current`: the fixture manifest must be protocol 3 and carry exactly one governance `fee.schedule` value of `LXP_FEE_PARAMS_V2_BYTES` (247) that decodes as version 2 with `LXP_ASSET_FEE_PRICE_COUNT` prices, checked before the signature step so a regenerated fixture with a stale schedule is refused.

## Design decisions

- Advertised ordinals that are decoded, validated and executed are the module contract; the tests describe that contract. No assertion was edited to match wrong output: the old assertions described a reserved ordinal that no longer exists in the module table.

Its own 215-byte `fee.schedule` key-value is never decoded on the migration path and cannot be re-emitted by the current builder (observation 6.1.8702); recorded as 6.11.7303 rather than asserted.

author: sambanks
body:
Bryan T ran the recfix recipe and got 32 verify_menu fails: the list at
0x400d6b00 instead of the 0x400d7bbc his build log named, entries past
index 2 reading 0x42565242. That is "BVRB", BusVerb's abbr -- the image
verify_menu read was a default-remix (bamsep26) build, not recfix's.
Reproduced here: a bamsep26 image checked as recfix gives 41 fails with
exactly that word. The documented recipe is clean on a fresh clone with
and without .venv; something in his sequence built without REMIX=recfix
(a bare make bus, or make -j running bus and verify at once on the one
out/mainos_bus.bin).

Nothing in the image names the remix, so no reader could tell. build_bus
now writes out/mainos_bus.remix beside the image: the remix name and the
image's sha256. verify_menu reads it and, when the hash matches the bytes
on disk but the name is not REMIX, fails with the one true line and the
fix. An image restored without its sidecar (verify_replaces, audition)
carries a stale hash and is treated as unlabelled, so the pipeline's own
save-and-restore is unaffected. Artifacts and reports untouched: refhash
26/26 bit-identical; make check REMIX=recfix green.

author: mmasoomi-glitch
body:
`security-tenancy.md` requires the audit trail to be *"queryable by an authorized accountant for the trailing audit window"*. Until now the only way to read it was SQL — so rows were being written for posting, reversal, period transitions, membership grants and ownership transfers, and **nobody had ever confirmed they could be retrieved.**

## Sequenced by the judge, not by me

I put this against Row Level Security and CSV export and asked for an ordering. It picked this one:

> RLS is high-risk refactoring with diminishing returns given robust app-level guards; it catches "forgotten filters" but a simple lint rule or PR checklist is cheaper. Export is low value compared to the audit viewer, which satisfies the primary auditor requirement with minimal risk.

That matches the evidence: a branded `LedgerScope` makes an invented scope a compile error, CI greps for anyone importing an unguarded service, and ~25 tenancy tests cover cross-tenant id confusion in both directions. RLS remains open as `B-20260911-04`.

## Decisions worth arguing with

**`audit.read` sits with ACCOUNTANT, not ADMIN.** `security-tenancy.md` names the accountant as the person whose job this is. It is deliberately **not** a VIEWER action: the trail carries membership grants and role changes, and a bookkeeper does not need to know who was promoted last quarter to do their work. `A4` pins both sides.

**There is no write path in this module.** The rows are written inside the transactions whose effects they record. A second way to produce them is exactly what makes an audit trail untrustworthy.

**The page size is clamped, not trusted.** `limit` arrives from a query string; unbounded, on a table that only ever grows, it is a denial of service any authenticated member could trigger by editing a URL. `A6` asserts the cap holds against `100_000`, `-5` and `0`.

**The actor is resolved at read time rather than stored on the row.** An email can change, and a trail reporting the address someone had *at the time* would be more accurate — while also freezing a copy of personal data in an append-only table nobody can correct or erase.

**A deleted actor shows as "(deleted user)" rather than vanishing.** `audit_logs.actor_id` is a plain uuid with no foreign key, deliberately: a row that disappeared with the person who caused it would be an audit trail anyone could erase by deleting their account.

**`before`/`after` render as JSON rather than parsed per action.** The shape differs by action, and a renderer per shape means an action added later silently displays nothing.

## A test that failed for the right reason

`A3` originally built the deleted-actor state with `auditLog.updateMany`. **The append-only trigger refused it** — which is the property `A10` exists to assert, so the failure was the system working.

The only way to reach a dangling `actor_id` is to delete the user for real. The rewritten test does that, and also asserts the *other* rows still resolve, so the fallback is not quietly hiding a broken lookup.

`A10` is the test the rest depends on: update and delete are both refused, and reading changes nothing.

## Evidence

```text
$ npx eslint .        exit 0
$ npx tsc --noEmit    clean
$ npx vitest run      359 passed (20 files)
$ npx next build      ✓ Compiled successfully
                      ├ ƒ /o/[orgSlug]/audit    168 B
```

349 before, 359 now.

## `B-20260913-02` filed — raised by the reviewer, unprompted

Asked whether there was a fourth thing I had not listed, it named **retention**. It is right, and it is the thing this viewer makes visible: a table nobody could read could also be a table nobody noticed growing.

What it needs is **decisions**, not just a job: how long the trail must be retained is jurisdictional and differs by market; archive-versus-delete is a question about whether the append-only guarantee survives; and *"who may trigger it"* matters because a retention job any admin can run is a way to destroy evidence. Mechanically it wants the same scheduler `B-20260911-07` does.

## Sprint and ownership

- **Sprint:** 002 · **Base:** `6f53490` · **Agent:** LEDGER-CORE with QA-AUDITOR
- No migration. No schema change — this reads a table that already existed.

## Known limitations

- **No pagination.** 200 rows maximum, most recent first. The page says so rather than implying it is the whole history.
- **No date-range filter**, only action. An auditor asks for *"everything in March"* first.
- **No export**, which for this page specifically is what an auditor actually wants — they will not read it on screen.
- **`reverseJournalEntry` still writes no audit row.** The entry rows carry `reversalOfId`/`reversedById`, so the *fact* is recorded; the actor and timestamp are not, and I9 lists "reverse" explicitly. Visible now that there is a page where its absence shows.
- **`request_id` is null on every row** and the column is not displayed. Nothing threads one from the adapter.

author: atomlink-ye
body:
## Why

`pnpm run verify` is `check && test && build`, and `check` is `lint && ... && test:web && ...` chained with `&&`. `lint` runs `prettier --check .` **first**, so any formatting violation anywhere in the repo exits 1 and **`test:web` never runs**.

Nine files had violated prettier for a while (`.shoot.mjs`, `REPORT-workui.md`, three docs, three source files). The effect was not cosmetic — the web browser suite was effectively **disabled in CI**, and the `deterministic` job's red was read as "formatting only" while the suite underneath it went unrun.

Master currently fails **45 browser tests across 11 files** that CI never reported. Those are fixed separately on `fix/wui3-web-suite`; this PR only restores the feedback loop.

## What

`prettier --write` output only. No behavioural edits.

## Verification

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm lint` | was exit 1, now **exit 0** |
| `pnpm web:check:types` | clean |
| `pnpm test:unit` | 1 failed / 205 passed |
| same test on **unformatted** master | **same 1 failure** |

The single unit failure is pre-existing (`host-native-require-native-postgres`, needs a live Postgres) and unrelated to formatting — verified by stashing the format changes and re-running.

`git diff -w` still shows changes because prettier also re-wrapped code: added parens around a `? :` expression and split a long `.map()` argument. Both reviewed individually; semantics unchanged.

body:
## What

Split each LLM interaction's **user input** and **LLM return** into two independent records in a new `llm_messages` table, with the return tracing back to the exact input it answers (`assistant.parent_id -> user.id`).

```
reason_turns (1)  -- run header (provider/status/usage/duration/run_id)
   |-- llm_messages (N)  user input (seq 0) + assistant output (seq 1, parent_id -> input)
   `-- llm_events   (N)  raw provider stream (unchanged, still gated by AUTONOMY_LLM_EVENTS)
```

## Decisions (from review)

1. **Do not remove** the existing `reason_turns.input / raw_output / normalized_output` columns for now -- they are dual-written; fully backward compatible.
2. **Accept** the `Store` signature change: `BeginReasonTurn` returns `ReasonTurnHandle{TurnID, InputMessageID}` and `FinishReasonTurn` consumes it.

## Changes

- `src/store.go`: `Store` gains `ListLLMMessages`; new `LLMMessage` / `ReasonTurnHandle` / role constants; `Begin`/`Finish` signatures updated; `InsertReasonTurn` documented as writing both messages.
- `src/sqlite_store.go`: `llm_messages` DDL + indexes; transactional writes (one-shot `InsertReasonTurn` writes header + both messages, linked); `recordAssistantMessage` (idempotent via `UNIQUE(turn_id, seq)` + `INSERT OR IGNORE`); `ListLLMMessages`; idempotent backfill of pre-existing `reason_turns` rows.
- `src/llm_trace.go`: carry the handle through Begin/Finish/flush.
- Tests: new `src/llm_message_test.go` (separate + linked records, one-shot path, streamed path, backfill idempotency).
- Docs: new `docs/llm-message.md`; updated `docs/llm-event-stream.md`, `docs/store.md`, `docs/README.md`, `README.md`.

## Notes

- `llm_messages` is always written; `AUTONOMY_LLM_EVENTS` still only controls `llm_events`.
- No data loss: existing DBs get messages backfilled on open; existing header columns are untouched.

## Tests

`go test ./...` passes.

author: zerithza
body:
The host-ownership rule that #281 (arb-gphi) applied to eight test classes was written
down in exactly one place: a doc comment on `CategoryParamCapTests.DisposeAsync`. This
states it in the standards and enforces it in IL, so the ninth instance fails the build
rather than being rediscovered.

## The rule (docs/standards/process.md)

A new section, "A class that creates a config directory owns the host", between *Test
categories* and *Cecil IL scans*. A class that creates a `/config` directory must:

- take its root factory from `ArbitarrWebApplicationFactory.OverConfigDirectory(dir)` (or
  an owning factory it constructs), never from a shared `IClassFixture<WebApplicationFactory<Program>>`;
- implement xunit's `IAsyncLifetime`, **never a bare `System.IAsyncDisposable`** — xunit v2
  awaits the former and silently ignores the latter, so the second spelling means the
  teardown never runs and says nothing about it;
- await the factory's own `DisposeAsync` **first**, draining the host and returning its
  pooled handles, and only then call `ConfigDirectoryTeardown.Delete`.

The shape this rules out is the one that looks harmless: deriving with `WithWebHostBuilder`
from a shared fixture. The derived host belongs to the root, which xunit keeps alive until
the assembly finishes — so the delete runs under a live host, `Delete` throws by design, and
it fails whichever test happened to be disposing rather than the one that caused it. That is
a teardown fault, not a flaky test, and switching to the non-throwing `TryDelete` makes it
silent rather than fixing it.

**Per-test `WithWebHostBuilder` on a root the class OWNS stays fine** and is called out
explicitly — the rule is about where the root came from, not about deriving from it. The
teardown helper's own remarks are linked, not copied. The Cecil-scans section gains a bullet for the new scan; the earlier "four to five" count is superseded by the second commit, which corrects the census to seven Cecil scans plus eight other classes (HostBlockingAsyncCallTests and SqliteConnectionOwnershipTests were already scans and unlisted).

## The scan (ConfigDirectoryHostOwnershipTests)

A Cecil scan over `Arbitarr.Integration.Tests`: no type may both take the shared
`WebApplicationFactory<Program>` (by `IClassFixture<>` row **or** constructor parameter) and
call `ConfigDirectoryTeardown.Delete`/`TryDelete`. `TryDelete` is banned alongside `Delete`
for the reason above. `ClearPools` is deliberately not banned — clearing pooled handles under
a live host is harmless and is what the caller-supplied-directory host does legitimately.

No allow-list: the fix is to give the class its own root, and an exemption would preserve
exactly the fault the scan detects. Nothing was added to `ProductionProcessGlobalStateTests`'
allow-list. The scan passes on current master — zero instances after #281, so there is no
offender to report.

## The positive control bit, and what it found

Per CLAUDE.md §4 the detection was mutation-tested, and the mutation caught a live defect:
the **first version of the scan passed on a genuine offender**.

Grafting the banned shape onto `CategoryParamCapTests` showed why. A correct teardown is
`async Task DisposeAsync()`, so the compiler moves the body into a nested
`<DisposeAsync>d__6` state machine — the `call` to the delete helper is not in any method the
class itself declares. A walk over `type.Methods` therefore found nothing on precisely the
shape the scan exists to catch: it would have missed **every realistically-written offender**
while its own non-vacuity test stayed green. That is the vacuous-assertion shape CLAUDE.md §4
records as having shipped three times, and non-vacuity discipline alone would not have caught
this one either.

Fixed by recursing into nested types; re-running the mutation confirms it now reports
`CategoryParamCapTests/<DisposeAsync>d__6.MoveNext calls ...ConfigDirectoryTeardown::Delete`.
The in-assembly bait is now `async` for the same reason, so the gap cannot reopen unnoticed,
and a sibling bait that takes the fixture but deletes nothing proves the scan requires *both*
halves rather than flagging every fixture consumer.

One deliberate deviation worth review: the name-anchor test checks the fixture type against
**field** types rather than asserting that some type takes it. Since #281 no type takes it,
and that absence is the rule holding — an assertion that a violation-shaped consumer exists
would fail exactly when the tree is correct.

## Verification

Measured, re-run after rebasing onto current master (which touched an Integration.Tests
file); counts were identical before and after the rebase, so these figures are current rather
than superseded.

- `dotnet build --no-incremental` — 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `dotnet test -m:1 tests/Arbitarr.Architecture.Tests` — **39 passed**, 0 failed (master 36; +3)
- `dotnet test -m:1 tests/Arbitarr.Integration.Tests` — **434 passed**, 0 failed (unchanged)

body:
`×` on a split chat pane now opens **Archive chat?** whether the agent is running or stopped. Confirm stops a running agent, archives the session, and drops the pane; the split re-flows as today. When the chat is the tab's only session and the tab has drawer shells, the existing **Archive all?** shows instead with its counted body. `⌘W` in a split does what `×` does, through one `PaneCloseBehavior` fork shared by the button and the `close-pane` handler. The empty stub `×`, the terminal `×`, `⋯ → Archive chat`, the sidebar's Archive, and Restore are untouched, and the tooltip stays **Close pane**.

The dialog uses the archive icon with the danger button every other confirm uses. The body follows the pane's card: a running chat reads `<name> is still running. Archiving stops it. You can restore the chat from Settings → Archived.`, a stopped one `You can restore <name> from Settings → Archived.`, with `<name>` the same label the sidebar and the fork dialog use and `this chat` as the fallback.

The pane leaves the persisted layout only after the archive marker is set: confirm records the close intent and archives through the existing sidebar path, and the archive completion drops the pane once tabs have reloaded and the leaf is an empty stub. That ordering is the bug being fixed; closing first let the next tree read re-adopt the session as a fresh single-pane tab at the end of the project. The intent captures the requesting tab at request time, is kept per session while the archive runs, is released only by the archive that attempted that session, and is applied to the layout found by tab id, so overlapping closes in a split, a tab switch while archiving, and a tab shortcut pressed under the dialog all land on the right pane.

author: zacxdev
body:
**Split out of #1586.** This shipped there as commit 2 of 2. A round-1 audit of #1586 returned two 🔴 against the *other* item (the restore-refusal rework) and **nothing against this one** — the audit's own words: *"Retention numbers check out: 22.73 MiB at 672 (claimed 22.6), richer_generation 21.56 ms at 672, linear not O(n²), prune fine."* It is the operator's explicit ask, it has no dependency on the rework, and it should not wait on it. #1586 keeps the refusal fixes and reverts this change on its own branch.

⚠ Both branches touch `scripts/session-analysis/tests/test_tmux_session_restore.py`, so whichever merges second will need a trivial merge. These tests are appended at the end of the file here to keep that to a minimum.

---

## What this changes

`KEEP_GENERATIONS = 192` → **672** in `scripts/tmux-session-restore.py` — 7 days at continuum's 15-minute autosave, up from 48h. Plus its comment block and the `scripts/README.md` row.

⚠ **Premise restated correctly:** *"store all saves instead of just the most recent"* is **already shipped** — that is #1383, which introduced generations and they are live on both hosts. This PR is **purely the retention window**. Nothing about what gets written changes.

**Why 48h was not enough.** The 192 constant was argued from a worst case of "a Friday-night crash noticed Sunday" (~40h). 2026-09-11 refuted that worst case: the tmux server died **twice in 24h**, and the second recovery leaned on generations from before the first.

## Measured at the new bound

672 synthesised generations of the live 53-entry shape (~34 KiB each, plan + cheat-sheet), host at load ~78:

| n | disk | `richer_generation` (warm) | `prune_generations` (no-op) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 138 | 4.6 MiB | 5–8 ms | 0.2 ms |
| 192 | 6.5 MiB | 7–8 ms | 0.3 ms |
| **672** | **22.6 MiB** | **25–38 ms** | 0.6–0.9 ms |

An independent re-measurement during the audit got 22.73 MiB and 21.56 ms at 672, and confirmed the scaling is linear rather than O(n²).

⚠ Those figures are **warm** — the directory had just been written. The previously recorded **0.26s cold at 138** was a genuinely cold page cache; the measured 138→672 ratio (~3–7×) puts a cold scan at 672 around **~1–2s**. That is an extrapolation from a measured ratio, **not a measured number**, and the source says so. I could not drop the page cache without root.

**Live dir today: 192 generations / 6.53 MiB — it is sitting AT the old cap.** (An earlier draft of this comment said 146 / 4 MiB, which was already stale when written; corrected in-source.)

## 🔴 What the extra retention does NOT buy

It widens **manual** recovery — `restore --plan <generation>` can now reach a week back instead of two days. It does **not** widen the automatic remedy: `richer_generation` scans at most `RECOVERY_ALERT_WINDOW` (4) generations behind the pointer, so `--best` reaches exactly as far at 672 as at 192. That bound is deliberate and measured (an unbounded scan fired on 134 of 140 pointer positions). They are independent knobs, and if the ask had been "make `--best` see further" this would be the wrong constant. Now stated in the source, in the README row, and pinned by `test_the_automatic_remedy_is_NOT_widened_by_retention`.

## Red / green matrix

Base **`663bc86a`** (`origin/main`). `nix develop ~/workspace/devrc -c python3 -m pytest scripts/session-analysis/tests/test_tmux_session_restore.py -q`, `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`.

| | result |
|---|---|
| base script + new tests | **1 failed**, 139 passed — `test_retention_spans_a_week_at_continuums_cadence`: *"retention spans 48h … short of the 7 days asked for"* |
| HEAD | **140 passed** |

The claim is pinned as a **derived span**, not as `== 672`: the literal is a consequence of the ask *and* continuum's cadence, and `== 672` would go green for a cadence change that silently halved the window.

Two of the three new tests are **labelled INVARIANT GUARDS in-source** and are green at base by construction — they are not counted as regression coverage:
- `test_pruning_still_behaves_at_the_FULL_retention_bound` derives its fixture size from the constant, so it is green at 192 and 672 alike. It is the mechanical confirmation the pruner still behaves at the real bound — nothing exercised it before (every other pruning test runs at a fixture-sized 3).
- `test_the_automatic_remedy_is_NOT_widened_by_retention` pins the two knobs as independent.

## Mutation matrix

`PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, restored from a `cp -a` pristine copy between mutants (never `git checkout --`), whole test file per mutant (no `-k` filter), occurrence count asserted before each replacement. **Green control 140 passed → restored control 140 passed.**

| mutant | result | killed by |
|---|---|---|
| R1 retention constant reverts to 192 | KILLED | `test_retention_spans_a_week_at_continuums_cadence` |
| R2 `prune_generations` hardcodes 192 | KILLED | `test_pruning_still_behaves_at_the_FULL_retention_bound` +1 |
| R3 `prune_generations` keeps one too many | KILLED | `test_pruning_still_behaves_at_the_FULL_retention_bound` +2 |
| R4 `prune_generations` ignores `protect` *(positive control)* | KILLED | `test_pruning_never_deletes_the_generation_the_pointer_is_on` +3 |
| R5 the scan window is coupled to retention | KILLED | `test_the_automatic_remedy_is_NOT_widened_by_retention` |

**5/5 killed, 0 survived.**

## Deploy note

🔴 `scripts/tmux-session-restore.py` **runs from the working tree** (the systemd unit and the continuum post-save hook both exec `%h/workspace/devrc/scripts/tmux-session-restore.py`), so `ship.sh`'s fast-forward *is* the deploy for this file — no `home-manager switch` needed. Retention takes effect on the next `save`; the dir grows from 192 toward 672 at ~96/day and nothing prunes retroactively.

author: xnilsit
body:
### 10G-only L2 announcements

`CiliumL2AnnouncementPolicy` had no `interfaces` set, so any UP link could win the leader election. kube-srv-01 has its 1G onboard NIC up alongside its 10G port, so LoadBalancer traffic could land on 1G.

| node | 10G | other UP |
|---|---|---|
| kube-srv-01 | `enp1s0f0` | `enp2s0` (1000 Mb/s) |
| kube-srv-02 | `enp5s0f0np0` | — |
| kube-srv-03 | `enp1s0f0` | — |

`^enp[0-9]+s[0-9]+f[0-9]+(np[0-9]+)?$` matched with Go's `regexp` against every interface name on the three nodes: matches `enp1s0f0`, `enp1s0f1`, `enp5s0f0np0`, `enp5s0f1np1`; rejects `enp2s0`, `enp3s0`, `enp4s0`, `bond0`, `lo`, `cilium_host`.

### Dual-stack external gateway VIPs

`envoy-external` and `envoy-external-direct` get `fd2e:9a41:6b8c:1::151` and `::152` alongside their v4 VIPs, matching `envoy-internal`. Both are inside the `CiliumLoadBalancerIPPool` block `fd2e:9a41:6b8c:1::/112`, and the EnvoyProxy service already runs `ipFamilyPolicy: RequireDualStack`.

author: rcarback
body:
iOS suspends a backgrounded app, and a suspended process runs no code, so it
cannot send or answer keepalives. This change takes the two things the platform
does allow.

**One app-wide background task assertion.** `SessionManager` asks iOS to defer
suspension when the app backgrounds, and releases the assertion on return. The
grant runs about 30 seconds and belongs to the app rather than to each
assertion, so exactly one lives in `SessionManager`. No new `UIBackgroundModes`
entry is declared, and no `BGTaskScheduler` work is added.

**The health check is decided on return, not on the way out.** Sessions used to
be marked for a health check the moment the app backgrounded, which meant a
10-second glance at another app cost a full transport rebuild. A session is now
covered on the way out, so a connection that drops mid-background does not
dismiss the terminal, and the decision of whether to check happens on return:
the process was interrupted, or the session is no longer alive.
`BackgroundResumePolicy` holds that decision as a pure function so it can be
tested. A pull-down of Control Center, which moves the app to `.inactive` and
back without a `.background` phase, costs nothing.

**Keepalives every 45 seconds.** A connected session sends
`keepalive@openssh.com` and counts the answers. Servers refuse that request
name, and the refusal is a complete round-trip, so a refusal counts as an
answer. Four consecutive unanswered ticks report the connection dead, which is
180 seconds after the last answered round-trip. That window is deliberately
wide, because a false dead verdict tears down a live session. This also fixes
idle foreground sessions being reaped by `ClientAliveInterval` or by
address-translation timeouts.

`checkConnection()` now uses a keepalive round-trip instead of opening an exec
child channel to run `true`, so a stalled socket fails faster. The timer stops
when the channel closes, so a session ended with `exit` does not report a
second, spurious death three minutes later.

Needs the matching `sendGlobalRequest` API in rcarback/swift-nio-ssh; the pinned
revision in `project.yml` moves with it.

Adds 23 unit tests across `KeepaliveTrackerTests`, `BackgroundTaskAssertionTests`,
and `BackgroundResumePolicyTests`. Suite goes from 178 to 201, 0 failures.

Long absences still end the connection. The platform allows no way around that,
and `docs/gnu-screen.md` now says so and points at Screen.

author: famibelle
body:
Mise en œuvre de [`REVISION-CARNET.md`](https://github.com/famibelle/LuxKeyb/blob/main/REVISION-CARNET.md), dont la section 11 — ajoutée ici — note les écarts par rapport au plan. Version **22.0.0**.

Le carnet gardait les mots gagnés dans les sept jeux ; il ne réparait pas l'oubli. Une carte lue une fois à l'ouverture de la pochette était rangée dans une grille que rien n'obligeait à rouvrir : une étagère à trophées là où il fallait un paquet qui revienne vous voir.

## Ce que ça fait

- **Six boîtes de Leitner**, intervalles 1-3-7-16-35-90 jours. Une carte sans faute est acquise en six révisions et cinq mois.
- **Douze cartes par session**, les plus anciennement dues d'abord puis les plus fragiles.
- **La difficulté monte avec la boîte.** Boîtes 0-1 : reconnaissance, on retourne la carte du carnet elle-même. Boîtes 2+ : production, on **écrit** le mot sur le pavé de Kräizwuert, seul clavier de l'application à porter `Ä Ë É Ö Ü`.
- **Le clavier est l'examen.** Un mot écrit dans un vrai message monte d'une boîte sans qu'on le demande.
- **Placement** : ligne « à revoir » sur la bannière du hub et bouton qui passe de « Ouvrir » à « Réviser » ; pastille `🔁` dans l'en-tête du carnet ; barre de six segments sous chaque vignette.

Des boîtes de Leitner et non SM-2 ni FSRS : SM-2 demande au joueur de noter sa propre réponse de 1 à 4 et fait de cette note un exposant, question à laquelle personne ne répond honnêtement ; FSRS s'ajuste sur un journal de milliers de révisions, or rien ne sort de l'appareil — nous livrerions des paramètres ajustés sur les révisions de quelqu'un d'autre, dans une autre langue. C'est le refus déjà écrit pour la rareté des cartes.

## Deux mesures qui corrigent le plan

**Les phrases du LOD sont indexées par famille.** 97,1 % des formes des viviers ont une phrase, mais **66,6 % seulement y apparaissent littéralement**. Masquer une forme sœur ferait noter la carte sur un mot qui n'est pas le sien, donc le tiers restant tombe sur le repli par la glose — bien plus souvent que le plan ne le supposait.

**L'ambiguïté des gloses avait été mesurée sur un tirage uniforme.** Un carnet ne se remplit pas au hasard : il prend d'abord les mots que les jeux servent le plus, donc les plus polysémiques. En ordonnant par fréquence, **12 à 15 %** des cartes partagent leur premier sens à 120 cartes, contre 1 à 2 % annoncés. Ce n'est donc pas le tableau qui autorise le repli mais la règle d'acceptation — n'importe quelle carte du paquet dont la glose est celle affichée — qui devient le mécanisme et non un raffinement.

## Vie privée

Le bilan « vous l'avez écrit vous-même » demandait une seconde donnée de frappe que le plan n'avait pas vue : savoir **quelles** cartes le clavier a promues. Écrite dans les préférences — sauvegardées dans le nuage — cette liste ferait franchir la frontière à la trace exacte des mots tapés. Elle ne vit qu'en mémoire ; ce qui part dans les préférences est la seule échéance, où une carte montée par le clavier est indiscernable d'une carte révisée. La référence des compteurs vit dans `filesDir`, à côté du fichier d'usage.

**Correction apportée en cours de PR.** Le premier commit ajoutait un `<exclude domain="file">` explicite aux deux fichiers de règles de sauvegarde, pour que l'invariant soit écrit plutôt que déduit. **Android ne le permet pas** : `FullBackupContent` n'accepte une exclusion que dans un chemin *déjà inclus*, et comme le domaine `file` n'est inclus nulle part, l'exclure est une erreur fatale pour `lintVitalRelease` — les deux builds de release sont tombés dessus au run #159. La protection de `filesDir` reste donc ce qu'elle a toujours été, une omission ; ce qui a été ajouté à la place est `SauvegardeInterneTest`, qui échoue si ce domaine apparaît dans l'un des deux fichiers, dans un sens ou dans l'autre, et qui garde aussi les deux moitiés inverses : `sharedpref` doit rester inclus (sinon le carnet repartirait de zéro à chaque changement de téléphone) et `device.xml` exclu.

## Le débit reste le risque, et le test le dit

Six révisions par carte : en régime établi la charge quotidienne vaut six fois le nombre de cartes ajoutées par jour, donc **12 par session soutiennent 2 nouvelles cartes/jour** là où une grille de Wuertplaz en verse neuf. Simulé sur 400 jours : 0 carte de retard à 2/jour, 381 à 3/jour, 2 772 à 9/jour. `WidderhuelenPlanTest` fige cette arithmétique et échouera, avec un message explicite, si quelqu'un monte le plafond en croyant rendre service. La sortie n'est pas d'élargir la sortie mais de vanner l'entrée : la preuve par le clavier est le premier robinet, et l'usage dira s'il suffit.

## CI

Commit indépendant : chaque release poussait le même SHA deux fois — sur `main` puis avec son tag — et déclenchait deux builds complets. Mesuré sur la 21.0.0 : runs [#157](https://github.com/famibelle/LuxKeyb/actions/runs/34674997933) (7 min 13 s) et [#158](https://github.com/famibelle/LuxKeyb/actions/runs/34675002682) (8 min 35 s) sur `5406086`, à sept secondes d'intervalle. Le run de branche construisait quatre artefacts pour les jeter, `create-release` étant gardé par `startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')`.

Un groupe de concurrence nommé par le SHA les réunit, et **seul un run de tag annule ce qui tourne déjà** : il est le seul à publier, il doit toujours gagner. Un `cancel-in-progress: true` inconditionnel aurait laissé un run de branche tuer un run de tag si le tag était poussé en premier — huit minutes de runner contre une release perdue, silencieusement.

## Vérification

Le code a été écrit **sans compilateur** : `maven.google.com` est bloqué par la politique réseau de l'environnement d'exécution, donc AGP n'y est pas récupérable et ni `compileDebugKotlin` ni `testDebugUnitTest` n'ont pu y tourner. En contrepartie, toutes les attentes des deux fichiers de test ont été calculées indépendamment contre les actifs livrés : l'échelle `[0, 1, 4, 11, 27, 62]`, la coupure de 4 h, le décalage de fuseau, l'étalement de migration, les taux 89 / 97 / 66 %, et les 0 / 381 cartes de retard.

C'est donc la CI de cette PR qui a tranché, et elle l'a fait en deux temps : le run #159 a validé la compilation et les tests tout en rejetant l'exclusion de sauvegarde (voir plus haut), le run [#160](https://github.com/famibelle/LuxKeyb/actions/runs/34679874783) est **entièrement vert** sur `aa04fe9` — tests unitaires, APK et AAB debug, APK et AAB release signés, validation des artefacts.

Un test avait par ailleurs été attrapé avant même d'exister : la première version de « les grilles sont entièrement glosées » échouait sur `Betruecht` et `Gaang`, glosés sous leur forme minuscule. Le code de production les résout — le test était plus strict que ce qu'il gardait, et suit maintenant l'ordre de `TranslationDictionary.fiche`.

## Fichiers

| Fichier | Rôle |
|---|---|
| `carnet/Widderhuelen.kt` | Le calendrier seul : boîtes, jour local, file, étalement, notation. Sans `Context`, donc testable sur la JVM |
| `carnet/SessionWidderhuelen.kt` | La session : question, révélation, pavé, repassage, bilan |
| `carnet/PreuveClavier.kt` | Le clavier comme examen, et la frontière `filesDir` / préférences |
| `carnet/CarnetModels.kt` | Deux entiers par carte, et l'API de révision |
| `carnet/CarnetFragment.kt`, `CarteCarnet.kt`, `SettingsActivity.kt` | Bouton, barre de six segments, ligne de bannière |
| `WidderhuelenPlanTest`, `CarnetRevisionAssetTest`, `SauvegardeInterneTest` | Calendrier, débit, règle de notation, garde sur les actifs, frontière de sauvegarde |

author: promodeler314-a11y
body:
単体評価は「何も持っていない構成へ 1 つ足す」で測るので、既に持っているものと食い合うスキルを過大に評価する。並べ替えも、貪欲な初期解も、近傍の足切りも、その値で動いていた。

## 何が起きていたか

東京 芝1800m は終盤開始が 1200m、最終直線が 1275m で、差は 75m しかない。終盤に入ると目標速度が上がり、そこへ追いつくまでの間だけ加速が効く。モデルではこの追いつきに 261m かかるので、1275m の時点ではまだ 3.1 m/s の余地が残る。

その余地は、先に出た加速スキルが食う。実測は次のとおり。

| 先に持つもの | 真っ向勝負 | ハイボルテージ | 心弾んで | 足任せ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 何も無い | 0.1274 秒 | 0.2124 秒 | 0.1317 秒 | 0.1290 秒 |
| 終盤の加速を 1 つ（継承版） | 0.0800（63 %） | 0.1311（62 %） | 0.0833（63 %） | 0.0811（63 %） |
| 同じものの固有 Lv6 | 0.0239（19 %） | 0.0396（19 %） | 0.0253（19 %） | 0.0243（19 %） |

シミュレーション自体はこの食い合いを正しく再現していた。探索が単体の値しか見ていなかったのが原因である。

## 直したこと

初期解は 1 つ採るたびに残りの候補を測り直しながら積む。全部を毎回測ると候補数と採る数の積になるので、前に測った値を上界として扱い、上界でも首位に届かないものは測らずに飛ばす。噛み合って伸びる組み合わせでは上界が成り立たないため、この刈り込みは近似である。

初期解ができたあと全候補をそこへ足して測り直し、以降の並べ替えと近傍の足切りはその値で行う。

候補が数百あると 2 つのパスで数分かかるので、25 件ごとに途中経過を出す。探索の面と CLI にも限界貢献度の列を足した。

## 効き方

東京 芝2400m、候補 459 個、予算 600 pt で走らせた結果から。

| スキル | 単体 | 限界 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| アングリング×スキーミング | 0.2026 秒 | 0.1061 秒（52 %） |
| 彼方、その先へ… | 0.1828 秒 | 0.0973 秒（53 %） |
| レッツ・アナボリック！ | 0.1995 秒 | 0.1066 秒（53 %） |

レース 232,000 本、構成の評価 1047 回、198 秒。パスが 1 つ増えたぶん、評価の回数はおよそ倍になっている。

## これでは直らないもの

季節と天候と時刻と、他のウマ娘に関する条件を無視しているせいで、パッシブが積み上がる問題はそのまま残っている。これは PR #43 で直した。

順位条件の判定そのものの精度も、この変更では触っていない。

## 確かめたこと

- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm test`（181 件、限界貢献度の回帰検査を 1 件追加）
- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm e2e`（単体評価の表に限界の列が出ることを確認）

author: aepler315
body:
## Summary

Every world so far is a variation on **one** graphical experience — same painterly pipeline, same three wireframe characters, same post-FX stack — differing only in palette, silhouette profile, and a `drawXWorld()` branch inside `BiomeManager`. **Cathode** is the first that looks like a different *program*: low-resolution pixel art behind a CRT, chosen by hand rather than by the analyzer.

This is phase 1 of 4 (see phasing below) — the world, its renderer, and the picker. The cast lands in a later PR.

### It's a sibling renderer, not a `kind` branch

A `kind` branch only replaces *scenery*: the vector cast and the whole post-FX stack would still draw on top, and pixel scenery under bloom-lit wireframes isn't a different graphical experience. `main.js` only ever asks a renderer for `draw(sim, alpha)`, an optional `dispose()`, and an optional `composer` — so a world can implement that surface and own the frame. The renderer is already created **per song** (`main.js`, after the world is known), so dispatch is one new optional field:

```js
{ id: 'cathode', kind: 'cathode', renderer: 'pixel', manualOnly: true, ... }
```

Worlds without `renderer` take the existing path byte-identically, and `?renderer=webgl` is unaffected. `BiomeManager.js` (6854 lines) is untouched — it still runs and still owns the section schedule; Cathode just never calls its draw path, and instead **reads** `currentBlend` to pick its persona.

### Authored pixels, not downsampled ones

Cathode draws into its own 320×180 buffer and scales up nearest-neighbour. That's what separates it from the existing `8bit` stage preset: the preset rasterizes vector art into a small buffer (soft, drifting edges), while this places whole pixels on purpose (hard edges that stay put). Its internal resolution is **independent of the stage preset**, so it looks like Cathode at 4K and the preset stays a pure performance lever.

### Biomes are hardware, not weather

`PHOSPHOR` (amber terminal) · `DMG` (Game Boy) · `BREADBIN` (C64) · `APERTURE` (NES) · `COMPOSITE` (CGA) — so the song moves between *eras* instead of between hours, rotated per section by the dramaturgical casting every world already has. This is the "its own variants" requirement, satisfied by existing machinery.

Ramps are curated rather than computed — an even RGB cube (what `PaletteQuantize` produces) reads as "downsampled"; these read as "authored" — and Bayer-dithered, so a four-colour sky is a gradient rather than four stripes.

### `manualOnly` is load-bearing

`buildCustomWorld` picks its base from `scoreWorlds(feat)[0]`, so a rankable Cathode could be cloned into a custom world carrying `kind: 'cathode'` — which the painterly renderer has no draw path for. Filtering at that one choke point covers recommendation and base-pick together. An explicit `worlds` argument is still honoured verbatim.

### The picker already existed

`#worldSelect`, its grid, the back button, and the entire `.worldCard` / `.worldCardPreview.<kind>` CSS vocabulary were already in `index.html` and `style.css` — nothing had ever populated the grid, because `offerWorldsThenStart` always auto-confirmed the custom world. It now renders cards (analyzed match first, hand-picked worlds next, the rest by score) and hands the click to the existing `confirmWorld()`. Manual-only worlds deliberately show **no score**, since printing one would imply a measurement never made.

Because that changes the user journey, `tools/smoke.mjs` now picks the recommended card instead of expecting playback to start on its own.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --test test/*.js` — **2212 passing, +21 new**. One unrelated pre-existing failure, see below.
- [x] `npm run test:smoke` — 16/16 checks pass, including the two updated for the new flow.
- [x] End-to-end in Chromium against a real upload: picker appears; 10 cards render with the analyzed match first and Cathode carrying no score; selecting Cathode yields `worldId: 'cathode'`, `backend: 'cathode'`, no `composer`; the stage comes back in **exactly 4 distinct colours** (the CGA persona the section cast into) with the sim advancing.

### ⚠️ Pre-existing failure on `main`, not from this PR

`test/sectionDetection.test.js` → *"a harmonic SSM boundary is not moved onto a nearby energy release…"* fails. It **reproduces on clean `main` with this branch's changes stashed**, and the test was **added by #204 itself** — it has never passed. The detected 60s harmonic boundary is still being pulled onto the 64s energy release (sections come out `0, 30000, 64000`), which is audit finding #6. Not fixed here deliberately: it's unrelated to this PR and fixing it would widen it. Happy to take it as its own PR.

## Phasing

1. **This PR** — picker, registration, renderer dispatch, pixel buffer + personas.
2. Backdrop layers, parallax, richer CRT pass.
3. The cast (sprites, family routing, beat-quantized choreography).
4. Persona transitions and perf tuning.

body:
## Phase 4.24: AI コーチング機能

### 概要
個々のユーザーの学習パターンを分析し、AI が自動生成した個別コーチングアドバイスを提供するシステム。

### 新規ファイル

#### 1. `lib/models/coaching_model.dart`
13 の Freezed モデルで構成：
- **CoachingSession**: セッション管理（userId, sessionId, advices, learningInsight）
- **CoachingAdvice**: 個別アドバイス（category, title, priority, actionableHint）
- **LearningInsight**: 学習分析結果（継続度、エンゲージメント、トレンド）
- **SubjectInsight**: 教科別分析（appId, accuracy, topicStrengths, strugglingTopics）
- **TopicStrength**: トピック別習熟度（masteryLevel 0-100）
- **CoachingGoal**: 学習目標・進捗管理（deadline, currentProgress）
- **CoachingFeedback**: ユーザーフィードバック（helpfulnessScore 1-5）
- **AICoachPrompt**: AI アドバイス生成用入力データ
- **CoachingAnalyticsEvent**: 分析イベントログ

#### 2. `lib/providers/coaching_provider.dart`
Firestore 統合と状態管理：
- **CoachingService**: Firestore ベースサービス
  - `getCoachingSession(userId)`: 現在のセッション取得
  - `getLearningInsight(userId)`: 学習分析結果取得
  - `getCoachingAdvices(userId)`: 優先度順アドバイス取得
  - `getCoachingGoals(userId)`: 未完了ゴール取得
  - `generateLearningInsight()`: パターン分析・洞察生成
  - `generateCoachingAdvices()`: 3-4 件のアドバイス生成
  - `recordAdviceAction()`: アドバイス実行記録
  - `createCoachingGoal()`: 学習目標作成

- **CoachingNotifier**: StateNotifier for mutable state

- **Riverpod Providers**:
  - `coachingSessionProvider`: セッション（FutureProvider.family）
  - `learningInsightProvider`: 学習分析（FutureProvider.family）
  - `coachingAdvicesProvider`: アドバイス一覧（FutureProvider.family）
  - `coachingGoalsProvider`: ゴール一覧（FutureProvider.family）
  - `coachingNotifierProvider`: StateNotifierProvider

**分析アルゴリズム**:
- 継続度スコア（-1.0～1.0）: 連続学習日数からトレンド計算
- エンゲージメント（-1.0～1.0）: 総学習時間からトレンド計算
- 学習パターン判定: consistent/bursty/irregular の 3 パターン
- 弱点検出: 教科ごとに accuracy < 70% を抽出
- 推奨フォーカス: 最も accuracy が低い教科

#### 3. `lib/widgets/coaching_dashboard.dart`
Material Design 3 UI ダッシュボード（~550 行）：
- **CoachingDashboard**: メインウィジェット（userId required）
  - LearningInsight と CoachingAdvice を監視
  - Loading/Error/Empty 状態対応

- **5 つのカードコンポーネント**:
  1. _CoachGreetingCard: 🤖 挨拶（学習パターンに応じた動的メッセージ）
  2. _LearningPatternCard: 継続度・エンゲージメント（パーセンテージ表示）
  3. _StrengthWeaknessCard: 強み・弱み分野（Chip で表示、最大 5 個）
  4. _CoachingAdvicesCard: トップ 3 アドバイス
     - カテゴリ別 emoji（🎯 weakness, ⭐ strength, 💪 motivation）
     - 実行済み（✓ アイコン）状態表示
     - onTap で `recordAdviceAction()` 呼び出し
  5. _TrendAnalysisCard: fl_chart LineChart で継続度・エンゲージメント可視化

### Firestore スキーマ

```
coaching/sessions/{userId}/current
  - sessionId, analyzedSubjects[], advices[], learningInsight, motivationScore

coaching/insights/{userId}/latest
  - subjectInsights: Map<appId, SubjectInsight>
  - overallLearningPattern, strengthAreas[], weaknessAreas[]
  - consistencyTrendScore, engagementTrendScore

coaching/advices/{userId}/{adviceId}
  - category, title, description, priority, givenAt, isActedUpon

coaching/goals/{userId}/{goalId}
  - targetSubject, goal, targetValue, deadline, currentProgress, isCompleted
```

### 使用例（各アプリ）

```dart
// ① 学習分析を取得
final insight = ref.watch(learningInsightProvider(userId));

// ② アドバイスを取得
final advices = ref.watch(coachingAdvicesProvider(userId));

// ③ アドバイス実行を記録
await ref.read(coachingNotifierProvider.notifier)
  .recordAdviceAction(userId, adviceId);

// ④ ダッシュボード表示
Navigator.push(
  context,
  MaterialPageRoute(builder: (_) => CoachingDashboard(userId: userId)),
);
```

### Integration Points

- **shared_core**: 全 7 アプリ（eigo, sansu-kore, kokugo-kore, newrepo, social_quiz_app, shinshin, shogaku-kore-programming）で利用可能
- **Firebase**: Firestore コレクション統合
- **Flutter Riverpod**: 既存 Provider パターンに準拠
- **Material Design 3**: 既存テーマと統合

### CI/CD 実行状況
- [x] Code generation (Freezed)
- [x] Lint analysis
- [ ] Tests (待機中)
- [ ] Build validation (待機中)
