body:
## Summary

- **GPT-6 Astra is the Codex preset model.** `gateway.defaultModel` → `gpt-6-astra` (Q-M3); `gpt-5.6-sol` stays selectable. The gateway lists Astra in `GET /v1/models` and answers `POST /v1/responses` for it. Template limits (`model_context_window = 372000`, `model_auto_compact_token_limit = 300000`) are unchanged on purpose: Codex's bundled model catalog lists Astra and Sol with identical `context_window` 272000 / `max_context_window` 872000. `get_codex_config_template` now returns `CodexConfigTemplate` (toml + the two limits) and the config card quotes the live model name and the numbers through parametrised strings in both locales instead of hard-coding `gpt-5.6-sol` / `300000` / `372k`.
- **Fast UI toolkit re-pinned to the current Codex desktop builds** (ADR-0007): `CodexFastUI-Minimal-2026.09.12.zip` replaces 2026.08.19; `TESTED_CODEX_BUILD` = `OpenAI.Codex 26.903.8094.0 / 26.908.4834.0` (offline MSIX at persistent.oaistatic.com / Microsoft Store + auto-update). The gate string occurs exactly once in `webview/assets/app-initial-<hash>.js` of both builds, so the patch logic is unchanged; the candidate file regex additionally covers `app-primary`, and `TOOLKIT_SHA256` is re-pinned.
- **Two defects fixed on the way.**
  1. The toolkit's `verify.ps1` / `restore.ps1` failed before doing anything when launched the way the app launches them (`-File` without `-Root`): the `[CmdletBinding()]` param default derived `-Root` from `$MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path`, which Windows PowerShell 5.1 leaves null there. Present since `2026.07.30-minimal`, so "Check the copy" / "Undo the patch" never worked. The scripts now resolve the root in the body.
  2. The app ran the script copies `install.ps1` left in the install root, i.e. whichever toolkit made that root. `fast_ui::command_for` now runs all three actions from the freshly extracted, hash-verified toolkit and passes `-Root <install root>` to Verify / Restore, so existing pilot installs need no rebuild.

## Verification

- `npm run check` green: 405 frontend tests, 341 Rust tests, clippy pedantic `-D warnings`, i18n parity (807 keys), nsis check.
- Host dry run of the rebuilt toolkit (never launched, nothing under WindowsApps / `~/.codex` touched): install against the installed 26.908 client and against the 26.903 MSIX tree → `patchStatus: patched` on both; `verify.ps1` exit 0 on both copies (gate / syntax / isolated profile / shortcut OK); `restore.ps1` exit 0, `app.asar` back to the recorded source hash. The old `verify.ps1` under the same launch exits 1 with "Cannot bind argument to parameter 'Path' because it is null".
- New tests: Astra template rendering, DTO ↔ toml consistency, camelCase wire shape of `CodexConfigTemplate`, `-Root` argument for Verify / Restore, archive top-level directory pinned to `TOOLKIT_DIR_NAME`, card hides number-quoting strings until the first template response.
- Adversarial review (5 lenses × 3 refuters): 2 confirmed findings, both fixed in `90518ac`.
- **Not yet run:** the clean-VM regression round in EzRouter (the wizard installing 26.903, applying `config.toml` with Astra, building the patched copy, Speed row at runtime). It is staged and blocked only on a UAC click on the build host; details and the exact job list are in the round-6 report.

## For testers

- CI is green on this PR (web + Rust on Windows and macOS), but the `bundle` job only runs for pushes to `main` and for `release/*` branches, so this PR produces no installer artifacts by itself. Installers come from a pilot tag through the release workflow (unsigned pre-release, as for the `v0.1.0-test.N` rounds) once the PM wants one.
- A locally built Windows installer with the same code exists on the build host as `SeedRouter Onboarding_0.1.1-test.1_x64-setup.exe` (build-time version label only; no version files changed), SHA-256 `30c1d197f3496c1e1ed10c400f61225d499e3395e38a7dd06e692e17cdd019b4`.
- What to look at: the Codex tab suggests `gpt-6-astra`; the config.toml card names the model you typed and the 300000 / 372k figures; the Fast UI caveat names both tested builds; "Create the patched copy" → "Check the copy" → "Undo the patch" all complete on a machine with the current Codex client.

## Decisions / follow-ups

- Default model switched to Astra per PM; one line in `app-config.json` restores Sol.
- Observation for the gateway team: `POST /v1/responses` echoed `service_tier: "default"` even when `priority` was requested.
- Release still needs the usual version bump + CHANGELOG cut (docs/RELEASE.md); `[Unreleased]` already carries the entries.

author: steipete
body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

Maintainers can edit this same-repository branch using their repository permissions. GitHub's **Allow edits from maintainers** toggle applies to cross-repository PRs.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

The updater's ten real-signal tests repeatedly start the TypeScript loader in fresh child processes, adding avoidable work to the slow CLI test group. A separate corruption fixture also failed on machines with a group-writable default file mask, including Testbox.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each signal child now uses the existing invocation-scoped compiled runtime. Two test-only entry descriptors expose the admission and retained-recovery fixture; the ledger, database and executor descriptors are reused. All five imports resolve into the same compiled graph, preserving shared admission and database ownership. Source/watch execution retains its source loader.

The corruption fixture explicitly creates a private file, so it reaches the intended corrupt-content refusal instead of the separate unsafe-permissions recovery path.

## User Impact

No product runtime behavior, schema, configuration, shard count, test deadline or assertion changes. Every signal case still starts a fresh process, receives a real OS signal, joins cleanup and checks persisted run/sibling state. Production LOC is unchanged; the three test/support files add 27 lines and remove seven.

## Evidence

On the same source and dependencies, all ten signal cases passed before and after. Test/hook time fell from **56.633s to 16.677s**; total command time fell from **84.58s to 32.04s**. User plus system CPU fell from **125.30s to 43.74s**. Host load also fell from 53 to 31, so the full wall-time difference cannot be attributed solely to the patch; no memory saving is claimed.

The paired compiler preparations took 10.571s and 8.168s, with one additional source input and a net three additional outputs. A separate diagnostic preparation took 15.480s and verified the five concrete JavaScript entry URLs and all 4,579 output hashes before canonical disposal. Preparation varies with host load; the aggregate effect across CI's repeated preparations is not measured. The new fixture input is 5,059 bytes, and the two new stable output facades total 5,088 bytes; bundler hash propagation is not counted as thousands of independent new files.

The original corruption case failed under `umask 0002`: its default `0664` file correctly triggered unsafe-file quarantine. With explicit `0600` creation, the same rejection and byte-preservation assertions pass under `0002` and normal `0022`. Neighboring native executor, admission/schema, handoff database/recovery and URL-resolver checks passed **118 tests**, with one existing skip. This includes the current requester-revocation-before-Doctor case.

All selected changed-file checks passed, including core test types, scoped lint/format, ratchets, dependency guards and dead exports. Independent P2 review returned no findings on the final diff. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34680677217) passed. In its [targeted Node job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34680677217/job/103518746561), all ten signal cases passed with rounded case times totaling **6.42 seconds**. This is targeted PR CI, not a paired main-run or whole-job timing comparison.

author: fomotsar-commits
body:
## The bug

`useZapPlan` built its descriptor with `chainId = useChainId()` — the wallet's chain — and then passed *that same value* as `planZap`'s `expectedChainId`:

```ts
const descriptor: ZapDescriptor = { …, chainId, … };
return planZap(descriptor, routes, chainId);   // ← both sides are the wallet
```

The planner's only chain guard is `descriptor.chainId !== expectedChainId` ([planner.ts:252](frontend/src/lib/zap/planner.ts#L252)). Comparing the wallet's chain with itself, it could not fire on any chain, for any wallet. `chain-mismatch` was unreachable.

## What was and wasn't exposed

Nothing shipped broken. Two unrelated gates stood in front of it:

- `ZapPanel` disarms Start on `wrongChain = isConnected && chainId !== CHAIN_ID`.
- `useSwapQuote` deliberately gates its reads on the wallet's chain, so a wallet on Base composes no routes at all.

But the second gate is *why* this stayed invisible, and it produced the wrong answer: off-mainnet, the zap refused with **`route-unavailable` — "no floor to submit"**, blaming the route for a network problem. Meanwhile the planner's own guard sat behind two gates it doesn't own, either of which could move.

## The fix

Pass `CHAIN_ID`. That is where every address the plan targets is compiled in, so it is the only chain the plan can execute on.

`descriptor.chainId` stays the **wallet's** chain on purpose — it is the persistence key (`zapRunKey(account, chainId)`) and part of `planId`, and `useZapRun` loads runs back with the wallet's chain. A plan that reached the run machinery off-mainnet would persist under a key nothing reads; the refusal now prevents that instead of relying on the panel's button state.

The detail string assumed the expected chain was the wallet's ("composed for chain X; the wallet is on Y"), which is false once the expected chain is the venue's. Reworded to name both chains and say which way to switch. No other caller or test pinned the old copy (swept the repo, including e2e and docs).

**Panel check:** on the wrong chain the refusal card now renders the accurate reason, alongside the existing "Switch to Ethereum mainnet" line by the button. One nit left alone as pre-existing generic copy for all refusal codes: the card's footer offers "the steps are still available one at a time on the Trade page…", which also needs mainnet.

## Tests

`useZapPlan.test.ts` gains a chain block that hands the hook **usable routes on the wrong chain** (the mocked quote ignores the chain entirely) — that is what makes it fail against the old call, which had routes in hand and no reachable chain check. Wallets on 8453 and 4663, plus a positive control on `CHAIN_ID` proving the same inputs otherwise compose.

Mutation-checked in both directions:

| Mutation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| restore `planZap(descriptor, routes, chainId)` | the 3 new hook tests fail, **nothing else** (positive control still passes) |
| restore the old detail string | the planner's reworded assertion fails |

`planner.test.ts`'s existing chain test was flipped to the production orientation (descriptor composed on 4663, venue on 1) and now pins both numbers in the detail.

## Gates

`npx tsc -b --force` (all three projects) · `npx eslint .` → 0 errors, changed files clean · `node scripts/check-unread-signal.mjs` ok · full `npx vitest run` → **602 files / 8583 tests, all passing**.

## Sibling PRs

Only #526 and #537 touch `useZapPlan.ts`; nothing else touches `planner.ts`.

Both make the *same* edit (#537 carries #526) to a different region — ungating the `routerFee` read. `useZapPlan.ts` auto-merges cleanly against both. I materialized the #537 merge and re-ran the zap suites: **113 tests, green**.

#526 does conflict with this branch, but in `frontend/src/test-utils/wagmi-mocks.ts`, a file this PR does not touch — it is **pre-existing**: #526 conflicts with `mvp-launch` on that same file today, independently of this change.

Worth noting: #537's new comment says *"The wallet's chain still decides the plan, below."* Before this PR that was not true — the planner compared the wallet with itself, and what actually stopped an off-mainnet plan was `useSwapQuote` returning empty legs. This fix makes that justification accurate.

author: hayes
body:
Fixes the three P2 findings from the `@pothos/plugin-validation` whole-plugin review. Each finding has its own commit with a regression test added first; all tests are new GraphQL-level executions in `packages/plugin-validation/tests/chained-validation.test.ts`.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Fix 2 changes runtime behavior for a supported combination. See [Behavior change](#behavior-change-input-type-validate-option--chained-validate) below before merging.

## 1. Input object chains executed backwards

`InputObjectRef.validate` prepends each schema, so the stored list is in reverse declaration order. Field schemas were reversed before use, but type schemas were consumed as stored, so input object chains ran last-declared-first.

**Fix:** reverse the stored type schemas at the consumption site in `src/index.ts` (`onOutputFieldConfig`), matching the existing field schema handling.

**Verified:** an add-one then multiply-two chain on `{ n: 2 }` returned `5` before the fix and returns the documented `6` after.

## 2. An input type `validate` option discarded chained validators

`onTypeConfig` read prior schemas from the obsolete `extensions.validationSchemas` key, while `InputObjectRef.validate` stores them under `extensions['@pothos/plugin-validation'].schemas`. When an input type declared both a `validate` option and chained validators, the hook replaced the namespaced storage with only the option schema and every chained validator was silently dropped.

**Fix:** read and merge the namespaced storage, mirroring `onInputFieldConfig` exactly.

**Verified:** two tests — a transform chain that returned `4` (option only) before and now returns `6`, and a chained `min(2)` constraint that was silently skipped before and now rejects `{ n: 1 }` with the expected issue message.

### Behavior change: input type `validate` option + chained `.validate()`

With the storage fixed, chained schemas run in declaration order followed by the options schema. That is the ordering already produced for arguments and input fields (instrumented transforms give `["A", "B", "OPT"]` for all three paths after this PR), so input types now behave consistently with the rest of the plugin.

**This is user-visible in a patch release.** Because the options schema runs last, a chained schema that reshapes the value can now fail at runtime where it previously "worked":

```ts
const reshape = zod.object({ n: zod.number() }).transform(({ n }) => ({ label: String(n) }));
const expectsN = zod.object({ n: zod.number() });

const Input = builder
  .inputType('In', { fields: (t) => ({ n: t.int({ required: true }) }), validate: expectsN })
  .validate(reshape); // TypeScript says args.input is { label: string }
```

For `{ value(input: { n: 2 }) }`:

- **before:** resolves with `{ n: 2 }` — the chained schema was dropped entirely (the bug this PR fixes), so the value silently disagreed with its declared type.
- **after:** `data: null`, `Validation error: input.n: Invalid input: expected number, received undefined` — the options schema now runs against the reshaped value and rejects it.

So this fix trades a silent wrong value for a loud error; it does not resolve the underlying type/runtime mismatch. `.validate<R>()` re-types the ref (`src/global-types.ts:81,93,97`) while the `validate` option does not (`:62,69,77`), so the declared type is always the last chained schema's output even though the options schema produces the runtime value. That mismatch is **pre-existing and plugin-wide** — the same failure already occurs for arguments on `main` — and making the options schema run first everywhere is a larger, breaking change that belongs to a maintainer decision, not to this patch. Raised separately; deliberately unchanged here.

## 3. A successful null transform skipped the rest of the chain

The schema reducers in `src/utils.ts` returned `null` both when a schema reported issues and when a schema successfully transformed a value to `null`, and `reduceMaybeAsync` treats `null` as the signal to stop. Standard Schema allows `null` as a successful output, so a null-producing transform silently skipped every following schema even though the inferred type promised the last schema's output.

**Fix:** a small `reduceSchemas` helper wraps values while reducing, so the failure state stays distinct from valid values. `reduceMaybeAsync` itself is untouched, so its existing tested contract still holds.

**Verified:** three tests — a sync `number -> null -> 7` chain and the async equivalent both returned `null` before and now return `7`; and a schema that rejects `null` after a null transform now reports its issue instead of being skipped.

## Checks

- `pnpm --filter @pothos/plugin-validation run test` — 7 files, 209 tests passing (203 before, 6 added), no type errors
- `pnpm --filter @pothos/plugin-validation run type` — clean
- `pnpm biome check packages/plugin-validation` — clean, no fixes applied
- `pnpm --filter @pothos/plugin-errors run test` (the only dependent package) — 63 passing, 4 skipped, unchanged

The full external Standard Schema provider matrix was not run; tests use zod and the plugin's own execution paths.

author: dericklobo
body:
Seven commits: the probe pass that now covers all nine subsystems (documentation only), and the fixes it produced.

## The probe pass — `docs/audits/2026-09-12-the-probe-pass/`

213 findings re-read against the code by nine read-only agents, each asked the question the 11 September verification pass did not: **is the finding's own suggested fix sound?** It was not, thirteen times.

- **Two fixes would break working, test-pinned behaviour.** ACC-23's "stop synthesising the retained-earnings line" would break a balance sheet that is currently self-correcting; ACC-25's `{name, url}` attachment payload re-opens the expiring-signed-URL and stored-XSS hole `domain/banking/attachments.py` exists to close.
- **Eleven more would break something smaller** — SALES-13 would print the CA practice's UPI ID on the client's own outward invoice; TDS-23 would turn a visible 422 into a silently mis-routed 26Q row; TDS-19 would drop a genuine §194-IA credit; FA-14's `is None` divides by zero. §9 lists them all.
- **Five materially false premises**, including PUR-28's, whose fix might `DROP` the four live policies it claims are absent.
- **Stale rates far above the 10% the last pass measured** — sales 59%, payroll 53%, fixed assets 50%, TDS 44%. Five tranches landed since the last rescore and none re-scored, so the finding files are no longer a usable work list on their own. These ten slice files are.

## What was wrong, and what changed

Every fix here is one shape: **a value the code needed and nobody supplied, answered with a plausible default instead of a question.**

### Things that were invented

**A TAN and a deductor PAN.** `/tds/returns` assembled the whole quarterly statement in the browser, so it wrote `const tan = "MUMB00000A"` and `deductor_pan: "AAAAA0000A"`. Both are the RIGHT SHAPE, so every validator passed and the return saved as "prepared" under a TAN belonging to nobody — worse than TDS-28 ("the CA re-types it"), because neither ever appeared on screen. Migration 325 was created for exactly this and nothing read it. `domain/tds/deductor.py` now resolves the block from `client_statutory_identity` and the client's own columns and refuses by name, one sentence per thing somebody has to go and record.

**A place of supply.** `POST /receipts` took `is_interstate` from the sales screen, which derived it from the CUSTOMER's state — the wrong party. An advance under §12(2)/§13(2) is taxed by the SUPPLIER's place of supply (CGST §25 with IGST §§7-8). Derived server-side now, and refused with a named gap when the client has no state recorded.

**Every quarter's deposits.** TDS-29: the browser sent every deductee out with `tds_deposited_paise` equal to the amount DEDUCTED, so `deducted − deposited` was zero by construction and the engine's shortfall check could never fire. §201(1A) charges 1.5% a month from the date of deduction on exactly that difference.

**A §211 calendar for a year that ended.** IT-33: the Income Tax hub carried "15 Jun 2025" through "15 Mar 2026" under a heading hardcoding "FY 2025-26". All four had elapsed, and the panel said so the only way it can — four rows reading "Due passed", which is exactly what it shows in March of a year it *is* right about.

**Twelve more year pickers.** Sweeping for the array spelling of the same defect found ten FY lists and two AY lists, of which **eight ended at 2025-26** — so from 1 April 2026 the current year could not be selected on the year-end screens, the tax-audit screen, the §32 screen, the Tally migration screen, the documents screen or the 26AS reconciliation. `assessmentYearChoicesAround` is added and is derived from the FY helper, not a second parser.

### Things that were asked for and could not be given

**Form 15CA (TDS-25).** The register raises a gap on every §195 bill whose acknowledgement is blank, and since PUR-14 that gap reaches the CA — so the product spent months telling them, on every foreign remittance, to record something no screen let them record. The panel is on the BILL (15CA is per remittance under Rule 37BB), keys on the server's resolved section, and contains no button: 15CA is filed on the portal under the remitter's own login.

**Professional tax with no state (PAY-05).** Ticking "PT" on the client-workspace form produced ₹0 every month forever, with no gap and nothing on the payslip. Article 276 makes deduction the employer's duty, so the shortfall plus interest is the firm's.

**EPS and Gratuity Act coverage (PAY-12 residual).** Both columns `NOT NULL DEFAULT true`, both read at six sites, on no model, in no CSV and on no form. A wrong `eps_eligible` diverts 8.33% to EPS **on the ECR**; `gratuity_act_covered` picks which limb of §10(10) exempts a leaver's gratuity.

### Things that were computed and shown to nobody

**IT-08's own working.** `basic_exemption_absorbed_paise` and `basic_exemption_absorption` were documented as existing "so a CA can see WHICH gain the exemption was set against"; a grep across the routers and the whole frontend found no reader. So the tax tab showed ₹20,800 on a ₹5,00,000 STCG and no account of the ₹4,00,000 that vanished — on an allocation the statute does not fix and the engine chooses.

**Exempt income.** Rendered as an input, sent, declared by the router and by the engine's request — and `compute()` never read it.

**A disposal's part-month shortfall**, and **the Rule 36(4) working**, both returned by the server and dropped by the screen.

### Things that were wrong

**§206C on a vendor.** TCS is collected by a SELLER from a BUYER and reported on 27EQ. Nothing refused it, and the supplier dropdown is served straight from the registry — so marking a vendor §206C withheld 0.1% of every rupee (its threshold is zero) and stamped the row 26Q.

**A guard that could not fail.** `test_every_registry_section_resolves_to_a_fileable_statement` called `return_type_for(residency)`, which never sees the section — so it asserted the same thing about the same two constants on every iteration. Demonstrated: the old body passes for 194IA, 194M, 206C and 194J alike.

**The Act's form number in a routing column (TDS-18).** `statement_form` returns "140" for a FY 2026-27 26Q; `tds_returns.return_type` CHECKs the four routing keys. Every save from that screen was rejected by the database from 1 April 2026.

**Server-side request forgery.** `_remote_image` fetched any URL with `follow_redirects=True` on every fee-invoice render, from Render's Singapore network. Now refused by literal, by internal name and by every address `getaddrinfo` returns, following redirects one hop at a time.

**Plus:** the second reverse of a payroll run gave nothing back (PAY-08 one cycle later); soft-deleted assets in the Gross Block; `asset.get('asset_code', default)` on a NULLABLE column producing one shared posting reference; a credit note reading a stranger's invoice date for its §34(2) window; an "Opening Balance" row becoming a zero-on-both-legs transaction; a delete-rule docstring that migration 322 had made false; an `import_status` chip that said "pending" forever; quantities to four decimals against a `NUMERIC(10,3)` column; `ledger-span` raising in mock mode; asset creation not lock-checked while correct and delete were; a UAN accepted at the API and refused by the ECR months later; §206AB FY-blind and documented as current law; three CSV columns required and discarded.

## Verification

**Negative controls run per fix**, staged and reverted individually — the counts are in each commit message. Highlights: `_undo_loan_recoveries` restored → 4 of 6 netting tests fail; `apps/api` reverted → 24 of 29 surfacing tests and 17 of 28 gap-field tests fail; the bill editor alone reverted → the 15CA guard fails by name; a §194IA rate row added → the rewritten registry guard fails while the old body passes on the same row.

**Four existing guards caught this work in the act**, which is what they are for: `test_every_gap_code_carries_a_sentence` on a gap with no message; `test_silent_s

author: jagduvi1
body:
## What

Adds "Fortsätt med Google" to login and register, mirroring **Cellarion's OAuth implementation** (the Google part; generic OIDC deliberately stripped per scope decision).

- **Backend** ([backend/src/routes/oauth.js](../blob/feat/google-auth/backend/src/routes/oauth.js)): authorization-code flow via passport-google-oauth20. Login-CSRF protection through a cookie-based state store (ported from Cellarion) + PKCE S256. Custom callback so no token ever travels in a URL — the httpOnly refresh cookie is set server-side and the SPA fetches its access token via the existing `/api/auth/refresh`.
- **Account resolution** (three steps, pinned by unit tests): already-linked `(provider, providerId)` → returns the account · existing account with the same **verified** email → links Google to it (per decision: accounts are linked) · otherwise → creates a new account with a generated unique username. Unverified Google emails are rejected outright (linking on one would be account takeover).
- **Token issuing** extracted to `services/authTokens.js` so SSO and password login mint identical sessions (same JWT claims, same rotating refresh cookie with replay detection).
- **User model**: `password` becomes conditionally required (SSO-only accounts have none, and can add one later via forgot-password); new `authProviders` array + index; `toJSON` exposes `hasPassword`/`linkedProviders`.
- **Frontend**: button + "eller" divider on Login/Register, hidden unless `GET /api/auth/sso/providers` says Google is configured (runtime probe → enabling SSO needs **no frontend rebuild**). `/login/callback` landing page with Swedish error messages. QR invites survive the round-trip (`/j/CODE` stashed in sessionStorage).

**Opt-in:** completely inert without `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`/`GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` — verified in Docker: button hidden, `/api/auth/google` → `?error=not_configured`, password login untouched.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` (backend): 13 tests green — account linking branches, verified-email guard, $elemMatch regression, username generation
- [x] `docker compose up --build`: all containers healthy; probe returns `{"google":false}`; nginx proxy + SPA fallback for `/login/callback` OK
- [x] Enabled-mode smoke (dummy keys): 302 to accounts.google.com with `state` + `code_challenge=S256`; `oauthState` cookie `HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/api/auth; Max-Age=600`; forged callback → `invalid_state`
- [ ] **End-to-end with real Google credentials** — blocked on the OAuth client (see below)

## For Johan (before this can go live)

1. Create an **OAuth 2.0 Client ID** (type *Web application*) in your Google Cloud Console: https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials
2. Authorized redirect URIs:
   - `https://glosan.app/api/auth/google/callback`
   - `https://glosan.jeklund.dev/api/auth/google/callback`
   - `http://localhost/api/auth/google/callback` (local Docker)
   - `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/google/callback` (Vite dev)
3. On the VM: add `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` + `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` to `.env`, then restart the backend only — the button appears by itself.
4. **One judgment call to review:** SSO-created accounts get `ageConsent: true`, carried by the consent text under the Google button ("Genom att fortsätta med Google bekräftar du att du är minst 13 år …") rather than a checkbox. Cellarion solves this with a post-login reconsent modal, which Glosan doesn't have. Say the word if you want a modal instead.

body:
## 概要

`.vrm` を含むパッケージが「モデルが無い」エラーで止まっていた問題への対応です。VRM の読み込みは再実装せず、[VRM format](https://extensions.blender.org/add-ons/vrm/) add-on が入っていればそちらに委譲し、無ければ標準の glTF インポーターにフォールバックします。バージョンは `1.1.0` → `1.2.0`。

### 変更点

- `.vrm` をモデル形式として認識（glTF バイナリなので glTF インポーターで読める）
- VRM add-on（`import_scene.vrm`）が登録されていれば委譲。add-on が MToon ノードグループ・アウトライン・Humanoid・スプリングボーン・表情を再現するので、マテリアルは組み直さず `.mat` 名が一致するものにカスタムプロパティだけ保存する（method `delegated`）
- インポートダイアログに "VRM via VRM Add-on"（既定 ON）を追加
- add-on がルートコレクションに置くオブジェクトとコライダー用コレクションをパッケージ用コレクションに移動（他のインポーターにも適用）
- 全モデルを委譲する場合は `.mat` 用テクスチャの展開を省略
- add-on が無ければ glTF インポーターで読み、同梱の `.mat` から組み直して警告で案内。組み直し後に不要になった埋め込み画像は削除
- VRM 0.x の制限付きライセンスで add-on が確認ダイアログを出した場合は、オブジェクトが作られていないことを警告（自動承認はしない）
- 統合テストの期待値に `enable_addons` を追加し、add-on を有効化した検証を可能にした
- README / README_ja / DESIGN.md を更新

### 検証

- 単体テスト 70 件成功（`_local/` の VRM 系パッケージで失敗していた 1 件も解消）
- 合成パッケージの統合テスト 53 件（`.vrm` 名の glb によるフォールバック経路を含む）、既存サンプルの統合テスト 42 件成功
- VRM 1.0 の実パッケージで add-on 委譲（警告 0）とフォールバック（9 マテリアルを `.mat` から再構築）の両方を確認

### 補足

- glTF フォールバックでは Blender の glTF インポーターが `glTF_not_exported` コレクションとプレースホルダーメッシュを 1 つ作る。無害なのでパッケージ用コレクション配下に移すだけにしている

author: 0xplayerone
body:
Closes #1889.

Web and smashers each restated the same deferred-telemetry plumbing: the activation-event list with a `started` guard, the `requestIdleCallback` schedule with a 3-second ceiling, and the entire GTM container bootstrap (data-layer start push, script element, append). The container bootstrap has been shared since M4.0 and docs already calls it; these were the last two copies.

## Shared pieces extended, not duplicated

- **`scheduleDeferredActivation` gains an `idleTimeout`** (default `1000`, so existing callers are untouched). Web and smashers want "first idle period, ceiling 3s"; the default is "wait 5s, then idle", so they would otherwise have kept their own scheduler.
- **`loadGoogleTagManager` gains a script id** (default `_next-gtm`). Web passes `web-gtm` and smashers `smashers-gtm`, so adopting the loader changes nothing observable in their DOM.

## What stays app-local, and why

Each module now records the reason in a comment:

- **The gating.** Web reads `data-analytics="true"` from a `#web-telemetry` element and only ships the module on production builds; smashers reads `data-sentry-enabled` / `data-analytics` from the document element. Unifying them is an analytics-policy decision.
- **The web-vitals payload.** Both apps send `metric_id`/`metric_rating`; the shared `sendWebVitals` sends `metric_label`/`non_interaction` and rounds CLS to an integer. Adopting it changes what GTM receives, so it needs an analytics owner rather than a refactor.
- **Sentry options and enable flags.**

## Verification

Production-mode builds of both apps (`PUBLIC_DEPLOY_ENV=production`), driven in real Chrome with `*googletagmanager.com/gtm.js*` blocked so the inserted element itself could be observed through a `MutationObserver`, plus a data-layer dump:

| | before (main) | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| web script | `web-gtm`, `…gtm.js?id=GTM-MHCXVXJZ`, `async: true` | identical |
| web data layer | `[{gtm.start, event}]` | identical |
| web Sentry | initialized | initialized |
| smashers script | `smashers-gtm`, same source, `async: true` | identical |
| smashers data layer | `[{gtm.start, event}]` | identical |
| smashers Sentry | initialized | initialized |
| activation | first idle period, 59–75 ms | first idle period, 34–97 ms |

The timings are three samples per side and overlap; the 3s ceiling never binds on localhost.

```text
bun run lint             9 workspaces, 0 warnings / 0 errors
bun run type-check       9 tasks, 0 errors
bun test test/contract/  570 pass / 0 fail
packages/ui tests        217 pass / 0 fail (incl. the new deferred-activation cases)

```

New `packages/ui/src/lib/deferred-activation.test.ts` covers the interaction path, the `delay: 0` path with the caller's ceiling, and the unchanged default. `gtm-source.test.ts` now expects the URL literal in exactly one module — its `PENDING_MIGRATION` allowlist is empty — and `route-surface.test.ts` asserts the apps *don't* restate the start push or the idle request any more.

author: ink-mapleshadow
body:
fix #16900

**问题**

vite 编译小程序时，页面 wxml 缺少 `<page-meta>` 节点：配置了 `enablePageMeta` 的页面里使用 `<PageMeta>` 完全失效（webpack5 编译器无此问题）。Taro 4.0.5 ~ 4.2.1 均可复现。

**原因**

`packages/taro-vite-runner/src/mini/emit.ts` 生成页面模板时存在两个问题：

1. 调用 `buildPageTemplate` 时未传入页面配置，平台覆写（如 [微信小程序](https://github.com/NervJS/taro/blob/main/packages/taro-platform-weapp/src/template.ts)）拿不到 `enablePageMeta`，不会生成 page-meta 片段；
2. 页面模板先于 base 模板生成，而覆写读取的 `transferComponents` 依赖 `buildTemplate` 填充，此时仍为空。

**修复**

- 生成页面模板前先计算 base 模板（结果复用于后续 emit，不重复生成），使组件信息就绪；
- `buildPageTemplate` 传入 `{ content: pageConfig, path: page.name }`，与 webpack5 编译器（MiniPlugin）行为对齐。

**验证**

- 最小复现仓库（React + TS + Vite，weapp）：https://github.com/INK-MapleShadow/taro-issue-16900-repro
- 修复前：`dist/pages/index/index.wxml` 只有 `<import src="../../base.wxml"/><template is="taro_tmpl"/>`；
- 修复后：页面 wxml 正常输出 `<page-meta ... page-style="{{pageMeta.p5||''}}" ...>`；
- `pnpm --filter @tarojs/vite-runner run build`（tsc）与 ESLint 均通过。

body:
## #352「下一击有优势」未生效：复现 ＋ 一行根因 ＋ 失败基线

### 根因（一行）

`Game.Combat.applyEffect`（`15-tables.twee:655`）确实写了 `fight.adv += eff.adv`（给「**下一击**」），但**同一轮结算末尾的回合推进块**（`10-core.twee:409-414`）紧接着：

```twee
<<set _f.adv to 0>>        ← 刚被 applyEffect 记上，就被清零
```

→ **宣告了却永不生效**。对照：`guard` / `skipFoe` 是**同轮消费**（本轮减伤/免挨），清零正确；`adv` 是**跨轮**语义，清零即 bug。

### 实测（状态级证据）

```
轮2：点「吹哨引它偏头，趁隙出刀」→ last.adv=1（UI 因此显示「下一击有优势」）｜fight.adv 结转=0
     → 下一手仍单骰
```

### 新增门 `test/combat-adv.mjs`（已知缺陷形式入链）

- 播种盟约/龙醒/好哨 → 最多 4 轮找到「产 adv」的那一手 → 断言**下一手骰数 > 1**（或以优势文案出现）；
- 现状 `⏳ [已知缺陷 #352]` **不判失败**（避免卡住 main）；修复后自然转绿，届时删 `KNOWN` 标记；
- **为什么此前没覆盖**：本仓所有战斗门都只测**同轮内**效果，**跨回合状态**是盲区（与 #350 那条「重放型缺陷在确定性 RNG 下隐形」同类）。

### 建议修法（供实现侧取舍）

1. **不在回合推进时清 `adv`**，改为**下一手消费时**清零（`fightresolve` 里已有 `<<if _f.adv>> <<sitecheck … "adv" …>>`，顺势清）；
2. 或把 adv 存到独立字段跨过推进块，消费后再清。

`npm test` **0 失败**（已知缺陷不计失败）。

Refs #352 · #350

author: foxalike-dev
body:
Implements the proposal in #42.

Two plots for unsupervised / continual learning runs. Both read the per-epoch `model.pt` checkpoints that `MontyExperiment` writes (`<experiment_log_dir>/<epoch>/model.pt`), or an explicit list of model files:

- `graph_growth_over_epochs`: one graph's nodes colored by the checkpoint in which they were added, on top of the ground-truth mesh.
- `graph_surface_distance`: per checkpoint, the median distance of the graph's nodes to the ground-truth mesh and the fraction farther than a threshold (default 15 mm), plus the last checkpoint's nodes colored on/off surface.

The mesh is placed as `GtMeshWidgetOps` places it (centered, YCB rotation, then the object's rotation and position). Object name and pose default to the episode that created the graph, read from `train_stats.csv`; both can also be given explicitly. Checkpoints are read with `PretrainedModelsLoader`, so `tbp.monty` does not need to be installed. Node identity across checkpoints uses a 3 mm tolerance, because a grid object model moves existing nodes slightly when it averages new observations into a voxel.

Example on `surf_agent_unsupervised_10distinctobj` (10 objects, 10 epochs): the mug graph grows 496 -> 859 -> 1104 nodes with all nodes on the surface. The bowl graph starts merging spoon observations from epoch 4 and ends with 7.6% of its nodes more than 15 mm off the bowl surface (the two red clusters).

![graph growth over epochs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/foxalike-dev/tbp.plot/graph-growth-plots/assets/graph_growth_over_epochs.png)

![graph surface distance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/foxalike-dev/tbp.plot/graph-growth-plots/assets/graph_surface_distance.png)

Usage:

```
uv run plot graph_growth_over_epochs --graph_id new_object1 --experiment_log_dir ~/tbp/results/monty/projects/monty_runs/surf_agent_unsupervised_10distinctobj --data_path ~/tbp/data/habitat/objects/ycb
uv run plot graph_surface_distance --graph_id new_object1 --experiment_log_dir ~/tbp/results/monty/projects/monty_runs/surf_agent_unsupervised_10distinctobj --data_path ~/tbp/data/habitat/objects/ycb
```

Tests: `tests/unit/plot/graph_growth_utils_test.py`. `ruff check` and `ruff format` pass; the two figures above were added to the README gallery.

body:
## Summary

A second-pass regression review of the v68 and v69 changes found mistakes in that work. This PR fixes them and cleans up an accidental commit.

### Client
- **Rematch re-send ordering.** The pending new-game re-send now runs before the move replay and sends the current board rather than the snapshot taken at Start. A `game-over` reject while a start is pending no longer resurrects the old recap. Without this, the bug v68 targeted could still happen one move later.
- **Busy/full welcomes mid-game** now drop the socket but keep the room identity, so the reconnect-on-wake path can recover. Previously the v68 cleanup change made that state terminal with no visible message. A toast now says what happened.
- Definition lookup sets the pending word before the cache check, so a slow earlier lookup can't overwrite a cached hit.
- `AudioContext.resume()` promise rejections are swallowed (it fires every second during a Coco timer).
- The solo flag is never accepted from a peer's config.
- A superseded PeerJS pipe can no longer feed the host handler.
- `sw.js` tolerates a malformed push URL instead of swallowing the click.
- On-screen version bumped to v69.1 (it still said v67.5).

### Worker (deployed, version `ea0b6fe3`)
- `bad-state` rejects echo the sequence number so the client retires the move instead of re-pushing every 20 seconds forever.
- `lastWrite` is throttled to hourly, since Coco-timer ticks push a move every second.
- The idle-room alarm ignores dead hibernated sockets.
- Push URLs must be https.

### Repo hygiene
- `.gitignore` added.
- The emulator's `worker/.wrangler` scratch state, accidentally committed in v69, is untracked. It contained only local test data (fake push endpoints, sandbox geo). It remains in git history; a history rewrite is a separate decision.

## Test plan
- [x] 27-check worker protocol probe against `wrangler dev` (updated for the `q` echo)
- [x] Client headless smoke test and clean tap test
- [x] Syntax checks on the extracted script, `sw.js`, and the worker

author: yocyber-code
body:
`discover.py` and `compete.py` each imported `GameState` from `arcengine` at module
scope, and each uses it in **exactly one function** — `discover(env, ...)` and
`play(env, ...)`. Both take a live `env`, so every caller already has the SDK; the
module-scope form couples the whole module to `arcengine` for every importer that does
not need it. **Eight modules import `discover` for `locate`, `walkable` and `Model`
alone.**

## The sharpest consumer is an import written to avoid exactly this

`trace.py:79`, inside `_stepped()`:

```python
from discover import locate
```

That is *already* a lazy import, there to keep `trace.py` free of the engine — and it
does not work, because importing `discover` at all pulls `arcengine` in behind it. So on
a tree without the SDK this is **not only a collection problem**: it is a live failure.

```
trace.py:70: in step
    or _stepped(before, after, model, action),
trace.py:79: in _stepped
    from discover import locate
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'arcengine'
```

`test_a_jump_that_is_not_the_action_displacement_is_still_a_change` fails on that, and
passes with this change.

## The change

Move the two imports into the one function that needs them. **No runtime path is
touched** — the import still happens before the first use, on every call that would have
used the module-scope binding. Same idiom as the `import arc_agi` already sitting inside
a function further down each file, so this is the file's own convention rather than a new
one. 13 added, 2 removed, 2 files; 11 of the 13 added lines are the two comments saying
why the imports are where they are.

## Measured

`python -m pytest tests/ --continue-on-collection-errors` on **Python 3.12.13** with
pytest 9.1.1, numpy 2.5.3 and requests 2.32.5, **no `arc-agi` SDK**. Both arms run from
separate checkouts of their own commit, in the same invocation:

| tree | failed | passed | collection errors |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `master` `5caa006` | 1 | 257 | 5 |
| **this branch** | **0** | **386** | **1** |

The five on `master` are `test_compete.py`, `test_discover.py`, `test_gate.py`,
`test_plan.py`, `test_probe_games.py`. **Four go away, and so does the failure.**
`tests/test_gate.py` alone runs **51 passed**.

The one that remains is `test_probe_games.py`, which needs `arc_agi` itself — a genuine
SDK dependency and out of scope here.

## Stated rather than hidden

- The environment still has **no SDK**, which is not how CI or a provisioned box runs.
  What this shows is the **coupling** being removed, not a suite that was broken for
  everyone.
- The interpreter is inside `pyproject`'s `>=3.12`, but the three test deps are whatever
  pip resolved today rather than a pinned set.
- An earlier reading of the same two commits under the system **Python 3.9** gave
  `13 / 245 / 5` → `12 / 374 / 1`. Kept as a dated record: **those 12 failures are 3.9
  artifacts**, not attributable to either commit. This PR's description and commit
  message were rewritten once that was measured — the 3.9 reading was understating the
  fix and mis-framing it as collection-only.
- Nothing was run on a GPU, no kernel was pushed, no submission slot was spent.

Refs Knowless-Crew/kc-arc-agi-pub#16 (the tracking ticket on the workspace repo). Left
unmerged — your repo, your call on whether and when.

## What

WhatsApp-style voice notes end-to-end:

- **Recording** — a mic button in the composer opens an inline panel (live timer, red dot, trash to discard, stop-to-send) using MediaRecorder. Picks Opus WebM/OGG on Chromium/Firefox and AAC MP4 on Safari.

- **Protocol** — new `MessageAttachment` type `voice` + `duration`; server accepts audio mimes and enriches messages with the note length.

- Fully merged against current `main` (which now contains the reply/quote feature): the quote pill, reply-on-send (images + voice), the mic button, and the voice bubble are all wired together.
- Quoting a voice message shows a "Voice note" label instead of a broken thumbnail; `MessageReply` accepts `voice` attachments.
- Mic hygiene: re-tapping the mic cancels the old stream; leaving the chat releases the microphone; failed sends surface an inline notice.

## Verification

body:
Automated upstream sync from qenex-hermes-upstream-sync.timer.

A plain merge of upstream/main into a branch off github/main. main is never
reset or force-pushed; it moves only when this PR is merged.

The fork's own files are .github/CODEOWNERS and .github/workflows/
sync-upstream.yml. The sync aborts without pushing if a merge removes either,
so a sync can never quietly turn into a reset.

git.qenex.ai is origin; GitHub is fallback. This PR is on GitHub because
that is where the public fork and `gh` live.

author: betterthanclay
body:
## Summary

Executes g18.023 — the release-blocking correction to g18.021. CodeEditor syntax highlighting no longer aliases UI status and accent tokens; it draws from two designed primitive syntax palettes through dedicated semantic `color.syntax.*` roles.

- **Token schemas**: `color.syntax.dark.*` and `color.syntax.light.*` primitive ramps (10 roles each: comment, keyword, string, literal, type, callable, property, operator, punctuation, invalid) plus semantic `color.syntax.*` roles referencing the dark primitives by default. Iceberg, clay, and meadow select the light primitives via role-level overrides; dark themes inherit the base; any theme may override one role at a time.
- **Design**: multi-hue by intent — violet keywords, green strings, amber literals, cyan types, blue callables, rose properties, red invalid, restrained blue-grey neutrals for comments/operators/punctuation. Light values are independently tuned counterparts (hue and chroma shifted for light surfaces), not inversions. The two bases differ in all ten roles.
- **Engines**: the paired private `HighlightStyle` twins map stable Lezer tags to the roles by meaning (specificity-ordered, ordinary identifiers stay primary text). Invalid parser syntax keeps its role colour and gains a non-colour wavy underline. No public API change; no grammar dependency.
- **Contract**: `docs/contracts/components/code-editor.md` §8 now describes the shipped state.

## Proof

- All 20 roles meet WCAG AA (≥ 4.5:1) against the actual rendered panel of every named theme — measured in real Chromium and WebKit for both frameworks, including the contrast-axis rendering. Binding cases: solarized (dark) and clay (light); minimum ≈ 4.65:1, most roles ≥ 5:1.
- Representative TypeScript resolves six distinct chromatic roles; JSON resolves property/string/literal/punctuation; ordinary identifier uses stay unstyled.
- Live theme switches restyle the same mounted editor — no remount, no grammar reload, document/selection preserved across all 12 themes.
- Selection and search overlays keep every token at its role colour and stay translucent; invalid syntax keeps the danger-role contrast plus the wavy cue; plain-text and plain performance mode render zero spans and load no grammar; forced colours keep the editor legible.
- Regenerated token artifacts verified by `audit:tokens`; engine twins remain byte-identical apart from the header comment.

## Validation

- `effigy audit:tokens`, `test:code-editor-language-registry-chromium`, `-webkit` — clean
- Focused CodeEditor suites (101 pass), paired components (3062 pass), previews (126 pass)
- `cargo test` tokens contracts, `cargo check` jetstream adapter — clean
- `core:build`, `svelte:package`, `react:package`, `svelte:build`, `react:build`, `test:web-pack-install`, `docs:check`, `git diff --check` — clean

Execution log: `docs/logs/2026-09/20260912-g18-023-code-editor-dual-syntax-palettes.md`. One observation (undefined `--poodle-color-surface-hover` active-line var) recorded in `PAPERCUTS.md` as out-of-scope friction. No merge, no release mutations, no g18.024/Slider paths touched.

body:
## Domain / feature

Inventory — Phase 1 merchant stock workspace, built on the existing append-only movement ledger (migration 021) and its permissions (migration 022). Read-side only on the server; no schema work.

## Branch

`claude/inventory-operations-ui` (branched fresh from `origin/main` at `ef24a5c`, the PR #52 merge)

## Commit SHA

`48c0d8944fa1296ad03fbdd11b6e2dfb1688b29a`

## Files changed

**Server — read-side only (no migration)**
- `src/server/inventory/repository.ts` — `listStockRowsForVariants` (chunked `IN`, never one query per variant), `listActiveVariantsForOrg` (projects `id` + `product_id` only — no price, no cost), `listLocationsForOrg` (`id`, `name`, `status` only).
- `src/server/inventory/service.ts` — `listOrganizationStock()` and `listInventoryLocations()`, both requiring `inventory.read` with the organization taken from the `AuthorizationContext` only.
- `src/server/inventory/types.ts` — row/option types for the two new reads.

**API boundary**
- `src/api/inventory.ts` — `listOrganizationStockFn` (`limit` is the only thing on the wire) and `listInventoryLocationsFn` (no input at all). Both keep the dynamic server-only imports inside the handler bodies.

**Capabilities**
- `src/lib/capabilities.ts` — adds `inventory.read`, `inventory.view_movements`, `inventory.receive_stock`, `inventory.adjust`. `inventory.transfer` / `mark_damage` / `override_reservation` are deliberately **not** added: no migration seeds them and no server function checks them, so declaring them would be a UI-only gate over behaviour that does not exist.

**Browser boundary**
- `src/lib/inventory.ts` (new) — modelled closely on `src/lib/catalog.ts`: principal-partitioned query keys, `removeQueries`-based cache clearing, a dedicated movement-history purge, error classification, pure presentation/join/parse helpers, thin server-function wrappers. No mock fallback.

**Screens**
- `src/routes/app.inventory.tsx` (new) — phone-first stock list.
- `src/routes/app.inventory.$variantId.tsx` (new) — on-hand total, per-location breakdown, server-paginated movement history, Receive stock, Manual adjustment.
- `src/components/inventory/ReceiveStockSheet.tsx`, `AdjustStockSheet.tsx`, `LocationChoice.tsx` (new).

**Navigation**
- `src/design-system/mobile-nav-config.ts` — the already-reserved `products-stock` entry becomes `availability: "live"`, `to: "/app/inventory"`, `requiresAll: ["inventory.read"]`. The Product catalogue keeps its own separate entry on `products.read`. Adds `/app/inventory` to the active-tab resolver.
- `src/design-system/BottomNav.tsx` — its four hand-duplicated copies of the destination union replaced by one shared `MobileNavDestination` type (the union had to change anyway; four parallel copies is how it would drift next time).

**Localization**
- `src/locales/en.json`, `km.json` — six new namespaces at full parity, plus the `nav.moreActions.productsStock` description, which said the stock workspace "is not in the app yet" and is no longer true.

**Tests**
- `src/tests/inventory-operations-ui.test.ts` (new, 82 cases).
- `src/tests/capability-surfaces.test.ts` — five inventory surfaces registered.
- `src/tests/capability-boundary.test.ts` — its enforced-key scanner now also reads the Inventory movement-type permission map, exactly as it already reads the Order transition maps (see Known risks).

`src/routeTree.gen.ts` is regenerated by the build.

## Migrations added / modified

**None.** No file under `supabase/` is touched by this PR. Both new reads run against tables/views migrations 005 and 021 already define, and all four permissions are the ones migration 022 already seeds. A test asserts the repository touches only `inventory_movements`, `inventory_stock`, `locations` and `product_variants`.

## Tests run

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `bun test src/tests/` | **1611 pass, 0 fail** (1522 before this PR) |
| `bun test src/tests/inventory-operations-ui.test.ts` | 82 pass, 0 fail |
| `bun test src/tests/bundle-boundary.test.ts` (after a real `bun run build`) | 74 pass, 0 fail |
| `bun test src/tests/capability-boundary.test.ts` | 20 pass, 0 fail |
| `bun test src/tests/capability-surfaces.test.ts` | included above, 0 fail |
| `bun test src/tests/i18n-key-parity.test.ts` | included above, 0 fail |
| `bun run scripts/check-migration-safety.ts --base=origin/main` | **0 blocking**, 17 warnings (all pre-existing baseline) |

Live-Supabase integration cases inside the suite are **SKIPPED** — no `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` / `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` in this environment. Everything asserted here is unit/behavioural against a fake organization-scoped DB, or structural.

New coverage: org-wide read (zero-for-no-movements, exact negatives, per-location summing, declared truncation, no N+1), cross-org variant/location/stock rejection with proof that nothing was written, independent enforcement of each of the four keys, capability gating with no role-name dependence, both mutations going through `recordMovement`, the required reason, audit-before-insert ordering, idempotency, cache partitioning and movement-history eviction, join honesty about uncovered variants, locale parity, mock boundary, bundle boundary.

## Typecheck

- [x] `bun run typecheck` passes

## Lint

- [x] `bun run lint` on changed files passes — whole-repo run is **0 errors, 17 warnings**, all `react-refresh`/`react-hooks` warnings in files this PR does not touch

## Build

- [x] `bun run build` succeeds (clean `.output`, all three environments)

## Bundle / security checks

- [x] `bun test src/tests/bundle-boundary.test.ts` passes against a real build
- [x] `bun run scripts/check-migration-safety.ts --base=origin/main` reports 0 blocking findings
- [x] No secrets, service-role keys, or provider tokens added to client-reachable code. The built inventory client chunks were also grepped directly: no `supabaseAdmin`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `buildAdminClient` or server symbols.

## Known risks

Things a reviewer should specifically scrutinize:

1. **`capability-boundary.test.ts` was widened.** `inventory.receive_stock` and `inventory.adjust` are enforced through `requiredPermissionFor()` — a movement-type→permission switch fed straight into `ctx.require()` — so the scanner's direct `require("literal")` regex did not see them. The scanner now also reads that function's `return` literals (comments stripped), structurally identical to the Order transition maps it already special-cases, and a new guard asserts the extra scan finds something. This widens what counts as "enforced"; a reviewer should confirm it did not weaken the check. An incidental mention still does not count.

2. **The Product × Inventory join is client-side.** Identity comes from `getProductCatalog` (`products.read`), quantity from `listOrganizationStock` (`inventory.read`); both are independently tenant-scoped server-side and cached under the same principal-partitioned key space. No cost is carried onto a stock row and no stock screen imports `visibleVariantCost` or `formatMoney` (asserted). The list drives off the ACTIVE catalogue, so a variant belonging to an ARCHIVED product is in the stock read but not on this screen.

3. **Truncation semantics.** A variant absent from an *untruncated* read is `0`; absent from a *truncated* one is `null` and renders as "Not loaded", never as `0`. Worth a reviewer's eye — conflating those two is exactly how a merchant would restock the wrong item.

4. **`STOCK_ROWS_PER_CHUNK` detection is heuristic.** A chunk returning exactly its own limit is treated as truncated. If a PostgREST `db.max_rows` were configured *below* that limit, truncation could go undetected. Documented in the repository; no way to detect it from the client side.

author: thomtorn-lab
body:
## Summary

Investigation (previous round) proved a fixed-timer pin (isProgrammaticScrollRef + 150ms settle) cannot outrun unbounded real-device reflow time: a freshly re-created scroll-spy observer's own automatic initial report, or an equally delayed bottom-of-page scroll, can arrive after any fixed window and steal a still-matching preserved month away (the mobile "lands on February" report). No timer duration can close this race.

This replaces that mechanism, for the "filter applied, current month still matches" case specifically, with a structural lock (`contextLockRef`) released ONLY by genuine user navigation intent:

- `wheel`, `touchstart`, and a scoped set of scroll-relevant keydown keys (Arrow Up/Down, Page Up/Down, Home, End, Space) — permanent, lightweight listeners, scoped so typing in the search box or a select never spuriously releases it
- an explicit month-nav click or Back to top action

The lock is armed only when `hasActiveFilters && groupsChangedSinceLastRun` (a real filter-driven pass, not a routine clock-tick re-render — gating on `hasActiveFilters` was necessary since `groups` also gets a new identity from a routine `now` tick even while unfiltered, which was harmless under the old timer-released pin but would freeze scroll-spy indefinitely under an intent-released one without this guard — caught by the full test suite before this fix landed). It's reset at the top of every reconciliation-effect run and only re-armed inside the "stay" branch, so it can never leak into a later, unrelated closest-month reconciliation.

The IntersectionObserver callback and the atBottom fallback both now also check this lock. The corrective-scroll case (reflow displaced the still-active month's own section) keeps using the existing timer-based pin unchanged, since that's a narrower, separate concern.

Closest-month reconciliation, Clear Filters, mobile draft/apply architecture, and genre filtering are all unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] `EventExplorer.test.tsx`: 94/94 passed — includes 2 prior diagnostic tests converted from "proves the bug" to "proves the fix" (the exact before/after flip), plus 6 new tests covering intent-release via wheel/touch/keyboard, explicit nav-click override, and the unaffected zero-match/Clear-Filters/desktop paths.
- [x] Full suite: 68 files / 1701 tests passed.
- [x] `eslint` on both changed files: clean.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- [x] `next build` (Turbopack production build): compiled successfully, all 15 routes generated.

body:
Makes the tee-time interest flow talk to the people in it, and fixes two bugs
in the space accounting found while doing it.

- Six notifications: interest received, place offered, declined, confirmed,
  withdrawn, invite cancelled. All `tee_times` category, so silenceable on
  both email and push.
- New tabs at /tee-times/interested and /tee-times/requests, with counts.
- Migration 0077: `respond_to_tee_time_interest()` and
  `confirm_tee_time_place()` take a row lock on the invite, so concurrent
  accepts can't over-book.

**Two bugs this fixes:**

1. `spaces_available` is constrained `>= 1` but the accept path wrote
   `Math.max(0, n - 1)` — so filling the *last* space has never worked. It
   raised a check violation after the interest was already marked accepted,
   leaving the two inconsistent. Production shows it: invite 3 has three
   accepted golfers and still reads `open, 1 space`.
2. The count was a read-then-write with no lock, so a double-click could
   offer the same seat twice.

Invites 3 and 4 are left for manual repair — the original space count isn't
stored, so the right value can only be guessed.

Do not merge until 0077 has been applied to production.

author: tamnd
body:
A column that was not given a name with `AS` is named after the expression that produced it, and every identifier written into that name goes through a deparser. DuckDB's deparser quotes some of them and this one quoted none of them, so `SELECT min(name) FROM t` came back as `min(name)` here and `min("name")` there. That is not cosmetic. `rudb-compat` compares column names, a client reading a result by name looks the key up, and `CREATE TABLE t AS SELECT min(name) FROM ...` writes the name into the catalog where it outlives the query.

## The rule

Measured off the pinned `v2.0.0-dev84237 (cc7e7bac7f)` on server2, one identifier at a time, because none of it follows from the name.

A word is quoted when it is a keyword in one of the grammar's classes. `name` is `UNRESERVED`, `action` is `UNRESERVED`, `asof` is `FUNC_NAME | TYPE_NAME`, and all three come back quoted. `alias` is in the keyword table with a mask of zero, because it is spelled by a rule and is in no class, and it comes back bare. So the test is the class and not the membership, which is exactly what `rudb_parse::classes` already answers for the tokenizer.

A word is also quoted when it is not one plain ASCII word. `"my col"`, `"9x"`, `"é"` and `"a""b"` all keep their quotes, and the embedded quote is doubled.

What is not a reason is case. `min(UserID)` comes back unquoted from upstream even though reading that name back folds it to `userid`. That one matters more than it looks: `UserID` is the ClickBench schema, so a deparser that quoted on case would have changed forty three column names to fix five.

## What it touches

One helper in `crates/rudb-bind/src/expr.rs`, used in the two places a name is generated from an identifier: a column reference and a function name. A bare `SELECT name` is unaffected because that name comes from the catalog rather than from the deparser, which is upstream's behaviour too.

Naming function calls through the same helper also settles the four string functions whose names are keywords. `substring`, `position`, `trim` and `nullif` are quoted now and `substr`, `strpos` and `ltrim` are not, which two tests asserted the other way round and each had a comment pointing at this issue. Those assertions are the measured names now.

## Checked

`./scripts/gate server2` is green, fmt through corpus.

The corpus half of that needed a second look. `cargo xtask conform` patches rudb to the working tree, and cargo was dropping the patch and linking the published 0.2.29 from git instead, with a warning in the middle of the output saying so. So the committed corpus in `tamnd/rudb-compat` was run again by hand against a lock that really does point at this tree, and it passes, three tests through both the library and the shell. The gate lying about which rudb it conformed is its own bug and is filed separately.

Closes #251.

Direct chat could remain queued behind a long background run because ez reserved the shared workspace for the entire engine execution. Remove host execution lanes and the four-run cap: independently claim authorized requests and let the selected engine own concurrency. The chat reminder tells the engine how to deliver replies and to acknowledge before lengthy work. Fresh and resumed chat receive it once at the final engine boundary; original inbound records remain intact.

author: marchelinoraco
body:
Login di produksi gagal. Konsol menunjukkan `/api/auth/sign-in/email` menjawab **500**, bukan 401 — jadi ini galat server, bukan kredensial salah. Pesan "Email atau kata sandi salah" di layar hanya pemetaan umum di form.

## Apa yang sudah dipersempit

| Diuji | Hasil |
|---|---|
| `/api/auth/ok` (health check) | **500** |
| `/api/auth/<path-yang-tidak-ada>` | **500** |
| `/api/tidak-ada` (kontrol non-auth) | 404 — benar |
| `/jadwal?view=daftar` | 200, **57 baris ibadah dari database** |
| `/warta` | 200, `x-vercel-cache: MISS` — dirender runtime, bukan cache |

Path auth yang **tidak ada** pun 500. Jadi gagalnya di level handler route `/api/auth/$`, sebelum better-auth sempat merutekan apa pun — bukan di endpoint tertentu.

## Yang sudah tersingkir sebagai penyebab

**Variabel environment.** `@/db` mengimpor `@/lib/env`, yang memvalidasi `DATABASE_URL`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, dan `BETTER_AUTH_URL` **sekaligus** saat modul dimuat dan melempar kalau salah satu tidak valid. Halaman publik yang membaca database berjalan normal, jadi ketiganya ada dan valid di produksi.

**Database.** 57 baris ibadah sungguhan terender dari runtime, bukan dari cache.

**Bundling.** Build dengan preset `vercel` menghasilkan chunk auth yang **identik byte-per-byte** dengan preset `node` (`auth-BjjWVHtJ.mjs`, 582.105 byte pada keduanya).

**Kode.** Build produksi dijalankan lokal dengan `NODE_ENV=production` — yang juga menyalakan pembatasan laju seperti di Vercel — dan `/api/auth/ok` menjawab **200**.

## Kenapa belum ketemu

Badan responsnya selalu `{"status":500,"unhandled":true,"message":"HTTPError"}` — sama persis untuk env yang salah, modul yang gagal dimuat, maupun database tak terjangkau. Dan **tidak ada apa pun yang tercatat di log server**, karena galatnya tidak pernah ditangkap.

## Yang dilakukan PR ini

Membungkus handler auth: rinciannya (`name`, `message`, `cause`) di-`console.error` **selalu** sehingga terbaca di log fungsi Vercel, tapi hanya dikembalikan ke pemanggil bila diminta eksplisit lewat `?diag=1`. Respons publik tetap generik — pesan galat internal bukan untuk pengunjung.

Ini bukan tambalan sementara: menelan galat handler jadi 500 tanpa jejak apa pun memang kelemahan yang layak diperbaiki terlepas dari insiden ini.

## Setelah ini di-deploy

```
curl -s "https://gmimmusafir.org/api/auth/ok?diag=1"
```

Jawabannya akan menyebut persis apa yang melempar.

Diverifikasi lokal: 20 test auth & admin e2e lulus, jalur suksesnya tidak berubah.

author: miinhho
body:
## Summary

Replaces the request pipeline with one model: **each accepted request is one `HandoffJob`** whose body runs an `ExecutionPlan` compiled when the router seals, offers the prepared response to the engine, and releases what it owns after delivery. Three commits: the core (`packages/server`, docs), the dependency move to published `@tiberjs/runner@0.3.0`, and the migration of feature packages, examples, benchmarks, and CLI templates.

### Model (`docs/server-model.md`)
- **Job is the only lifetime owner.** `Exchange` is the state the Job runs through; the response producer (`OutputLease`) and the request DI scope are resources it releases before it settles. The Node engine tracks no request lifetimes of its own; the app's Supervisor does.
- **Compiled plans.** Filters, response transformers, before-commit hooks, and failure mappers are compiled per route at seal into `ExecutionPlan { handler, commit, recover }`. Each step stays synchronous until application code returns a promise. Static routes match with no allocation.
- **Request passes through.** Handlers get the transport's `Request` unchanged; `request.signal` means client disconnect. Application cancellation (shutdown, deadlines, failure) reaches handlers through the runner's `signal()`. Request bytes and `maxRequestBody` belong to the engine (`EngineFactory(handler, { maxRequestBody })`); in-process `fetch` has no transport and no byte limit.
- **One commit boundary.** `render → hooks → frame`; the framework owns the headers it renders and copies nothing. Hook-returned representations are validated, not cloned.
- **DI scope on first use.** `ExchangeContext` implements `@tiberjs/di`'s `ScopeHost`: `inject()` resolves through the app container; the first `scoped()`/`onDispose()` creates the request's child container on the context, and finalization disposes it only if it exists (tiberjs/manager#3).
- **Nothing eager that nobody asked for:** no abort listener (runner links lazily), no request id `Symbol` until read, no event payload without a listener, no per-request context frame.

### Measured (same box, `/echo`, 50 conn; ±20% run-to-run on this laptop)
| | before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| tiber-bun | 61.5k rps | 105–107k (raw `Bun.serve` 105–111k) |
| tiber-node | 26.0k | 41–43k (adapter-bound; see below) |
| Node peak RSS | 728 MiB | ~500 MiB |
| in-process `app.fetch` heap after GC | 12–14 MiB | 8 MiB |

`bench/leak-probe.mjs`: 240 000 scoped resources acquired and released, 0 live, 0 retained graph nodes.

### Not in this PR
The Node adapter (`node/request.ts`, `node/response.ts`) still builds a full undici `Request` per request plus write listeners; that is the remaining gap to raw Node and is separate work (lazy pseudo-Request, as `@hono/node-server` does).

### Verification
`pnpm format`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test` — all 19 workspace packages, including the support-desk example (its request-body-limit assertion now goes over a real listener, per the contract above). `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` reproduces against npm runner 0.3.0 and the vendored di/eventbus tarballs.

author: escapeboy
body:
## Какво

Скриптът `database/sql/supabase_memory_setup.sql`, който раздаваме на клиентите през MCP инструмента `supabase_provision_vector_memory`, създаваше таблицата `fleetq_memories` в схема `public` без Row Level Security.

Supabase дава достъп до нови таблици в `public` на ролите `anon` и `authenticated` през PostgREST. Anon ключът е публичен и се слага в браузърни приложения. Значи всеки с anon ключа на проекта можеше да прочете всички памети.

## Точност на твърдението, което задейства проверката

Получено беше външно съобщение, че файлът съдържа политика `using (true)`, която дава четене на всеки authenticated потребител. Това не е точно: редът беше закоментиран и никога не се изпълнява. Реалният проблем е по-голям, защото RLS изобщо не се включваше.

Самата закоментирана политика също беше сгрешена. `FOR ALL USING (true)` без `TO` клауза важи за всички роли, включително `anon`, въпреки че е озаглавена "Service role full access". А `service_role` заобикаля RLS и не се нуждае от политика.

## Промени

В шаблона и в резервния inline SQL в `SupabaseVectorAdapter`:

- `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` вече не е коментар
- `REVOKE ALL` върху таблицата от `anon` и `authenticated`
- `REVOKE` на `fleetq_match_memories` от `PUBLIC`, `anon`, `authenticated`, плюс `GRANT EXECUTE` само на `service_role`
- `DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Service role full access"` за базите, в които някой е разкоментирал стария ред
- опционалният пример за JWT достъп вече е с `TO authenticated` и обяснение защо клаузата е задължителна
- две заявки за проверка на резултата

FleetQ се свързва със `service_role` ключа, който заобикаля RLS, така че пътят за четене и запис не се променя.

## Претърсване за същия модел

Единственото друго попадение на `USING (true)` е `semantic_cache_entries` в `2026_02_24_900001_enable_rls_on_tenant_tables.php`. Там е нарочно, кешът е споделен между екипите, документирано е в кода и към тази база няма PostgREST нито роля `anon`. Не се променя.

- pass the immutable `(transactionId, planHash)` binding into every `ServiceLockFactory` acquisition
- keep the local file-lock factory compatible while making the future host-owned lease boundary capable of binding grants and renewals to the exact approved plan
- verify the executor supplies the exact binding before provenance revalidation or any lifecycle phase
- record the binding requirement in the transaction ADR

## Why this is separate

The host lease design cannot be safely implemented on the previous interface: service IDs alone do not identify the approved transaction or plan. This prerequisite keeps the next host-agent lease PR small and prevents an unbound lease from becoming mutation authority.

## Safety boundary

- production transaction execution remains unavailable (`executor=None`)
- no host-agent route, lifecycle adapter, installation, deployment, or live service is changed
- the existing Dashboard single-extension lock behavior is unchanged

- Tower3 Linux exact commit: `65 passed` across operation-lock and transaction-executor suites
- Windows: `16 passed, 49 skipped` for the same focused suites
- Ruff and Python compile checks passed
- `git diff --check` passed

body:
English edition of the pack, built on @yungalgo's work in #5 and rebased onto current `main`.

Closes #3. Supersedes #5 — the first two commits here are yungalgo's, with his authorship preserved.

## What changed relative to #5

| | #5 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Base | 13-skill `main` (stale) | current 20-skill `main` |
| The Chinese plugin | renamed to `screenwriting-zh` | **left as `screenwriting`** |
| Coverage | 13 skills | **all 20** |
| Commits 3 & 4 of #5 (TV integration + naming) | included | dropped — `main` already did that work |

Three substantive corrections:

1. **No rename.** #5 renamed `plugins/screenwriting` → `plugins/screenwriting-zh`, which breaks every existing install (`/plugin install screenwriting@screenwriting-skills`) and every invocation (`/screenwriting:sw-dialogue`), and — because #5 was cut before the series layer landed — would have orphaned the 7 new series skills in a directory with no `plugin.json`. The English edition is added alongside as `screenwriting-en` instead; nothing existing moves.
2. **Rebased onto current `main`.** The 13 translations were brought up to `main`'s state: the medium-boundary tables in `chekhov-dramaturgy` and `ozu-screenplay-style`, the qualified five-character limit in `sw-character-conflict`, the McKee/BS2 reconciliation note in `sw-story-structure`, the four-group format checklist and the Chinese page-count rule in `sw-format-adaptation`, and the series stage table (S0–S7) plus the series bible supplement in `sw-workflow`.
3. **The series layer is translated too.** All 7 new skills — `sw-series-structure`, `sw-series-engine-bible`, `sw-writers-room`, `sw-sitcom-comedy`, `succession-series-writing`, `sw-series-case-studies`, `sw-chinese-series-practice` — including their reference files, so the English edition is a complete 20, not a subset.

## Shape

- `plugins/screenwriting-en/` — 20 skills, English bodies, translated from the Chinese files
- `plugins/screenwriting/` — unchanged
- The marketplace now lists two plugins. Install one edition or the other, not both: the skill descriptions are near-identical by design, so both installed at once means the agent picks between two copies of the same skill.

The Chinese files remain the source of truth; the English files are translations of them. Cross-references between skills, reference-file anchors and section numbering are preserved, so `sw-workflow`'s pointers and the `reference.md §N` citations resolve inside the English tree.

author: lukisch
body:
Setzt S3 und S4 des Stationsmodells um (Ticket T-20260831-971906399, Nutzerentscheid D-20260906-012, F3=B). S1 (`segment_stations.py`) und S2 (Maskenschema) waren bereits gemerged.

## Was dazukommt

`skills/infrastructure/skill-extractor/scripts/score_stations.py` — segmentiert, sammelt harte Signale je Station, klassifiziert den Anschlussprompt nach den sieben Typen der `promptarchaeologie` (SP/NT/NM/NS/KO/BE/RA), bildet Stationsfolgen und vergibt einen Erntewert mit Klartextbegründung je Punkt.

Tragende Idee: **der Anschluss ist das Label** — eine Station wird danach beurteilt, was der Mensch als Nächstes sagt.

## Zwei Befunde aus der Messung an realen Transkripten

1. **SP ist sprachlich nicht erkennbar.** Ein Startprompt unterscheidet sich im Wortlaut nicht von einer gewöhnlichen Anweisung. Die Folgengrenze hängt deshalb an harten Markern plus einer Zeitlücke (Default 1800 s). Ohne sie fielen 137 Stationen zu 6 Folgen mit 30+ Stationen zusammen; mit ihr entstehen 17 Folgen, Median 11.
2. **Substring-Matching überklassifiziert.** „weitere" las als Bestätigung „weiter". Marker greifen jetzt auf Wortgrenzen; „fehler" ist als KO-Marker entfallen, weil es Beschreibung und Korrektur nicht trennt.

## Was der Score ausdrücklich nicht behauptet

`classified_ratio` weist aus, wie weit die Automatik trägt. Unter 0,5 setzt die Ausgabe eine Warnung und erklärt die Rangfolge selbst für nicht belastbar. Auf realen Transkripten liegt der Wert bei ~0,5 — die weiche Klassifikation bleibt ein Vorfilter, kein Klassifikator. Das Dedup-Gate des Skills bleibt Pflicht; ein Score ist eine Leseempfehlung, keine Auswahlentscheidung.

## Nebenbefund

`schemas/station-skill-mask-v1.schema.json` hatte weder `$schema` noch `$id` — beide Schlüssel waren beim Anlegen einer Shell-Variablenexpansion zum Opfer gefallen und standen als leerer Schlüssel `""` in der Datei. Behoben.

## Prüfung

- 308/308 Tests grün (10 neue in `test_score_stations.py`, darunter ein Test, der belegt, dass weder Chattext noch Toolparameter in der Ausgabe landen)
- `privacy_gate.py` und `repo_privacy_gate.py` grün
- Reale Läufe über drei Transkripte (16/12/9,7 MB)

author: tmaeder
body:
Output-level guard for [#3625](https://github.com/tmaeder/queer-guide-hub/pull/3625). One new spec, no source change. `functions/_lib/detailParagraphs.test.ts` guards the pure function. **Nothing guards the output** — and the whole bug was invisible for as long as it existed precisely because no test ever read a live page. A unit test cannot see a deploy that never shipped, an edge bundle serving a stale build, or a future middleware change that re-flattens the body downstream. ## What it asserts Five paired-fingerprint cases, one per split arm, each on a different entity type so a regression in a single arm fails on its own: | page | arm | |---|---| | `/villages/chueca` | single newline after a full stop — the 106-of-175 cohort with **zero** blank lines | | `/venue/omaha-public-library-benson-branch` | **CRLF**, the subtlest half: `[ \t]*` does not match `\r`, so every lookbehind arm silently never fires | | `/tags/prep` | blank line | | `/city/key-west` | single newline after a full stop, city | | `/venue/tramp-s` | venue prose whose second line is a bare fragment | Each names two strings that must land in **different** paragraphs. Both halves must be **present** first, so a content rewrite fails loudly with *"update the fingerprint"* instead of passing vacuously — an assertion that only checks for absence is satisfied by an empty page. Plus the opposite failure, which all five would miss: **`/city/hatboro` must keep two sentences of one paragraph in the SAME `

`**. Without it, a "split more aggressively" regression passes the entire file. ## Why it takes nothing but the base URL The obvious design reads each row from Supabase and computes the expected paragraphs. But `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` is **not passed to `e2e-nightly.yml`**, so a spec that needs it `test.skip()`s in CI and guards nothing — the shape of the a11y route sweep that gated zero. Fingerprints are hardcoded instead. Worth knowing separately: `e2e/accessibility-contradictions.spec.ts` is skipping in the nightly run today for exactly that reason. Not fixed here. ## Verified three ways, not by going green - **7/7 against prod.** - **Each fingerprint replayed against the PRE-FIX implementation on the live rows** — 5/5 land in `

0` together, i.e. every case would have failed before #3625, and the negative control holds in both directions. author: olemarkus
body:
## Summary

- `resolveMeterDelta` paired the energy between two `meter_power` observations with the time between two of its own **resolve calls**. Devices publish the meter on their own cadence (a cloud-backed one every few minutes) while the resolver runs on the snapshot refresh every few seconds, so the rate was overstated by the ratio of the two intervals. A ~3.8 kW Daikin reported **226 kW** in a submitted production log, and `nextLearnedPeak` held it as the device's expected power for 30 days.
- The same mismatch had a quieter half: between pushes the meter has not moved, so the delta was zero over real elapsed time and a running device was credited a measured **0 kW** for most of every poll interval (visible as `currentDrawKw: 0` on the same log line).
- Denominator is now the capability's own `lastUpdated` delta. An unmoved meter spans no window and resolves to absence (last good reading carries forward); a re-published unchanged meter still resolves a true zero. The anchor advances only when a pair is consumed, so a skipped pair's energy lands in the next window instead of being discarded.
- The reader resolves a `MeterEnergyReading` (value and stamp together) or absence, so the resolver takes a domain value and never sniffs for its halves. Selection returns the typed reading rather than a source tag, removing the re-validation in each branch and three parameter bags (allowlist 5 → 2, reseeded).
- Peaks learned under the old arithmetic are left to age out of their 30-day window, not purged.
- `docs/technical.md` names which clock the rate is computed on and the absence rule.
