author: aleksa-dragnic
body:
## What

3 new files, 3 edited: a functional suite over real HTTP, plus the one production fix it found.

## Why

Until now 409, 422 and 404 were covered by the smoke scripts only, and the claim that an
unhandled failure returns problem details with a traceId and no stack trace had never been
tested. This covers every user-visible flow over real HTTP against a real database.

## Notes

- ApiFactory takes an optional service configuration and setting overrides. The 500 test replaces IPermissionLookup with one that throws, so there is no test-only endpoint in production code.
- The suite found a real inconsistency: a body MVC cannot parse was answered with application/json rather than application/problem+json. The default InvalidModelStateResponseFactory returns an ObjectResult offering application/json first, and [Produces] on the controller then rewrites its content types outright. ProblemDetailsResponses.FromModelState returns a JsonResult instead - the same mechanism ResultExtensions already uses for domain failures, and for the same reason. Status and body are unchanged; only the content type moves.
- Deviation: the M6 guide expects 422 for a malformed body. A body that is not JSON never becomes a command, so no validator can name a field; MVC answers 400 problem details, which is what RFC 9110 calls a malformed request. 422 stays for a well-formed body with bad values, and both are asserted.
- NSubstitute is referenced by the integration test project with a bare PackageReference. It was already pinned centrally at 6.2.0 for the Application unit tests, and under central package management "dotnet add package" without --version would have raised that pin for both projects.

Tests: Domain 95, Application 79, Integration 83 (257 total). Smoke run against the local
instance and against compose, all checks passing.

author: ponack
body:
Fixes the red build on `main`.

## What broke

`URLError: [Errno 111] Connection refused` — the job downloads the IEEE registry to diff the generated table against, and GitHub's runners cannot reach it.

Reaching for it was the wrong design anyway. The registry publishes new assignments continually, so the job would go red whenever IEEE moves — which says nothing about whether this repo is correct, and trains everyone to ignore the badge. **A CI check should fail only when this repository is wrong.**

## What replaces it

An offline validation of the committed header against the invariants the firmware actually relies on:

| Invariant | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Both tables sorted | the lookups are binary searches; unsorted silently returns the wrong vendor |
| No duplicate prefixes | same |
| Tables disjoint | a prefix in both could let benign labelling suppress a detection |
| Vendor indices in range | an out-of-range index reads past the end of the names array at runtime |
| Declared counts match rows | catches a hand-edited or half-regenerated file |

Each of the five was verified by injecting the fault it describes and confirming the check fails — it isn't decoration.

Refreshing from the registry stays a deliberate manual step (`python3 tools/gen_oui_table.py`), now stated in the README.

author: stateofintent
body:
Rejecting a gossip message that came from a peer other than the one the round was initiated with is currently charged to the receiving node: eight of the nine such checks build the error with `K2Error::other`, so `handle_gossip_message` takes its generic arm and calls `incr_local_errors`. `ring_sector_details_diff.rs` already used `K2GossipError::peer_behavior` and this makes the other eight match it.

It also makes each of those functions internally consistent: the `session_id` mismatch check immediately after each wrong-peer check already uses `peer_behavior` in all eight files, so two consecutive checks on the same message disagreed about whose fault it was.

No test changes were needed. The two tests that assert on this text, `respond::agents::tests::receive_agents_from_wrong_peer` and `respond::busy::tests::busy_from_wrong_peer`, match with `contains`, and `PeerBehaviorError`'s `#[error("Rejected peer behavior - {ctx}")]` keeps the message. `cargo test -p kitsune2_gossip --lib` is 67 passed / 0 failed, and `cargo clippy -p kitsune2_gossip --all-targets` and `cargo fmt` are clean.

I raised this as a question first in #638, where the full site-by-site table is, and offered it in either direction — this is the direction that seemed right to me, but if you would rather `ring_sector_details_diff.rs` change to match the other eight instead, say so and I will swap it for a one-line PR.

**A question for reviewers, and the reason I asked before patching:** `peer_behavior` errors increment a peer's behavior counter, so this changes what the peer meta store records for a peer sending misdirected messages. If that counter feeds anything that eventually acts on a peer, this is a behavioural change and not only a bookkeeping one — I could not tell from reading whether `incr_peer_behavior_errors` has downstream consequences, and you will know. Happy to narrow the change to `accept.rs` alone if the blast radius matters.

author: ksh0660
body:
## 1. 실전 모의고사가 실제 시험과 다르게 나오던 문제

돌발 세트가 **8~10번에 고정**되어 있고 나머지 네 구간을 전부 배경 설문에서 채워서, 매번 **서베이 4 / 돌발 1**만 나왔습니다. 2000회 표본에서 예외가 없었습니다.

실제 시험대로 **서베이 3 / 돌발 2**를 뽑고, 어느 구간이 돌발이 될지는 회차마다 무작위로 정합니다.

| 구간 | 번호 | 유형 | 출처 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 세트 1 | 2·3·4 | 묘사 → 습관 → 경험 | 배경 설문 또는 돌발 |
| 세트 2 | 5·6·7 | 묘사 → 경험 → 기억에 남는 경험 | 배경 설문 또는 돌발 |
| 세트 3 | 8·9·10 | 묘사 → 경험 → 기억에 남는 경험 | 배경 설문 또는 돌발 |
| 롤플레이 세트 | 11·12·13 | 질문하기 → 문제 해결 → 관련 경험 | 배경 설문 |
| 어드밴스 세트 | 14·15 | 비교 → 이슈 | 배경 설문 또는 돌발 |

- 롤플레이 구간만 예외로 늘 배경 설문입니다. 돌발 문제은행에 `roleplay_*` 문항이 없습니다.
- 한 회차에 같은 주제가 두 구간에 나오지 않고, 세트를 완성할 수 없는 배정이면 다른 구간 조합으로 백트래킹합니다.
- 최소 배경 설문 주제 수가 4개 → 3개로 내려갑니다 (`MIN_FULL_EXAM_SURVEY_TOPICS`).
- 6000회 표본에서 6가지 배치 조합이 균등하게(각 ~1000회) 나오는 것을 확인했습니다.

### 돌발은 제공 자료 안에서만 만듭니다

번호별 유형은 **배경 설문 구간에만** 적용합니다. 돌발은 주제마다 가진 유형이 제각각이라 유형을 강요하면 없는 문항을 지어내야 하는데, 그러면 실제 시험에 안 나올 것을 연습하게 됩니다. 특히 습관 문제는 잘 나오지 않습니다.

돌발 일반 구간은 **자료의 1번을 고정**하고 나머지 두 문항을 자료 순서를 지켜 무작위로 뽑습니다.

| 주제 | 나올 수 있는 조합 |
| --- | --- |
| 재활용 | 1·2·3 / 1·2·4 / 1·3·4 |
| 병원·치과 | 1·2·3 / 1·2·4 / 1·3·4 |
| 약속·예약 | 1·2·3 / 1·2·4 / 1·3·4 |
| 미용실 | 1·2·3 / 1·2·4 / 1·3·4 |
| 산업 | 1·2·3 |
| 구직·진로 | 1·2·3 |
| 직업·직장 | 1·2·4 |

비교·이슈는 어드밴스 구간 몫이라 일반 구간에서 뺍니다. 앞 질문을 전제로 하는 산업 문항은 그 앞 질문 뒤에만 나옵니다. 14~15번은 비교 → 이슈 순서를 지키므로 두 유형을 모두 가진 재활용·산업·구직·진로·직업·직장만 들어갑니다.

**돌발 문제은행(`surprise-bank.ts`)과 오디오는 한 글자도 건드리지 않았습니다.** 35문항 그대로입니다.

## 2. 오늘의 말하기

홈 화면에 오늘 답한 문제 수와 After 따라 읽기 횟수, 두 가지의 추정 문장 합계를 보여 주는 카드를 더합니다.

- 따라 읽기를 **읽은 날짜와 당시 문장 수**로 기록해, 나중에 피드백을 다시 받아도 지난 연습량이 바뀌지 않습니다.
- 날짜가 없던 기존 읽기 횟수는 연습 종료와 마지막 저장이 같은 날일 때만 복원합니다. 여러 날 누적분을 마지막 저장일에 몰아넣지 않습니다.
- 오늘 합계를 별도 키(`yumi-opic:daily-speaking`)에 보관해 기록 20회 제한에 줄지 않고, 회차 ID로 묶어 새로고침·재분석에 중복 합산되지 않습니다.
- 기록 삭제·전체 삭제가 합계에도 반영되고, 저장 시 `HISTORY_CHANGED_EVENT`를 쏴 홈이 새로고침 없이 갱신됩니다.
- 포커스·가시성 변화에 다시 읽고 자정에 재설정해, 탭을 켜 둔 채 날이 바뀌어도 어제 숫자를 보여 주지 않습니다.

## 확인

- 테스트 216개 통과 (`npm test`)
- 타입체크 통과 (`npx tsc --noEmit`)
- 빌드 통과 (`npm run build`)
- 돌발 35문항 · `public/audio` 185개 — 둘 다 변화 없음

body: Adds Node regression tests for three still-untested helper groups on high-blast-radius paths. No production behavior changes. ## Risky behavior now covered - **Social dock placed rounding** (`socialDockCoordsRounded`, `clampPlacedSocialDockInViewport`): After a drag, placed docks only get integer `left`/`top`. Unplaced docks and missing coordinates are left alone. Off-screen positions stay off-screen — this helper must not start calling `clampSocialDockToViewport`, which would fight a user who parked the bar near an edge. - **Affiliate price text and disclosure badges** (`buildInlinePriceText`, `retailerBadgeHtml`, `formatRetailerName`): Inline setup-page prices prefer a live current amount (`| Now $X`) and otherwise show paid/legacy. Official Amazon or AliExpress click URLs stay labeled Affiliate; official AliExpress `/item/` pages keep the non-commission note; official shops such as Wooting stay unlabeled so the site does not claim compensation that is not there. - **Donators kind labels** (`kindLabel`): Donation and bits copy stay fixed. Twitch subscriptions with more than one subscriber render as Gifted subs; a single Twitch sub, YouTube memberships, and malformed subscriber counts stay Subscription; unknown kinds fall back to Support. ## Test files added/updated - `test/social-dock-placed-round-regression.test.mjs` (added) - `test/affiliate-price-badge-regression.test.mjs` (added) - `test/donators-kind-label-regression.test.mjs` (added) ## Why these tests materially reduce regression risk These helpers had no coverage on main or in open coverage PRs. A silent clamp change would yank a customized dock back into the viewport after every gesture. A badge regression would either hide required Affiliate labels or mark unpaid official shops as compensated. A kind-label slip would misreport gifted Twitch subs as ordinary subscriptions on the Donators page. Tests are deterministic Node `vm` extracts (no browser, no network). Validated with `npm test` (9/9).

## Problem

The fork had drifted 386 upstream commits behind pingdotgg/t3code main (last sync at `09aac715`). Upstream shipped the Effect rc.112 upgrade, TypeScript 7, multi-PR link management, per-project settings overrides, simulator/emulator device support, conversation rewind, load balancing, and a large performance sweep.

## What was taken from upstream

- **Toolchain**: Effect rc.112 + Alchemy beta.76 upgrade, TypeScript 7.0.2, knip export classification across server/desktop/web/contracts/shared/client-runtime/ssh/acp.
- **Pull requests**: multi-PR links per thread (`pullRequests` array + legacy `linkedPullRequest` derivation), PR stack navigate/merge/rebase, PR merge defaults, linked-PR search, PR page selections in new drafts.
- **Settings**: per-project overrides for scopable server settings (`projectSettingsOverrides` + one-time fold), settings environment/project selects, default permissions for new threads, shared project defaults.
- **Devices**: iOS Simulator / Android Emulator support, SSH simulator hosts, concurrent agent sessions across hosts, `device_*` MCP toolkits and the `agent-device` CLI shim, cross-platform window capture.
- **Chat/threads**: conversation rewind keeping file changes, provider history restore on rewind, context-compaction message queueing and draft preservation, async question dismiss, file drops into sidebar threads, image zoom/pan, gallery navigation, minimap turn navigation.
- **Usage**: pooled subscription limits per provider across accounts/environments (web + mobile), remaining-quota view, hub reset-credit redemption, Codex Spark limits, unpriced-activity flagging, Usage opens on Limits tab.
- **Connections**: load balancing across machines with resource-based preference, environments in command palette search, project favicons persisted across reloads.
- **Performance**: huge-thread switch without blanking, completed code-line DOM reuse while streaming, markdown prefix reuse, message-sync speedup on desktop/mobile, sidebar bulk-update responsiveness, checkpoint map rebuild skip, plan-body summary skip, full-thread-read avoidance on turn start.
- **Providers**: Codex qualified model ids, Claude result status/error mapping share, retried-turn usage limits, expired-login/usage-limit naming, Cursor model discovery cache, OpenCode sequential CLI commands, Antigravity skill loading + Google sign-in persistence.
- **Relay**: Android device registrations (dormant in this fork), queued iOS alert rechecks, notification policy sharing, APNs routing fixes.
- **Mobile**: drag-to-reorder threads, several new-task drafts per project, Material You layout option, Android wallpaper colors, outbox queueing improvements, work-log folding fixes.
- **Desktop**: macOS installer artwork, hold-to-quit fix, WSL test coverage, context menus in the browser.
- Everything else in the 386 commits (marketing, CI, docs, tests).

## What was preserved from the fork

Operator, machine-owned automations (edit/history/permissions/settle-on-success), Vibe-Proxy usage and account pooling, image generation via Codex CLI / Grok Imagine, usage-limit auto-resume with queued messages, provider capacity retries, Web Push notifications, workspace backgrounds, Android agent status foreground service with Live Updates, browser mod-key flip, native task notifications, remote environment renaming, task references, worktree cleanup, Vercel Dark default theme, instant Cmd+Q, alert splash bounding, and DND-surviving alerts.

## Notable resolution decisions

- **Android notifications**: kept the fork's local foreground-service system; upstream's push-based relay module was kept dormant (inert infrastructure) rather than excised, since the fork's app never registers Android push.
- **Migrations**: upstream's three new migrations were renumbered 53-55 after the fork's own 41-52 sequence; their tests were updated to match.
- **Effect rc.112 migration**: fork-only files (OperatorService, AutomationService, ImageGeneration, threadReference, vibeProxy, worktreeCleanup, toolkits) were migrated to the new `Schema.TaggedError` API.
- **Settlement**: merged the fork's automation-aware sweeps with upstream's per-project auto-settle settings and inactivity-first pass; automation sweeps bypass the sidebar settlement gate as before.
- **Claude adapter**: upstream's structured outcome design now carries the fork's usage-limit payload for auto-resume; the fork's CLI API-error text extraction (used by retry classification) takes precedence over the generic overload notice; auth-failure evidence is recorded before the fork's synthetic-error suppression.
- **Pooled usage UI**: took upstream's latest components wholesale (the fork's copy was a byte-identical vendor); the fork's Vibe-Proxy sections in Settings → Usages were kept on top.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean on server, web, mobile, desktop, contracts, shared, client-runtime, ssh, tailscale, effect-acp, effect-codex-app-server, relay.
- `vp build` succeeds for web (regenerated routeTree includes fork routes).
- Targeted suites pass: contracts (131), shared (77), client-runtime state (508), server orchestration/providers/mcp/server tests (~2,240), web keybindings/timeline/usage (369), mobile theme/activity/agent-status (130).
- Remaining full-suite failures were confirmed to fail identically on the pre-merge fork HEAD (environment-dependent: npm/mise prefix detection, symlinked entrypoints, Grok CLI ACP mocks) or are pre-existing fork ACP hangs.

body:
## What

The `vault-mcp` skill documented the agent's own secrets (`vault_store_secret` / `get` / `list` / `delete` / `create_platform_secret`) but **not** `vault_list_browser_creds` — the tool that lists the user's saved browser credentials (logins, addresses, cards) for form-filling.

Adds a **Browser credentials** section documenting it:
- Each entry is `alias` + `kind` (`site_creds` | `address` | `card`) + `fields` (field names, never values).
- Read-only to the agent; values never come back — pick by `kind`, reference a field as `"ALIAS.field"`, and let the browser skill fill it so the value never passes through the agent.
- No store/get/delete here (the user manages these in their console).

Threaded into the frontmatter description, an example, and a Rules bullet.

## Why now
Backs the `kind` that akela now stores and returns on browser creds (clode-labs/akela#47): the listing tool surfaces `alias + kind + fields`, with the redundant `type:"browser_creds"` field removed (these already live in their own scope). Console surfaces the same kinds (clode-labs/console-web#531).

Docs only; no internal service names in prose (tool names + "the vault" / "console" only).

body:
## Summary

Adds a **payment-terms policy to Purchase Orders**, fixes several problems in the printed PO, and hardens two things found along the way (public handbook credential leak, account-management access).

## PO payment terms (COD / 7 / 15 / 30 / 60 / 90 / 120 days)
- New **Terms** field on the New PO form and Edit PO form. Blank = "Supplier default" (falls back to the supplier record's terms).
- One term per PO. Stored on `purchase_requests.payment_terms` (migration `061`), round-tripped through the field mappers (`toSbPR` + load).
- On **delivery receipt**, the term sets the payable's **due date**, counted from the delivery date. A PO-level term **overrides** the supplier default; blank falls back to it.
- Term prints on the PO (header "Payment Terms").
- `core.js`: `PO_TERMS` constant; `paymentTerms` on `emptyPR()`.

## Printed PO fixes
- Company letterhead now uses the registered legal name **GMD PRODUCTIONS INC** on all printed docs (PO / WO / Delivery Receipt), removing the "GMD Pro" vs "GMD Pro Solutions" mismatch on supplier- and BIR-facing documents.
- "Approved by" now shows the PO's **actual approver** instead of a hardcoded name.
- Header meta row is 4-up so Payment Terms sits beside Supplier / PO Number / Date Issued.

## Handbook (public/handbook.html)
- **Removed the plaintext password table** that was published in a publicly-served file. Replaced with guidance that passwords are Manager-reset in-app and listed nowhere.
- Purchase Orders section documents the new Payment Terms field.

## Account access
- **Account Management is now Manager-only** (view users, reset passwords, create/deactivate). Finance access removed; dead Accounts nav links removed from the Finance and HRAdmin menus.
- Login-help hint generalized from hardcoded names to "Ask a Manager".

## Verified
- `npm run check-imports` clean; `react-scripts build` compiles.

body:
## RPC blindada — a IA redige o rascunho direto no chamado (na trilha), incapaz de causar dano

Hoje o rascunho é escrito no chat e copiado à mão — mensagem avulsa fora do chamado, fora da trilha. `fn_sugestao_responder` exige `auth.uid()` e **barra service_role** (corretamente — quem responde cliente tem que ser identificável); **não contornei** aquele guard. Esta é um caminho **separado**, desenhado para não conseguir causar dano:

1. **SEMPRE `resposta_aprovada=false`** — sem parâmetro para mudar. A RPC **não aprova nada**.
2. **SEMPRE `resposta_origem='ia'`, `resposta_redigida_por=NULL`** — claro na tela que foi a IA.
3. **RECUSA** se `resposta_aprovada` já for true → `ja_aprovada` (não sobrescreve resposta enviada).
4. **RECUSA** se status terminal → `status_terminal`.
5. **Só `service_role`** — `GRANT service_role` + `REVOKE public/anon/authenticated` → **não exposta ao app**.
6. **Não envia e-mail** — `sugestoes` não tem trigger; e-mail sai só em `fn_sugestao_aprovar_resposta` (aprovação do CEO). **Fluxo intocado.**

O CEO segue o **único que aprova** — lê o rascunho na tela e aprova/corrige/descarta. Salvaguarda intacta.

### Tela (atendimento)
Selo discreto quando `resposta_origem='ia'`: **"rascunho escrito pela IA — revise antes de aprovar"** (âmbar), para o CEO saber o que está aprovando. O `'assistente'` antigo continua rotulado.

### Prova (RD-59) — em transação com ROLLBACK, sem tocar produção
| teste | resultado |

| aberto **#63** | `ok:true` · **resposta_aprovada=false** · origem=ia · redigida_por=NULL ✅ |
| aprovado **#57** | `ok:false, erro=ja_aprovada` ✅ |

author: jurisacchetta
body:
Splits dependabot's #5, which cannot install as one piece.

#5 grouped three dev-dependency majors. `npm ci` fails on it before any code runs:

```
While resolving: typescript-eslint@8.70.0
Found: typescript@7.0.2
Could not resolve: peer typescript@">=4.8.4 <6.1.0" from typescript-eslint@8.70.0
```

No published `typescript-eslint` accepts TypeScript 7 — `8.70.0` is latest and its recent alphas all cap at `<6.1.0`. TypeScript 7 is the Go port and the lint toolchain has not caught up, so the only ways to take it today are dropping `typescript-eslint` or forcing `--legacy-peer-deps` onto an unsupported combination.

## This PR

Takes the two bumps that are not blocked, and holds the one that is:

| | from | to |
|---|---|---|
| `@types/node` | 22.20.2 | 26.5.1 |
| `vitest` | 3.2.x | 5.0.0 |
| `typescript` | 5.9.3 | **held** at `^5.9.0` |

No source changes were needed. Typecheck, lint and the full suite pass, and a clean `npm ci` resolves with no peer conflict.

## One thing worth a decision

`@types/node@26` describes Node 26's API surface, while `package.json` declares `engines.node >= 20` and CI runs 20 and 22. Types ahead of the runtime floor can let code compile against APIs the supported runtime doesn't have. It's inert here — this codebase only touches long-stable `fs`/`path`/`os`/`url`/`util`/`child_process`/`http` APIs, and CI exercises the suite on Node 20 — but pinning `@types/node` to `^22` to match the floor would be the stricter choice. Happy to change it if you'd prefer that.

TypeScript 7 stays for a follow-up once `typescript-eslint` supports it.

author: bharanikh-design
body:
## Where I put them, and why not the top right

You offered top-right or left nav. **There is no top bar in this shell** — `.app-stage` holds two empty divs where a header used to be, then the page. A top-right cluster means inventing chrome for two links.

The rail already carries a `Your career` heading and was built for a second group under it. So:

```
YOUR CAREER          ← the flow, read top to bottom as a sequence
  Dashboard
  Career Direction
  Find Roles
  Opportunities
  Analyse a Role
  Résumé Studio
─────────────────
SETTINGS             ← destinations, not steps
  Email Alerts
  Integrations
  Admin              ← administrators only
  Diagnostics        ← administrators only
```

Not *inside* the career flow either: that list is read as a sequence, and putting a setting in it would say it was a step. Separated by a rule rather than a gap, because a gap reads as spacing.

## The Admin link was broken in every way a link can be

```tsx
{session?.user?.email === "bharanik.h@gmail.com" && (
  <li style={{ marginTop: "16px", paddingTop: "16px", borderTop: "..." }}>
    <Link className={`as-nav-link${...}`}>
```

1. **A hardcoded email compiled into the browser bundle** — shipping a personal address to every visitor, and disagreeing with the `isOperationsAdmin()` check `/admin` itself performs. A second administrator on the `SARTHO_ADMIN_USER_IDS` allowlist could reach the page and **never see a link to it**.
2. **An `<li>` with no list around it**, where every other item renders a `<Link>`.
3. **`as-nav-link` appears in no stylesheet** — I grepped every CSS file. The link drew with browser defaults.
4. Its inline border was meant to separate it from the items below. It sat **above** them.

Admin status now comes from the server, through the journey status the shell already fetches — one definition of who an administrator is. It gates a **link**, never access: every admin route still checks for itself.

## The admin page now answers what an operator actually arrives with

**This deployment** — commit, branch, environment — first, because *"a merge is not a deploy"* cost two afternoons today and no panel could say which build was running. Plus links to the provider checks, which until now lived at JSON endpoints you had to know the URL of and read by eye.

## Two bugs caught on the way

**A duplicate.** `getNavigationForPath` appends the current page to the rail when it is not already there — so visiting `/integrations` would have drawn it in the career rail *and* in Settings. Settings pages are now excluded from that append; it still works for pages belonging to neither group.

**A test asserting the opposite of its title.** `"labels supporting workflow pages without adding them to primary navigation"` checked `primaryNavigation`, which is an alias for `allNavigation` — the lookup table every page label and active-state check reads, not the career rail. **A page has to be in that table to be labelled at all.** It now asserts against `getPrimaryNavigation`.

## Verification

- `npm run lint` — clean
- `rm -rf .next && npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npx vitest run` — 895 passed, 4 skipped (was 890; +5 including the settings group)
- `npm run build` — compiled successfully
- Grepped: the hardcoded email is gone from every source file

## Suggestions I did not act on

**The profile menu is now thin** — identity, upload résumé, data & privacy, log out. "Upload résumé" is arguably a flow step hiding in a settings menu; it belongs on the Dashboard, where the navigation comment says it already is until it is done. Worth removing, but it is a behaviour change and you were not asking for it.

**`/journey` has no entry point.** It is in `allNavigation` but in no group, so it is reachable only by typing the URL or being sent there.

**`/diagnostics` and `/admin` are two halves of one thing.** Now that both are in Settings this is survivable, but the honest structure is one Operations page with tabs.

author: mesanjusk
body:
Follow-up to #29. With Gemini finally reachable by the image route, the next layer showed itself: `Every image provider refused this request outright: gemini (gemini-2.5-flash-preview-image)`. That message is true — the key has no image allowance — but two things around it were wrong.

## 1. The refusal was recorded under a key nobody reads

Google does not always name the model that was requested. A call for `gemini-2.5-flash-image` comes back refused naming `gemini-2.5-flash-preview-image`, because that is what the free-tier quota is registered as.

`markModelUnavailable` used the reported name. `imageRouteCandidates` only ever checks the *requested* one (`modelFor(providerId)`). So on exactly the deployment this mechanism exists for, the note went into a key nothing reads, and every later job spent another doomed request rediscovering the same refusal — the waste `core/ai/provider-health.ts`'s own docstring says it exists to prevent.

Now recorded under both names when they differ, so the router's skip actually fires.

## 2. Every dead-end message omitted the one free way out

All of them ended at "enable billing, choose a different model, or switch the image provider in Settings", which quietly leaves out the route this studio is built around: Flow draws images in a browser with no API allowance involved at all. When no Flow session is connected, that is one setup step between a stuck pipeline and a working one — the same step `core/production/progress.ts` already puts a button on.

Both dead ends now name it, and neither suggests it to someone who already has a session connected.

## 3. A benched model is not an unconfigured deployment

`explainNoImageRoute` had two answers; it needed three. A model skipped because of a refusal it already reported would have reported "No image provider is configured" — on a deployment whose credential is present and correct, which sends an operator to check configuration that is fine. It now says what was refused, quotes Google's own answer, and notes that the record re-tests itself in 24h.

## What this does not do

None of it makes an unavailable model available. The underlying fact is unchanged and is not a code problem: image generation needs either billing on that key's Google project, or a connected Flow browser session so images are drawn in Flow instead.

## Verification

`npm run verify` — typecheck clean, lint 0 errors (8 pre-existing warnings in untouched files), **312 tests passing** (was 308).

New tests: the refusal recorded under both the requested and reported model names (and the router dropping the provider afterwards), the benched-model message, the browser-route hint appearing when no session exists, and not appearing when one does.

author: mashkovd
body:
Closes the two P3s left on #303, which merged before they were addressed. Test-only; `scripts/portal-allowlist-apply.sh` is untouched.

## The real one: the probe vouched for itself

`probeRecorder` is the positive control that makes an empty call log mean "no request went out" rather than "the recorder is dead". It supplied its **own** `STUB_CURL_LOG` instead of inheriting the one the run used — so it proved the stub's append works, not that the stub was recording for the run it was vouching for. The comment above it names two ways the recorder can die, *"STUB_CURL_LOG no longer exported, the append broken"*; the probe only closed the second.

Verified by mutation rather than by reading. Dropping `"STUB_CURL_LOG=" + logPath` from the run's env, on the previous head:

```
--- FAIL: TestApplyCheck  (9 of 12)
    portal_allowlist_apply_test.go:457: no curl call log at .../curl.log;
        the no-PUT assertion below would be vacuous
```

The three `wantEmptyLog` cases **passed**: the script records nothing, the log never appears, `readErr != nil` skips the emptiness assertion, and the probe records anyway off its own value. Exactly the three cases whose entire evidence is an absence were blind to it.

`probe.Env = cmd.Env` sends the probe's line nowhere too, so the post-probe read fails and the case says so.

## Mutation results

| mutation | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `STUB_CURL_LOG` dropped from the run's env | 9/12 fail | **12/12 fail** |
| stub's `append` disabled (`if false`) | 12/12 fail | 12/12 fail |
| `--check` comparison bypassed → real `PUT` | 7 fail | 7 fail |
| clean tree | `ok` | `ok` |

One honest note on the third row: that mutation is caught by the exit-code and output assertions, not by the call-log `PUT` check. I tried to isolate the log guard — bypass the comparison *and* have the stub answer `PUT` with a success envelope so the exit code survives — and the `in sync:` output assertion still fires first. The no-`PUT` log assertion is a backstop that no reachable mutation isolates; it is not doing nothing, but its own effectiveness is not independently proven, and I would rather say so than imply it is.

## The second P3: a comment describing the fix as the bug

*"Both assertions below are gated on a successful read … would skip them and leave every case passing"* was an accurate account of the head **before** `df64c1a`. On the current one the `else` branch `Fatal`s on `readErr != nil` before asserting anything. Rewritten to state the rule the code enforces — each half carries its own positive control.

author: rigel-mintaka
body:
<!-- start jj-vine stack -->
This PR is part of a stack containing 7 PRs:

1. `main`
2. #1110
3. #1111
4. #1118
5. #1138
6. #1141
7. **"feat(server): resolve the at-rest master key at boot (RIG-3655 T4)" (this PR)**
8. #1155
<!-- end jj-vine stack -->

Adds a COMPASS_ reserved server-secret prefix and renames the at-rest
master key GATEWAY_CREDENTIALS_MASTER_KEY -> COMPASS_MASTER_KEY, since
one key now covers both the user-secret and gateway_credentials stores.
The rename is what the new prefix is for: the name carries neither
existing prefix, so without it the row is undeclarable.

resolveMasterKey resolves the key, decodes 64 hex chars to 32 bytes, and
reconciles it against the server_key_state tripwire -- first boot writes
a salted fingerprint, a later boot constant-time compares it and fails
closed, so a swapped key cannot mis-decrypt existing rows. It never
generates a key: operator-seeded custody, so an absent key is a startup
failure naming the provisioning runbook.

Errors never echo the value or any part of it, verified by a test that
sweeps every failure arm for any 8-char substring of the secret.

Also documents all seven server secrets in docs/self-host.md, which
named none of them before -- the master key's runbook is incoherent
without the six forge secrets beside it.

resolveMasterKey's boot caller lands with the rest of T4, which is
blocked on the session-binding work; the function, its store accessor,
and its tests ship complete.

Refs RIG-3655

## Summary

Add a versioned, read-only DSH History adapter for Agent Console while keeping DSH's native persistence format and session lifecycle private to dsh-runtime-kit.

## Issues

- Refs [serenvia/agent-console#480](https://github.com/serenvia/agent-console/issues/480)

## Changes

- Add `capabilities`, header-only `list`, selected-session `summaries`, and bounded `messages` operations under the `dsh-runtime-kit.history.v1` envelope.
- Build the adapter from DSH's public session, persistence, query, and title packages and refuse any runtime composition other than the reviewed exact versions.
- Project only top-level sessions and visible human-user/assistant text, isolate corrupt records, preserve cursor paging, and cap public message output.
- Document the trust boundary and add durable development-log evidence.

## Test-First Evidence

- Before the implementation existed, `node --test test/dsh-history-adapter.test.ts` failed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for the adapter module.
- Follow-up regression failures covered orphan worker filtering, corrupt surface/header isolation, exact-version refusal, and output-size bounds before their fixes.

## Test plan

- `npm run build && node --test test/dsh-history-adapter.test.ts` — pass (6 tests).
- `npm run build && npm run build:provenance && npm test && npm run typecheck && npm run benchmark:policy && npm pack --dry-run --json` — pass.
- Read-only smoke against the existing DSH store — list, summaries, and messages envelopes validated without logging provider content.

## Risk / Notes

- The adapter is intentionally non-resumable and has no mutation operation.
- Callers still own process-group timeout and a 16 MiB stdout cap; adapter failures degrade History only.
- Catalog listing remains header/revision-only, and transcript reads are restricted to explicitly selected session IDs.

author: jrosberg
body:
This pull request updates how thread sleep timeouts are represented and traced, switching from unsigned to signed integers to properly handle special values like `K_FOREVER` and absolute deadlines. The main changes ensure that negative timeout values are preserved and correctly interpreted across the trace infrastructure, including the CTF and SystemView tracing formats.

**Tracing infrastructure updates:**

* Changed the timeout parameter type from `uint32_t` to `int32_t` in `ctf_top_thread_sleep_ticks_enter` and `ctf_top_thread_sleep_ticks_exit` functions and their usage, ensuring signed values are passed through tracing events (`ctf_top.h`, `ctf_top.c`, `metadata`).
* Updated the SystemView trace macros to cast timeouts to signed 32-bit integers before tracing, preserving special negative values like `K_FOREVER` and absolute deadlines (`tracing_sysview.h`).

**Trace format and description updates:**

* Added a new `SleepTicks` named type to the SystemView description file, documenting that sleep timeouts are signed and explaining the encoding for absolute deadlines (`SYSVIEW_Zephyr.txt`).
* Updated the trace event for `k_sleep_ticks` to use the new `SleepTicks` type, ensuring correct display and interpretation of signed timeouts (`SYSVIEW_Zephyr.txt`).

These changes make the tracing of thread sleep timeouts more robust and accurate, especially when dealing with special timeout values.

body: Four field reports from one session on Demi's desktop app (12 Sep), one PR. ### "I pressed stop monitoring but it didn't stop" `/monitor` derived *running* from the heartbeat file's age (<30 s), so a Stop read as monitoring for up to half a minute. The backend that **owns** the engine process answers first now (`_ApiBackend.engine_alive`); the heartbeat still decides when nobody has started/stopped an engine through the API (a headless terminal run). ### "I don't see any videos rendered" Two bugs stacked: - `frames.json` outlived the engine that wrote it, and every run publishes on a fresh port → after a Stop the app resolved a dead URL. The publisher now removes its marker on `stop()`, and `/cameras/{id}/stream` answers **503** while the engine is stopped. - A tile (`CameraStream.tsx`) resolved its stream **once** at mount. Open the wall, press Start, and every tile stayed "offline" until remounted. While offline a tile now re-resolves every 5 s (one small request per tile). ### "Alerts should go to Telegram and the app both" `_resolve_live_config` hard-coded `"notify": "console"`, so switching to Live EarthCams silently turned phone alerts off. Feeds inherit the home site's delivery target (`_home_notify()`), and `_spawn_engine` falls back to it. ### Public EarthCams flooding `loitering_watch` fired at `dwell_seconds >= 1.5` while its own zone said 45 s ("someone CAMPED in view") — 100 auto-confirmed alerts in minutes, now aimed at the phone channel. The rule matches the zone. ### Verified live Start → engine args carry `--notify console,telegram:…`; Stop → `/monitor` says `stopped` immediately; `/stream` → 503 `engine_unavailable`; `frames.json` gone after exit. ### Tests `test_engine_api.py` 24 pass (+2), publisher/backend/feed/notify suites 61 pass (+1), frontend `vitest` 107 pass, `tsc --noEmit` clean. Note for Demi: the only frontend change is the offline retry in `CameraStream.tsx`. Confirmed while here that in API mode the tile is a plain `` straight at the engine's MJPEG publisher (WebRTC straight to go2rtc) — no proxy or transcoding in the render path. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: jeedo
body:
## Summary
Implements plan task 16 (T6 — DoS via creates; T12 — malformed input / parser abuse). First API endpoint.

- `Api/SecretsApi.cs` — `POST /api/secrets` reads `{ ciphertext, nonce, ttlSeconds? }` with strict `JsonSerializerOptions`: unmapped members disallowed, `MaxDepth = 8`, `NumberHandling = Strict` (no numbers-as-strings), `AllowDuplicateProperties = false`, no comments, no trailing commas. Non-JSON content type → 415. Malformed/non-strict JSON, a JSON `null`, or a non-object → 400 `malformedJson`. Missing fields → `ciphertextRequired` / `nonceRequired`; bad encoding → `ciphertextEncoding` / `nonceEncoding`. Omitted TTL defaults to 1 h.
- Store results map to `ValidationError` → 400 with the camel-cased failure kind (`ciphertextTooShort`, `nonceLength`, `timeToLiveTooLong`, …) and `CapacityExceeded` → 503 `capacityExceeded` with `Retry-After: 30`. Success → 201 `{ id, expiresAt }` and one `create` audit event. Decoded buffers are zeroed on every failure path.
- `Api/Base64UrlStrict.cs` — accepts only unpadded, URL-safe, canonical base64url (re-encode check), mirroring the client codec. Note: `Base64Url.TryDecodeFromChars` throws `FormatException` on malformed input despite its name (it returns `false` only for a short buffer) — caught and treated as invalid.
- `Api/ApiProblems.cs` — fixed RFC 7807 bodies (`application/problem+json`) whose only variable part is a stable `code`; nothing from the request is ever echoed. Task 24 layers the global exception handler on top.
- Tests (`[Trait("Threat", "T6")]`, `[Trait("Threat", "T12")]`, 34 new, on a fake clock): happy path with exact `{ expiresAt, id }` shape and the secret peekable; default TTL; anonymous audit event with the returned Id; eleven malformed/non-strict bodies → 400 with nothing stored; depth > 8; missing/misencoded fields with typed codes (padding, `+`, `/`, non-canonical trailing bits, junk); every store bound on both sides → typed 400 and the response never contains the submitted base64; 415 for form content; full store → 503 + `Retry-After: 30`, nothing stored, only the first create audited; failed creates write no audit event.
- `docs/plan.md` marks task 16 complete.

## Test plan
- [x] Red phase: all 34 new tests failed with 404 before the endpoint existed
- [x] `dotnet build OneShot.sln` — 0 warnings, 0 errors

author: barenatico
body:
## Por que

O PR #898 criou o vínculo (quem indicou × quem colheu). Faltavam as **portas de entrada**: sem elas, registrar indicação continuava sendo trabalho manual que ninguém faz.

## As três portas

**1. O link do cliente.** `/f/<form>?ref=<id do cliente>` cria o vínculo sozinho. O cliente encaminha o link no grupo de lojistas dele e a indicação nasce creditada a quem o link diz (`?refby=`) ou, sem isso, ao **dono do cliente** (o link é dele, quem cuida dele colhe). Fail-open por construção: link velho ou id errado não derruba o envio de quem está do outro lado preenchendo, e teste da equipe com `?ref=` não entra como indicação.

**2. O plantio na integração.** O Formulário de Integração ganha o pedido de dois nomes no fim, no momento de maior entusiasmo do cliente (acabou de comprar, está montando a operação).

O nome dado ali **não vira lead**. Telefone de terceiro sem consentimento é lead frio e exposição desnecessária, e o formulário promete ao cliente, com essas palavras, que ninguém é procurado antes de ele ser avisado. Os nomes ficam na ficha do cliente (`referralSeeds`) e geram **tarefa** pro dono pedir a ponte, já com o valor da coleta na descrição.

Isso exigiu a primeira exceção à régua "tudo que está visível é obrigatório": o novo `optional: true`. A régua existe para não faltar dado da integração, e pedido de indicação não é dado de integração. Questionário vai para a versão 3; linha em branco não vira registro, mas linha começada tem que ser terminada.

**3. O registro na mão.** Campo "Indicado por (cliente)" no form de lead, com o que a coleta paga escrito no help. O coletor sai da sessão: quem registra leva o crédito.

## Na tela

- **Bloco Indicações** na ficha do cliente: quem ele já indicou e em que pé está cada um, os nomes plantados que ninguém foi buscar (com botão que abre o lead já vinculado) e o botão de copiar o link de indicação dele.
- Linha **"Indicado por Azul Pet · colhido por Jonan"** no resumo do lead, que o drawer do pipeline e o Meu dia mostram igual (régua dos blocos compartilhados).

## Teste

`referral-captura.test.js` (4 casos: crédito pelo dono, `?refby=` e usuário inventado, ref inválido que não derruba o envio, teste da equipe) e 3 casos novos em `integration-form.test.js` (opcional em branco, indicação começada pela metade, e os nomes indo pra ficha + tarefa sem criar lead).

Suíte da API: **1416 passando, 0 falhando**. Build do web: ok.

author: aganesy
body:
Closes #1597.

## The line this replaces

> 1. Run the core interview for concept, scope, stakeholders, and constraints.

That was the whole of step one. It named no method, so an agent that asked
nothing had followed it — which is the behaviour the grilling work was reported
against, stated in the skill's own process.

It runs through the `qfai-grilling` skill now, over every topic in the coverage
checklist, and cites `.agents/rules/grilling.md` rather than restating it. A case
asserts the skill carries none of the method's mechanics: two copies drift, and
the drift reaches an agent as two instructions to choose between.

## The policy moved with it

| Bucket | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auto-decide` | `equivalent-option pick` | the same, plus what equivalent means — which a design choice is not |
| `ask-user` | no design decision | every decision the interview puts on the frontier, and the confirmation that closes the session |

A design choice sitting under `equivalent-option pick` is how a design nobody
agreed to gets recorded as decided. Running the interview is what this skill
performs, so its questions are its own operations rather than an entry added to
the prototype's closed list.

## Authoring waits

A pack drafted mid-session records a design that was still being decided, and
from then on the run defends the draft rather than the decision.

The completion matrix makes it blocking, and says why it has to be: a pack
authored mid-session is indistinguishable from one authored after — same fifteen
files, same coverage, same register. What is missing is that anyone agreed to
what is in them, and no later gate can recover that.

Under a no-question mode the confirmation has nobody to give it, so the session's
remaining decisions are registered as open questions and the existing open-count
condition blocks instead. Same guarantee, other route.

The Reviewer Gate gets the matching check, because every other check it runs
reads the fifteen files, and a session that never happened leaves them complete.

## Checks

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `discussionGrilling` (new) | 14 passed, both trees |
| `pnpm -C packages/qfai test:assets` | 3527 passed, 4 skipped |
| `pnpm check-types` / `pnpm lint:md` | clean |
| `pnpm sync:ssot` | mirror in step |

author: mps2210
body:
## What this fixes

Three tracked files named the maintainer's employer directly, and one also quoted a third party's personal name, on a public repository.

Both breach standing rules that this project had already written down:

- the maintainer's employer must not appear on any public Surfaceplate surface;
- `audit/REVIEW_INVITATION.md` already states that reviewer names *"are deliberately not published there before the recipients consent."* `H16` quoted a name anyway.

## Where it was

| File | Rows |
|---|---|
| `org/HUMAN_ACTIONS.md` | `H4`, `H6`, `H18`, `H16` (also the personal name), `H19` |
| `activity/register.md` | `ACT-108`, `ACT-073` |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | the `H19`/`H18` paragraph in the 0.18.0 section |

Introduced between 2026-09-08 and 2026-09-11. The earlier instance in `audit/PRE_AUDIT_FINDINGS_0.6.0.md` was correctly redacted on 2026-08-31 under `F18` — these are new, and were introduced while that rule was in force.

## What changed, and what did not

Redactions are **disclosed, not silent** — a new section at the foot of `HUMAN_ACTIONS.md` records what was changed and why, following the same convention `PRE_AUDIT_FINDINGS_0.6.0.md` uses for its own redactions.

**No substance changes.** The route is still a real engagement with a real firm; `F6` still closes only on a returned recomputation recorded under `governance/assurance/AE-0002-framework-anchor.yaml`, with the reviewer named and not the maintainer.

## The underlying defect is a missing control

`tests/check_identifiers.py` polices organisation-identifier *spellings*. `gitleaks` scans for secrets. **Neither checks for employer or third-party names**, so this rule was enforced by memory alone — which is why it was restated correctly in one file on 2026-08-31 and broken in three others a week later.

Worth considering a follow-up that adds a name guard to the identifier checks, so the rule is enforced by something other than recall.

## Not addressed here, deliberately

The four introducing commits still carry the name in their **commit messages**, and PR #106's body did too (now edited). Commit messages are not reachable by this PR.

Rewriting them was considered and rejected on three grounds: GitHub retains every PR head under `refs/pull/N/head` server-side, so the text would remain fetchable regardless; the `main-required-checks` ruleset blocks non-fast-forward pushes anyway; and rewriting those SHAs would invalidate the `pypi/0.18.0` review packet's stated provenance — it attests to published commit `a345f2b`, which is the exact commit an external reviewer is meant to recompute the anchor from under `F6`. Breaking that to tidy history would cost more than it buys.

If full removal from GitHub is wanted, the mechanism is a GitHub Support request to purge the commit data, not a force-push.

author: niclaslindstedt
body:
## What & why

A replay **is** a run — `startReplay` stands the stage up with `mode: "replay"` and nothing else changes — so a recording reaches the results card exactly as a driven run does. Watching a replay of a run that ends with a dead engine therefore put up the driver's card, offering **RETIRE** and **RESTART STAGE**: there is no run to retire from, and `restart` over a recording rewinds it to its first step (`run-events.ts`) rather than putting anybody on a grid. Both presses did the right thing under the wrong name, which is exactly how it read — as if it were still your race.

`FinishCard` now takes a `replaying` flag and swaps the two words — **EXIT** and **WATCH AGAIN** — while the handlers stay exactly as they were. `WATCH AGAIN` is offered at the end of every recording rather than only a retirement. The nudge under a slow finish (`TOP 3 TO GO ON — RUN IT AGAIN`) goes with them: it is spoken to a driver. The headline stays — `ENGINE DEAD` is the news the recording stops on, and it is why the picture has stopped moving.

**…and the strip cannot stand on that card.** The comment over `.hud-replay` claims the card's title and sheet clear it. Neither does: at the card's own `top: 7%` the strip crosses the results card's title and the whole of the retirement notice, which *is* its own headline. Measured across four viewports the overlap ran 13–54 px. Nudging down by the strip's height settles nothing — `--replay-height` is a reserve rather than a measurement, 3.9 rem against a bar standing 79 px tall at 1280×720 — so over a recording the card takes the middle of the frame instead.

That centring is safe for every card a recording can raise **because** a replay is entered with no level id: it reaches no board, no points and no result sheet, so what is left is short. A card at its full `max-height: 86%` would centre straight back under the strip, which is the condition to keep in mind if that ever changes.

The driver's cards are untouched.

## Test plan

- `make fmt-check`, `make lint` (eslint + whole-program typecheck) — clean on the rebased tree.
- `npx vitest run tests/replay_test.ts tests/screenshots_test.ts tests/touch_test.ts tests/file_size_test.ts tests/changeset_test.ts` — 99 passed. The root suite is DOM-free and cannot mount `FinishCard`, so the card itself is verified by capture.
- No handling or generator change, so no `make sim` table.

**Captured the real states**, not mocks. Two run tapes forged headlessly — full throttle into the trees kills the engine at 10.18 s on seed 42, and `make record` for a clean 77 s lap — seeded into the replay roll in IndexedDB, opened off the REPLAYS page and driven to their own endings.

| Card over a replay | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retirement | `RETIRE` · `RESTART STAGE`, headline behind the strip | `EXIT` · `WATCH AGAIN`, clear of it |
| Finish | `RETIRE`, `STAGE CLEAR` clipped behind the strip | `EXIT` · `WATCH AGAIN`, clear of it |

Card/strip boxes re-measured for **both** cards at 1280×720, 1920×1080, 844×390 (phone landscape) and 390×844 — no overlap at any of them (e.g. the results card at 1280×720 went from `top: 55` under a strip ending at `89`, to `257`).

- `node scripts/screenshot.mjs shot-retired` and `shot-finish-trial` re-shot: the driver's retirement card still reads `RETIRE` / `RESTART STAGE` and the trial card `RETIRE` / `RETRY`, both in their usual place at 7%.

## Checklist

- [x] `make lint`, `make fmt-check` pass locally; the suites this change reaches pass (whole `make test` left to CI, green on the current head)
- [ ] Tests added/updated for behavior changes — the root suite is DOM-free and cannot mount `FinishCard`; verified by capture instead
- [x] `make sim` before/after included (handling or generator changes) — n/a
- [x] Changeset fragment in `.changes/unreleased/`
- [x] Docs updated per AGENTS.md → Documentation sync points — none owed; `docs/getting-started.md` describes the replay flow but not this card's presses
- [x] PR title is a conventional-commit subject

author: dorkmo
body:
## Summary

Closes #144. The shared atlas crosses the peer trust boundary and feeds a **capped** local store (`MAX_ENTRIES = 64`), and two things went wrong at that seam. One file plus tests.

## 1. The gossip stamp was unbounded

`isSharedAtlasEntry` validated `updatedAt` as `typeof number` and nothing more, so a planted far-future value won every merge comparison in `pullSharedAtlas` permanently. Entries stamped more than 6h ahead of our clock are now refused.

Unlike ventures (#143), this **is** a real ingest boundary — the doc is not the store, `pullSharedAtlas` writes localStorage — so bounding here keeps the stored value stable rather than time-varying. That's exactly what the write-boundary guidance in #144 was about, and why it holds here while it didn't for `ventures.ts`.

## 2. Eviction ordered on that same peer-supplied value

`writeAtlas` sorted by `lastSeen`, which derives from `updatedAt`. A peer could float its own entries to the top of a 64-deep list and push out rooms the player had actually walked through.

**This isn't only an attack.** A single join absorbs an *entire station* — `pullSharedAtlas` merges the whole shared map, and that map converges toward the full station layout by design ("a visiting ship that joins ANY room of the station downloads the full map"). So entries accumulate per *station visited*, not per room, and the cap is reached in ordinary play at roughly **7–8 octagon stations**, or ~5 once stations run past `SMALL_STATION_MAX = 12` — which PR #133 explicitly expects. For a game whose roadmap pushes players outward to a colony network, that's normal play. Working shown in [#144](https://github.com/Bella-Addormentata/StarStationFurlong/issues/144#issuecomment-5645928417).

**The fix:** `AtlasEntry` gains `localSeenAt`, stamped only by this install. `writeAtlas` then evicts in two tiers: first-hand rooms outrank gossip-only ones regardless of how fresh a peer claims to be, each tier ordered by its own recency.

**What earns a first-hand stamp is narrower than it looks, and deliberately so:**

- ✅ `harvestIntoAtlas` — you stood in the room.
- ❌ **Never gossip.** An earlier cut stamped first-learn with `Date.now()`, which still let one station sweep outrank earlier visits. The **tiering** is what fixes this, not the extra field.
- ❌ **Never the neighbour stubs a door reveals.** These come from `readAllDoors()`, which is peer-written and capped at `MAX_PAIRINGS = 64` — exactly `MAX_ENTRIES`. An earlier cut stamped them, which hands a hostile room doc a full atlas's worth of protected entries and reinstates the very eviction this fixes. What you see first-hand is the *room*, not a peer's claim about where its doors lead.
- ⚠️ `noteRoomSeed` would stamp a handed seed, but **it has no production callers** and has had none since it landed in a65d66a, long before this work — the seed paths (`addPass`, ledger mints) never wired up to it. Documented in place rather than wired, since wiring it is a behaviour change beyond the retention fix.

So in practice today: **standing in a room is the only thing that earns tier 1.**

Legacy entries have no stamp and land in tier 2, ordered among themselves by `lastSeen`: an upgrade loses the visited/gossip distinction for old entries rather than mis-ranking them.

The ordering now lives in one exported `compareAtlasRecency`, used by `writeAtlas` and by the docking picker (`docking.ts`), which had its own `b.lastSeen - a.lastSeen` sort and would otherwise have kept ranking on the peer-supplied value.

## 3. Two follow-ons the guard alone does not reach

- **A store poisoned before the upgrade.** The ingest bound cannot reach a value already sitting in localStorage, so `readAtlas` repairs out-of-window stamps to `0` — and **persists the repair**. An in-memory-only fix is temporary: the ceiling is `Date.now() + 6h` and keeps moving, so a stamp only a few hours out falls back under it within the hour and returns.
- **The outbound stamp.** The monotonic `+1` bump exists so a corrective re-push always out-ranks the record it corrects, but unclamped it lands one millisecond past the bound — and then our own reader, and every peer on a similar clock, refuses the record we just wrote. It is clamped to the same ceiling the ingest guard enforces.

## Known limitation: the clamp has a tie at the boundary

Stated precisely, because an earlier version of the code comment claimed this "self-resolves" and that was wrong:

When `known.updatedAt` sits **at** the ceiling, the clamp returns that same value, so our record ties rather than out-ranks. A peer already holding the boundary-stamped entry skips it (`prior.lastSeen >= value.updatedAt`, same door count) and the correction doesn't reach them. It isn't lost — once our clock passes the stamp the bump fits under the ceiling again — but it propagates only at the **next push**, and pushes are event-driven (join, door change), never on a timer. Time passing alone does nothing.

Reaching this needs an existing record stamped a full 6h into our future, which no honest clock produces; it's the adversarial/badly-skewed edge. It is also not fully fixable as posed: **bounding the stamp, out-ranking an adversary sitting at the bound, and having peers accept the result are not simultaneously satisfiable.** Publishing a record nobody can ingest is the worse trade. A scheduled retry at the moment the ceiling clears would close it — that's a timer this module doesn't currently own, and a reasonable follow-up.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- `npm test` → **125 passing** (109 before; `stationAtlas.test.ts` adds 16).
- Tests drive the real ingest path (`bindStationAtlasDoc` → `pullSharedAtlas`) with entries a hostile peer could write, rather than calling internals.
- **Discrimination checked, not assumed.** Each behavioural case was re-run against the pre-fix code and confirmed to fail: the eviction tiering, the persisted legacy repair, and the outbound clamp. The plain bound cases pass either way, since they exercise a separate change.
- The clamp case needs a **frozen clock and a single push** to be reachable — the ceiling moves between push and assertion, and a second push quietly repairs the out-of-window record before it can be observed. My first attempt had neither and passed with the clamp reverted; I then claimed on the branch that it "needs a clock seam we do not have," which was wrong — `vi.useFakeTimers()` is that seam. Review caught it. The assertion is a round trip rather than arithmetic: the published record is handed to a second peer running our own ingest guard, which has to accept it. Both of its assertions were checked against a reverted clamp and each fails on its own.

## Not covered

- **Per-entry serialized size is unmeasured**, so whether 64 is the right cap once it's reached honestly remains an open question — flagged on the issue, not answered here. This PR stops peers from controlling *which* entries survive; it doesn't argue the number.
- The credential rule is untouched: seeds still ride only on a doc's own-room entry while passage is public.
- `noteRoomSeed` stays uncalled, and the boundary tie above stays open.

author: rasros
body:
## What changed

- Fix whole-vector sparse gather dispatch to reach the selected backend, retaining the measured short-vector and JVM fallbacks.
- Align native x86 scaling stores for vectors of at least 128 elements and process fixed 16-element blocks.
- Add arithmetic benchmarks, regression coverage, and reproducible performance reports.

## Why

Gather previously bypassed the selected kernel through interface delegation. The fix delivers measured native speedups of 3.71x at 1,024 stored values and 2.68x at 16,384.

Scaling suffered from misaligned stores and scaled-index addressing. At 4,096 elements, alignment improves misaligned native CPU time by 1.87x; fixed blocks add another 11–14% improvement over alignment alone. The standard arithmetic benchmark improves from 225 ns to 207 ns, versus oneMKL's 201 ns. Gains depend on size and alignment; detailed measurements and limitations are retained in the reports.

## Testing

Passed `./gradlew :koblas:check :koblas-bench:check lintDocs check` and `./gradlew :koblas:jvmTest -Pkoblas.noSimd=true`. Scalar-oracle tests cover offsets, boundaries, tails, untouched storage, and exceptional values. Native tests exercise the C kernel; benchmarks use a pinned core and single-threaded references.

author: kfeofantov
body:
The inventory e2e confirmed a `pprof_profile` for its Go sample but asserted
nothing about `goroutine_counts`, though the sample serves the very index page
the reading comes from. Noted as owed in
[`docs/plans/goroutine-leak-sensor.md`](docs/plans/goroutine-leak-sensor.md); this
pays it.

## What it asserts

**Two samples is the assertion that matters.** One reading proves the parser;
only a second proves what the kind exists for, since no single count is a
finding. It also shows the reading repeats — the part of the promise in
`security.md` §10.3 that a single fetch cannot demonstrate.

Beside it: the window's kind, source and length, a non-zero `captured_at`, the
**pod name** (the one place this funnel names a process rather than a build), the
image digest, and the coverage block reporting the readings that produced the
series with no unreadable answers.

Verified in kind against the merged agent:

```
goroutine series for goworkload-5bb85d86f8-z6f87: 2 samples, 5 then 8 goroutines
goroutine count coverage: {Sampled:6 Unreachable:0 Unreadable:0}
```

## A pre-existing failure this found

The counters assertion required `observed_nanos >= 20s` while the test installs
`scanInterval: 15s`, so it could only pass when a scan pass drifted a third past
its own interval. It fails on `main` with the same agent image: `observed_nanos =
15004472048`.

`observed_nanos` is the wall-clock gap between two readings of one process
(`now.Sub(prev.at)`), and the two readings sit at different points inside their
scan passes, so the gap jitters either side of the interval — **14.981s** and
**15.002s**, both measured here. The floor is now the installed interval less a
second of slack, from one constant, because two numbers that merely agree drift
(ADR 0073 §5). The target's `-timeout` goes to 20m to match the test's own 20m
context, which it was silently cutting short.

## What is still red, and is not from here

`TestGoInventoryEndToEnd` also fails at `checkOptOutRemovesTheRecord`: the
opted-out workload stays in the `go_inventory` payload past the check's deadline.
**This reproduces on `main` with the same agent image**, so it is neither caused
nor unmasked by this PR:

| run | test tree | counters assertion | opt-out assertion |
|---|---|---|---|
| this PR | branch | pass | fail |
| control | `origin/main` | fail (20s vs 15s) | fail |

It wants its own investigation rather than a wider deadline. The two halves are
unit-tested — `Retain` in `internal/inventory/store_test.go`, pod-level exclusion
in `internal/collector` — and `UpdateFunc` does call `dropPod` when admission is
withdrawn, so what is uncovered is the composition: pod update → drop from the
index → `Retain` → the cadence gate → the spool file. Whether the record never
leaves or merely leaves late decides whether this touches the promise in
`security.md` §11, and that needs controller logs from a run, which I have not
taken. The check's own message still says "after 4 minutes" while its deadline is

author: daften
body:
## Summary

Upgrades Vitest and `@vitest/coverage-v8` to 5.0.0 and drops Node 20 support, which the upgrade forces. Replaces #95 and #96, which cannot merge separately.

## Why one PR instead of two

Dependabot raised the pair as two PRs — #95 (`vitest`) and #96 (`@vitest/coverage-v8`) — but `@vitest/coverage-v8@X` peers `vitest: "X"` **exactly**. Each half fails `npm ci` with `ERESOLVE` on *every* matrix node, 22 and 24 included, so neither could ever go green on its own:

```
npm error While resolving: @vitest/coverage-v8@4.1.11
npm error Found: vitest@5.0.0
npm error Could not resolve dependency:
npm error peer vitest@"4.1.11" from @vitest/coverage-v8@4.1.11
```

They only install together. Both are closed in favour of this branch.

## Why Node 20 goes

Vitest 5 declares `engines: ^22.12.0 || ^24.0.0 || >=26.0.0`. Node 20 also reached end-of-life in April 2026, so this retires an already-dead runtime rather than a supported one. 0.4.6 deliberately pinned Vitest at 4.1.11 "while retaining Node 20 support" — that trade-off has now expired.

`engines.node` becomes `>=22.12.0`, matching Vitest 5's own floor exactly so that `package.json`, the README, the docs site and `AGENTS.md` all state a single number. The published server contains no Node-20-specific code and will still *run* there, but 20 is no longer tested and no longer supported, and npm will `EBADENGINE`-warn on it.

## Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `package.json` | both deps → `^5.0.0`; `engines.node` `>=20` → `>=22.12.0` |
| `package-lock.json` | regenerated; `vite@8.2.1` dedupes with the copy VitePress already pulls, so v5's newly-unbundled `vite` peer needs no new direct dependency |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | matrix `[20, 22, 24]` → `[22, 24, 26]`; the coverage job and its sticky PR comment stay keyed to 22 |
| `.github/dependabot.yml` | new `vitest` group matching `vitest` + `@vitest/*`, listed first and with no `update-types` filter, so a version-locked pair can never be split across two PRs again |
| `README.md` (×2), `docs/guide/{index,stdio,http-pat,http-oauth}.md`, `AGENTS.md` | Node.js 20+ → 22.12+ — every Node version claim in the repo |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | four `### Changed` entries under `[Unreleased]` |

No other workflow needed touching: `nightly.yml` was already on 22, and `publish.yml`, `auto-release.yml`, `auto-merge.yml`, `docs.yml` and the `Dockerfile` on 24.

**The Dependabot grouping fix governs nothing until it reaches `main`** — Dependabot reads that file from the default branch only. Until the next release promotes it, a Vitest major could still arrive split.

## No test or source changes were needed

The suite steers clear of every v5 breaking change: no `sequential`, `test.for`, `expect.poll` or `vi.hoisted`, and all 21 test files import bare `vitest` rather than a removed `vitest/*` entry point. Mocks are built per test, so v5's clear-mocks-by-default is a no-op here. Coverage still writes `coverage/coverage-summary.json` where `vitest-coverage-report-action` looks — v5's "output to `.vitest/`" change affects the json/junit/blob reporters, not the coverage directory.

## Type of change

- [x] chore (dependencies, config, scaffolding)
- [x] docs (documentation only)

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated — n/a, no source or test changes
- [x] `npm test` passes locally — 438 passed, 13 skipped, 20 files
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` passes locally
- [ ] README tool table updated (if a new tool was added) — n/a
- [ ] CLAUDE.md updated (if architectural) — n/a; `AGENTS.md` runtime line updated
- [ ] Verified relevant fields against the Firefly III OpenAPI spec (if API-touching) — n/a

Also verified locally on Node 22.16: `biome ci`, `npm run test:coverage`, `npm run build`, the 14 automation `node:test` cases, and the VitePress docs build.

Release note: this is a minimum-runtime drop, so the next release should be a minor bump (`0.5.0`), not a patch.

author: alsaadii98
body:
## What this changes

`cast-health.svg` was a broken image on the site. Root cause is in `fmt::truncate`, not the
screenshot pipeline, and it has been there since the table engine was written.

`visible_width` skips ANSI escape sequences when measuring. `truncate` did not — it walked
every char and counted each as a column, escape bytes included. Two consequences:

- A coloured cell was cut short by the length of its own colour codes
- When the cut landed **inside** a sequence, a bare `ESC` byte was left in the output

A terminal swallows a bare ESC quietly, which is why nobody noticed. An SVG does not: the
file was malformed XML. `health`'s probe column was just the first place a long enough dim
string got cut at exactly the wrong byte.

`truncate` now copies escape sequences through whole at no width cost, and appends `\x1b[0m`
before the ellipsis when any colour was open — so the cut colour no longer bleeds into the
`…` and the gutter after it, which was a third, cosmetic effect of the same bug.

## Output before / after

Any truncated coloured cell — `ps` NAME / IMAGE / PORTS, `images` REPOSITORY / TAG,
`health` LAST PROBE — now cuts at the right visible column with colour closed. Before, the
cut was a few columns early and the colour ran on.

## Verified

- 4 new tests in `fmt`: no split escapes, visible-width counting, reset before ellipsis,
  short strings untouched — 25 total
- Screenshots regenerated; **all 26 SVGs in `docs/img` parse as XML** (before: 1 failed)
- `fmt` and `clippy -D warnings` clean

## Checklist

- [x] CHANGELOG updated
- [x] Width maths goes through `fmt::visible_width` / `truncate` — this *is* that rule being fixed

body:
## Summary
This PR implements **Phase 3 Track B (Deep Analytics & Progression Curves)** and fixes the runtime startup crash in **Expo Go on Android** introduced in Expo SDK 53.

---

### Key Features & Improvements

#### 1. Interactive SVG Progression Curves (`ProgressionCurveView.tsx`)
- **Dynamic Curves**: Smooth cubic bezier progression curves (`react-native-svg`) plotting historical performance across 4 switchable metrics:
  - **Estimated 1RM (e1RM)** (Brzycki formula)
  - **Heaviest Weight**
  - **Total Session Volume**
  - **Max Reps** (calisthenics/bodyweight rep PR tracking)
- **Haptic Scrubbing & Touch Inspection**: Interactive drag and tap gestures allow scrubbing through timeline data points with instant tactile feedback (`expo-haptics`) and floating stat callouts displaying date, value, sets, gym provenance, and PR podium tags.
- **Trajectory Summary Header**: Displays Starting Value, Current Best, Absolute Net Delta (+/-), and Percentage Growth (+X%) over the selected timeframe.
- **Bodyweight & Calibration Support**: Correctly renders bodyweight exercises (`BW` or `BW + X kg`) and handles gym provenance tags.

#### 2. Lifetime Training Overview Banner (`AnalyticsScreen.tsx`)
- Highlights all-time aggregated training statistics at the top of the Analytics screen:
  - Total Workouts Completed
  - Total Volume Lifted (formatted cleanly in kg or lb)
  - Total Sets & Reps
  - Total Training Duration (hours & minutes)
  - This Week's Pacing (workouts & volume)

#### 3. Muscle Group Breakdown & Timeframe Filters (`AnalyticsScreen.tsx`, `analytics.ts`)
- **Volume vs. Sets Toggle**: Switch muscle distribution between total volume lifted (kg / lb) and total completed set volume to provide a balanced picture across strength and endurance work.
- **Timeframe Filters**: Added time horizon selectors (`1M`, `3M`, `6M`, `1Y`, `ALL`) across both muscle distribution and progression charts.
- **Trophy Room Exercise Drill-Down**: Direct 1-tap drill-down from any trophy card into its detailed progression curve and historical log modal.

#### 4. In-Workout Exercise Detail Modal Enhancement (`ExerciseDetailModal.tsx`)
- Added integrated `ProgressionCurveView` directly into the modal for real-time progression inspection during active workouts or from the exercise library.
- Added timeframe pill toggles and Reps metric for bodyweight movements.
- Added session-level 1RM and volume summaries for each historical workout entry.

#### 5. Expo Go Android SDK 53 Notification Crash Fix (`restNotifications.native.ts`, `restNotifications.ts`)
- **Issue**: Expo SDK 53+ removed remote push notifications from Expo Go on Android. Static evaluation of `expo-notifications` unconditionally executed `DevicePushTokenAutoRegistration.fx`, which called `warnOfExpoGoPushUsage()` and threw `Error: expo-notifications: Android Push notifications functionality provided by expo-notifications was removed from Expo Go with the release of SDK 53` during bundle initialization ("runtime not ready").
- **Fix**:
  - Replaced static module import with TypeScript type-only import (`type NotificationsModule = typeof import('expo-notifications')`).
  - Implemented `isExpoGoAndroid()` check via `isRunningInExpoGo()` and `expo-constants`.
  - Added safe lazy loading `getNotificationsModule()` that cleanly bypasses `require('expo-notifications')` when running in Expo Go on Android, while retaining background system notifications in development builds (`expo run:android`), standalone builds, and iOS/Web.
  - In-app countdown timer, screen keep-awake, and 3-2-1 multi-stage haptics continue to function normally.

---

### Verification
- **Automated Tests**:
  - `npm test`: 258 passing unit tests across 58 suites (+16 new tests in `tests/unit/analytics-progression.test.ts` and `tests/unit/rest-notifications.test.ts`).
  - `npm run test:integration`: 116 passing integration tests across 7 suites.
- **TypeScript**: `npx tsc --noEmit` passed with 0 errors.
- **Roadmap**: Updated `ROADMAP.md` reflecting completed Track B milestones.

author: drawmeanelephant
body:
Implements **M51/SSH1 (#1168)** — the SSH wire codec + binary packet/stream layer (ADR 0025 D6, `docs/ssh-scoping.md` SSH1 row). Userland only: **0 new syscall slots, no kernel changes**.

## Deliverables
- `user/src/lib/ssh/wire.zig` — RFC 4251 codec: `byte`/`boolean`/`uint32`/`uint64`/`string`/`mpint`/`name-list`, bounded and allocation-free; minimal two's-complement `mpint`, strict name-list.
- `user/src/lib/ssh/packet.zig` — RFC 4253 §6 framing: `packet_length` + `padding_length` (≥4), 8-byte alignment, 35000-byte total cap; encode/decode fail closed on any malformed/over-cap input.
- `user/src/lib/ssh/stream.zig` — the stream adapter over `sys_tcp_*` (slots 30–33) behind an injected `Ops` seam (the `netauth.zig` pattern):
  - bounded caller-owned buffer, concatenates in-order ≤192-byte chunks and parses complete packets;
  - **drains the one-slot RX to exhaustion** before heavy work;
  - **paces TX to one outstanding ≤192-byte segment** (send, then drain until the injected `tx_pending` predicate clears);
  - **fails closed** (disconnect) on overflow / over-cap length / malformed padding — never truncate-and-continue.
- Class-A tests in-file (run by `zig build test`): wire round-trips, packet length/padding bounds, split-packet reassembly across many segments + one byte at a time, ring-overflow fail-closed, over-cap fail-closed, one-outstanding TX pacing, pacing give-up, transport error — all over the injected seam.
- `user/src/sshpacket.zig` (`SSHPACKET.BIN`, DSK3) + `tools/gate/specs/live-ssh-packet.spec` (class B): the deterministic VMRunner responder (`--net-tcp-respond …:packet`) pages a known 1512-byte SSH packet out as **8 paced segments**; the guest reassembles it and echoes a SHA-256, which the gate independently recomputes from the same bytes.
- `docs/gate-fleet-inventory.md` regenerated (new spec discovered).

## Honest limits (as the scoping doc requires)
- The kernel ABI exposes **no `tx_pending` read**, so production `sysTxPending` cannot observe the ACK. Production drains to exhaustion between segments and the injected seam proves the bounded one-outstanding loop; the kernel RTO remains loss recovery. Documented in `stream.zig`.
- Correctness under a dropped segment leans on the peer's TCP retransmission (a segment arriving while the one-slot RX is full is dropped and not ACKed, `kernel/src/tcp.zig:765`). The class-B responder paces one segment per ACK for exactly this reason.

## Verification (observed)
- `zig build test` rc=0
- `just verify-portable` rc=0
- `bash tools/inventory-gates.sh --check` rc=0
- `zig fmt --check user/src/lib/ssh/*.zig user/src/sshpacket.zig build.zig` rc=0
- `just gate live-ssh-packet` — **PASS** on VZ (8/8 chunks, digest match)
- Regression: `just gate live-fetch` PASS (default `--net-tcp-respond` unchanged), `just gate live-fs` PASS (boot default unchanged)
- Note: `just gate live-args` fails **identically on pristine `origin/main`** (verified in a separate worktree) — a pre-existing timing flake, not from this change.

Closes #1168. Umbrella #1164 stays open.
