author: ibaifernandez
body:
**Tarjeta `9dbfbd0d`** (`urgent`). Commit `907c3bc`.

## ⚠️ Lo primero: no eran cuatro ubicaciones, eran once

Medido sobre el árbol versionado antes de tocar nada:

| dónde | |
|---|---|
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `PERMISSIONS.md`, `PRD.md`, `SECURITY.md` | documentación viva |
| `docs/BACKLOG.md` ×2 | una en prosa y **una dentro de una consulta SQL** |
| `docs/INCIDENTS.md` ×2 | una de dominio personal y **otra de un buzón distinto** |
| `docs/CHANGELOG.md` | registro histórico |
| `docs/audits/…/REPORT.md` · `findings.json` | los dos artefactos de la auditoría |
| **`scripts/rail-blindspot.sh`** | **tecleada dentro de un guardián** |
| **`server/tests/…assignee-resolution.test.js`** | **fixture de test con la dirección real** |

Y al retirar la declaración aparecieron **dos más** en el dominio legado, que hasta entonces quedaban tapadas.

## ⚠️ Y el guardián no era el que dice la tarjeta, ni su alcance era el problema

La tarjeta señala a `docs/…`/`scripts/docs-guard.sh` y dice que *«solo mira dos ficheros»*. Medido:

- **`docs-guard` no tiene ninguna regla de correo.** Sus reglas son `V1 V2 V3` y sus cruces `PORTS LINKS ELIDED ATLAS`. Nunca miró esto.
- **Quien vigila esto es `email-guard`**, y **ya deriva su alcance de todos los ficheros versionados** — hoy mira 279. La tercera tarea de la tarjeta *(«que el guardián derive su alcance de los ficheros versionados»)* **ya estaba hecha**.

Entonces, ¿por qué estaba verde con once direcciones dentro?

**Porque `ibaifernandez.com` y `lfi.la` estaban declarados como dominios ENTEROS**, con su motivo escrito al lado:

> «publicar su propia dirección es decisión suya y ya la tomó»

**Un `dominio` abre ese dominio para siempre y para cualquier dirección futura.** Así que cada vez que alguien escribía la dirección en un documento nuevo, **entraba en silencio y el guardián seguía verde**. El defecto era **la declaración, no la cobertura** — y eso cambia el arreglo: no había que ensanchar nada, había que retirar dos líneas.

Esa declaración no era un descuido: era **una decisión con su razonamiento escrito**, coherente con `CLAUDE.md`, que distingue entre la dirección de quien publicó el repositorio y la de quien no. **El Operador tomó la decisión contraria el 2026-09-12**, y es la que se aplica aquí. Lo digo porque quien lea el fichero verá desaparecer un motivo bien argumentado, y merece saber que se retiró a sabiendas.

## Qué se hizo con el dato

**El custodio es la tabla `users`.** Los documentos pasan a nombrar **el papel** —«el operador humano», «la cuenta superadmin»—, que es lo que decían de verdad.

**Los registros históricos no se borran: se redactan.** Incidencias, changelog e informe de auditoría narran hechos; quitarles la línea entera habría perdido el hecho. Se sustituye el dato y se conserva la frase.

**Y el guardián del riel deja de identificar al dueño por su dirección y lo hace por su papel:**

```sql
-- antes:  x.email = '<la dirección personal>'
-- ahora:  x.role = 'superadmin' AND x.email <> '<la cuenta de rol del riel>'
```

Era lo que la condición quería decir: **el dueño no es esa dirección, es quien tiene ese papel.** Consecuencia declarada en el propio fichero: **si algún día hay un segundo superadmin humano, el alcance se ensancha solo.** Es correcto —serían dos dueños de verdad— pero conviene saberlo antes, no descubrirlo por un rojo. `RAIL_SCOPE_OWNER` sigue existiendo para fijar una dirección concreta al depurar.

## Medido en las dos direcciones

```
árbol versionado          →  0 direcciones sin declarar  (279 ficheros)
la dirección en un fichero nuevo cualquiera  →  email-guard exit 1
```

**La segunda mitad es la condición de cierre de la tarjeta, y antes no se cumplía.**

Y hay **caso propio** para que no se reabra, con **tres mutaciones rojas**:

| mutación | |
|---|---|
| se reabre el dominio personal *(el defecto)* | 🔴 |
| se reabre el dominio legado | 🔴 |
| el fichero de declaraciones queda vacío | 🔴 |

La tercera existe porque un caso que solo comprueba **ausencias** se satisface no leyendo nada.

## 🔻 Queda una ubicación sin tocar, y es decisión tuya

**`docs/legal/dpas/railway-dpa-2026-05-27.pdf` contiene la dirección personal cuatro veces.**

No lo toco, y no es pereza:

- Es un **PDF firmado**, archivado como prueba de un acuerdo de encargado. **Redactarlo altera un artefacto legal**; **retirarlo del árbol** quita esa prueba de donde el registro la busca.
- **`email-guard` no lo ve.** Salta los binarios al no poder decodificarlos, y lo declara en su cabecera. **Su verde no cubre este fichero**, y por eso lo digo aquí en vez de dejar que el verde lo tape.
- **Los otros seis acuerdos archivados están limpios**: comprobados uno a uno.

## Batería

**44 suites / 411 pruebas** verdes · `docs`, `changelog`, `contract`, `pipefail`, `correo-cero`, `email`, `ci-cableado`, `base-consultable` OK · sellos de `email-guard` (17) y `rail-blindspot` (26) verdes.

`[obrero · las once ubicaciones y las dos del dominio legado, medidas por mí sobre el árbol versionado; la ausencia de regla de correo en docs-guard, leída en su lista de reglas; el motivo de que email-guard estuviera verde, leído en su fichero de declaraciones; tres mutaciones y la contraprueba del guardián, medidas por mí; el contenido del PDF, extraído y contado por mí — los otros seis, también]`

author: patriotnewsactivism
body:
Every CI job on `main` has failed since 2026-09-11 21:10 (`0b94c6c`), and the deploy has been skipped with it.

```
[ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE] Cannot install with "frozen-lockfile" because
pnpm-lock.yaml is not up to date with <ROOT>/packages/api-server/package.json
  Failure reason:
  specifiers in the lockfile don't match specifiers in package.json
```

`84e0c04` added a `test` script and `vitest: catalog:` to `packages/api-server/package.json` without regenerating the lockfile. The lockfile's last touch was `e3e93f1`, which predates that commit.

## Why this is worse than a red branch

`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` is the **first step of all three CI jobs**, so each died before running anything:

| Job | Result |
|---|---|
| `production-checks` | ❌ install — typecheck, all 30 agent guards, dashboard build all **skipped** |
| `mobile-layout` | ❌ install — dashboard build, Chromium, overflow check all **skipped** |
| `convex-experimental` | ❌ install — typecheck **skipped** |

And `Deploy to Cloud Run` runs on `workflow_run` gated on CI, so it has been **skipped too**. APEX has not deployed since `d2675ba` on 2026-09-10.

That has a concrete consequence: **PR #136 is merged but not live.** The `workforce_paused` health state that makes a stalled workforce visible is sitting in `main` undeployed, which is why `/health` still reports the old values.

## The fix

`vitest ^3.2.4` is already in the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` catalog, so the specifier was always valid — only the lockfile was stale. Regenerated with `pnpm install --lockfile-only`.

No `package.json` touched. The supply-chain settings are untouched: `minimumReleaseAge: 1440` and the `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` allowlist are unchanged, and the regenerated lockfile passes the policy check at 366 entries — the same count CI reported immediately before the install step failed.

## Verification

- Reproduced `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE` locally first, then confirmed `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` succeeds after the fix
- `pnpm run typecheck:production` — clean across all packages
- **All 30 deterministic agent guards pass**, invoked the way CI does

One note on that last point, because it burned me first time through: seven guards read `process.env.GITHUB_WORKSPACE ?? process.cwd()`, and `pnpm --filter <pkg> exec` sets cwd to the *package* directory. Run without `GITHUB_WORKSPACE`, they resolve `packages/core/packages/core/src/llm-client.ts` and fail with ENOENT — seven convincing-looking false failures. With it set as CI sets it, all pass. Worth knowing before anyone debugs a "broken guard" locally.

`verify-mobile-overflow.mjs` gets through its static half here ("view coverage: all 17 nav views are checked") and then needs the Chromium build CI installs with `playwright install --with-deps`. This sandbox doesn't have that exact headless-shell revision, so I'm reporting it as **unverified locally**, not as passing.

## After this merges

The deploy should run for the first time since 09-10, and `/health` should begin reporting `workforce_paused` when the workspace allowance is exhausted — the behaviour #136 added.

author: seyhachim
body:
I am starting a new feature/bug fix in:

**Repository:** `seyhachim/dse-program-management-system`

**GitHub issue:** `#1083`

Closes #1083

Inspect the current GitHub repository and the issue before making recommendations.

## Goal

Implement #1083 using the smallest maintainable change that fits the existing architecture: a safe **local-development only** workflow that lets a chosen email authenticate as the seeded Student Portal persona without creating or rewriting academic records.

## First: inspect, don't code

Before writing code:

1. [x] Read #1083, `AGENTS.md`, and the root `pull_request_template.md`.
2. [x] Inspected the current implementation on `main`, including `gen-token.ts`, auth mode/token verification, Prisma User/Role/UserRoleAssignment/Student models, seed behavior, and Student Portal lookup.
3. [x] Identified the existing dev-token path and seeded Student Portal fixture.
4. [x] Identified the missing pieces: targeted email selection, a guarded persona setup command, and session-role consistency for `/api/auth/me` when an existing multi-role User is used as a student persona.
5. [x] Traced the complete affected flow: Prisma/database, shared types, backend auth/service/router, frontend token consumption/navigation, authorization, and tests.
6. [x] Checked plugin impact; only the existing auth plugin `/me` response needs a small session-role scoping fix.
7. [x] Preserved plugin-registry boundaries; no new cross-plugin imports.
8. [x] Confirmed no migration is required and academic fixture data can be reused safely.
9. [x] Added fail-closed handling for auth mode, missing JWT signing configuration, invalid email, fixture state, and existing Student-link collisions.
10. [x] Reviewed security/permission implications and addressed Codex review findings before merge.

## Give me an implementation plan

### Summary

- Extend `gen-token` with optional `--email` targeting while still requiring the requested DB role assignment.
- Add `dev:student-persona`, hard-blocked unless `AUTH_MODE=dev` and `JWT_SECRET` is configured before any database write.
- Re-link only the seeded Student fixture's `userId` to the selected dev User and ensure that User has the programme-scoped `student` role.
- Preserve all pre-existing User roles, but make `/api/auth/me` reflect the authenticated session roles so a student-only dev token does not expose staff navigation/permissions.
- Mint a student-only dev JWT for the selected email.
- Keep personal emails runtime-only and out of Git.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] `bun run gen-token --role student --email <email>` targets a specific existing user.
- [x] Omitting `--email` preserves the existing first-user-by-role behavior.
- [x] `bun run dev:student-persona --email <email>` exists.
- [x] Student persona command refuses any auth mode other than explicit `AUTH_MODE=dev`.
- [x] Student persona command refuses to write when `JWT_SECRET` is missing.
- [x] No personal target email is committed.
- [x] Existing seeded Student academic fixture is reused; no synthetic Student ID/enrollment/result records are created.
- [x] Target User receives the scoped `student` role without deleting existing roles.
- [x] A target User already linked to a different Student profile fails closed.
- [x] Missing/inactive source Student fixture fails closed.
- [x] Successful setup prints a student-only JWT for `NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_TOKEN`.
- [x] `/api/auth/me` reports the authenticated persona roles, keeping frontend navigation/permissions aligned with backend authorization.
- [x] No Supabase Auth, production academic, CourseSpec, curriculum, result, attendance, or QA/SAR mutation path is introduced.
- [x] Focused parsing, safety, and session-role tests added.
- [x] Exact-head CI verification is green.

### Files that need changes

- `apps/backend/package.json`
- `apps/backend/scripts/dev-auth-cli.ts`
- `apps/backend/scripts/dev-auth-cli.test.ts`
- `apps/backend/scripts/dev-student-persona.ts`
- `apps/backend/scripts/gen-token.ts`
- `apps/backend/src/plugins/auth/me-role-scope.test.ts`
- `apps/backend/src/plugins/auth/router.ts`
- `apps/backend/src/plugins/auth/service.ts`

### Database changes

No schema or migration changes. The dev-only command performs one controlled local transaction: ensure a dev User, ensure its existing `student` role assignment is programme-scoped, and update the seeded fixture's `Student.userId`. It does **not** create or rewrite enrollment, attendance, results, CourseSpecs, curriculum, or QA records.

### Shared contract changes

None. `/api/auth/me` keeps the existing response shape; it now scopes the returned roles/permissions to the authenticated session roles when supplied.

### Backend changes

- New reusable CLI parsing/safety helpers.
- Email-targeted dev token generation.
- New dev Student persona setup command.
- Small auth-service/router change so `/me` uses authenticated session roles; Supabase behavior remains unchanged because middleware already resolves those roles from the DB.

### Frontend changes

None. The emitted token continues to use the existing `NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_TOKEN` local-development path. The existing frontend receives a correctly student-scoped `/me` response when using the persona token.

### Authorization changes

No permission is added or bypassed. `gen-token --email` still requires the requested DB role assignment. The persona command adds the existing programme-scoped `student` role only in explicit dev auth mode and emits a token containing only `student`. `/me` now reports that session scope instead of broadening it back to every role stored on a multi-role User.

### Edge cases

- `AUTH_MODE=supabase` or unset -> refused before any DB query/write.
- missing/empty `JWT_SECRET` -> refused before any DB query/write.
- invalid/missing email -> refused.
- source Student fixture missing/inactive -> refused.
- target User already linked to another Student -> refused with no write.
- target User already has admin/lecturer roles -> those DB roles remain, but the student-only dev session exposes only student navigation/permissions.
- rerunning seed restores the canonical `student@dse.dev` -> Ada link; rerun the persona command afterward when needed.
- Student Portal continues to display the seeded fixture's canonical Student identity/email; the selected email is the authenticated dev User identity. This deliberately avoids rewriting seed identity data.

### Test plan

Focused:

```powershell
bun test "apps/backend/scripts/dev-auth-cli.test.ts"
bun test "apps/backend/src/plugins/auth/me-role-scope.test.ts"
```

Canonical repository gate:

```powershell
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bunx prisma validate --schema apps/backend/prisma/schema.prisma
bun run typecheck
bun run lint
bun run test
bun run test:backend
bun run build
```

CI also runs the fresh-database migration/seed/security verifier and isolated backend authorization integration suite.

### Recommended implementation order

1. [x] Inspect repo/issue/auth/seed/Student Portal flow.
2. [x] Create #1083 and branch from current `main`.
3. [x] Add reusable CLI parsing and dev-only guards.
4. [x] Add email-targeted token generation.
5. [x] Add transactional dev Student persona setup.
6. [x] Add focused tests and package script.
7. [x] Review exact-head CI and all review threads; address both Codex findings.
8. [x] Reconcile final PR against #1083 and the root PR template; merge-ready.

### Existing problems discovered

- **P1 — fixed:** `gen-token` could not select a specific dev user by email.
- **P1 — fixed:** no guarded workflow existed to reuse the representative seeded Student Portal fixture with a developer login identity.
- **P1 — fixed during review:** a multi-role target User could receive a student-only token while `/api/auth/me` re-expanded the UI to all DB roles, creating frontend/backend permission mismatch.
- **P1 — fixed during review:** missing `JWT_SECRET` could have failed token minting after persona DB changes; signing pr

author: keerhee
body:
## 요약

2026-06-28 과 07-02 사이 **나흘 만에 1위 국가가 미국에서 베트남으로 바뀌고 글로벌 지수가 32.5 → 40.0 으로 올랐습니다.** 한류가 변해서가 아니라 수집 실패가 조용히 통과했기 때문입니다.

원인 셋이 겹쳤고, 셋 다 고쳤습니다. 덧붙여 L1 경제층을 **키가 필요 없는 UN Comtrade** 로 옮겨 `REVIEW_REQUEST.md` 7번(콘텐츠 분야 국가별 L1 부재)의 보완책을 일부 확보했습니다.

## 무엇이 일어났나

```
2026-06-28  kfood L1_norm 고유값 15개   US=100.0  VN=10.8
2026-07-02  kfood L1_norm 고유값  1개   US= 50.0  VN=50.0
```

1. **기준월** — 관세청 수집이 직전월을 요청합니다. 무역통계는 익월 중순 공표라 07-02 실행(→2026-06)은 아직 없는 달을 물었습니다. 06-28 실행(→2026-05)은 19억 달러가 정상 수집됐습니다.
2. **빈 응답** — 파서가 `<expDlr>` 태그가 하나도 없어도 `0.0` 을 돌려주고 오류 플래그를 붙이지 않았습니다. 45행이 전부 0 이 되었는데 `customs_error` 는 비어 있었습니다.
3. **상수 정규화** — `minmax()` 가 "모든 값이 같으면 50.0" 이라 K푸드·패션·뷰티 L1 이 전 국가 50.0 상수가 됐습니다. 미국이 잃은 50점이 순위를 뒤집었습니다.

그런데 같은 날 산출된 `kwci_latest.json` 에는 이렇게 적혀 있습니다.

> "L1은 국가별 수집분(관세청 푸드·패션·뷰티, KTO 관광)이 DSI에 실제 반영됨"

반영되지 않았습니다. 상수가 들어갔고, 그 파일이 배포됐습니다.

## 변경 내용

### `collectors.py`
- 관세청 기준월을 **2개월 전**으로. 파서가 `(합계, 항목수, 결과코드)` 반환
- 항목 0건이면 `0` 이 아니라 **`NaN`**. 전량 실패면 `RuntimeError`
- **KTO 의 조용한 샘플 대체 제거.** 매칭 실패 시 국가명을 로그에 남기고 예외를 던집니다. 기존에는 `sample_kto` 합성값이 K관광 L1(가중 0.5)에 그대로 들어가고 있었습니다
- **YouTube `search.list` 예산 상한 + 7일 캐시.** `search.list` 는 100 units 라 15×8 조합이 전부 검색으로 빠지면 12,000 units 로 한도(10,000)를 넘습니다. 실제로 06-28 은 84건, 07-02 는 69건이 `search_http_429` 였고 120행 중 유효값은 28·43행뿐이었습니다
- **`collect_comtrade_export()` 신규**

### `processor.py`
- `minmax` 가 상수·단일 관측이면 **`NaN` 반환**. 정보가 없으면 점수도 없어야 합니다
- `youtube`/`trends` 의 **`fillna(0)` 제거.** 0 은 "관심 없음"이 아니라 대개 매칭 실패이고, 0 으로 채우면 정규화가 척도의 min 을 측정 인공물에 내줍니다
- L3 결합에서 결측 신호를 빼고 **남은 가중으로 재정규화**
- **`validate_coverage()` 신규** — 경제층 커버리지가 기준 미달이면 산출을 중단합니다. 결측을 결측으로 표시하는 것만으로는 부족합니다. DSI 가 없는 층위를 빼고 재정규화하므로 **L1 이 통째로 비어도 지수는 계속 나오고**, 다만 그 점수는 "절반이 경제"가 아니라 100% 관심 신호로 만든 다른 자입니다

### `config.py` · `run_pipeline.py`
- L1 1차 경로를 **UN Comtrade** 로. 관세청은 키가 있을 때만 교차검증용

## REVIEW_REQUEST 항목과의 연결

**7번 — 콘텐츠 4분야의 국가별 L1 부재, 보완책?**

일부 확보했습니다. 실물 음반·영상매체는 재화라 HS 코드가 있습니다.

| | 이전 | 이후 |
|---|---:|---:|
| 국가별 L1 가중 커버리지 | 0.28 | **0.48** |
| 덮는 도메인 | 푸드·패션·뷰티 | + **K팝**(가중 0.20) |

다만 한계가 분명합니다.
- K팝 L1 은 **실물매체 채널**입니다. 스트리밍·공연·MD 는 재화가 아니라 HS 코드가 없습니다
- **K영상·K게임·K웹툰(가중 합 0.44)은 여전히 불가능합니다.** 서비스 수출이라 HS 코드 자체가 존재하지 않습니다. KTO 가 실측으로 들어오면 상한은 0.56 이고, 그것이 이 설계의 천장입니다
- 즉 **"DSI 의 절반이 경제"는 8개 도메인 중 5개에서만 성립합니다**

**5번 — Min-Max 단일창 정규화의 극단값 취약성**

취약성이 가설이 아니라 실제 사고로 나타났습니다. 다만 발현 형태가 극단값이 아니라 **반대쪽, 분산 0** 이었습니다. 상수 입력에 50.0 을 주는 처리가 정보 없는 값을 실측처럼 흘려보냅니다.

**10번 — verified-fixed 폴백이 신뢰성·재현성에 주는 영향**

`sample_kto` 와 `sample_baseline` 이 지수에 그대로 들어가고 있었습니다. 설문은 L3 하위가중 0.40 을 차지합니다. 이번 PR 은 KTO 폴백을 제거했습니다. `survey_baseline` 은 대체 자료가 없어 그대로 두었으나, 합성이라는 사실이 산출물에 표시되지 않는 점은 별도 논의가 필요합니다.

## 검증

**① 기존 준거를 독립 통계와 대조** — 12개국 × 59~60개월

| 도메인 | 국가 배분 상관 | Δ12 동행 평균 | 양의 상관 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| K뷰티 | +1.000 | +0.985 | 12/12 |
| K패션 | +0.990 | +0.546 | 12/12 |
| K푸드 | +0.987 | +0.602 | 12/12 |
| K팝 | +0.890 | +0.716 | 12/12 |

48개 국가-도메인 조합 전부에서 시간 동행성이 양수입니다. 다만 **수준은 다릅니다** — K팝에서 중국 비중을 11.7% 대 25.7% 로 과소, 일본을 46.0% 대 35.4% 로 과대 잡습니다.

**② 고장난 자료 재통과** — 07-02 자료를 고친 파이프라인에 넣으면

| | 이전 | 이후 |
|---|---|---|
| `minmax([0]*15)` | 전부 50.0 | **전부 NaN** |
| K푸드 L1 유효값 | 15/15 | **0/15** |
| 커버리지 검사 | (없음) | **산출 거부** |

**③ 키 없이 전체 파이프라인 완주**

```
[comtrade] 최신 공표월 = 202512 · 유효 관측 52/60
US 77.28 · CN 65.60 · JP 59.76
```

## 주의사항

**HS 8523 을 4자리로 쓰면 안 됩니다.** SSD·메모리카드가 대부분이라 2023년 최대 파트너 한 곳에만 60억 달러가 잡힙니다. `지표마스터테이블` 의 "음반 수출액(HS 8523)" 은 6자리 **852349**(광학 기록 매체)로 읽어야 합니다. 이 경고를 `config.py` 주석에 남겼습니다.

## 호환성

- 기존 `collect_customs_export()` 는 그대로 두었습니다(교차검증용)
- 산출물 스키마 변경 없음
- 커버리지 기준은 `KWCI_L1_COVERAGE_MIN` 환경변수로 조정 가능(기본 0.46)

author: k0b3n4irb
body:
Reported from the GUI: a stutter in Kirby Super Star's intro, right before the star transition.

The emulation was not at fault — the pacing log held a steady 60-61 fps with no audio underrun. The game force-blanks for **31 consecutive frames** there, and the GUI holds the last picture for up to 8 of them before publishing black. So the display froze on the old picture for ~130 ms, then went black, then the new scene arrived.

Hardware blanks the screen the moment a game sets INIDISP bit 7, so every held frame is a picture the console does not show. At two frames the freeze is ~33 ms — below what an eye catches — and an isolated blank frame is still absorbed, which is what the hold exists for.

## Why two is safe

The hold was added for double-buffered Super FX titles that blank roughly every other frame. Measured before lowering it: across Star Fox, Doom and Stunt Race FX, in the intro and in gameplay, `frame_showed_content` never reported a whole-frame blank. The per-frame content latch (added later) counts a frame with *any* un-blanked line as content, so the alternating case no longer reaches this policy at all.

## Not a defect: the green frames

The same sequence shows large green frames with stars. Those are authentic: Mesen2 renders that transition identically — a **pixel-exact match** against luna's frame, two frames of boot offset apart — and the game itself asks for OBJ-only output (`$212C = $10` every frame) with the backdrop showing through.

Confirmed in the GUI after the change.

author: profmohit-edu
body:
## Description

`syncUserRepositories()` can complete a synchronization run while reporting that one or more repository writes failed. However, `singleRepositorySyncResponse()` currently ignores the `failed` count when deriving the API response status.

As a result, a run such as:

`{ synced: 7, failed: 2, hasInstallation: true }`

can be reported as `success: true` with `status: "COMPLETED"`, even though two repository writes did not complete.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactoring
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] CI/CD changes
- [ ] Security fix

## What changed

- Added a `PARTIAL` status when one or more repository writes fail.
- Partial synchronization now returns `success: false`.
- Explicit synchronization errors continue to return `FAILED`.
- Missing GitHub App installations continue to return `NO_INSTALLATION`.
- Runs without write failures continue to return `COMPLETED`.
- Intentionally skipped repositories are not treated as failures.
- Added regression tests for partial synchronization and status precedence.

## Motivation / Background

The API response should accurately represent the result of the synchronization operation. Reporting `COMPLETED` when repository writes have failed can cause callers to treat incomplete synchronization as successful.

This change only corrects response classification; it does not modify repository ownership, synchronization, or persistence behavior.

## How to Test

The unit tests cover:

- successful synchronization with no write failures;
- partial synchronization with both successful and failed writes;
- explicit error precedence when failures are also present;
- skipped repositories without write failures;
- existing `FAILED`, `NO_INSTALLATION`, and `COMPLETED` behavior.

## Screenshots

Not applicable — this is an API response classification fix.

## Checklist

- [x] Changes are focused on a single correctness issue
- [x] Regression tests added
- [x] Existing response behavior preserved where appropriate
- [x] No unrelated refactoring included

body:
Upstream issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/31240

Mirror issue: https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/issues/2270

## Summary

The prepared `main` base already contains the narrowly proposed fix: `get_processor()` resolves a non-`None` `model_name` through `resolve_runai_obj_uri()` before calling `AutoConfig.from_pretrained()`. It also already contains an issue-specific regression test. No additional source change was justified.

This PR records the investigation, structured result, and raw evidence. A controlled failing-before check temporarily removed only the existing two-line `model_name` resolution block. The focused regression then failed and showed the raw `s3://bucket/model` reaching `AutoConfig`; restoring the prepared base made it pass.

## Reproduction and validation

```bash
/tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-a5ad9a42af80/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/utils/test_hf_transformers.py::TestGetProcessor::test_resolves_model_name_before_loading_config \
  test/registered/unit/test_runai_utils.py
```

Result: 10 passed. The boundary tests cover S3, Google Storage, Azure, case variants, local and relative paths, Hugging Face repository IDs, unsupported schemes, `pathlib.Path`, and cache-path determinism.

## Limitations

No object-store credentials or endpoint and no Qwen3.5 weights were supplied, so this does not claim a real RunAI object-store download, full multimodal server startup, or semantic inference. The defect is CPU-side path routing before model/GPU execution; no unrelated GPU smoke was used as evidence. The prepared checkout is a grafted one-commit snapshot, so the earlier commit introducing the already-present fix could not be attributed from local history.

body: ## Summary This PR adds an HTTP API endpoint for creating users, following the established hexagonal architecture pattern, **with complete end-to-end wiring**. **Depends on:** #1 (UserService must be merged first) ## Changes ### View DTOs (`view-dtos/`) - **`user.go`**: Request and response DTOs - `CreateUserRequest` with `name` field - `UserResponse` with `ID` and `Name` fields - `UserFromDomain` mapper function - **`user_test.go`**: Unit test for domain-to-DTO mapper ### Handler (`handlers/`) - **`create_user.go`**: HTTP handler factory - Accepts `UserService` interface - Decodes `CreateUserRequest` from JSON body - Calls `userService.CreateUser(name)` - Returns 201 Created with `UserResponse` - Returns 400 Bad Request for invalid JSON or domain errors - **`create_user_test.go`**: Handler test using `httptest` - Mocks `UserService` interface - Asserts correct service method call - Asserts HTTP status and response mapping ### Adapter (`adapter/`) - **`user_repository.go`**: SQLite implementation of `UserRepository` - `Save(user)` method persists users to SQLite - Uses upsert pattern (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT) - **`user_repository_test.go`**: Adapter persistence test - Verifies user is saved to database correctly ### SQLite Schema (`sqlite/`) - **`sqlite.go`**: Added users table migration - `id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL` - `name TEXT NOT NULL` ### Bootstrap (`bootstrap/`) - **`bootstrap.go`**: Added `NewUserService` factory - Wires `SQLiteUserRepository` with event publisher - Same pattern as `NewListService` and `NewItemService` ### Route Registration (`cmd/server/`) - **`server.go`**: Added `userService` parameter to `newAPIServer` - Registered `POST /api/users` route - **`main.go`**: Wire `userService` and pass to `newAPIServer` - Creates `userService` via bootstrap - Fully functional endpoint ready to use ### Generated Files - **`api-types/index.ts`**: TypeScript types for `CreateUserRequest` and `UserResponse` ### Manual Testing - **`bruno/api/Create User.bru`**: Bruno HTTP request for manual testing - POST to `{{apiBase}}/api/users` - Example body: `{"name": "Alex"}` ## Testing All tests passing: - ✅ Handler test: `TestCreateUser` - ✅ DTO test: `TestUserFromDomain` - ✅ Adapter test: `TestSQLiteUserRepository_Save` - ✅ All personal-productivity-context tests: `go test ./internal/personal-productivity-context/...` - ✅ CI checks passing ## CI Fix **Root Cause:** Initial PR updated `newAPIServer` signature to require `userService` but didn't wire it in `main.go`, causing build failures. **Resolution:** Implemented complete stack: 1. Added SQLite users table migration 2. Created `SQLiteUserRepository` adapter 3. Added `NewUserService` bootstrap factory 4. Wired everything in `main.go` The endpoint is now fully functional end-to-end with persistence. ## TDD Process Followed strict TDD workflow: 1. ✅ **Red**: Created failing test with stub handler returning 501 2. ✅ **Green**: Implemented handler to decode request, call service, return response 3. ✅ **Verified**: All tests passing + CI green ## Architecture ``` HTTP POST /api/users → CreateUser handler → UserService.CreateUser → domain.CreateUser ↓ ↓ ↓ CreateUserRequest UserRepository.Save (ID: "US_...", Name) ↓ ↓ ↓ UserResponse ← mapper ← domain.User SQLiteUserRepository → SQLite users table ↓ EventPublisher.Publish ``` ## Hexagonal Architecture Compliance - ✅ Handler depends only on `UserService` interface (application layer) - ✅ Application layer depends only on `UserRepository` port interface - ✅ Adapter implements repository port and depends on SQLite infrastructure - ✅ Uses named DTOs (not inline structs) - ✅ No domain validation in handler (delegates to service/domain) - ✅ Proper HTTP status codes (201 Created, 400 Bad Request) - ✅ TypeScript types generated for UI consumption - ✅ Complete separation of concerns across all layers

body:
Merges feat/app-preview into main and finishes the flow on top of it.

Landing

- Copy rewritten in short plain sentences: what you get, who has to trust whom, where Attestcoin and the zero-knowledge proof do their work, and a visible way in for people without stablecoin pay (demo faucet). Footer tagline removed.

Wallet
- Only the wallet linked to the login is used. Signatures go through that wallet's own provider with a timeout, instead of a library call that never settled when the address was not connected.

Review

Statement

Borrow

- Disbursement verifies the statement subject matches the authenticated wallet.


Tested
- Existing wallet path end to end on the deployed contracts (statement orru:cred:576b974c, 900 mUSDC drawn).
- Fresh wallet through the demo faucet to a statement and a draw.
- Public verification without a wallet.

author: jdx
body:
## What this enables

Tools provided by installed vfox backend plugins now show up where users look for tools:

```console
$ mise search formatter
biome
my-ecosystem:fast-formatter

$ mise use my-ecosystem:fast-formatter@latest
```

The same results are available to shell completion. Running `mise use` with no arguments also includes tools from plugins that publish a finite catalog.

This supports two different ecosystem shapes:

- A plugin for a small, known catalog can implement `BackendListTools` once and return every tool it provides.
- A plugin for a very large ecosystem, such as npm, can implement `BackendSearchTools`. Mise passes the user's current query to the plugin, so typing `mise search eslint` or completing `mise use npm:esl…` searches for matching packages without downloading or enumerating all of npm.
- A plugin may implement both: a curated list for browsing and dynamic search for the long tail.

Results are namespaced as `<plugin>:<tool>`, so they can be selected and installed without colliding with mise's built-in registry. `mise registry` remains registry-only.

## Behavior and resilience

- `mise search <query>` merges matching registry entries with results from installed plugins.
- A prefixed query such as `npm:eslint` is routed only to that plugin and is passed to it as `eslint`.
- Independent plugins are queried concurrently with a fixed concurrency limit.
- List and query results are cached separately; timeouts can fall back to stale cache data so one slow plugin does not make discovery unusable.
- Invalid or unavailable plugin results are ignored rather than offered as broken selections.

This closes the implementation gap discussed in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13109.

## Plugin API

Adds two optional vfox backend hooks:

- `BackendListTools(ctx)` for bounded catalogs
- `BackendSearchTools({ query })` for query-driven discovery

Both return tool names with optional descriptions. Existing plugins remain compatible and do not need to implement either hook.

## Contributor guidance

Updates `AGENTS.md` to require PR descriptions to lead with user impact and include concrete examples and material tradeoffs for user-facing changes.

## Testing

- `mise --cd crates/vfox run test backend_`
- `mise exec -- cargo test --all-features tool_catalog`
- `mise run test:e2e e2e/plugins/test_backend_plugin_discovery e2e/cli/test_search`
- `mise run render`
- `mise run lint-fix`
- `mise --cd crates/vfox run lint`
- `git diff --check`

author: mlmariss
body:
Six faults — five in the build overview, one in what a build starts as.

### 1 — One row per ability, at the level you hold

The conditional list was built by walking every owned level, so a level-3 Artery Strike listed 560%, 680% *and* 800% as though you had all three.

An ability's level text is a complete restatement — level 3 **is** the ability — so only the level you hold is listed. A perk's levels are riders that stack, and two *different* riders are both still true, so those both stand; only a restatement of the same rider collapses. That is what Fleet of Foot's two separate riders needed and Fate's Favour's 6/12/18 did not.

Maxed Swordmastery: 40-odd rows → **22**.

### 2 — Criticals never counted

`readEffect` knew two shapes: a signed delta (`+25% max stamina`) and a leading number (`2 Slots available`). The game writes a chance with the number **in the middle** — `Weapon Critical Hit : 6% chance` — which reached neither, so every crit chance in the game fell out of the totals and into the conditional text list.

Thirteen lines, across Fate's Favour, Clawpierce, Evil Eye, Potent Blood, Unholy Fervour and Forager. They total now, and the per-perk "highest level wins" rule already in place means a maxed Fate's Favour reads `Weapon Critical Hit chance 18%`, not 36%.

### 3 — Totals were adding up things that are not the same number

Three perks reduce "Cooldowns" and three more add "Slots available", each scoped by its **own effect line** to one tree's abilities:

| Tree | Perk | Its effect says |
|---|---|---|
| Witchcraft | Aether Flow | Reduces **Witchcraft** Ability Cooldown |
| Swordmastery | Restless Blade | Reduces Cooldowns of **Swordmastery** Abilities |
| Vampirism | Endless Ferocity | Reduces Cooldowns of **Vampiric** Abilities |

The level text drops that scope, so all three keyed to one label and were **summed**: three unrelated −10/−20/−20 reductions became `Cooldowns -50%`, and three separate four-slot pools became `Slots available 12`. Same for `Cooldowns on Critical Hits`, and for `Damage`/`Armour` across trees.

The scope is in the perk's own effect, so it is read from there and the rows stay apart:

```
Cooldowns (Swordmastery abilities)                -20%
Cooldowns on Critical Hits (Swordmastery ab.)      -5%
Slots available (Swordmastery abilities)             4
```

### 4 — A stat label is a name, not a sentence

The test for a label was "contains no digits", which let whole sentences through. Omniblock's last level printed

> Stamina cost. Directional Block works like Omniblock if wrong direction is chosen — **-40%**

as a stat name, filed under **Defence**, while the `Stamina cost` it should have joined sat under **Resources**. A label is now one clause of at most six words. The seven lines that fail that test are genuinely conditional prose (`per enemy affected`, `for each soul compelled`, `You can run while Encumbered`) and are listed as text.

### 5 — The three long lists fold and scroll

Conditional effects, manuals and phials run to dozens of rows each (22 and 63 on a maxed tree) and sat fully laid out *below* the totals that are the reason to open the overview at all.

Each is a `<details>` carrying its count, closed by default, opening into a scroller of its own with a heading that sticks to the top of the overview's own scroller — so reaching the fifteenth conditional effect never means scrolling twenty-two manuals past first, and opening one cannot push the overview off its column.

Which ones are open is remembered. The overview body is rewritten on every click anywhere in the planner, and a section that snapped shut each time would be useless.

The perk name is off the rows: every one of these is something the tree gives you, and the name was the widest thing in the list.

### 6 — The story's abilities are not an offer

Five abilities are handed over, not bought, and there is no build in which you do not have them. The planner now opens with all five at level 1 (*Astral Communion*, *Burning Blood*, *Compel Soul*, *Dirty Trick*, *Voracious Bite*).

- **Reset** puts them back rather than clearing them.
- **Refund** refuses level 1: *"The story grants level 1 outright — it cannot be refunded."*
- Their level-1 gate no longer applies, so the two manual-gated ones (Dirty Trick, Burning Blood) stopped counting as manuals to go and find, and turning "Manuals found" off no longer strips them.
- A build link records only the levels you bought on top and re-seeds the rest, so **existing links keep working**.

### Verification

Driven in Chromium at 1600, 1280 and 420 wide with Swordmastery maxed:

- the three scoped rows read separately, crit chance totals at 18%,
- the conditional list is 22 rows, no perk names, latest ability version only,
- both sections fold, scroll internally, and the open ones survive a re-render,
- refunding a story level is refused with its message; "Manuals found" off does not strip Burning Blood's story level; Reset restores all five at 0 points / 0 segments / 0 manuals,
- a share link after Reset is `#b=1;c15;m1;t=wc` — clean, and re-seeds on load,
- no horizontal page scroll and the overview ends level with its column at every size,
- no page errors; `tools/verify_perks.py` passes unchanged (54 perks, 9 ultimates, 27 abilities).

### Known limitation, not silently changed

Because Omniblock's −40% level is prose, Omniblock contributes its −30% level to the `Stamina cost` total; the −40% is visible in the conditional list. Making prose levels supersede numeric ones is a larger change to the effect parser and is not in this PR.

author: konradmichalik
body:
## Decision

Closes #28. The issue asked for a decision between keep / replace / drop. **Drop.**
The service does not exist any more, and the step never ran in the first place.

## Evidence

**The step has never executed.** Verified, not inferred: neither `tests-php.yml`
nor `tests-typo3.yml` declares a `secrets:` block under `on.workflow_call`, and
scanning all 28 consumers of the test workflows shows **not one** passes `secrets:`
at all — let alone `secrets: inherit`. So `secrets.CC_TEST_REPORTER_ID` always
resolved to an empty string, `if: env.CC_TEST_REPORTER_ID` was always falsy, and
the step was always skipped. This confirms the issue's central claim.

**The service is gone.** Code Climate Quality was spun out to Qlty Software in
November 2024, and per [Qlty's own migration doc](https://docs.qlty.sh/migration/coverage):

> The Code Climate API was disabled on July 18, 2025. […] Any remaining attempts to
> upload coverage via the old `cc-test-reporter` will fail your CI builds.

Checked live: `api.codeclimate.com/v1/test_reports` now 301s to the Qlty docs, the
`test-reporter` binary download 404s, `codeclimate/test-reporter` is archived under
`qltysh-archive/`, and `codeclimate.com/signup` redirects to qlty.sh.

**The action is archived and says so.** `paambaati/codeclimate-action`
(`archived: true`, last push 2025-07-23) carries the notice: *"CodeClimate has now
been deprecated in favour of Qlty."*

**Nobody is using it.** Zero of the 28 test-workflow consumers has a
`.codeclimate.yml`; zero has a CodeClimate badge in its README.

Note I did not enumerate repository secrets to check for `CC_TEST_REPORTER_ID` —
dumping secret names is exactly the kind of command that should not run in an agent
session. The evidence above settles it without needing to.

There is a silver lining worth stating: because the secret was never wired up, the
broken step was inert. Had #28 been "fixed" by simply declaring the secret, every
consumer's coverage job would have started failing against a dead API.

## Changes

- Removed the CodeClimate step from `tests-php.yml`, `tests-typo3.yml`, `tests.yml`
- Removed the now-unnecessary `archived-uses` ignore from `zizmor.yml`
- README: the "Optional Coverage Reporting" section claimed CodeClimate was
  configurable and did not mention Coveralls at all. Rewritten to describe what
  actually happens, with a note for anyone who set that secret that it is inert
- README: two workflow descriptions said "coverage reporting to CodeClimate and
  Coveralls"; corrected

Nothing replaces it. Coveralls already provides line coverage, PR diff coverage,
badge and history — the only thing Code Climate added was the maintainability
grade, which now lives at Qlty and would be a *new* integration, not a preserved one.

## Not in scope, found while doing this

- **`pages.yml` is undocumented.** It is in neither the README's workflow list nor
  any README section, though CLAUDE.md calls the README "the public usage contract
  for consumers". It was added in #54 and the docs never followed.
- **`#29` is still open and visible here.** The Coveralls step sits right where the
  CodeClimate step was and is still unguarded and untokenised. Deliberately left
  alone so this PR stays a single decision.

## Test Plan

- [x] `actionlint` clean
- [x] No `CodeClimate` / `CC_TEST_REPORTER` reference remains in any workflow
- [ ] `zizmor` without the `archived-uses` ignore — CI on this PR
- [ ] One canary run confirming the coverage jobs still complete without the step

author: assay-desk-app[bot]
body:
## Why

`changelog-check` passes a PR only when the PR itself adds a `changelog/<slug>.md` fragment or carries the maintainer-only `changelog:skip` label. A fork PR (#920 today) can receive neither without cost: maintainers cannot commit to a branch they do not own, and `skip` would drop a notable fix from the release notes.

## What

- `tools/changelog/check.sh`: an optional `PR_NUMBER` input and a fourth outcome — PASS when the **base** commit already carries `changelog/pr-<N>-<slug>.md` for this PR's number with a real highlight bullet (same emptiness rule as any fragment). Ordered after the added-fragment rule so a PR's own bullet-less fragment stays visible. With `PR_NUMBER` unset or non-numeric every existing verdict is byte-identical, so this script half can merge before the workflow half supplies the value.
- `tools/changelog/check_test.sh`: fail-first rows P1–P7 (proxy greens, wrong number does not, unset ignored, bullet-less rejected, proxy-named fragment added by the PR greens the ordinary way, non-integer treated as unset, failure message documents the path). The header now records the retired gate's true baseline RED set.
- `changelog/README.md` "Fragment by proxy (fork PRs)": a maintainer or the review desk merges a fragment-only PR crediting the contributor, then adds or removes any label on the fork PR to re-run this check (the workflow already triggers on label events); if the fork PR closes unmerged the proxy is removed before the next cut. `tools/changelog/README.md` documents the input and outcome.
- `tools/changelog/changelog-check.yml` (staged copy) gains the `PR_NUMBER` env line. The LIVE `.github/workflows/changelog-check.yml` needs the same line (and the `HEAD_REF` line the staged copy already passes and the live one never did); that is a human-pushed follow-up on this issue.

## How to verify

```
tools/changelog/check_test.sh                       # 17 passed, 0 failed
CHECK_IMPL=testdata/old-check.sh tools/changelog/check_test.sh   # P1, P7 red against the retired gate
tools/changelog/aggregate_test.sh                   # 6 passed
```

## Limits

Until the live workflow passes `PR_NUMBER`, the proxy path is inert in production; nothing else changes.

author: xgamingtechnology
body:
### Motivation

- Nginx only had a prefix `location ^~ /admin/` which canonicalizes an exact `/admin` request to `/admin/`, while Next.js (global `trailingSlash` not enabled) canonicalizes `/admin/` back to `/admin`, producing an infinite redirect loop. 
- The goal is to ensure an exact request for `/admin` is proxied directly to Next.js without changing Next.js trailing-slash behavior or weakening the `/admin/` subtree isolation.

### Description

- Add an exact-match `location = /admin` that proxies to the same Next.js upstream in the staging edge template to allow exact `/admin` to reach Next.js normally. (file: `docker/edge/staging-templates/default.conf.template`).
- Add equivalent exact-match `location = /admin` blocks to the generic edge template for both the production and staging server blocks using the correct upstreams (`si-cuti-production-app:3000` and `si-cuti-staging-app:3000`). (file: `docker/edge/templates/default.conf.template`).
- Extend the staging reconcile helper to assert both exact `/admin` and the `/admin/` subtree are present in the template and effective config, keeping its existing production-attachment protections. (file: `scripts/staging-edge-reconcile.sh`).
- Add unit/regression coverage asserting exact `/admin` proxying, retaining `/admin/` subtree and other routes, and asserting there is no intentional `/admin`→`/admin/` redirect. (file: `tests/unit/edge-routing.test.ts`).
- Branch: `fix/admin-edge-redirect-loop`.

### Testing

- `sh -n scripts/staging-edge-reconcile.sh`, focused Node assertions for exact `/admin` and `/admin/` subtree upstreams, and `git diff --check` all passed (effective routing assertions succeeded against the modified templates). 
- `npm ci` / `npm run lint` / `npm run typecheck` / `npm test` could not complete because dependency installation failed in this environment due to package-registry/network constraints (missing cached package and missing executables such as `prisma` and `vitest`), so automated JS/TS gates did not run to completion. 
- Confirmations: no database changes, no migrations, no workflow logic changes, and no deployments or production infrastructure modifications were performed.

author: htenkanen
body:
The reader accepts schema 8: the feeds table is GTFS only, loses the `gbfs` block and gains `realtime_feed_ids`; a `realtime.parquet` table may sit in a country partition and in `international` (never in `links`), and is checked like the other tables, digest, columns, row count and snapshot included. A schema-7 snapshot listing one is refused as outside its layout.

`Index.realtime` is the companion table (the whole index's, or the country's), `Index.realtime_in(partition)` reads another partition's once, and `Index.realtime_unlinked()` lists the companions naming no feed of the index. A feed returned for a place carries its companions as `IndexedFeed.realtime`, `RealtimeFeed` records with the static feed, link method, entity types and endpoints; for a country load a link feed's companions come from the partition holding it. The `spec` filter keeps its meaning: another spec than `gtfs` returns nothing on schema 8. Release members and the refresh unpacker know the fourth table; the shared fixture writes a schema-8 index on request.

Plan: transitio-index `plans/spec-separation.md`, PR 6. Stacked on #135.

Verification: partition tests over whole and country loads with linked, unlinked and dangling companions, the layout refusals and a packed archive round trip; black and flake8 pass locally and the suite runs in CI.

author: carlosboeing
body:
`quotacap update` reported a failure on a perfectly good upgrade:

```
service stopped for this login session; registration kept for next login
service restart failed: service did not become ready on port 8787
Updated 0.0.23 to 0.0.24
daemon upgrade failed: service restart exited 1; run 'quotacap web' to retry
```

The binary upgraded fine and a manual `service start` moments later worked, which is the tell.

## Cause

`restart()` was `stop()` then `start()` with nothing between, and `stop()` calls `bootoutQuiet` then immediately prints success — it never waits for teardown:

```ts
bootoutQuiet(run, uid, print);
print("service stopped for this login session; registration kept for next login");
```

`launchctl bootout` is asynchronous. The dying process can still hold the port when `start()` bootstraps its replacement, so the new job fails to bind and `start()` fails its readiness check. Waiting a few seconds and starting by hand works, which is why the service was recoverable.

Reproduced twice independently. `systemctl --user stop` has the same shape, so both backends are fixed.

## Fix

`defaultWaitReleased(port)` polls until nothing answers, then `restart()` waits on it between stop and start. If the port never frees it warns and starts anyway, so the behaviour is never worse than before — `start()`'s own readiness check still reports the real failure.

Placed beside `defaultWaitReady` in `macos.ts`, which `systemd.ts` already imports shared helpers from.

## A second bug found while testing

The first version called `readConfig()` directly for the port. That made the systemd test time out — it probes the port from config, which on a developer machine is the **real running daemon on 8787**, not the test's `18787`. Same class as the config-write bug in #57: a test reaching out and touching live state.

Both backends now use `deps.port ?? (await readConfig()).port`, matching what systemd's `start()` already did, so tests stay on their injected port.

## Verification

- `npm test`: 70 files, 749 passed, 3 skipped. `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Two regression tests assert ordering (`bootout` → wait → `bootstrap` → `enable`) and the never-frees warning path. **Confirmed failing without the fix.**
- End-to-end on a real machine: `service restart` now prints `service started and ready on port 8787`, exit 0, `/health` reports ok — the operation that failed during the 0.0.24 upgrade.

author: dbn1972
body:
## Summary

An independent review found that **PERF-003's "~2ms exit" claim did not hold** under a realistic test: with an ordinary HTTP/1.1 keep-alive client (the normal condition for any persistent inter-service caller — e.g. gateway-service calling another service, or a monitoring probe), the 6 originally-wired services instead **hang for the full 8s `forceExitMs` and are then force-killed**, logging an error and exiting 1.

**Root cause** (already isolated by the review, re-verified here against the installed Fastify 4.29.1 / Node 22 sources): Fastify's `forceCloseConnections` defaults to `'idle'` on Node ≥19, which sweeps idle keep-alive sockets exactly **once**, at the instant `app.close()` runs. A socket that is genuinely mid-request at that instant and goes idle a moment later is never revisited, so `app.close()`'s callback never fires.

`forceCloseConnections: true` is **not** a safe fix for this — verified directly against Node's own `lib/_http_server.js`: on Node ≥18.2 it maps to `server.closeAllConnections()`, which destroys **every** tracked socket unconditionally, including ones actively sending a request or awaiting a response (`closeIdleConnections()`, by contrast, explicitly skips any socket whose `_httpMessage` isn't `finished`). Setting it to `true` would trade the hang for occasionally severing a real in-flight response — worse, not better.

## The fix

`packages/observability/src/lifecycle.ts`'s `registerGracefulShutdown()` gains an optional `server` option (pass Fastify's `app.server`). When supplied, it re-runs Node's own in-flight-safe `closeIdleConnections()` on an interval (default 200ms) for the duration of shutdown, in addition to Fastify's own one-shot sweep — closing the gap without ever touching a socket mid-response. Fully backward compatible: omitting `server` (e.g. from `worker.ts`, which has no HTTP server) is a no-op, unchanged from today.

Wired via a one-line `server: app.server` addition into **all 12 services currently using the shared helper**:
- PERF-003's original 6: gateway, identity, hrms, payroll, revenue, procurement (`revenue-service` was missed in an earlier pass of this fix and is now included — confirmed via grep it does call `registerGracefulShutdown`)
- court, finance (REL-012)
- inspection, meeting, visitor, works — PERF-015 tranche 2, already merged via #1194; this PR only adds the missing `server:` line on top of that merged work, nothing else changed there

**The other 54 services have no SIGTERM handling at all** and are deliberately left untouched — wiring graceful shutdown into them from scratch is PERF-015's separately-tracked, much larger scope, not a small mechanical change riding along here.

## Verification

**Real keep-alive load, not one-shot connections** (`http.Agent({keepAlive:true})`) against a real DB-backed authenticated endpoint, on **identity-service, hrms-service, and procurement-service**: ~40 concurrent requests each, all completing with clean 200s across SIGTERM, process exit in 39–990ms (vs. the 8s timeout previously hit).

**Sabotage check** (hrms-service) — used an external Postgres `LOCK TABLE employee.hrms_employees IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE` to force a deterministic, jitter-immune in-flight window (a plain concurrent-burst test turned out to be too fast/cache-served on this endpoint to reliably catch genuine in-flight state; the lock sidesteps that entirely):
- **Fix reverted:** process hung **8038ms** after SIGTERM (matching `forceExitMs`) — hang reproduced. All 39 requests that were genuinely blocked on the lock at signal time still completed with clean 200s once the lock released (confirms the *hang*, not data loss, is the bug).
- **Fix restored:** process exited **3476ms** after SIGTERM — bounded by the test's artificial 3s lock, not by the bug — with the same 39/39 clean 200s.

## Regression

- `pnpm --filter @civitasone/observability test`: 22/22 passing (added a focused unit test for the new interval-sweep behavior, verifying it re-sweeps until cleanup finishes and stops afterward — no leaked interval).
- `turbo typecheck`/`build` across all 13 touched packages: 31/31 tasks green.
- `turbo lint`: 0 errors (783 pre-existing warnings, none introduced by this diff).
- Full `vitest` suites for the 13 touched services against a fresh `bootstrap-postgres.sh` container: revenue-service 466/466, works-service 461/461, finance-service/gateway-service/court-service/payroll-service all clean. identity-service, hrms-service, inspection-service, meeting-service, procurement-service, visitor-service each have pre-existing, unrelated failures (DB-role auth in this fresh worktree, RLS/migration-state checks, PII-key mismatches, disabled-adapter flags) — confirmed via `git stash`/re-run A/B on three of them (identity, meeting, inspection) that the exact same failures reproduce with this diff completely removed, so none of it is a regression from this change.

## Not verified / scoped out

- Only 3 of the original 6 named services got the full live-load treatment (identity, hrms, procurement per the task's own "at least 3, identity+hrms specifically" ask); gateway, payroll, court, finance, revenue got the mechanical `server:` line plus typecheck/build/lint but not a dedicated live-SIGTERM-load run each.
- The 54 zero-shutdown-handling services are unverified because they're untouched by design (see above).
- Did not re-run PERF-015's own inspection/works live-SIGTERM verification — only confirmed typecheck/build/lint/tests for the one-line addition on top of its already-merged, already-verified work.

## Gap report

Updated `docs/ENTERPRISE-GAP-REPORT-2026-09-07.md`:
- **PERF-003**: appended a correction explaining the original claim didn't hold, plus this fix and its verification (kept the original text intact rather than overwriting it, matching this doc's existing convention for status updates).
- **PERF-015**: added a short note that its already-merged tranche 2 (#1194) picks up this fix automatically via the one-line addition — no other change to that row.

Not merging — leaving open per this repo's gap-workflow convention, for independent review.

Run `34704675809` proved that both OIDC identities work, the source Gateway capture succeeds, the ephemeral digest manifest is cleaned up, and the destination comparison fails closed. The current command intentionally redacts all exception text and therefore reports only `MigrationControlError`, which is too coarse to distinguish a replica fence, RBAC-scope mismatch, destination capture failure, file-set divergence, size mismatch, or SHA-256 mismatch.

This PR keeps the proof read-only and adds only sanitized failure-stage reporting:

- `file_set`

Unknown errors remain `unspecified`; underlying exception text is never emitted. Tests explicitly prove that private exception details are not echoed.

No Azure mutation, Gateway/Table write, source fencing, replica activation, RBAC change, protected payload upload, or cutover behavior is added.

After CI/review, merge and rerun the manual Gateway byte-equivalence proof on `main` to identify the exact failed invariant before changing destination state.

body:
## Problem

The Docker build failed at BUILD_IMAGE with "flag '--mount=type=cache,id=pnpm,target=/pnpm/store' is missing the cacheKey prefix from its id". Railway requires BuildKit cache mount ids to be scoped as s/<service-id>-<suffix> so caches don't leak across services, but the Dockerfile used the bare id "pnpm".

## Solution

Updated the cache mount id to s/845cec88-ffd7-408c-9a98-146f1d0e267e-pnpm, matching Railway's required service-scoped prefix, so the Dockerfile validates and the build proceeds to pnpm install.

### Changes

author: nomansheikh
body:
## What

Fixes the release workflow so tagging actually publishes what the README
promises, and adds a changelog the release notes come from.

Tagging stays manual — you push the tag, this does the work that follows.

## Why

The workflow ran on a tag push and set `:latest` with
`enable={{is_default_branch}}`. That is false for a tag ref, so `:latest`
would never have been published — while `docker-compose.yml` in the README
pulls exactly that. The first person to follow the quick start would have
got `manifest unknown`.

## How

- `flavor: latest=auto` moves `:latest` to the highest release and skips
  prereleases. `v0.1.0-beta.1` publishes as `0.1.0-beta.1` and nothing else:
  not `0.1`, not `latest`.
- The workflow now creates the GitHub release too, taking its notes from the
  matching `CHANGELOG.md` section and marking any version containing a hyphen
  as a prerelease.
- `CHANGELOG.md` seeded in Keep a Changelog format.
- `docs/releasing.md` records how to pick a number, which tag to pin, that
  downgrades are not supported because migrations are forward-only, and that
  a bad release is fixed forward rather than by moving a tag.

## Verified

Workflow structure checked field by field: both architectures, the version
reaching the build arg, `latest=auto` present, and the prerelease branch of
the notes step.

The version reaches the UI — `ldflags` → `main.version` → `/api/health` →
the sidebar. A build with `-X main.version=v9.9.9-check` reports it back,
which is why the running dev panel shows `dev`.

**Not verified:** the workflow has never run, and cannot be until a tag is
pushed.

author: iekip95mod-arch
body:
Two defects in the review workflow, found by watching it fail rather than by reading it.

### The reviewer cannot reach the base commit

Run [34702887258](https://github.com/iekip95mod-arch/cx2-ag/actions/runs/34702887258), reviewing #72, gave up after 6m19s with four of its eight checklist items unticked and posted no verdict. Its own words:

> git checkout/worktree add are refused in this sandbox, so I'm using `git apply -R`/`git apply` against the PR diff to reconstruct origin/main content in place for the baseline, rather than switching branches

It never finished. The `--allowedTools` list has `git diff`, `git apply`, `git log`, `git show`, `git status` and `git rev-parse`, and nothing that reaches another commit. A reviewer with no baseline cannot answer "did the branch break something that used to work", which is half of what AGENTS.md asks a review to be.

Four prefixes added: `git fetch`, `git worktree`, `git checkout`, `git merge-base`. None of them publishes anything, and `actions/checkout` above already runs at `fetch-depth: 0`, so the base commit was present the whole time and only the spelling was missing. The prompt now tells the reviewer to put its baseline tree under `.Internal/workspaces/` rather than disturbing the branch it is judging.

### The prompt told reviewers to accept five failures that are about to stop existing

This is the worse of the two, and it is the kind AGENTS.md warns about directly: a guard that reads as coverage.

The prompt said:

> The suite is RED on main for five failures that are nothing to do with any branch you will see: two vector_components golden rows and three criterion 4 invariant rows, all from issue #4. Establish that baseline on the base commit before you judge the branch, and hold the branch to "the same five and no others". A sixth is the branch's.

That was true when it was written. #74 fixes issue #4 and takes main to `nps: 9839 checks, 0 failed`. The moment it merges, this paragraph is a standing instruction to every future reviewer to tolerate five failures that no longer exist, and any branch that introduced up to five would read as clean.

The fix is not to update the number. It is to stop putting a number there at all. The prompt now says to measure the baseline and compare against what was measured, and says out loud why: a count written into a prompt goes stale silently, and this one already did.

### Ordering

This should merge **after** #74, or the new wording is telling reviewers main is green while it is still red. Either order is survivable, that one is honest.

### Stages reached

None, and none are reachable. This is a workflow file and a prompt. The evidence that the first half works is the next review that runs with it, which is why #72 is the branch to point at it: its reviewer is the one that died on this.

author: akshaydotsharma
body:
## Summary

- Three Italy trip expenses showed a 50/50 split with Papa on the Mac and no split on the phone, €95.25 of disagreement about my share. The phone's oplog for City Tax Rome went 11578 (no `splitsData`), 11579 (split), 11580 (no key again) — that last one was the clear. Both devices recorded lamport 11580 from the iPhone with different content hashes, so the Mac applied the clear and kept the split.
- `preservingFieldsAbsentHere` keeps any key the payload does not carry, which is what stops an older peer nulling a column it has never heard of (#428). Synthesized `Codable` drops nil optionals, so a CLEARED field was absent for the same reason an unknown one is. `SyncOp.swift:106` has named this trade since #428.
- The sender now walks the DTO's `Mirror` and writes an explicit null for every property the encoder omitted. The receiver is unchanged: a present null already overwrites. `deletedAt` and `archivedAt` are in the same family, so un-deleting and un-archiving start working too.
- The key set is derived, not restated, so a new DTO field needs no sync-side registration (the #449 failure mode).

Closes #516

## The cost, stated plainly

The hash now covers the filled payload, because `verify()` rehashes what it receives and rejects any op whose bytes disagree with its own `contentHash`. So every content hash changes and each device re-publishes every record once, roughly 2,600 each. `testHashesAreStableAcrossPasses` pins that it is exactly once.

Sequencing: the 4 currently diverged rows are being repaired by hand FIRST, so the re-publish has nothing left to resolve by last-writer.

## Test plan

- [x] New `SyncClearPropagationTests` (7 tests), including the reported case end to end through `SyncApplier`.
- [x] Reverting the fill fails 3 of them, the headline one being "a split the sender cleared must clear here".
- [x] `SyncNarrowPeerTests` still green — an absent key is still preserved, so #428 does not regress.
- [x] `PersonalDashboardTests`: 568 tests, 0 failures. `DexterMacTests`: 126 tests, 0 failures.
- [ ] Both devices: confirm the 4 repaired rows agree, then confirm a fresh clear propagates.

## Problem
Build a new Nova successor from scratch using the approved dark blue/purple reference layout without modifying or destabilising the current Nova application.

## What this PR adds
- new isolated `nova-next/` application surface;
- approved splash, login, Home, side drawer, Chat, Tools, Tasks, Projects, Settings and completion-state UI shell;
- primary `Home / Chat / Tools / Tasks / More` navigation and full reference drawer;
- route state and reduced-motion-aware transitions;
- Admin-only auth policy and injectable auth adapter contract;
- current-Nova capability parity registry;
- fail-closed protected-action policy and narrow API adapter;
- isolated `/nova-next/` PWA scope and `nova-next-dev-v1` cache namespace;
- promotion configuration/runbook that records the current Nova production identity but does not activate it;
- design, security, parity, adapter, testing and validation documentation.

## Isolation evidence
Repository comparison shows this PR only adds files under `nova-next/`, `docs/nova-next/` and the Nova Next implementation plan. It does **not** modify existing `nova/`, `android/`, `supabase/`, `.github/` or other production application files.

No production Supabase schema/RLS/Edge Function, deployment, signing, OTA, pricing or Guardian authority change is included. Current Nova remains untouched.

## Risk
**Medium.** This adds a new application surface and policy contracts, but deliberately leaves production auth/backend wiring disconnected. Protected actions remain blocked/fail-closed.

## Validation
Fresh local contract verification:

```text
action-policy: ok
auth-adapter: ok
auth-policy: ok
capability-registry: ok
isolation: ok

No false screenshot-parity claim is made; visual acceptance should be done on a deployed/CI preview.

## Rollback
Before any future production routing exists, rollback is simply removing the isolated `nova-next/` surface/docs. Existing Nova behavior is unaffected.

After this bootstrap is validated, live Nova service adapters and the separate Android Nova Next wrapper can be implemented on follow-up branches. Authentication/production release/signing changes will remain separately reviewed high-risk work.

author: sanxi33
body:
## Description

This is a follow-up to #713. Thanks to @erning for the native Seed-ASR engine; I've been using it for Chinese dictation on Hyprland, and it has made a real difference to my setup.

With `type_partials = true`, a correction such as `这个云书法` → `这个语音输入法` can leave the first version on screen until the utterance becomes definite. The recognizer has already corrected itself, but the new hypothesis no longer extends the old one, so the reconciler suppresses it. A later correction to an already-definite prefix can end the session altogether.

This patch gives live mode a full-transcript `Snapshot` event. The output session compares each snapshot with the text it has rendered, keeps the common prefix, and replaces only the divergent suffix. Empty acknowledgement/final packets retain the last nonempty hypothesis. File output replaces its accumulated text without counting it as keyboard input.

The default stable-only mode is unchanged. Existing output hooks are retained; in live mode the post-processor runs once on the complete final transcript. A failed output transaction stops further rewrites rather than guessing what is left on screen.

**Dependency:** #713 is still open, so this branch contains its five commits unchanged. My patch is just [d30148b](https://github.com/sanxi33/voxtype/commit/d30148ba4d1d020cee8bee153a3a84ac9b886cc9), touching six files. This is a draft against `dev`, not a replacement for #713; the single commit can also be cherry-picked into that branch.

author: ablayed
body:
## Le défaut

`claimSyncState` (`lib/woocommerce/sync.ts:119` avant ce lot) se prononçait sur la **valeur** du statut, jamais sur la **fraîcheur** de `updated_at`. Un `running` orphelin — dépassement de durée de fonction, redéploiement, plantage — rendait `sync_already_running` **définitivement**. Un marchand dont la synchronisation initiale s'interrompait n'avait aucune sortie.

## La correction

Un bail seul aurait déplacé le défaut : un scan paginé peut durer plus longtemps que son bail, et l'ancien worker pourrait reprendre la main après le nouveau. Il fallait un **jeton de fencing**.

- **Réclamation par comparaison-et-échange.** Un `running` dont le bail de 150 s a expiré est repris par un `UPDATE` dont le prédicat porte `id`, `status='running'`, **`attempt = <valeur lue>`** et `updated_at < <seuil>`. PostgREST n'accepte aucune expression de colonne (`attempt = attempt + 1` est impossible) : c'est cette comparaison-et-échange qui rend la reprise atomique.
- **Zéro ligne n'est pas une erreur.** Une relecture unique rend quatre verdicts distincts : `already_completed`, `sync_already_running`, `sync_lease_lost`, `sync_claim_conflict`.
- **Fencing en un seul point.** `updateSyncState` est le point d'étranglement des quinze sites d'écriture (progression, clôture, treize `markFailed`). Il porte la génération réclamée dans son prédicat et devient tri-état `ok` / `lease_lost` / `error`. Un `lease_lost` court-circuite `markFailed` : le worker s'arrête sans insister.
- **Renouvellement toutes les dix commandes**, pour qu'une page de cent ne se fasse pas voler son propre bail.

**Aucune migration.** `attempt` et `updated_at` existaient, sont `NOT NULL`, et n'étaient exposés à aucune interface — `attempt` n'avait aucun lecteur. Sa sémantique ne change pas : « numéro de réclamation » et « génération de bail » sont la même quantité.

## Sur la durée du bail

150 s, **choisis pour limiter l'attente utilisateur**, pas dérivés d'un pire cas — il n'en existe aucun tant que les appels RPC n'ont pas de délai côté client. La sûreté vient du fencing : une expiration prématurée provoque du travail redondant, jamais un écrasement. La justification est écrite en commentaire à la constante.

## Preuves

- `tests/unit/woocommerce/sync.test.ts` — 17 tests (7 existants, 10 ajoutés). Le faux client admin a été **réécrit** : il modélise un vrai prédicat d'`UPDATE` et rend un nombre de lignes appariées. L'ancien aiguillait sur la forme de la charge et ne supportait qu'un seul `.eq()`.
- `tests/rls/r2-woocommerce-sync-lease.rls.test.ts` — 5 tests contre un **vrai PostgREST**, dont la course de réclamation. Le test **appelle `claimSyncState`** et ne reproduit pas son `UPDATE` : reproduire la requête prouverait PostgreSQL, appeler la fonction prouve que le code construit le bon prédicat. Preuve numérique : sur deux réclamations concurrentes, `attempt` n'avance que d'un cran.
- **Six mutations, toutes rouges**, puis restauration vérifiée par empreinte identique.

## Reste ouvert, nommé et non traité ici

`CHECK (attempt <= 1000)` ; absence de `statement_timeout` sur `service_role` ; appels RPC non bornés côté client.

author: kuzzrus
body:
## Summary

Вторая половина шага 3 плана NaiveProxy (полная запись решений/плана — в памяти проекта): собственно жизненный цикл Caddy-процесса на инбаунд, по образцу `internal/mtproto`'s `Manager` (один внешний процесс на инбаунд), а не `internal/wireproxy`'s глобального тумблера — архитектурный разворот на "полноценный инбаунд" зафиксирован ранее.

- **`types.go`** — `Instance` (пакетный тип, будет конвертироваться из `*model.Inbound` на шаге wiring) и `Client` (один username/password Basic-Auth креденшл на Naive-клиента).
- **`caddyfile.go`** — `renderCaddyfile` собирает реальный текст Caddyfile: `forward_proxy` за вручную поставленным сертификатом (Caddy никогда не сможет пройти свой ACME-челлендж здесь — видит только то, что сплайсит SNI-relay фронтпрокси, не прямое публичное соединение), по строке `basic_auth` на клиента, опциональная `upstream socks5://127.0.0.1:<port>` для Xray-routing моста (решение #2) — сверил, что эта директива реально поддерживает localhost-адрес с socks5-схемой, по собственной документации `klzgrad/forwardproxy`, не предположил. Рендер сам же служит фингерпринтом изменений (Manager сравнивает строку напрямую), плюс та же защита от newline-инъекции, что уже стоит у `amneziaWGConfigText`.
- **`process.go`** — `Process`, почти дословно зеркалит `internal/mtproto/process.go` (graceful SIGTERM→kill, `procLogWriter`, один процесс на инстанс) плюс `waitForListener` из `internal/psiphon` (forwardproxy публикуется одним бинарём, как и Psiphon).
- **`manager.go`** — `Ensure`/`Remove`/`Reconcile`/`StopAll`. Инстанс без клиентов **останавливается**, а не просто не стартует — неаутентифицированный `forward_proxy` это живая дыра по собственному предупреждению плагина ("UNAUTHENTICATED! USE ONLY FOR TESTING"), а не просто простаивающий процесс, так что это нужно было сделать правильно сразу, не откладывая.

## Проверено

- Полный набор тестов `Manager`/`Process` спавнит настоящие (фейковые) процессы через тот же паттерн "тест-бинарь ре-эксекает сам себя", что уже есть в `internal/mtproto` — реальный бинарь Caddy не нужен.
- Отдельный **`TestRenderCaddyfileValidatesAgainstTheRealBinary`** скачивает настоящий пиненный релиз и гоняет `caddy validate` по рендеру — директивы `forward_proxy` писались руками по README плагина и ни разу не исполнялись на реальном бинаре до этого теста (ни WSL, ни Docker недоступны на этой машине для локальной проверки). Скипается без сети/вне linux-amd64, так что может только усилить CI, не заблокировать его флуктуацией.
- Реальный, платформенный баг пойман по пути: `exec.Command` на Windows требует точного совпадения включая расширение — фейковый дочерний бинарь без `.exe` не находился. Поправлено через `BinPath()`, учитывающий платформу (тот же приём, что `internal/mtproto`'s `GetBinaryName()`) — на настоящий бинарь не влияет вообще, `checkPlatform` и так отсекает не-linux/amd64 до всякой загрузки.
- `go build`/`go vet`/`go test -v`/`gofmt -l` — чисто.

## Дальше

`model.Inbound`/`model.Client` wiring (шаг 4) — новое поле под креды, регистрация протокола, оба дублированных required-field свитча.

tables, fail closed on conflicting duplicate identifiers, and preserve config-declared absence
