body:
Related to narrowed #1088. The inspected full-precision AuK path exceeds the stated 16 GiB host's memory before VAE and activation allocations. An offline TTS addition needs measured value over the app's installed system-voice baseline.

This dossier pins model/runtime/licence and dependency evidence, records the supplied parameter/download accounting separately from measurements, and explains the complete encoder/decoder requirement. Full AuK is a preflight no-go on that stated host; Flash and alternative Apple paths remain separately unqualified. A conditional protocol covers native decoding/playback, quality, cold/warm timing, resource use, cancellation and cleanup.

Pinned-source, baseline, resource arithmetic and git diff checks pass. No weights/dependencies were downloaded, no runtime built, and no inference, playback or memory benchmark ran. Historical host capacity must be rechecked before any later authorised experiment.

No new adapter/picker/dependency, blanket platform rejection, runtime choice, account change, release or automation is included. #1121 ownership and later asset/native qualification remain separate gates.

author: bearyjd
body:
## Summary

Closes the hole #17 shipped with. Nothing verified that `ScaleSessionWorker` passes `reason.name` rather than only the coarse outcome — `recordAttempt` reached the log via `applicationContext as? BasculeApplication`, which is null under the plain `Application` this JVM lane uses, so the whole body was a silent no-op in tests and the one thing worth asserting could not be.

## How

An injectable seam **matching the established ones**, per CONTRIBUTING's "do not invent a new pattern":

- `ScaleSessionWorker.captureAttemptLogProvider` — same shape and rationale as `BridgeForegroundService.enqueuerFactory`, because a `CoroutineWorker` is built by a factory and cannot take constructor parameters.
- `recordAttempt` becomes `internal`, on the same precedent as `BridgeForegroundService.enqueueOnce` ("internal so a test can drive it without going through `onCreate`").

Production behaviour is unchanged by the defaults.

## Two tests, and why the second one matters

1. `recordingAnAttemptStoresTheFineGrainedReasonNotJustTheOutcome` — the reason reaches the log.
2. `twoReasonsSharingAnOutcomeAreStillDistinguishable` — `HANDSHAKE_FAILED` and `MISSED` **both** map to `NO_READING`, so two reasons sharing an outcome must still be told apart afterwards. Without this, passing a constant or the outcome's own name would satisfy test 1.

## Mutations

Both red on both tests, green on restore:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| drop `reason.name` (exactly what #17 shipped untested) | red |
| pass `outcome.name` instead of `reason.name` | red |

That second mutation is the one that proves these tests check the *reason* specifically, not merely that something was stored.

## Testing

**689 tests, 0 failures**, detekt clean — on a `--rerun-tasks` full run, not an up-to-date one. (Gradle reported `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 932ms` on a plain invocation after restoring files; that is a skip, not a pass, so I forced it.)

author: nkolosov097
body:
The Contact section currently returns a generic service-unavailable error because production has no usable persistence path, and an SMTP failure can lose the owner notification. This restores the section with a fresh Drizzle/PostgreSQL schema: valid submissions are committed once, owner email is attempted immediately, and durable failures are retried by protected scheduled workers.

The change also adds strict server validation, idempotency, trusted-IP rate limiting, accessible draft-preserving form states, EN/RU copy, Gmail-safe mail handling, bounded leases/timeouts, aggregate operational health, targeted terminal-message requeue, serialized deployment migrations, and production/preview workflows. Prisma is removed because there is no existing database to migrate.

Validation:

- TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier, Stylelint
- 241 unit/DOM tests
- production Next.js build
- 60/60 Contact E2E scenarios across 12 Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit viewport projects
- PostgreSQL/Mailpit integration and outage matrices documented in `docs/superpowers/verification/2026-09-12-feedback-restoration.md`

author: azeezish
body:
## Summary

Adds `crates/atlas-coldsnap`, a CUDA-free Rust client for the [ColdSnap](https://github.com/sparksq/coldsnap) controller protocol, so Atlas can eventually be driven by a placement manager's `sleep` / `wake` / `status` lifecycle.

This is scaffolding for that integration, not the integration itself — see the caveat under **Notes for reviewers**. The crate is purely additive: one line added to the workspace `members` list, and `time` gains the `parsing` feature in `Cargo.lock` (already in the graph transitively).

## What it owns, and what it deliberately does not

It owns the foreign contract and nothing else: request format 4, receipt format 2, the `coldsnap capabilities` document, argv construction, the single process-I/O seam, and the restore-shaped derivation of `sleep`/`wake`/`status`. Field names and validators are transcribed from the controller's Go source (`internal/snapshot/schema.go`, `receipt.go`, `internal/cli/capabilities.go`, `internal/canonicaljson/canonical.go`) rather than its prose.

It does **not** own Atlas lifecycle policy. What "sleep" means for an Atlas CUDA context — release weights and KV, retain the process — is a `spark-server` decision. A foreign-protocol adapter that also owned that would invert the dependency and make every lifecycle change a change here.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt -p atlas-coldsnap -- --check`
- [x] `ATLAS_SKIP_BUILD=1 CUDARC_CUDA_VERSION=13000 cargo clippy -p atlas-coldsnap --all-targets` (clean under the workspace `warnings = "deny"` + `clippy::all` policy)
- [x] `cargo test -p atlas-coldsnap` — **119 passed** (93 unit + 26 integration), on macOS, with no GPU and no `coldsnap` binary
- [x] `typos crates/atlas-coldsnap`
- [x] 500-LoC cap and SPDX header checked directly (every file ≤ 500 LoC; line 1 of every `.rs`)
- [ ] `bash scripts/check-license-headers.sh` — **not run**: it requires Docker, which is unavailable on this host. The same rule was verified directly against `.licenserc.yaml` instead.
- [ ] Runtime/hardware — **N/A**: no runtime behaviour changes; nothing here is wired into `spark-server`.

Scoping the checks to `-p atlas-coldsnap` is deliberate: the workspace as a whole needs a CUDA host to build.

The 119 tests are possible because the runner seam (`CommandRunner`) is the only place a process is spawned. Every failure mode below is therefore reachable on a laptop with a scripted fake.

## Notes for reviewers

**Two things are deliberately left undone, and both are load-bearing.**

1. **No request is emitted for an engine other than `vllm`/`sglang`.** ColdSnap's `engineadapter.Lookup` registers only those two, and `OperationReceipt.Validate` independently rejects any other engine — so `"engine": "atlas"` is structurally invalid, not merely unsupported. The tempting shortcut was to emit `engine: "vllm"` for an Atlas workload; that would produce a receipt asserting a vLLM engine for a workload that is not vLLM, making lifecycle decisions look evidenced when they are not. The engine type is consequently a **closed** enum on the request side and a **tolerant** one on the wire side, so a future engine cannot make an otherwise valid receipt unparseable.

2. **The receipt's `request_sha256` is not compared against the digest of the bytes sent.** `snapshot.RequestSHA256` is `sha256(CanonicalJSON(json.Marshal(request)))` — over the *decoded, default-resolved* struct, with recursively sorted keys and Python-style `ensure_ascii` escaping. It is not a checksum of the submitted bytes, and a byte-level comparison would reject **every valid receipt** (whitespace, key order, omitted fields resolved to driver defaults, and Unicode escaping all change it while the semantic request is identical). Identity rests instead on the echoed `operation_id` and `operation`, which are exactly comparable; the controller digest is retained for audit. `PreparedRequest` additionally verifies that its serialized bytes actually encode the id and operation it is correlated against, so that check cannot be vacuous.

**Outcomes are four-way, not two-way.** `Success` / `OperationFailed` / `Unknown` / protocol violation. A timeout or a receiptless nonzero exit is **`Unknown`, never failed**: `sleep`/`wake` take a fresh id each time, so the controller does not deduplicate them and a retry is a second operation rather than a repeat. `UnknownOperation::retry_is_safe()` returns `false` and points the caller at `status` for reconciliation.

**Deferred to a follow-up PR:** the `spark-server` lifecycle surface (a `LifecycleEngine` seam over `ModelHost`, plus an opt-in admin endpoint). It is not here because it modifies the live serving path and its "release weights + KV, keep process" behaviour is exactly what cannot be validated off-hardware — it deserves its own review rather than riding along with the adapter crate.

**Upstream question, not yet filed:** whether ColdSnap intends an Atlas engine adapter at all, or whether the boundary is manager-side coordination with ColdSnap never seeing an `atlas` engine. The answer determines whether item 1 above is a temporary gap or the permanent shape. Worth resolving before anyone builds toward an adapter that isn't coming.

**Peer review:** the process-boundary logic was independently reviewed by a second model, which caught a timeout race (a child exiting between the poll and the deadline check was killed and misreported as `Unknown(TimedOut)`), an unguarded `kill(-pid)` where a zero pid would have signalled the *caller's* process group, a missing `EINTR` retry, a cap-arithmetic overflow, a leaked child on wait error, and the fact that stderr truncation could SIGPIPE a healthy process. All fixed, each with a regression test.

author: tweggen
body:
**Proposal 48 M4 — the finish, and the documents.** The last milestone; with it the
proposal's milestone list is CLOSED.

**This branch is STACKED on `feat/p48-m3-meters` (#186), which is not merged yet** —
it is the PR's base. Merge #186 first, or merge this one and #186 becomes empty.

## What M4 turned out to be

Three of the four ACs were mostly already true and the work was in gating them. The
fourth had to be measured before it could be scoped.

**AC4.1 — the fader's double-click reset** landed in M3a. What is new is the
assertion: `db=0.0` beside `faderDb=0.1`, which is the integer curve's failure to
round-trip stated as a number. The **plugin-slider** half is inherited with no code —
the mixer mounts the arranger's own `SPluginEffectStrip`, whose generic editor got
`sdefaultreset::onDoubleClick` in `fix/detail-pane-layout` — and is deliberately not
re-gated here.

**AC4.2 — the context menu is THREE items, and that number came from reading what
each item of the arranger's head menu depends on**, not from taste:

| Item | Shareable? | What it reads |
|---|---|---|
| Remove / Group / Ungroup | **yes** | `pathOf`, `childLinks` |
| Indent / Outdent | no | `rowIndexOfTrack()` / `rowAt()` — the arranger's visible ROW list |
| Take lanes, lane height, automation picker | no | row concepts; the AC excludes them by name |
| Create asset from range | no | the ruler RANGE |
| Insert / remove / delete sample | no | a click POSITION on the timeline |
| New track (below) | no | a row position |

So `app/timeline/strackgestures` holds exactly the three, **with the SUBMIT
INJECTED** — the arranger stamps the active TAB's root, the mixer stamps its own
(D12): one body, two submitters. `SStdMixerView`'s three `ct*` slots are four lines
each now. The AC's escape clause ("drop the menu rather than duplicate it") was not
needed.

**AC4.3 — colour needed a new KIND of assertion**, because nothing that already
exists can see one: no audio, no geometry and no `describe()` of the arranger's would
move if the strip grew a palette of its own. The strip resolves through
`sclipcolors::indexForLane` from the PROJECT root — the same two calls `sClipBodyOf()`
makes for `assert-take-lane` and `assert-lane-overlay`, the arranger's own PIXEL
classifiers — and `describeMixerPane` reports `colorMismatch=` by comparing them, plus
`colors=` (distinct headers). Measured: `colorMismatch=0`, `colors=3` over four strips.

**AC4.4 — the wheel was a STALE CLAIM in the arranger, not a missing feature in the
mixer.** `SSMVMixerControl::wheelEvent`'s comment read "1.0 dB per notch, see its
singleStep" and had been wrong since it was written: the curve is `x^0.5`, so ten
slider units are a tenth of a dB only nominally (one dB is ~16 units at unity, ~6 at
−60), and `QAbstractSlider` multiplies `singleStep` by `wheelScrollLines()` on top —
a notch was ~1.9 dB at unity and ~5 dB at −60. `sFaderWheelValue()` does the
arithmetic in dB and **both** faders filter `QEvent::Wheel` to use it, so the comment
is now true in both mounts rather than in the new one.

The **pinned master** was M1's shape and had never been measured; the seam now drags
the pane's own scrollbar to its maximum and compares both strips' global positions,
with `scrolled=` as the control.

## Two things worth knowing that this milestone paid for

**A hard failure hid behind a known flake for one full-suite run.**
`mixer-strip-menu`'s `readXml` refuses an empty required attribute, so
`action_roundtrip_test` could not build one and failed — reporting
`Exit code 0xc0000374`, which CLAUDE.md records as that test's intermittent
heap-corruption flake (7 in 30 on `main`). The suite's one failure was exactly the
failure the notes tell you to expect. Looping it said **12 of 12**, which 7-in-30 is
not. Fixed with a fixture and an accept/refuse row; the same box then read 11 of 12.
Recorded in CLAUDE.md beside the flake itself: **a named flake is a reason to measure
the rate, not a reason to move on.**

**The FIFTH Qt layout floor, caught by M1's own gate within minutes.** The colour
tint is a stylesheet with `padding:1px 2px`, and a `QLabel`'s minimum width is its
text PLUS its padding — so the narrow strip's layout minimum went to 61 px against
the 60 D9 names and three cases failed at once with `SMixerStrip(w 60<61)`.

## Gated

- **`mixer_pane_polish.qxa`** (new) — colour agreement, the muted variant, the wheel
  at exact dB values, the reset, the pinned master, the three menu commands, the
  system-lane refusal, and the menu's own arrangement-root stamp.
- **Sabotage: EIGHT, each biting `mixer_pane_polish` and only it.**
  `mixer_pane_layout`, `mixer_pane_strips`, `mixer_path_root` and `mixer_write_pass`
  stayed green under every one. The first spelling of sabotage 6 was a **no-op** — it
  changed a constructor parent that `addWidget()` overrides one line later — and read
  as a vacuous gate until the patch was corrected; that is recorded too.
- **The arranger side of the extraction IS gated**, measured rather than assumed:
  `group-track` / `ungroup-track` are testkit gesture verbs that call
  `ctGroupTrack()` / `ctUngroupTrack()` directly, and seven existing cases drive them.
  Only `ctRemoveTrack` has no headless route.
- Four checkers clean.
- **Full suite: 380 of 381**, 400 s at `-j4`; **384 registered / 381 run / 3 disabled**
  (the macOS-only `au_*` trio). Measured, not quoted. The one failure is
  `action_roundtrip_test`'s known heap-corruption flake — 11 of 12 in isolation on
  this box after the fixture landed, against 7 in 30 on `main`.

**An unreproduced flake, named rather than left out.** An intermediate full run timed
out `qxa.fade_handle_cursor` at 600 s. Its log ends three lines into startup, at
`theme=system; keeping the platform style windows11` — before any action ran, and the
mixer is not in that case at all. **6 of 6 in isolation at 0.4 s each**, and it passed
in the next full run. One observation, cause not established.

## NOT gated

- **Pixels and aesthetics anywhere.** Nothing here says the header is painted at all,
  only what colour it resolves to. No `paintEvent` of the pane is measured.
- **The menu POPUP, its labels and its enabled states.** There is no menu verb in this
  repository; `mixer-strip-menu` calls the same function each item's lambda calls.
- **`ctRemoveTrack` from the arranger** (context menu only).
- **Indent and outdent from a mixer strip** — not offered, for the reason the table
  gives. Re-expressing them over `slaneorder::flattenTrackLanes` is named as later
  work, not smuggled in here.
- **The wheel over the arranger head's fader** — the step is shared, but no case
  drives that widget's wheel.
- **The master/lane-0 colour collision.** `autoIndexForLane()` answers 0 for a lane it
  cannot find and a master lane is not in the walk. `colorMismatch=0` reports that the
  two mounts agree; it does not endorse the answer. Fixing it is a change to the
  arranger's palette.
- Everything on the proposal's own standing list: the dock's docked/floating/closed
  round trip, the View-menu item and the shortcut, repaint cost with many strips, a
  send lane's own strip.

author: sgelias
body:
The harness half of the project-scoped memory graph. Pairs with
crab-shell-proxy#48, which resolves it.

## The defect

A turn inside a project wrote its memory into the member's **global** graph. The
one MCP server a ganglion container is given carries the member's token and
nothing else, so nothing in the request said which project the work belonged to.

## The fix

The project travels in `X-Ganglion-Project` — the same name `crab-shell-proxy`
sends in the other direction on a turn, because it is the same fact.

Read from the **request's context**, which is the turn's. That is what makes it
correct by construction rather than by discipline:

- `initialize` and `tools/list` run at boot under no project and send nothing;
- a tool call sends whatever the turn is in.

It is never a tool argument. The project is a property of the conversation, and a
model able to name it could read and write another project's memory.

Set before the configured headers, so a server block may still override it, and
sent unconditionally — a server that does not know the header ignores it.

## Tests

- `TestACallCarriesTheTurnsProject` — boot requests carry nothing; a call made
  under a project carries it.
- `TestACallOutsideAProjectCarriesNoProject` — the regression bar: a turn in the
  agent's own workspace is byte-identical to before.

Whole suite green, `go.mod` still at zero requires.

author: jimmy-guzman
body:
## What

Note reads, writes, moves, deletions and attachment writes now run on the folder they validated, through a directory handle, instead of on a path string. A symlink planted at that folder's name after validation cannot send the operation somewhere else. Temporary files are created and renamed inside that same handle, and a name that already exists is refused by the platform's rename rather than by a check. The index moves out of the notes folder into the app's cache folder, in a subfolder named after the notes folder, because SQLite opens its database by path and cannot be bound the same way. An old `.notras/` folder is left where it is. SPEC.md and ARCHITECTURE.md describe the new behavior, and DECISIONS.md records why as D77.

## Why

Closes #178. A local probe showed the old check-then-write could be redirected: rename the checked folder away, put a symlink at its old name, and the write landed outside the library. If this change is wrong, a write lands in the wrong folder or the app fails to open its index. The swap tests in `application.rs` fail in the first case, and the index tests in `lib.rs` fail in the second. Locally: 131 core tests, 42 shell tests and 901 frontend tests pass, along with Clippy, rustfmt, machete, knip, the bindings check, typecheck, lint and the web build. The Windows rename path and the junction test only run in CI. The desktop checks in the plan (fresh launch creates the index under the cache folder, an existing library still opens, and create, rename, move, delete and attach still land in the library) have not been run in the app.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Improvements**
  * Index files are now stored in the application cache instead of within each notes folder.
  * Notes and attachments use safer file handling that prevents symlink-based path escapes.
  * Scanning, rebuilding, and file updates remain reliable when validated notes folders are moved.

author: daltonganger
body:
## Summary

`django-filter` 25.1 removed the schema generation methods of its DRF filter
backend in favour of `drf-spectacular`
([CHANGES.rst](https://github.com/carltongibson/django-filter/blob/main/CHANGES.rst)),
but DRF's OpenAPI schema generator still calls
`get_schema_operation_parameters()` on *every* configured filter backend:

```python
# rest_framework/schemas/openapi.py
for filter_backend in self.view.filter_backends:
    parameters += filter_backend().get_schema_operation_parameters(self.view)
```

Because `DjangoFilterBackend` no longer implements that method, both the
`/api/schema` endpoint and the `generateschema` management command fail:

```
AttributeError: 'DjangoFilterBackend' object has no attribute 'get_schema_operation_parameters'
```

This is the same failure reported in #985. As a side effect, `openapi-schema.yml`
could not be regenerated and has been stale since v2.10.0.

## Changes

- Add `api.filter_backends.FilterBackend`, a `DjangoFilterBackend` subclass that
  re-implements `get_schema_operation_parameters()`.
- Use it as `DEFAULT_FILTER_BACKENDS` in the base settings.
- Add regression tests for the schema endpoint and for the presence of filter
  parameters in the generated schema.

The generated schema is **unchanged**: filter parameters keep the same names,
descriptions and types. Verified by generating the schema with the restored
command and comparing it to the committed `openapi-schema.yml` — the two parse
to identical data structures. The method is adapted from django-filter 24.3,
which is BSD licensed like Baby Buddy.

## Test plan

- `python manage.py generateschema ... --file openapi-schema.yml` now runs and
  produces output identical to the committed file.
- `manage.py test api` passes (121 tests).
- `black . --check`, `djlint --check .` and `prettier . --check` are clean.

Note: `babybuddy.tests.tests_views` has six pre-existing failures on `master`
unrelated to this change (verified against a clean checkout).

author: unseensnick
body:
## Summary

Fixes what a read-only many-agent audit of everything this fork has changed in `src/` (112 commits, 40 files) turned up, plus what four adversarial reviewers found in the fixes themselves. 106 findings were confirmed and 75 refuted; the refutations are recorded in the audit ledger.

The five High findings, each fixed and verified:

- A session did not keep the proxy it was created with, so every rebuild (lifetime expiry, the idle reaper, the cap, an engine fallback) silently solved from the server's own address.
- A Camoufox session returned every cookie in its browser context, so one site's clearance and login cookies went out with another site's page. Reproduced live and confirmed fixed by an A/B in the same window.
- The failed timezone lookup logged the proxy URL and the library's message, either of which carries the password, at the default level.
- The Chrome engine took a session's timezone from the request instead of from the proxy the browser exits through.
- Two tests named a clause they could not see: deleting `end_use` entirely, or hoisting the per-engine budget read out of the loop, left the whole suite green.

Everything else groups into the browser launch counting inside `maxTimeout`, one request at a time per session, the two engines agreeing on `disableMedia`, cookies, response headers, refusal wording and `solution.turnstile_token`, the passthrough (it honours `HOST`, reuses a session per site, and no longer pins a site's error page for the whole cache window), and the dead code the takeovers left behind.

`tabs_till_verify` is now a declared capability rather than a field one engine drops in silence, which is the counter-example the engine-layer law names, and `pipeline.verdict` reads the same fact off that capability instead of a second hardcoded copy.

FlareSolverr is audited through `fe5e1e8` (3.5.1 and 3.5.2): nothing to take, and the ledger says why.

## How it was tested

- Browser-free suite: 442 tests, green, and green under each documented environment setting. That sweep is now a CI step; it was red before this branch.
- Every new test was seen failing first: the clause it names was deleted, the test run red, then the clause restored. A separate mutation pass over 36 clauses found one survivor, which is now bound.
- Live, through an isolated container: interstitials cleared on both engines (3/3 each across two hosts), a real search page solved on both, PDF bodies, a Turnstile token, cookie-scope A/B, `maxTimeout` held on a tight budget, and two requests on one session serialising.
- Live through both proxy chains with a real indexer app: the built-in passthrough and the external proxy in front of `/v1` each passed the indexer test and returned identical result sets.
- Detection was re-checked against seven live gates captured today, four hosts, English and localized. One is kept as a fixture: the existing samples predate Cloudflare randomising the challenge element ids, so they exercise markup no gate still serves.

Not covered, so not claimed: the paid CAPTCHA escalation (needs a provider key), and the Chrome `tabs_till_verify` press against a live checkbox.

## Checklist

- [x] The browser-free suite passes: `PYTHONPATH=src uv run --no-project python -m unittest discover -s src -p 'test_*.py' -t src`
- [x] Commit messages follow `type(scope): summary`, at most 72 characters, with no em dash, no bare `#N`, and no AI attribution
- [x] No names of target sites in commits, docs, or code comments (see CONTRIBUTING.md for the words the check also rejects)
- [x] A change a client can notice lands for both engines, or the pull request names the capability one engine does not have
- [x] The `/v1` request and response shape is unchanged, apart from new optional fields
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` has an `[Unreleased]` entry if someone running Solverr could notice the change, and none otherwise

author: jtrefon
body:
## Red

`test(plugin): discovery must ignore manifest-less state dirs (red)` — 9c84734

The v2 runtime keeps per-plugin state at `~/.config/amber/plugins/<id>/plugin.conf` — the
same root external plugins install into. Discovery reported every manifest-less directory
as an incompatible plugin, so each state directory surfaced as an **unversioned ghost of a
real plugin** (`/plugin list` showed `clock v [incompatible] (manifest.json missing or
unreadable)` beside the runtime's `clock on v0.4.0`), and an id with no bundled plugin
became a phantom external entry in `/get plugin list`.

## Root causes (verified in code)

1. `lib/plugin.cpp:discover()` treated every subdirectory as a plugin candidate; `parse_manifest`
   then failed and the directory was recorded as `Incompatible` with an empty version.
2. `FeedManager::refresh_plugin_feed` hung `get.plugin.<id>` beside the static `list` command,
   so the drawer of `/get plugin` was `list` + one row per plugin — a command list that drowns
   as the bundled set grows.
3. A third surface (the root `/plugin` namespace) duplicated listing and offered a second write
   path, against D17 in the tracker.
4. `refresh_completions()` reset the tree and re-merged only the v1 manifests + MCP + plugin
   commands: every other feed (model, policy, job, provider) lost its leaves on any rebuild —
   a plugin toggle, an install, an MCP connect — until the next restart.

## Proposal (what this does)

- **Discovery requires a manifest.** A directory with `plugin.conf` alone is host state, not an
  install; broken manifests still surface as `Incompatible`.
- **Command-first, single-rooted surface.** Ids are values under their verb:
  `get.plugin.info.<id>` (state/tier/version in the help) and `set.plugin.on|off.<id>`.
  The drawers of `/get plugin` and `/set plugin` are command lists whatever registers.
  The subtree comes from a pure builder (`tui/plugin_feed.{h,cpp}`) the tests drive directly.
- **The root `/plugin` namespace is retired.** `/set plugin install|uninstall`, manifest detail
  merged into `/get plugin info <id>` (runtime status + author/url/license/dir/tools/error),
  external settings at `/get|/set plugin settings`. Install stages a plugin **disabled**;
  uninstall stops a live plugin before its files disappear.
- **Feeds survive a rebuild.** `refresh_completions()` re-merges the live feeds at the end; the
  hand-wired plugin refresh is gone.
- **Shipped plugins are versioned 0.4.0** (none is production-certified yet).
- Docs updated in the same increment: developer guide, framework spec, README, tracker (new
  decision **D23** superseding the packaging half of D17), website pages, AGENTS.md.

## Found while here, fixed not silenced

- `tests/completions_test.cpp`: **nine tests defined after `main()` never ran**. `main` now calls
  every test; that surfaced two stale assertions — the merge test looked up
  `live_srv.do_thing` instead of `mcp.live_srv.do_thing`, and `subagent.max`'s 1..16 range
  existed only in prose, so the JSON now carries `type: int, range: [1, 16]`.
- **A disabled plugin could not be re-enabled** (live-tested: `/set plugin on hello` after an off
  failed with "could not enable"). `CommandCapability` moved its `CommandSpec` into the registry,
  `PanelCapability` its `PanelSpec`, `WalletCapability` its fetch, so the replayed install saw an
  empty declaration; a `ToolCapability` handed a finished `unique_ptr` degraded to a silent
  decline for the same reason. Install is now repeatable (copy, not move) and the single-shot
  tool form is gone — the factory is the contract, and it runs on every activation. Red test:
  `bundled_hello_plugin_contributes_the_hello_command`'s cycle, plus a tool-factory cycle test.
- `plugin_console_lines`' hint still said `/set plugin <id> on|off`; the console test now pins
  the line.
- `tests/plugin_runtime_test.cpp`: range-for over a member of a temporary `PluginStatus`
  (cppcheck `danglingTempReference`); `bench/report.cpp`: a shadowed `eff` (cppcheck
  `shadowVariable` on 2.19).

## Green

7 commits on the branch; deliverables are 9c84734 → b5625a7 (discovery), 29c1257/24e52be
(cycle red + cppcheck), 8d36252 (surface), 6118f5f (versions), 88f9f4b (docs), 490f5dd (bench),
then dede2d1 → 7eb0510 (re-activation red + fix) and 51a10fb (console hint).

- `make test` green: run_tests 748 passed / 0 failed, completions_test (45 tests), plugin_test.
- `make check` clean; local cppcheck 2.19 `make analyze` clean; clang-tidy clean on the new code.

## Live smoke (TUI, scratch HOME, local model service untouched)

- `/get plugin ` drawer: `list`, `info`, `settings` only — no plugin ids.
- `/get plugin list`: every plugin with `v0.4.0`; console footer reads
  `toggle a plugin with /set plugin on|off <id>`.
- `/set plugin off hello` → drawer help flips to `off, bundled v0.4.0` / "enable this plugin";
  `/set plugin on hello` → back on, state persisted to `plugin.conf`, no "could not enable".

author: chris1howell
body:
# 2-line LCD backlight type (Monochrome / RGB)

Adds a web UI control for the OpenEVSE controller's 2-line character LCD
backlight type, on branch `RGB_LCD` across three repos. Previously this could
only be changed over RAPI directly (Blocked by OpenEVSE_esp32_firmware) or from the controller's own front-panel
menu; there was no way to set it from the app.

## Background

The Adafruit RGBLCD character display used on classic OpenEVSE V6 boards (and
in JuiceBox v2 conversions, which reuse the JuiceBox's RGB-backlit LED Strip) can
run in one of two backlight modes:

- **Monochrome** — single-colour backlight.
- **RGB** — full colour, used for the state-colour backlight (green/yellow/
  teal/red/violet, see `docs/lcd.md`) and required for a JuiceBox v2
  replacement.

The controller firmware already exposed this as `$S0 0|1` (RAPI) /
`ECF_MONO_LCD` (EEPROM flags bit `0x0100`), gated behind the `LCD16X2` +
`RGBLCD` compile flags — only the `m328p_LCD_WIFI` build defines both;
`m328p_core` ("WiFi, no text LCD") defines neither, so `$S0` NAKs there. No
change was needed on the controller firmware (`open_evse`) side. `OpenEVSE_Lib`
could already *read* the flag but had no method to *set* it — that was the
actual gap this closes.

## Changes by repo

### OpenEVSE_Lib (branch `OpenEVSE9`, commit `8e93b3a`)

- `OPENEVSE_LCD_TYPE_MONO` / `OPENEVSE_LCD_TYPE_RGB` constants
  (`src/openevse.h`).
- `OpenEVSEClass::setLcdType(uint8_t type, callback)` (`src/openevse.cpp`) —
  sends `$S0 0|1`, following the same validate-then-`sendCmd` shape as
  `setServiceLevel()`/`feature()`.
- Bumped `library.json` to `0.0.24`.

### openevse_esp32_firmware (branch `RGB_LCD`, commit `b572f4c5`)

- `EvseMonitor::setLcdType()` (`src/evse_monitor.h`/`.cpp`) — calls
  `OpenEVSEClass::setLcdType()`, then re-reads `$GE` to refresh the cached
  flags word and fires `_settings_changed`, matching the pattern used by
  `enableDiodeCheck()` and friends.
- `EvseManager::setLcdType()` (`src/evse_man.h`) — thin pass-through, next to
  the existing `getLcdType()`.
- `app_config.cpp` — `lcd_type` (`"mono"` / `"rgb"`) added to `GET /config`
  and handled in the `POST /config` deserializer, unconditionally (like
  `diode_check`, `boot_lock`, etc. — there is no RAPI capability bit for
  "has a physical LCD", so unsupported builds just NAK the `$S0` silently).
- `platformio.ini` — `openevse/OpenEVSE` pin bumped `0.0.23` → `0.0.24` (both
  the main `[common]` lib_deps and the `native_simulator` env).

### gui-nightshift (branch `RGB_LCD`, commit `a2ef421`)

- Display settings page (`src/routes/settings/Display.svelte`) — new "2 Line
  LCD" field, a Monochrome/"Red - Green - Blue" segmented control (same
  pattern as the existing Theme/Clock controls), gated on `lcd_type` being
  present in the config store. Defaults to RGB when absent.
- Description note: "JuiceBox v2 Replacement select Red - Green - Blue."
- i18n keys added to `en.json` and all three translated catalogs
  (`source/es.json`, `source/fr.json`, `source/hu.json`) to satisfy the
  locale-parity test.
- Tests added to `Display.test.js` covering the default-RGB state and the
  write-on-change behaviour.

author: lete0301
body:
Closes #48 · Gitea: [admin/afk-clicker#28](https://dev.tailbe22cd.ts.net/gitea/admin/afk-clicker/issues/28)

The window's height floor was `690 * s`, tuned by #14 for the single combined page that existed before #40 split it into tabs. Every pane has been shorter than that floor ever since: at the minimum window the tallest pane (Clicking with Eating) used 380px of 528, and Hotkey sat **78% empty**.

`WINDOW_MIN_H = 560`, derived by measuring the tallest pane's real content span at native scale and again at the compound worst case (`_dpi_s ≈ 0.75` × the 90% step), plus margin for font metrics this box cannot rule out. Measured independently twice, by the spec author and the implementer, agreeing.

The **tallest** pane is the binding constraint, not the smallest: nothing in this app scrolls, so a floor below what Clicking + Eating needs puts its lower rows out of reach rather than merely making them tight. Eating is Minecraft-only, so that case sets the bound.

Floor and default launch size stay one number, unlike the width axis that #41 had to split — there is no vertical collapsed state to gate, and the empty space this fixes is what a fresh launch already shows.

## The part that nearly shipped broken

The first attempt passed 289/289 and was visibly broken. At the new floor the Eating section's **"Hold for" row was clipped off the bottom edge**, unreachable, and the layout did not recover after 2+ seconds of continuous event-loop servicing. The suite missed it because the test had been given a settling loop that drove the panes to a fixed point the real app never reached.

Root cause: `eat_card` is built once and only pack-toggled, so re-packing does not give it its final height synchronously — `card()`'s own `<Configure>` redraw grows it across ~6 idle rounds (`eat_card` 129→141px, the pane's `natural` 196→383px). `_select()`/`_set_content_tab()`'s explicit `_fill_pane()` ran once, before that finished, and nothing re-triggered it: toggling a child's pack state inside a `pack_propagate(False)` pane fires no `<Configure>` on the pane. At `690` the oversized spacers still fit by luck. At `560` they overflowed and Tk unmapped the bottom spacer.

The fix ties the recompute to the event that was previously silent: `card()` takes an optional `on_settle`, called at the tail of every `_redraw()`, wired for `eat_card` to re-run `_fill_pane()`. Not a retry loop and not a clamp — a clamp on stale data can suppress the overflow but cannot produce the correct split.

The test's settling loop is **removed**, and it now converges on the first synchronous call. That is the evidence the race is actually closed rather than hidden.

291 tests green, and verified by driving the live app at the floor in both click orders with screenshots, not by the suite alone.

author: vimalvijayakumar1983
body:
## Why

The Adam & Eve Specialized Medical Centre test call on 12 September asked "What kind of departments you are having there?" and the agent said it had no verified information, while "What kind of services you are providing there?" returned the specialty list. The second answer was then read aloud as a markdown list ("- **Pediatrics**: ...").

## What

**Retrieval**

- "having" is a stop word, like "have", "has" and "had". Before this, every card had to contain the word "having" to pass the structured topic filter.
- "providing", "offering" and the "specialising" forms are dropped from a service-capability question the same way "provide" and "offer" already were, and "are/is ... providing" counts as a capability question. A bare "What are you offering?" asks for the service listing itself.
- "department", "specialty", "service" and "division" expand to each other as semantic variants, since clinic sites label the same listing "specialties" or "services" and group sites label it "divisions".

**Speech**

- The single-pass reply policy and the agent system prompt now state that every reply is spoken aloud: no markdown, asterisks, bullet points, numbered lists or headings; several items are named in one sentence separated by commas.

## Verification

- Reproduction test with an Adam & Eve style specialty listing: five phrasings ("departments ... having", "Which departments", "What divisions", "services ... providing", "What are you offering") all fail on the previous ranker and now retrieve the Pediatrics listing.
- The evidence-only instructions test asserts the plain-speech rule.
- Backend suite: 1980 passed, 33 skipped.

## After merge

No re-index or re-approval needed. Repeat the Adam & Eve call with the departments question.

author: varunhiremath
body:
`sessions.status` has been in the schema from the start and both backends could write it — but **no screen ever did**. So every session stayed `live` forever, and the app looked on a Wednesday exactly as it had on Sunday afternoon with a game on court.

## When a session is over

`isSessionOver({ session, games })`, derived first and stored second — the same rule the bracket line-ups follow:

- **Every fixture has a score** → over. Derived, so no write, no permission, and the same answer on every phone the instant the last score lands. This is the normal case and nothing is stored for it.
- **An admin said so** → over. The one thing the games cannot express: the evening that ran out of daylight with games unplayed. `status` is now written for this and nothing else, from **Finish the session**; `endedEarly()` is what offers **Reopen the session** back.

## What being over changes

| | Running | Finished |
|---|---|---|
| Club card chip | `live` (yellow) | `finished` (neutral) |
| Club actions | Tell everyone · Reshuffle · Change the finish · Finish the session | **Start the next session** |
| Today | On court, you play next, enter the score | Result · how you finished · share · final table · *"Ready for the next one?"* |

Today is a **different render**, not the running layout greyed out. "On court" and "you play next" are lies once there is nothing to play, and leaving them up was the whole complaint. Every mid-session control disappears for the same reason — offering "Reshuffle schedule" under a finished session is noise at best and a trap at worst.

A session an admin ended early says so rather than pretending: *"Ended with 12 games unplayed."*

## A trap fixed on the way

`getActiveSession()` was "the newest session **not marked final**". The moment anything could actually be marked final, that would have handed the app back an abandoned session from three weeks ago — because that older row was still marked live. It is now simply the newest session; whether there is anything left to play is a question the games answer.

## Verification

author: flemming-n-larsen
body:
Simple work. Two defects found while running CH-185 enter the inbox as proposed goals, for you to accept or decline.

## G-018 — coordination does not see in-flight claims

`clue id coordinate` seeds the allocator branch from the local ledger, and a branch's ledger additions reach `main` only at merge. So the allocator starts believing every number above the last merged claim is free.

It handed out an already-held identity three times in one session: `CH-181`, then `PDR-058`, then `AC-190`–`AC-192`, each held by one open pull request (#207). Each was caught only by reading that branch's ledger by hand. `clue validate` cannot catch it either — the colliding artifact is on a branch it never sees.

The gap is worst where the feature matters most: a repository enables coordination precisely when several people are working at once, which is exactly when unmerged claims exist.

## G-019 — the full loop cannot be completed without hand-editing the ledger

A change workspace's `tasks.md` and `open-questions.md` carry IDs. `clue validate` requires every artifact ID in the ledger. No command puts them there — `clue id next` rejects the non-numeric prefix, `clue id live` refuses an unreserved ID. The library has an opaque reservation path; nothing on the command line reaches it.

So the practice is to open `.clue/id-ledger.yaml` and type the entries in, which CH-181 did and CH-185 did after it. That is the append-only log whose own guidance says never to hand-edit it, because Git's union merge combines independent additions. Cliewen's own full loop therefore cannot be completed without breaking that rule — which makes the rule unenforceable and teaches every adopter that hand-editing is normal.

G-019 also names a question worth settling rather than inheriting: these entries persist after the digest deletes the artifacts, and the repository is inconsistent about the state they should end in — several changes left them `live`, two retired them.

## Notes

Both are `proposed` — the inbox. Promotion to `accepted` is yours.

Route is simple: a proposed goal changes no accepted contract. It is an idea awaiting a decision, and the decision is the promotion.

`clue validate` OK at 251 artifacts; whitespace clean. No CHANGELOG entry owed — nothing here touches `clue` behaviour, generated skill text, or an artifact materialized by `clue init`/`scaffold`.

author: inso1337
body:
Closes #940.

## The defect

`src/revl/boundary.py` collected two different populations under two names that the renderer printed as one:

- `stats["emissions"]` was a **set of labels** (`k.g`), built at `walk_expr` by labelling `call`/`req` nodes whose service method declares `spec["emission"]`, plus the spawn/instance seam and the arrow-parameter seam.
- `stats["compensated"]` was an **int of emit steps**, incremented in `walk_steps` for every step with `kind == "emit"` and a non-`None` `compensate`.

`src/revl/__main__.py` then printed them as `emissions: <labels> (N compensated)`, which reads as *N of the labels above are compensated*. It is not that number: it counts steps, so it can exceed the number of labels printed beside it, and two steps naming the same emission count twice.

## Exit taken: **(a)**, made type-compatible

Compensation is now a **set of labels**, keyed off the *same* expression the `emissions` enumeration labels, and reported as `len()` of that set.

`_boundary` gained a helper `_call_emission_label(node)` that returns `{label: declared_capabilities}` for a `call` node crossing the boundary through a `req` target or through a provision-method call off a spawn handle. Both the `emissions` walk and the compensated walk now call it, so **the compensated count is a subset of the printed label list by construction**, not by two walks that happen to agree. A label compensated at two sites is one compensated emission.

`(b)` was rejected for the reason in the issue: it leaves a number whose meaning depends on the reader parsing the wording. After `(a)` the report is internally consistent — the parenthetical now says `(N of them compensated)` and the claim is one the data supports.

**The JSON type is unchanged.** `"compensated"` is still an `integer`; it is `len()` of the set rather than a step tally. That matters, because it is consumed as an int:

- `src/revl/plan.py` `_totals` sums it (`sum(s.get("compensated") or 0 ...)`) and `emissionSurface.totals.compensated` renders it;
- `schema/revl-interchange-v1.schema.json` `$defs.boundaryEntry` declares it `"type": "integer"`, `"minimum": 0`;
- `playground/app.js` and `site/js/playground.js` interpolate it directly.

Returning a list would have been a schema break for all four; returning `len()` is not. `src/revl/audit_diff.py`, `src/revl/policy.py` and `src/revl/query.py` were checked and do not read this field (`counterfactual.py` reads a `compensated` key, but from the WAL's `boundary_of` payload built in `backends/python/replay.py`, a different producer, untouched).

## `emissions` and compensation: **overlapping, not the same population**

This is the finding. They are not the same set, and the honest fix had to say so.

Compensation can be attached to an `emit` whose expression carries **no `key.method` label at all**: an emitting **host** `fn`/`extern` (`emit boom() compensate boom()`). That crosses the boundary, has a compensating undo, and appears in no `emissions` list — so a naive label-set count would report `compensated: 0` there, a false-safe in the opposite direction from the bug being fixed.

Rather than drop it or inflate the count, the report names it: a new **additive, optional** `compensatedHostEmissions` array of names, emitted only when non-empty, so every boundary entry written before this change is byte-identical. The render gains a `compensated host emissions: ...` clause, and the component now renders at all in that case (previously a host-compensated-only component with no emissions/awaits/externs was skipped).

The schema's `compensated` description now states the population explicitly ("counted over distinct labels, never over emit steps"), and `additionalProperties: true` already admits the new sibling.

## Tests — the divergence is the observable

Four tests in `tests/test_manifest.py`:

| test | pins |
|---|---|
| `test_boundary_compensated_counts_labels_not_emit_steps` | the motivating case: two `emit k.g(...) compensate k.g(...)` sites, one label → `compensated == 1`, and `compensated <= len(emissions)` |
| `test_audit_render_prints_the_count_as_a_subset` | the **printed** value: `emissions: k.g (1 of them compensated)`, and `"2 compensated" not in out` |
| `test_boundary_compensated_host_emission_is_named_not_counted` | the overlap: `emissions == []`, `compensated == 0`, `compensatedHostEmissions == ["boom"]` |
| `test_boundary_omits_the_host_compensation_key_when_there_is_none` | additivity: no key on `examples/user_cache.rvl`, so old entries are byte-identical |

**Three of the four fail without the fix** (verified by stashing `src/revl/boundary.py` + `src/revl/__main__.py`): `assert 2 == 1` on the first, a missing render string on the second, `assert 1 == 0` on the third. The tests assert the divergence, not the happy path where the naive int and the honest count agree.

No compiler behaviour changes. This is a reporting change: `_boundary`'s output for programs with no host-extern compensation is byte-identical, and the pre-existing `compensated == 1` assertions (`test_audit_cli_json`/Migrator, `test_plan`, `test_query`) still hold.

## Verification

- targeted: `tests/test_manifest.py` 10 passed; `test_manifest + test_interchange + test_plan + test_query + test_cardinality_260 + test_docgen_doc_status_shape` 172 passed; a broader 19-file compensated-related run 492 passed / 75 skipped
- gate/docgen: `test_gate_crate_drift` + `test_selfhost_line_coverage` + `test_roadmap_gate_bites` 86 passed
- `crates/revl-gate` needed **no** regeneration (drift test passes — verified, not assumed); the selfhost line-coverage ratchet is unmoved (no `backends/*/emit.py` touched); no roadmap item added
- `python3 tools/docgen.py --check` clean
- `ruff check backends/ tests/ src/` clean
- full `tests/` suite: **12763 passed, 991 skipped, 21 xfailed, 3 failed** — the three failures are pre-existing on `main` and not caused by this change, see below.

## The 3 full-suite failures are pre-existing on `main`

`tests/test_gate_wasm_drift.py` fails 3/17 on this branch, on `3997b829` (the base I started from) and on current `origin/main` — identically. `tools/build_gate_wasm.py`'s `source_digest()` is a pure hash of `crates/revl-gate/GENERATED.json` + `tools/build_gate_wasm.py`, and it computes `6123be18…` at all three revs against a committed `66d62595…`; the frontier mismatch is `selfhost-admit:6033bc32…` (crate) vs `…781c0c68…` (wasm crate).

The cause is `3997b829` (PR #956): it regenerated `crates/revl-gate/GENERATED.json` and did not re-stamp `crates/revl-gate-wasm/GENERATED.json`. My diff touches none of the digest inputs, which is why the computed hash is byte-identical at base, main and HEAD. It is a red on `main` today, in the full-suite (`frontend`) job — not in any required check (`backend-wasm` runs `backends/wasm/ tests/test_wasm_backend.py`, which does not collect this file).

Left alone deliberately: it is unrelated to #940 and refreshing a generated artifact is not this PR's business. `python3 tools/build_gate_wasm.py` is the fix if you want it separately.

Docs updated to match the new render (`docs/capabilities.md`, `docs/design/260-emission-cardinality-bounds.md`, `docs/time-coeffect.md`) and the field described in `docs/interchange-format.md`. No em-dashes added to any doc in the `docs/DOC-STATUS.md` inventory.

author: yschimke
body:
The Glimmer sheet has had everything the comparison needs for a while — a kit index read from Figma (#371), references pointing at kit cells rather than sets (#373), a map CI keeps current (#372) — and nothing was comparing it. Design parity ran one job, hardwired to `:catalog`.

This adopts wear-m3-catalog's two-lane shape: a second job calling the same reusable workflow, with an `artifact-branch` of its own so neither board looks like the other has gone stale.

## Where it could not be a copy of that precedent

**Different kits, so a cache of its own.** Wear's two lanes reproduce the *same* kit — both maps name `B24oss2tTeXAFykyeyusz0`, and its cache branch holds exactly that one key — which is why one importer job serves both. These two reproduce different files (`ocdacdEsnHipMJD3egzxKb` and `HKfLClZDLRyMhf4IQQLna8`) with no node in common. So this lane gets `design-parity/glimmer-reference`, and `design-parity-import.yml` gets a second job to fill it.

Separate rather than shared because of the *write*, not the contents. On contents a shared branch would have been safe: the cache is keyed by file id and `prune` defaults off, so neither import can delete the other's nodes. But an import ends in a plain non-fast-forward `git push` with no retry, and the `concurrency` group serialises runs rather than the jobs inside one — two importers on one branch would race, and the loser would fail having already paid for its Figma traffic. Separate branches also keep a failed Material 3 import from withholding Glimmer's refs.

**`desktop-render` defaults to `true`.** This module renders through Robolectric and AGP, because `androidx.xr.glimmer` ships only as an AAR with no Compose Multiplatform port. Inheriting the default would install Mesa and run the render under xvfb for a Skiko daemon that is not the one drawing here. `design-artifacts.yml` already sets it false for this module.

**`glimmer-design-map.json` is in `cache-paths`.** The gate hashes `design-map.json` — the committed one, which belongs to `:catalog` — *before* `design-map-command` copies ours into place. Without that entry, this lane's cache key would track the Material 3 map: edit a Glimmer reference and the run would skip on a key that never moved. Same reason wear's Remote job puts its snapshot pin on the list.

## The rest

`design-map-command` runs no Gradle — the map is committed, so a discovery pass would re-derive a file the checkout already holds. It does install `platforms;android-37.0`: this is the only hook that runs before the render, and `:glimmer-catalog` is the repo's one AGP module. Same step `ci.yml` carries, same `-37.0` spelling that only fails in CI.

`block-on-verdict: false`, following wear-m3-catalog#145. The lane gates nothing, and a design-led board that genuinely diverges would be red on every run — which then cannot report a render crash, a lost reference cache or an expired token. The verdict still reaches the job summary, a warning annotation and the `blocked` output. Worth revisiting once the board has a baseline.

Also corrects the header comment in `design-artifacts.yml`, which still said Glimmer publishes no Figma kit — the premise #357 disproved.

## Verification

- Both workflows parse; jobs resolve to `[parity, glimmer]` and `[import, glimmer]`.
- `design-map-command` executed against a stub `sdkmanager`: exits 0 and leaves `design-map.json` holding 8 components / 9 refs, all under `HKfLClZDLRyMhf4IQQLna8`. Working tree restored afterwards.
- `ButtonSticker` carries an array-shaped `ref` (its `size=Large` axis). Confirmed `entryRefs` in `@design-parity/core` normalizes both the string and list forms, so the importer and resolver handle it.
- The reference cache import has been dispatched from this branch, so `design-parity/glimmer-reference` exists before this merges.

## Scope

Depth is capped at what the annotations reach today: 8 components, 9 references. #374 is what unlocks the rest — with no interaction states drawn, 34 of 50 kit cells stay unreachable. That stays parked.

One upstream nit found while reading, not blocking and not fixed here: the fileKey scan at `design-parity-reusable.yml:406` uses `select(startswith("figma:"))` directly on `.components[].ref`, which throws on a list-shaped ref. It only runs when no `reference-cache-branch` is configured, which is why neither this repo nor wear has hit it — but it would fail on both repos' committed maps.

author: miacorindolf
body:
An actual PAPER LTC fill exposed a broker identity mismatch: orders use the native LTC/USD listing UUID, while the position API returns a legacy LTCUSD UUID. Querying only the listing UUID returns404 and leaves a tick-requested full exit unable to reconcile its available balance.

Resolve a missing individual position through the complete portfolio and GET /v2/assets/<observed UUID>. Accept only an exact canonical UUID/symbol resolution, retain raw evidence, preserve the broker's precise quantity, and reject ambiguous balances or contradictory direct lookups. Retain verified alias proof so reciprocal equity/native account reservations recognize the same owned exposure. Same-UUID concatenated display symbols retain the existing parser behavior. A404 alone no longer establishes flatness.

Planner9 [13], native crypto lifecycle/selection feedback. No changed strategy threshold, ranking, sizing fraction, partial target, time window or LIVE endpoint. Full exits still target the entire currently available balance; actual broker partial fills are reconciled before the next residual sale.

Validation:57 targeted tests passed in152.08s on isolated DB26 (position aliases, real SQL owner, account bridge, PAPER HTTP). Regression reproduces the actual listing/portfolio mismatch, fee-reduced balance, two actual partial exits, wrong UUID resolution, wrong symbol, ambiguous balances, direct foreign responses and changed account balances. Initial verification found an unnecessary lookup for same-UUID concatenated symbols; corrected and the full targeted set passed. Local review passes covered transport/CID/flatness recovery and exact-identity/account-budget semantics. Running tree remains unchanged during the held position; operator recovery and subsequent rollout are recorded separately.

author: seabbs-bot
body:
Adds `plot_delays()`, a plot tool for the empirical delay distribution of a linelist.

Fixes #743.

## What the vignettes were doing by hand

The two hand-rolled blocks that motivated the issue share one shape:

1. take the delay as it was observed, `stime_lwr - ptime_lwr`,
2. bin it at the daily censoring width,
3. normalise to a proportion so datasets of different sizes compare,
4. draw it as columns, optionally with the true delay distribution over the top and optionally with a dashed line marking a bound.

What differs is only the trimmings. The getting started vignette compares two datasets side by side and overlays `dlnorm()` at the simulation truth. The left truncation vignette plots one dataset and marks `delay_min` with a dashed line. So the function's job is steps 1 to 4, with the comparison, the reference distribution and the line as arguments.

## Signature

```r
plot_delays(
  data,
  by = NULL,
  binwidth = 1,
  delay_min = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  family = "lognormal"
)
```

- `data` is an `epidist_linelist_data` or `epidist_aggregate_data` object, or a named list of them to compare, with the names labelling the strata. This mirrors `plot_events()`, which also takes the data class rather than pre-computed columns, and it means the comparison case needs no `bind_rows()` and no `type` column in user code.
- `by` stratifies a single dataset by one of its columns, named and behaving as in `plot_events()`. It is rejected alongside a list, which is already stratified by its names.
- `binwidth` defaults to 1, the daily censoring the data usually has. The plotted `density` is the proportion divided by `binwidth`, so the columns sit on the scale of `reference` at any width.
- `delay_min` draws the dashed line the left truncation vignette draws. When it is not given the `delay_min` column of the data is used, which is where the marginal model reads the same bound from.
- `reference` and `family` take the distributional parameters of a delay distribution, as `c(mu = 1.8, sigma = 0.5)`. This follows the package's own family machinery through `.validate_family()`, `.delay_family()` and `.delay_density_grid()`, so gamma and Weibull work as well as lognormal, rather than asking the user for a density function and its R-side argument names.

Counts are weighted by the `n` column when the data has one, so an `epidist_aggregate_data` object gives the same plot as the linelist it was aggregated from. The palette, the theme, the `@family plot` grouping and the `.check_ggplot2()` guard follow `plot_events()` and `plot.epidist_delay_draws()`.

## No circular dependency on the naive model

The delay is computed from the linelist columns directly, the single `mutate()` that `as_epidist_naive_model.epidist_linelist_data()` also does. The function never constructs a model object, so the getting started vignette can draw the observed delays in its data section without introducing a modelling step ahead of its narrative, which was the objection behind #743.

## Vignette blocks this replaces, as follow-up

No vignette is touched here, since #736 is rewriting them and #708 is on vignette staleness. The call sites, at their current lines on `main`:

- `vignettes/epidist.Rmd.orig` lines 304-351, the `<details>` block that builds `delay_histogram`. It becomes one call taking a named list of the two datasets plus `reference = c(mu = secondary_dist[["mu"]], sigma = secondary_dist[["sigma"]])`. Note that `obs_cens` and `obs_cens_trunc_samp` are plain data frames there, so the follow-up also has to convert them with `as_epidist_linelist_data()`, which `obs_cens` needs an `obs_time` for.
- `vignettes/left-truncation.Rmd.orig` lines 105-116, the `hist` chunk. It becomes `plot_delays(linelist, delay_min = delay_min)`, since `linelist` is already built on line 100.

The third block #743 named, in `vignettes/faq.Rmd.orig`, is not a call site. On current `main` that vignette has no empirical delay histogram left. Its remaining bar chart, line 309, is `add_predicted_draws()` output, a posterior predicted delay PMF rather than observed data, and the prior predictive histogram the issue was likely pointing at plots parameter draws, which `plot()` on `epidist_delay_draws` already serves. So this lands with two call sites, not three.

Tracked as #761.

## Testing

Red, green, refactor, a commit at each step. 55 assertions in `tests/testthat/test-plot_delays.R`, in the style of the existing plot tests: the class and layers of the returned object, the binned data it plots, the proportions summing to one within each stratum, aggregate counts matching the linelist, the reference line matching `dlnorm()` and `dgamma()` at the parameters given, the minimum delay line, the theme and palette, and the input errors. No snapshot image tests, as the repo has none for plots.

This was opened by a bot. Please ping @seabbs for any questions.

body:
## Phase A2: Role-aware layout rendering (facility-mfe, ADR-0016)

Extends `facility-mfe` (the console's Module Federation remote for this context) to render and configure the functional location roles introduced by Phase A1 (`feat(placement): functional location roles`, ADR-0016, PR #65). Pure `web/` change — no Go/backend changes, per the phased plan.

### What shipped

- `types.ts`: `LocationRole` union; `LocationSlot` gains `role`/`dockFlow`/`activities`, `LocationType` gains `role` — matching Phase A1's `dto.go` shapes exactly.
- New `roles.ts`: per-role glyph + accent color metadata. `Storage` renders deliberately muted (it's the pre-ADR-0016 default and the overwhelming majority of real slots) — every other role is what this feature exists to make visible.
- New `components/RoleBadge.tsx`: a compact `RoleBadge` (glyph + full label/dockFlow in its title) and a `RoleFilterChips` toggle row.
- `FacilityScreen.tsx`: every slot chip now shows its `RoleBadge`; a role filter row narrows the whole zone→aisle→slot tree to just one role, collapsing non-matching zones/aisles entirely rather than showing them empty — e.g. "show me this site's dock doors" without scrolling past a wall of storage slots.
- `configure/LocationTypesPanel.tsx`: the register form gains a Role select (defaults to Storage, so a bare submit still behaves exactly as before), and the location-types table gains a Role column.

### Verification (all real)

- `npm test -- --run`: 42/42 pass (10 new: `RoleBadge.test.tsx`, `FacilityScreen.test.tsx`, including a full filter-narrows/empty-state/clear-filter flow against a two-zone mocked layout).
- `npm run lint` (oxlint): clean.
- `npx tsc -b --force`: clean.
- `npm run build`: succeeds. The `[Module Federation DTS] TYPE-001` warning during build is **pre-existing** — confirmed by building the unmodified `origin/develop` `web/` baseline first and seeing the identical warning there; it does not fail the build (exit 0) either way.
- **Live verification against the real cluster**: port-forwarded the actual `facility-layout` OLTP pod (resolved by name, not the shared-selector Service, per the fleet's known port-forwarding pitfall), registered a real `WH1` site with a `Dock`-role zone/aisle/slot (`dockFlow: Outbound`) and a `Storage`-role zone/aisle/slot side by side, and confirmed `GET /sites/WH1/layout` returns exactly the wire shape `types.ts` now expects — proving the new TypeScript types match production JSON, not just the mocked test fixtures. Also confirmed CORS (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost:5186`) against the remote's real dev origin, and that `vite --port 5186` serves both `/` and `remoteEntry.js` with 200.

### Not in this phase

Per the plan, this stays scoped to rendering/configuring the ADR-0016 role vocabulary already shipped in Phase A1. Phase B3 (cross-context follow-ons, e.g. a floor-plan/geometry renderer using ADR-0017's data) remains separate future work.

body:
#71 で「仕組みが要る」として残した 4 本のうち 3 本。**rule は 39 → 42 本**になり、
L1/L2 の catalog はこれで埋まる。

| rule | 何を見るか | 仕組み |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `internal-jargon` | 社内でしか通じない語 | `chaff.yaml` の `jargon` |
| `required-sections` | この種類の文書に無いと困る見出し | `chaff.yaml` の `required_sections` |
| `proper-noun-density` | 固有名詞の密度 | 品詞解析の PROPN |

4 本目の `list-length-variance` は #72 で実測して落としたので戻していない
（箇条書き 27 個の変動係数が中央値 21% で、揃うのが普通だった）。

## chaff は中身を持たない

```yaml
jargon:            # 社内でしか通じない語
  - 横展開
  - 握る
  - 巻き取

required_sections: # この種類の文書に無いと困る見出し
  - リスク
  - 費用
```

```
1:1   error   「リスク、費用」の見出しがありません
5:1   warning 「横展開」は社内でしか通じないかもしれません（そういう語が 3 箇所）
5:20  warning 「握る」は社内でしか通じないかもしれません（そういう語が 3 箇所）
```

**何が社内用語かも、何の節が必須かも組織ごとに違う。chaff が決めると、合わない組織で rule ごと切られる。**

書いていなければ何も言わない。「用語を登録してください」とも言わない。押しつけない。

spec の初版は `required-sections` の見出し一覧を genre pack が言語別に持つ設計だった。
案は spec に残したが、採らなかった理由も書いた。

## 活用に当てるところで 1 度直した

利用者は辞書形で書く（`握る`）が、本文は活用している（`握った`）。最初の実装は表層しか見ておらず、
**当たらなかった**。

表層でも**原形**でも当てるようにした。品詞解析があれば原形で当たり、無くても表層で当たるので、
`requires: [pos]` は付けていない。

複合動詞はこれでも当たらない。形態素に割れて原形が現れないため。

```
巻き取ります → 巻き[巻く] + 取り[取る]     「巻き取る」はどこにも無い
```

語幹（`巻き取`）で書けば表層で当たる。**how_to_fix にそう書いた**ので、
当たらなかった人がその場で直せる。

author: gunbai-bot[bot]
body:
NAMESPACE-XL **XL-0** on the v2 route. This PR lands the instrument and **does not claim XL-0 is delivered** — `StageXL0Denominator` stays `NotDerivable`, because on the tree the production route yields, the denominator's own class does not reach the collector.

## What lands

- **`v2.compiler.reference_site_collector`** — the mention producer `v2.compiler.resolution_provenance` had been missing since it was written (its only `ReferenceSite` constructors were five fixture rows). Per-segment spine unwrap derived from the module name; the cheap reject is the first step of `v2.std.qualified_name qualified_name_from_node` itself, acceptance-preserving, and both `Bool` spine predicates are deleted rather than left as a second authority on the same shape; unreadable roots as a typed, located, **counted** refusal that travels with the result.
- **`std.repair_input_origin`** — the DeclarationRef-carrying source-declaration carrier the module's header defers to XL-0B/C, with its three departures from `std.coercion TypeDeclarationProvenance` stated beside the type (§3b).
- **`v2.compiler.repair_input_origin_roster`** — the producer and its digest lines, carrying the unreadable-root refusal through the seam.
- **Carrier edits** — `NotDerivable` with the cause stated from execution, and `RepairInputOriginRosterProducer` requiring a **non-empty** denominator over the production route so the earlier claim cannot be re-made on the same evidence.

- **`v2.workflow.floor_pure_producer_share`** — the production-route fixture ingest enrolled **warm**. The probes were returning `budget_interrupted` / `right_censored` at the per-claim CPU deadline — *interrupted before verdict*, which is neither pass nor fail, so the lane blocked on a missing answer rather than a wrong one. The floor builds a fresh evaluation frame per claim, so module-scope `data` rows do not share across it and `long/` cannot help a *changed* witness. The seam is the **ingest, not the collection**: that roster keeps normalize out so each claim still executes the stage it names, and these claims name the collector. Filed as the third specimen on `gunbc.recurring_failure_mode.shared_precondition_re_derived_once_per_claim_frame`.

## What the collector sees on the production route

Measured end-to-end through the real ingest (`module_roots_from_source_root_ingest` → `normalized_tree_roots_to_nodes`), over **every** ingested root, and cross-checked against XL-3 and XL-4 on their own routes.

| reference class | reaches | owning capability |
|---|---|---|
| bare same-module value reference, outside a call | **yes** | — |
| parameter reference | **yes** | — |
| type name in **parameter** position (imported or user-declared) | **yes** | — |
| type name in **field** position, even spelled bare | no — **cause UNVERIFIED** | not yet attributed: collector or tree |
| call argument | no | v2 body-lowering repair (XL-2, gunbc#11207) |
| callee name | no | v2 body-lowering repair (XL-2, gunbc#11207) |
| **qualified / dotted reference, any position** | **no** | **dotted-reference capability** |

**The last row is why XL-0 has no denominator.** An import→containment denominator is made of references that *cross a module boundary*; a bare same-module name resolves inside its own module and contributes nothing. So the surviving population is the part XL-0 cannot use, and a non-empty site list must not be read as a working instrument.

**The trigger is the cross-module capability, not the lowering repair.** Body lowering restores the call rows and nothing else; the qualified row is independent of calls and would still be missing afterwards. A trigger naming less than the capability it restores is retired while the capability stays dead (§4b(3)).

**"Type position" is too coarse a phrase to use here.** The same bare name reaches from a parameter and does not reach from a field, so a trigger named for "type positions" would cover one class that reaches and one that does not.

**The field row is reproduced on two routes, and its cause is still deliberately unattributed.** The tree-side discriminator has now run: on this route the *whole* `type Wrapper { f: T }` declaration — the type name, the field name, **and** the field type — is findable in the ingested tree as neither an atom nor a named edge, while a parameter-type control is present. The XL-4 lane measured the same on its own fixture and route and also left the cause unverified.

Two independent reproductions raise confidence in the **measurement**; neither attributes it. Two hypotheses remain and no fixture here separates them: normalization drops such a declaration, or it lives in a third representation neither an atom search nor a label search reaches. That distinction decides the owner — if the declaration is absent from the tree, a collector-side trigger would never fire — so no capability is named and no trigger is attached. The dotted case is why: an absence measured through one representation looked like a tree loss and was my own exclusion.

## Evidence

Every deficiency row is enrolled as a **measurement of what is true today**, so it goes red when the class is repaired and the repair must re-state what changed rather than silently widening a denominator nobody re-measured. Two walls make the census population itself a subject: it must speak for every ingested root, and the collection must be total.

## Open, and stated rather than implied

- Whether v2 resolution reads dotted body access is **unanswered**. Six harnesses of mine failed their own controls; the question is dispatched to a fresh lane. `v2.compiler.resolve` containing no dot-access reader is a **prior**, not a finding.
- Imports are consumed before the normalized tree, so the collector's import arm is empty **by construction** on this route; the classification is kept for a parse-tree consumer.
- Qualified `other.T` in a *field* type is untested on all three routes, and deliberately so: it would now be absent for two independent reasons, so it can discriminate nothing.
- The record-declaration absence above is measured on two routes and attributed on neither.

author: redtear1115
body:
`.docgrad.yml` 新增 `docs_files`：把 `docs_dirs` 之外的**單一** markdown 檔以**一般文件**（`type: 'doc'`）納入語料。

**`reference/rubric.md` 未改動，`rubric_hash` 不變，★1–★5 錨點文字一字未動。**

## 起因

oikos 要把 root 層的 `PRODUCT.md`（4,378 tokens / 12 claims）與 `DESIGN.md`（8,059 tokens / 3 claims）納入評分，發現 **schema 做不到**。語料收集全站只有 `scripts/lib.mjs#collectFiles()` 一處，五支腳本都經過它，而它只吃目錄（`docs_dirs`）與單檔入口（`entry_files` / `index_file`）。

三條繞路各有代價：

| 繞路 | 代價 |
|---|---|
| `docs_dirs` 放單檔 | **直接炸**：`ENOTDIR: not a directory, scandir '…/PRODUCT.md'`（寫成 `PRODUCT.md/` 也一樣，`path.join` 會正規化掉尾斜線） |
| `entry_files` | 收得到檔，但 `fileType()` 標成 `entry` → 直接進 `entry_cost.tokens_est`：oikos 實測 **9,037 → 21,474**，跨過 `entry_cost_tiers` 的 20,000 → 經濟性 **★3 → ★1**。**而且那個成本是假的**——這兩份在 oikos 是條件式載入，而 `init.md` 的判準是「每次任務都會自動載入」。`audit.md` §經濟性 又明訂稽核者查到 `entry_cost.files` 與現實不符要記失分點，等於拿灌水的固定成本換一個永久扣分 |
| `docs_dirs: [docs/, ./]` | `collectFiles` 對 `docs_dirs` **不去重**，整棵 `docs/` 被算兩次；repo root 底下還有 `.claude/worktrees/` 這類會浮動的目錄 → 分數機器相依、不可重現 |

## 與 `entry_files` 的差別是「載入時機」，不是「重要性」

- always-loaded → `entry_files`（計固定成本）
- 條件式載入 → `docs_files`（不計）

**選錯不會報錯，只會讓經濟性失真**——往上灌水或往下低報，方向相反。判準與選錯的代價寫進 `reference/init.md` 問卷（新增為第 3 項，其後順延）。

## 語意與既有單檔入口對齊

- 檔案不存在 → 靜默略過（同 `entry_files`）。`.docgrad.yml` 進版控跨 branch 共用，檔案暫時缺席不該讓五支腳本全掛
- `docs_dirs` 已掃到的檔不重複計
- `exclude` 仍然優先——列進 `docs_files` 也擋不住，該檔照算污染面
- **不是可達性起點**：`links.mjs` 的 roots 仍只有 `index_file` + `entry_files`，`docs_files` 比照一般文件判孤兒。這是刻意的——條件式文件若沒有任何文件連到它，agent 只能靠猜找到它

## 順手修：單檔入口指到目錄的錯誤訊息

原本要延到 `inventory.mjs` 讀檔才爆 `EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory`，訊息看不出是哪個設定欄位寫錯。而 `docs_files` 正是最容易被寫成目錄的欄位（它是 `docs_dirs` 的孿生）。

三條規則（不存在／目錄／去重）收進新的 `pushSingleFile()`，`entry_files` / `index_file` 共用——原本它們也有同一個潛在 EISDIR。行為上只有目錄那條從「晚爆、訊息無用」變成「當場爆、訊息可行動」。

## oikos 實跑對照

`--config` 外置指向 scratchpad 的暫存設定（= oikos `.docgrad.yml` + `docs_files: [PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md]`），**oikos 工作區未改動任何檔**。

| 指標 | 1.3.1 | 1.4.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `files_total` | 46 | **48** |
| `claims_total` | 317 | **332** |
| `entry_cost.tokens_est` | 9,037 | **9,037**（本欄位的重點）|
| `entry_cost.files` | `["CLAUDE.md"]` | `["CLAUDE.md"]` |
| 死鏈／壞錨／孤兒 | 0/0/0 | **0/0/0** |
| `reachable_ratio` | 1.0 | **1.0** |
| freshness `coverage_ratio` | 93.48% | **89.58%** |
| 污染面 | 11.77% | 10.88% |

`PRODUCT.md` / `DESIGN.md` 都是 `type=doc`，未進 `entry_cost`。五支腳本全跑完、無錯誤、無 non-zero exit。

## 測試

**66 → 71**，`node --test tests/*.test.mjs` 全綠。新 fixture `tests/fixtures/docs-files/`（6 檔）。

新增涵蓋：收錄 `docs_dirs` 之外的單檔、去重、缺檔靜默略過、`exclude` 優先、指到目錄丟錯、`type: 'doc'` 且不進 `entry_cost`、孤兒判定比照一般文件。

**守門員證明**：把 `for (const f of config.docs_files) pushSingleFile(...)` 那行刪掉重跑 → **66 pass / 5 fail**，還原後 71 pass。刪 `DEFAULTS.docs_files` 也會紅。

**evals 未動**（守的是星等可重現性／抽樣覆蓋率／偽陽性，不是設定管線），三個 fixture 重跑確認 `evals/README.md` 的機械基準值一位不差。

**dogfood 自評無退化**：本 repo 9 檔、dead 0 / bad 0 / orphans 0 / reachable 1.0、freshness coverage 1.0、污染面 0%。

`claude plugin validate .` → `✔ Validation passed`，EXIT=0，無 warning。

## ⚠️ 跨 1.4.0 的分數可比性

**只影響實際設了 `docs_files` 的 repo。** 納入新檔會同時動到 `files_total` / `claims_total` / `tokens_est` / 新鮮度分母 / 孤兒與可達率母體，該 repo 跨 1.4.0 的分數不可直接比較，基準要從導入這個欄位的那一輪重算（性質同 1.3.0 的新鮮度註記：量測範圍修正，不是品質退步）。

**沒設這個欄位的 repo 輸出完全不變**——預設空陣列，不必重跑 `init`。

## 已知但未處理（建議另開 issue）

1. **`retrieval.mjs` 的 `marginal_tokens` 有既存的重複計算**，被這個欄位照亮。`marginal_tokens = entryTokens + Σ(marginalSet)`，oikos 加了 docs_files 後 `CLAUDE.md` 從「索引連不到」變成 depth 3，於是同時出現在 `entryTokens` 與 `marginalSet` 裡被算兩次。**不是新 bug**（之前 unreachable 時 `chainToIndex` 回 `[doc]`，一樣會算進去），report-only 不計星，所以沒動。
2. **`loadConfig` 對 list 欄位零驗證**是共有的坑。使用者若寫 `docs_files: PRODUCT.md`（scalar 不是 inline list），`for…of` 會逐字元迭代、每個字元 `existsSync` 失敗 → **靜默收不到任何檔、沒有任何錯誤訊息**，症狀是 `files_total` 就是不動。`entry_files` / `exclude` / `src_dirs` / `scenarios` 全有同一個坑。沒單獨替新欄位加驗證（會製造不一致），值得一個 patch 版一次補齊。
3. **`reference/rubric.md` 全程沒碰**，因為任何一個字的改動都會變更 `rubric_hash`，讓每個 repo 的 `report` 畫出一條假的「尺有變更」斷點。代價是 rubric 經濟性那節仍只寫「固定成本＝`entry_files`」，沒提 `docs_files` 不計入。判斷這不構成矛盾（那句話依然為真），但若認為 rubric 該提一句，要當成「知情付出 rubric_hash 斷點」的決定來做，不該順手改。

body:
Refs #1404, #1405, #1406

**#1404, #1405 and #1406 each cite two analysis documents that are not in the repository.** The review never left the #1397 branch; the measure plan reached develop through #1395 and I removed it again in #1407 because it had ridden along on `git add -A` unread.

Removing it was right. Not checking who depended on it was not — three issues were left pointing at a source nobody could open.

## They come back with the check that was skipped

Sampled against the GitHub API:

| Claim | Verified |
|---|---|
| nine title chains in K1 | verbatim |
| eleven quoted titles in K2 | verbatim |
| `#1353` carries 37 of 243 | in the body |
| 23 issues name a predecessor in the title | 43 name any issue number; 23 is the predecessor-defect subset |

The headline figures in §1 drifted by time and nothing else: 327 closed issues today against 325 on 2026-09-11, 122 `bug` against 121, `security` unchanged at 47. **They stay as measured, under a dated note.** A dated data point is reproducible; a silently updated one is not.

## The measure plan gains its implementation status

**M1 is done and closed** — the guard lane is a required check at 41 s, and its falsification ran as a real throwaway PR rather than locally. Two things the plan did not foresee are recorded because they are part of the measure:
