ormastes
body:
## What this is, and what it is not

macOS bootstrap chain run 19 rejected Stage 2 with exactly one line —
`Module surface registry graph promotion failed after phase 2` — naming neither
the offending surface, nor the field, nor the transient scope state.
`module_surfaces_promote` had 26 distinct routes to the bare `false` behind it,
so the only way to learn which fired was a fresh ~25-minute bootstrap cycle.

**It is not a fix for that blocker, and an earlier draft of these records that
said it was has been withdrawn.** The blocker was already cleared by
`460aa9781cc` (the Linux BOOT-7 fix), which landed on `main` at 08:12 via PR
#754 — *after* run 19's PR #753 merged at 07:58. Run 19 measured a tree without
it.

That attribution was **measured, not assumed**: run 20's Stage 2 `native-build`
was replayed verbatim from its own `stage2-command.transcript` against
`origin/main` @ `601bc2787b2` with this branch's rewrite **reverted** (886
compiled, 0 failed, 450.3 s). The resulting candidate runs the positional
Stage-3 route with `grep -c 'promotion failed'` = **0**, logging
`phase2:surface:file:promote-done` / `commit-done` / `released seq=2`. Phase 2
promotes cleanly with no change of ours, so the 24-operand
`not rt_transient_heap_promote(a) or not …(b) or …` chain was not the false.

## What it does contribute

1. **A fail-closed diagnostic.** `module_surfaces_promote_reason` returns `""`
   or a text naming the field, the surface index and its logical/canonical/
   package names, the registry cardinalities, and a **scope sentinel** — a
   promote of a freshly built carrier, which separates "the transient array
   scope is not active+paused, so the runtime answers false for EVERY value"
   (`runtime_native.c:2430`) from a genuinely unpromotable field. Those were
   indistinguishable before. The driver interpolates it, so it lands in
   `stage2-receiver.log`. `module_surfaces_promote` stays as a wrapper.
2. **macOS has converged with Linux on site 8.** Run 20 reaches `native_compile`
   and SEGVs; crash report `simple-2026-09-13-083808.ips` names frame 0
   `compiler__mir__mir_json__serialize_mir_function`. That record is updated to
   say it is not Linux-specific, and a preserved candidate (sha256
   `630ad64b7194eec6…`, 139,327,000 B) makes the ~40-second witness loop
   available on macOS too.
3. **Two corrections carried into the records.** Run 19's "no rejected Stage 2
   candidate is preserved" was a look-in-the-wrong-place error —
   `bootstrap-from-scratch.sh:3091-3111` already moves it to
   `stage2-rejected/<PLATFORM>/` with a `rejection.env`, which is precisely why
   `stage2/<PLATFORM>/` reads empty; no script change was needed. And the
   reproduction recipe omits that the bootstrap needs `cargo` on PATH: a PATH
   trimmed to dodge run 13's Homebrew `cmp` trap dies in seconds with
   `failed to fingerprint Rust seed inputs`, whose real cause
   (`resolver-frontend=absent`) appears only in the fingerprint error log.

The 24-operand boolean chain is still replaced by one promote per statement —
not because it was measured to misbehave, but because a chain that can only
answer an unnamed false is untriageable. That is a diagnosability argument and
it is the only one claimed for it.

## Verification

`test/01_unit/compiler/hir/module_surface_promote_reason_spec.spl`, 4 examples /
0 failures under the Rust seed. Two are behavioural; two assert the failure
contract against the source, because the seed's interpreter stubs
`rt_transient_array_scope_*` and `rt_transient_heap_promote` to answer true
unconditionally and therefore cannot exercise the sabotage behaviourally — said
in the spec rather than papered over.

Pre-push guards, foreground, exit codes captured on the next line:
conflict-markers PASS, tree-size PASS, no-revert PASS, guard-wiring PASS, and
the divergence **delta** guard `PASS — 3218 pre-existing offender(s), 0
introduced by this range` (step-over recorded in the commit message with the
offender-list path, as that guard's contract requires).

No deploy. Stage 3 was not attempted — Stage 2 is not ADMITTED.

author: silvanotitusonline
body:
## Production-readiness hardening

After PR #17, Supabase is correctly the sole authentication authority. A remaining startup defect is that `RtcAuthenticationCoordinator.restoreSession()` still gives the entire restore path only 2.5 seconds, while `RtcRepository.restoreSupabaseSession()` performs server profile/role hydration before it returns. A valid persisted SDK session can therefore be timed out and presented as public on slow startup/network conditions.

### Intended boundary
- Auth restoration waits for Supabase's local persisted-session initialization without an arbitrary 2.5-second cut-off.
- The restore gate establishes only SDK-backed local identity and fails closed to `RESIDENT_A`; cached role data is never trusted.
- Network profile/role/MFA hydration remains in the existing post-restore `refreshLiveContent()` path before staff workspace initialization.

### TDD phase
This draft currently contains regression contracts only. The first CI run is expected to fail until the restoration path is split accordingly.

Scope is isolated from Daily Post PR #11 and community mutation PR #4.

author: kiwi-dev-la
body:
Addresses **lightwave-media/lightwave-core#474** (issues are disabled on this repo, so the contract issue lives there).

## What

Pins `version:` on all **11** `jdx/mise-action` call sites across 10 workflows.

## Why

`release-core.yml`'s own header promises:

> Determinism: no floating action refs, no network version lookups

The action refs are SHA-pinned and honour that. The mise **binary** did not: with `version` unset, mise-action resolves *latest* at run time, which is exactly the network version lookup the header disclaims.

It has already cost a release. createOS `v0.6.0-rc.2` ([run 32918335126](https://github.com/lightwave-media/createOS/actions/runs/32918335126)) died in *Install mise*: jdx/mise published `v2026.8.14` at 01:16:21Z and the action started pulling the asset while the upload was still in flight — five 404 retries, job dead. The asset existed minutes later and a plain re-run passed, which is the signature of a publish race rather than a broken pin.

## Version choice

**`2026.9.5`** — published 2026-09-10 and settled for two days. The failure mode was grabbing a *minutes-old* release, so "recent but settled" is the property that matters. Bump it deliberately, the same way the action SHAs are bumped.

Format verified against the action's own README at the pinned SHA: `version: 2026.3.10`, no `v` prefix.

## Alternative considered

mise-action offers `minimum_release_age: 7d`, documented as "select mise releases at least 7 days old **instead of** setting version". It would have prevented this exact incident and needs no bumping.

I went with the explicit version anyway, because `minimum_release_age` still performs the lookup the plane's header says it does not do — it makes the race unlikely rather than impossible. Worth revisiting if pin-bumping proves to be a maintenance drag.

## Coverage

| workflow | call sites |
|---|---|
| ci-mise.yml | 1 |
| pipelines-drift-detection.yml | 1 |
| pipelines-root.yml | 2 |
| pipelines-unlock.yml | 1 |
| pipelines.yml | 1 |
| release-container.yml | 1 |
| release-core.yml | 1 |
| release-node-package.yml | 1 |
| release-static-site.yml | 1 |
| release-tauri-app.yml | 1 |

`release-go-binary.yml`, `release-only.yml`, `release.yml`, `ci.yml` and `ci-node.yml` have no mise-action call and are untouched.

## Verification

- Every workflow still parses as YAML (10/10, no failures).
- A re-scan for any `jdx/mise-action@` without a `version:` within its block returns **none**.
- Both insertion shapes checked by hand: `release-core.yml` had an existing `with: install: false` (version added alongside), `ci-mise.yml` had none (a `with:` block created).

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Workflow-only pinning with no runtime application logic changes; main tradeoff is occasional manual bumps when upgrading mise.
> 
> **Overview**
> Pins **`version: 2026.9.5`** on all **11** `jdx/mise-action` steps across **10** reusable workflows (CI, Terragrunt pipelines, and release paths).
> 
> Without an explicit version, mise-action resolves the **latest** mise release at job time, which can fail mid-publish (404 while assets upload) and contradicts the release plane’s determinism goal. The chosen version is a settled release meant to be bumped deliberately, like the action SHA pins.
>

author: huttonhomehub
body:
## What

`#281`'s subject is the gap between a green `pnpm prepush` and a green CI. **Its diagnosis holds.**
All three numbers describing that gap are wrong, and one of them contradicts another row.

## `prepush` does not run format, and `#299` is the row that says so

`scripts/prepush.sh` contains **zero** occurrences of the string `format`. That is why
`pnpm format:check` has to be run separately, and it is exactly what `#299` exists to record.

This row opens *"`pnpm prepush` runs format, lint, typecheck, …"* — so the register holds **two rows
disagreeing about one script, one of them created specifically to record the gap the other denies.**
The `#93`/`#267` shape, between rows rather than inside one.

## Nineteen `check:*` gates, not sixteen

A full run prints **22** steps: `lint`, `typecheck`, `test`, and **19** `check:*`. ADR-0136 and
ADR-0138 added several between them, and `prepush.sh` derives its list from `package.json` — so the
number moves without anybody editing this row.

## CI is four declared jobs and ten check runs, not "six checks" and not one `e2e` job

`ci.yml` declares `quality`, `e2e-api`, `e2e-web` (a **4-way matrix**) and `image` — seven job
instances — and a pull-request head carries **ten** check runs once the PR-title check and the two
CodeQL runs are counted. ADR-0138 split the single `e2e` job this row describes; the row's own
2026-09-11 note saying *"all six checks ran"* was true then and is not now.

## None of this weakens the row — it sharpens it

The gap is **wider** than the text says: the local gate is one step smaller than claimed in one
direction (no format) and three larger in another (19 gates), and the remote side is five end-to-end
jobs rather than one. A reader estimating *"how much does `prepush` not cover"* from that paragraph
would get every term wrong.

The remedy is unchanged and still unbuilt: `ci.yml` and `prepush.sh` are both shared gates, so
ADR-0105 fires.

author: cmungall
body:
## Headline

**APOO is not an apolipoprotein.** The 55 kDa glycosylated, secreted species that gave this gene
its name was shown in 2023 — by the same laboratory that had proposed the three-form model, with
Anand and Reichert authors on both papers — to be a non-specific antibody signal
(PMID:37279200). It survives siRNA knockdown with three siRNAs, survives CRISPR knockout in four
human cell lines, is not produced by GFP- or myc-tagged MIC26, is unaffected by mutating the
predicted glycosylation sites, and yields no MIC26 peptides when the 47–63 kDa gel region is
excised and sequenced. Eight GOA rows rest on it. All eight are removed.

What is left is one identity: MIC26, a structural subunit of the MICOS complex at the crista
junction — and, unusually for a "peripheral" subunit, one whose own single-gene knockout has a
measurable phenotype.

## Actions

35 seeded rows, all reviewed; no `PENDING` left. Counts produced by
`.scratch/reconcile.py`, not asserted.

| action | n | rows |
|---|---|---|
| ACCEPT | 22 | MICOS complex ×7, cristae formation ×4, mitochondrion ×6, mitochondrial inner membrane ×3, MIB complex, mitochondrial crista junction |
| MODIFY | 4 | `GO:0007007` IC → `GO:0042407`; three bare `GO:0005515` IPIs → `GO:0005198` |
| REMOVE | 9 | `GO:0005576` ×4, `GO:0000139` ×2, `GO:0005789` ×2 (the withdrawn secretory identity) + `GO:0001401` SAM complex |
| NEW | 1 | `GO:1900208` regulation of cardiolipin metabolic process, IMP |

**The eight secretory rows.** Removing an EXP and three IDAs is not second-guessing a curator
from an abstract: it is following the primary literature to the paper, by the original authors,
that withdrew the observation using the knockout controls the 2015 and 2006 work lacked. The tell
was visible in 2015 and unremarked — the companion data paper records that MIC26 depletion lowers
the 22 kDa form "but not the amount of the secreted 55 kDa isoform" (PMID:26217777). An antibody
signal that does not fall when the gene is knocked down is not that gene's product. The three
`GO_REF:0000044` IEAs inherit the defect from UniProt statements that have not yet been
retracted, so they will regenerate until UniProt updates Q9BUR5; that is filed as a CURATION
knowledge gap. Note that the **mouse** record Q9DCZ4 already lists only "Mitochondrion inner
membrane" — the correction reached one species' record and not the other.

**The SAM complex row.** `GO:0001401` HDA from PMID:26477565. Reference-projection test run:
QuickGO by `reference=PMID:26477565&goId=GO:0001401` returns **12 entities**, each resolved
individually — MIC10, MIC13, MIC19, MIC25, MIC26, MIC27, MIC60, SAMM50, MTX1, MTX2, MTX3, HSPA9.
That is the whole MIB complex, not the SAM complex; everything that co-migrated got the term.
`GO:0001401` is defined as "A large complex of the mitochondrial **outer** membrane", and MIC26
is a single-pass inner-membrane protein. The same reference already supplies `GO:0140275` MIB
complex for this gene, which is the true statement, so nothing is lost.

**What is *not* removed.** PMID:25764979's mitochondrial conclusions are accepted in full — its
nine rows split three ACCEPT, three MODIFY, three REMOVE. Ott's negative cristae result
(PMID:25781180, "periphery subunits … their depletion does not affect cristae morphology") is
cited rather than ignored; the CRISPR knockout data break the tie.

## IBA propagation verdicts

PAINT slice committed at `interpro/panther/PTHR14564/PTHR14564-paint.tsv`. The family has
**one** node carrying **two** IBDs — exactly the two IBAs on APOO.

| term | node | IBD seeds (from the slice) | root_cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GO:0061617` MICOS complex | `PTN001803267` | `FB:FBgn0038400`, `UniProtKB:Q6UXV4`, `UniProtKB:Q9BUR5` | `NO_FAILURE_CORE` |
| `GO:0042407` cristae formation | `PTN001803267` | `UniProtKB:Q9BUR5` | `NO_FAILURE_CORE` |

Donors resolved rather than assumed:

- `FB:FBgn0038400` → **Q9VEY5**, *Drosophila* Mic26-27 (CG5903, dApoO) — the single
  pre-duplication gene. QuickGO shows it carrying `GO:0061617` by **IMP** (PMID:32439808) and
  IGI (PMID:38253420).
- `UniProtKB:Q6UXV4` → human **APOOL/MIC27**, two independent **IDA** `GO:0061617` rows.
- `UniProtKB:Q9BUR5` → **the target itself**. Recorded as `SUPPORTS_TRANSFER` with the comment
  that its four direct IDA/HDA rows are among the descendant evidences behind the IBD. Expected,
  not circular; never marked `CIRCULAR_OR_REDUNDANT`.

The cristae-formation IBD has a one-gene `WITH/FROM`. That is short because the clade is small,
not because the evidence is thin: the family's characterised members — *C. elegans* moma-1,
*Drosophila* Mic26-27, human MIC26 and human MIC27 — all shape cristae, and none contradicts it.
Both human paralogues and the fly gene receive IBA from this node (checked in QuickGO), placing
it at or near the family root, ancestral to the MIC26/MIC27 duplication. No IRD or IKR anywhere
in the slice.

**11 `propagation_review` blocks** in total — the 2 IBAs, 6 IEAs with `supporting_entities`
(2 InterPro2GO, 3 SubCell, 1 combined ARBA/Ensembl), 1 ISS, 1 IC, and the GO_REF:0000044 inner-
membrane row. `source_entities` are **generated by script from each row's seeded
`supporting_entities`**, with a hard assertion that the two lists match element-for-element; they
cannot drift. Each carries a source-specific comment, never a bare enum.

Non-`NO_FAILURE_CORE` verdicts:

- three `GO_REF:0000044` IEAs (Secreted / Golgi / ER): `SOURCE_BAD` + `COMPARTMENT_OR_COMPLEX_MISMATCH`
- `GO:0005576` ISS from pig F1SPZ9: `SOURCE_WEAK_OR_INFERRED` + `COMPARTMENT_OR_COMPLEX_MISMATCH`
  — the donor's own `GO:0005576` is an HDA from the same PMID:22261194 ECM proteomics run, one
  detection in a sequentially extracted matrix fraction of ischaemic myocardium, an organ dense
  with mitochondria; F1SPZ9's four other annotations are electronic and place it in the
  mitochondrial inner membrane.
- `GO:0007007` IC: `TERM_SCOPING_PROBLEM` + `GRANULARITY_MISMATCH` — the MIB-membership premise
  is sound, the term is the true-but-uninformative parent of `GO:0042407`, which the gene already
  has by IMP, IBA, IEA and NAS.

## NEW term, and the term deliberately not added

`GO:1900208 regulation of cardiolipin metabolic process` (IMP, PMID:32788226). Cardiolipin falls
significantly in **MIC26 single-knockout** human HAP1 cells and *not* in MIC27 single knockouts,
across all cardiolipin molecular species rather than a subset, and cardiolipin-synthase
overexpression rescues the downstream supercomplex defect — so the lipid is causally between
MIC26 and OXPHOS. The parent term is used rather than the positive-regulation child because
reduced steady-state cardiolipin does not distinguish decreased synthesis from increased
turnover.

**`GO:1901612 cardiolipin binding` is deliberately NOT added.** That activity was demonstrated
in vitro for the paralogue **APOOL/MIC27** (PMID:23704930, "It specifically binds to cardiolipin
in vitro but not to the precursor lipid phosphatidylglycerol"), and Anand 2020 restates the
attribution to MIC27. The only claim of cardiolipin recruitment by MIC26 itself is from
coarse-grained molecular dynamics on an AlphaFold 3 model (PMID:42647630, graded `LOW_QUALITY`
for evidence class, not for quality of work). Recorded as a knowledge gap instead.

Also *not* annotated: the yeast Mic26↔Mic10-oligomer antagonism (PMID:29733859 is
*S. cerevisiae*; the human result is reciprocal protein-level control, a different claim), and
the MIC26-specific mitochondrial-fragmentation phenotype, whose own authors write "Further
experiments are required to understand why and how MIC26 specifically regulates mitochondrial
dynamics."

## Bioinformatics

`genes/human/APOO/APOO-bioinformatics/` (uv project, live UniProt REST fetch, sequence lengths
asserted against each entry's ID line, no hardcoded results).

UniProt calls Q9BUR5 residues 1–25 a SIGNAL peptide with `ECO:0000255` — prediction only — while
the paralogue Q6UXV4 carries `TRANSIT 1..27`.

author: rjreeves
body:
## Summary

Finishes "production scripting foundation" → "Standard scripting APIs" — every bullet in that subsection is now shipped or explicitly, individually deferred with a concrete reason.

- `http.get(url) -> Result<http, str>` — wraps Certo's already-registered WinHTTP-backed client (`Http.get`/`HttpResponse.*`, confirmed in `Certo/crates/stdlib/src/seed.rs:1581-1594`).
- `http.status(response) -> int`, `http.body(response) -> str`, `http.content_type(response) -> str`, `http.ok(response) -> bool` — accessors mirroring `process.code`/`.stdout`/`.stderr`/`.ok` exactly, including the internal representation (`"h:"`-tagged JSON, same pattern as `"p:"` process results).
- A hard **10 MiB cap** on the response body: anything over that comes back as `Err` instead of the body. This is checked only *after* the full response is already downloaded — Certo's WinHTTP client (`http.rs:102-190`) has no streaming or early-abort mode, so this bounds what `http.get` hands back to the script, not the network transfer itself. Documented as such rather than implied to be more than it is.
- **Windows only.** Certo's non-Windows `Http.get` is a stub that calls `certo_panic` (an unrecoverable process abort, not a catchable `Result`) — consistent with this whole toolchain already being Windows-only (WinHTTP itself is Windows-only), but called out explicitly in `SPEC.md`/`README.md`/`ROADMAP.md` rather than silently assumed.

**Scope**: `http.get` only. `post`/`put`/`delete`, custom headers, and binary bodies are all already-registered Certo primitives — deferred as a scoping choice for a follow-up, not a feasibility gap.

**Testing note**: every existing `test.ps1` assertion is local and deterministic. This is the first one that touches the network — after discussing it with the maintainer, `test.ps1` now includes one live request against `http://example.com` (stable for over a decade), checking `status == 200` and that the body *contains* "Example Domain" (not an exact match, to tolerate incidental whitespace/CDN differences), clearly commented as the suite's one network-dependent check.

## Changes

- `src/lume.cto`: five new builtins registered, type-checked (reusing the existing `E0608` "requires str" template `dir.list` already uses, plus one new `E0703` for the "requires http result" accessor check), and implemented — reusing `requireText`, `resultOk`/`resultErr`, and a new `httpValue`/`httpField` pair that mirrors `processValue`/`processField` verbatim.
- `examples/http_get.lume` (positive) and `examples/invalid_http_get_args.lume` (bad-argument-shape).
- `test.ps1`: the one network-dependent assertion described above, plus the usual local bad-argument-shape check.
- `SPEC.md`/`README.md`/`ROADMAP.md` updated; `ROADMAP.md`'s "HTTP requests..." bullet split into shipped (`http.get`) vs. deferred (`post`/`put`/`delete`/headers/binary bodies/true request-time bounding), each with its concrete reason.
- No new AI-eval task — every existing task in `ai/tasks.json` asserts exact, deterministic stdout, which a live HTTP response can't guarantee without the same network dependency; the validation/accessor paths are still covered by `test.ps1`.

## Test plan

- [x] `.\build.ps1` — confirms `Http.get`/`HttpResponse.*` are callable via the existing dotted-namespace convention.
- [x] `.\test.ps1` full smoke suite green (with the standing 28→29→28 CRLF toggle for the one pre-existing environmental `core APIs` mismatch, unrelated to this change).
- [x] `examples/task_board.lume` sanity check unaffected.
- [x] Manual verification: real request against `http://example.com` (status 200, body contains "Example Domain"), an unresolvable domain correctly returns `Err`, `http.get(5)` produces `E0608`, and calling an accessor on a non-`http` value produces `E0703`.
- [x] `.\benchmark-10000.ps1` / `-features.ps1` / `-generic-dispatch.ps1` — all three still meet their throughput targets, no regression.

author: ewen-poch
body:
The first production run stopped on a public CDN HTTP 403 before uploading any objects. A missing S3-backed CDN object can return 403 and populate an error cache; public GET is therefore unsuitable for deciding whether an unpublished key exists.

Check the exact key with authenticated S3 HeadObject first, as Specialist does. Only explicit S3 404/NotFound/NoSuchKey responses mean absent. Authentication, access-denied and other errors remain fatal. Once S3 confirms existence, still download the public CDN bytes and enforce existing byte equality; a missing or forbidden public object cannot be treated as an empty store. Conditional immutable writes and CloudFront promotion/invalidation remain unchanged.

Validation:

- 15 transport/publication tests passed, including first publication with missing public keys returning 403, authenticated access-denied rejection, existing objects with CDN403/404, immutable conflict protection and interrupted promotion recovery.
- Format, metadata validation and publication dry-run passed.
- Release selection, approved review, source pin, source audit and content bytes are unchanged; the authorized initial snapshot remains the same.
- The existing publication rehearsal and full three-platform PR CI run before merge. No full local npm test or imported Skill execution.

[AWS HeadObject documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/API_HeadObject.html) describes missing-object 404 with ListBucket versus 403 without it. The uploader requires GetObject and sufficient ListBucket permission; this fix does not relax access failures.

Historical compatibility: none; no published artifact is changed. New enums/states: none. Persistence: no data/model changes; an additional read-only S3 metadata request precedes each publication-side CDN read. UI: unchanged. The already authorized first publication resumes on the new main only after this fix passes checks and merges.

author: gradybre
body:
`validate_save_registry_handoff.py` → **PASS**: 31 name/cursor/UTF-8 fixtures, 50 owners, 582 canonical records, 530 persisted packed fields. `--require-release-ready` still exits **nonzero**, as the ruling requires of this incomplete release state.

## The validator was never committed

It existed only in the working tree — the **same gap** that left three EH lanes reading files their branches did not contain. Committed here along with Astra's ADR 0111.

Running it found **two real defects in my own reconciliation** (#94), which is precisely why the instruction to run it was worth following literally.

## Defect 1 — `source_contract` is a closed set

The artifact carries a **C001–C167 dictionary** of `{unused, notes}`, and the validator asserts membership. My reconciliation used the strings `HAZ-001`, `HAZ-002` and `ECON-002` — which are ruling names, **not declarations in this artifact**. Eighteen fields referenced contracts that did not exist.

Added three real entries, each carrying the unused-value rule and the note that makes the field's loss legible:

- **C168** `needs._airless` — losing it silently restores a drowning resident to safety on load.
- **C169** `work`'s tool settlement — the lot and job references are full generation-carrying refs in the **INVENTORY LOT** and **JOB** namespaces, not `gear.gd`'s bare row indices, and must be saved with `gear.gd`'s claim columns or a load leaves a claim in one store with no binding in the other.
- **C170** `injury` — the rescuer is an EntityRef in the **DIRECTORY** namespace; `_last_incident_ordinal` is the one-shot dedup latch, and dropping `_airless_episode` creates a **second EXPOSURE incident on reload** for one the world already resolved.

## Defect 2 — two pins contradicted the ruling that requires growth

The validator hard-asserted `record_count == 564` and `packed_source_field_count == 512`. REG-R01 says in terms that the declaration **must be updated when EH-03/EH-04 or other concurrent state lands** — so those pins had to move with the reconciliation, not block it.

Now **582** and **530**, with comments stating they are pinned to the `197472b` snapshot and **not** to the format, so the next reconciliation knows they are expected to move.

A hardcoded `512` in a PASS message is now derived from the data. It was printing "512 persisted packed fields" while asserting 530 — reporting one number while checking another is exactly the shape of thing that makes a green check worthless.

## Note

This validator is Python over the artifact and its own fixtures. It establishes **no** Godot codec behaviour, no load, no save parity and no performance. `release_save_ready` stays false.

author: frankbria
body:
Closes #515

## Problem
`batch_prediction.py` started jobs as in-process `asyncio` tasks with no bound; one tenant submitting several jobs could saturate both gunicorn workers.

## Fix (the launch-relevant half the issue calls out: bound concurrency + per-tenant cap)
- **AC1 — per-process ceiling.** A `asyncio.Semaphore(MAX_CONCURRENT_BATCH_JOBS)` (default 2, env-tunable) gates the auto-started path: excess jobs queue behind it rather than all executing. Resolved per running loop via a `WeakKeyDictionary` (production has one loop for its life; the test suite has one per test, and a closed loop's entry is collected). `auto_start=False` (tests) bypasses it, staying deterministic. Both `create` and `retry` reach it through `_spawn_processing`.
- **AC3 — per-tenant cap.** `_enforce_per_user_cap` refuses a caller already at `MAX_CONCURRENT_BATCH_JOBS_PER_USER` (default 3) PENDING/RUNNING jobs with `BatchConcurrencyLimitError`; **create** checks it before the S3 upload (a refusal leaves no orphan object) and **retry** checks it before re-queuing. Both routes map it to **429**, and the refund middleware returns the `predictions` units the admission dependency reserved.
- A job cancelled while still queued behind the semaphore is skipped when it acquires (cancelling a job already running is #485).
- **AC2 / AC4 — streaming** was already the code's O(chunk_size) design (`_read_data_chunks` reads with `chunksize=`, results stream to a temp file, `_upload_results_file` streams from disk) and is covered by `test_process_batch_job_streams_results_across_chunks` / `_streams_valid_json_across_chunks`. This PR closes the task-spawn half.

## Tests
`test_services/test_batch_prediction.py`: per-tenant cap refuses over the limit (and does not upload), admits a different tenant, refuses a retry over the cap; the semaphore admits at most N concurrent `_process_batch_job` runs; a cancelled queued job never processes. `test_api/test_batch_concurrency_route.py`: the route returns 429 and the reserved units are refunded. Mutation: neutering the admission and the semaphore turns the behaviour tests red.

## Known limitations (filed as #653)
- The per-tenant cap is count-then-insert (TOCTOU): a same-tenant burst can momentarily exceed it. The per-**process** semaphore is the hard execution bound regardless, so the DoS this issue targets is contained; an atomic per-user admission is #653.
- The semaphore is held across the whole job with no wall-clock bound, so a hung job holds a slot until worker restart — a regression this PR introduces (before, a hang hurt only its own task). A per-job wall clock mirroring #500 is #653.

## Review
Cross-family (`codex review --base main`) and internal reviewer posted below; both findings dispositioned.

## Contexto

Correções das issues #504 e #505, achadas na auditoria geral de contabilidade x financeiro feita após o PR #502 (garantir que `lancamentos_contabeis` seja sempre reflexo fiel de `lancamentos`).

## Mudanças

- **`0141_desfazer_ofx_nao_reabre_fatura_paga_por_outro_fluxo.sql`** (issue #504): `desfazer_lancamento_ofx` reabria a fatura incondicionalmente quando não achava lançamento contábil próprio pra estornar. Isso também acontecia quando a fatura tinha sido paga por `baixar_faturas`/`baixar_pagamento_parcial`/`baixar_conta_pagar` e só depois vinculada retroativamente a uma linha do extrato via `conciliar_ofx_existente` (fluxo da issue #497). Agora só reabre quando há prova de que o vínculo desfeito foi de fato o pagamento (`conciliacao_baixa` estornada), ou quando não há lastro contábil em lugar nenhum (caso legado, comportamento histórico preservado). Se a fatura já está paga por um fluxo legítimo diferente (ou é transferência), o "Desfazer" passa a apenas desvincular a linha do OFX, sem tocar em `pago`/`conta_id`/`data_pagamento`.

- **`0142_conciliar_ofx_existente_exige_pago.sql`** (issue #505): `conciliar_ofx_existente` nunca conferia `pago = TRUE` no banco antes de vincular — a garantia vivia só no frontend. - Consulta de diagnóstico rodada em produção antes de escrever a correção: confirmado que o bug da #504 ainda não corrompeu nenhum dado real (nenhum lançamento contábil órfão, nenhuma fatura reaberta indevidamente) — as duas correções são preventivas.
- Nenhum arquivo TypeScript alterado (só procedures MySQL); comportamento das telas que já filtram no frontend (`conciliacao.tsx`) não muda.

author: lessevv
body:
`R2` says every rule that claims to be enforced refuses a planted violation, and it counts **one fixture per rule**. Five rules have **two clauses** and had one fixture.

| Rule | Clause with a fixture | Clause without one |
|---|---|---|
| **C6** | a broad `catch` | an **empty** `catch` — the half somebody actually writes, because it looks deliberate |
| **C9** | a nested ternary | `??` on an array subscript — different construct, different check |
| **M1** | a command answering a string | a **query answering an `Outcome`** — a question that reports whether it worked is a question that did something |
| **P2** | a dynamic property name | a **variable variable** — the older, stranger half |
| **W3** | a stray Blade file | a directory under `tests/` that is not a suite — the worse half, since tests in it pass by never running |

**Every one of those clauses is enforced already.** What was missing was the proof. R2 is not a check on the rules, it is a check on whether anybody has demonstrated them — and a rule with two clauses and one fixture reads as demonstrated when it is half demonstrated.

Found by the method that turned up D3: compare each fixture against its rule's *sentence*, not against the mechanism enforcing it.

author: fridaytaev001
body:
Closes #6.

## Purpose

Adds the local registry that records every skill candidate immutably and exposes only accepted versions to a future Action agent, per `hackathon_plan.md` §6.6 and the registry states in `skill_contract.md`.

The registry — not the Builder — assigns each candidate its version number and content hash. Recorded content is never edited: improving a skill adds a version, which is what keeps the experiment's improvement visible and reversible. Only an `accepted` version is ever offered as an available skill, so a proposed, validating, rejected, or retired candidate cannot contaminate the held-out evaluation.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/test_skill_registry.py` | New — 31 tests (committed first, failing) |
| `src/noob_agent/domain/skills.py` | New — `SkillStatus`, `SkillPackage`, `SkillVersion` |
| `src/noob_agent/skills/registry.py` | New — `SkillRegistry`, `content_hash`, registry errors |
| `src/noob_agent/skills/__init__.py` | New — package exports |
| `src/noob_agent/skills/communication.md` | New — module boundary doc, matching `domain/communication.md` |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | New `[ADDED]` entry |

No change to `storage/`, `runtime/`, `connectors/`, the connector or grader path, CI, configuration, or dependencies. `SCHEMA_VERSION` is untouched.

## Status machine

```
proposed ──▶ validating ──▶ accepted ──▶ retired
                   └──────▶ rejected ──▶ (repair proposes a new version)
```

Every other move raises `IllegalTransitionError`. At most one version per skill is `accepted` at a time; accepting a second raises `ConflictingAcceptedSkillError` until the live one is retired. A repair calls `propose()` with `parent_version` set to the rejected version it follows, and that rejected record stays byte-for-byte as it was.

## Tests added and their initial failure

Tests were committed first (`173d20e`) and confirmed failing before any production code existed:

```
tests/test_skill_registry.py:11: in <module>
    from noob_agent.domain.skills import SkillPackage, SkillStatus, SkillVersion
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'noob_agent.domain.skills'
=========================== short test summary info ===========================
ERROR tests/test_skill_registry.py
!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Interrupted: 1 error during collection !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
```

Coverage maps to the issue's acceptance criteria:

- **Content hashes are stable** — identical content hashes identically regardless of metadata key order; any source change changes the hash.
- **Source/metadata cannot be overwritten** — frozen records reject assignment; a later candidate never alters version 1; a caller mutating its own metadata dict afterwards cannot reach into the record.
- **Illegal transitions are rejected** — 14 parametrized illegal moves, each also asserting the status did not change.
- **Repairs retain their parent** — a repair keeps `parent_version` and leaves the rejected version untouched; a repair must name a recorded, rejected parent.
- **Rejected/proposed versions never appear** — parametrized over `proposed`, `validating`, `rejected`, and `retired`, `available_skills()` is empty and `accepted_skill()` is `None`.

## Automated check results

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tests | `uv run pytest` | **104 passed** (31 new) |
| Lint | `uv run ruff check .` | **All checks passed** |
| Format | `uv run ruff format --check` | Clean for both files added here |
| Types | `uv run mypy` | **Success: no issues found in 17 source files** |
| Build | `uv sync --group dev` | Unchanged — no dependency added |

## Manual verification

- Confirmed the test module fails with `ModuleNotFoundError` before implementation and passes after, with no change to the assertions in between.
- Confirmed the full pre-existing suite still passes (73 prior tests, unchanged).
- Confirmed `uv run ruff format --check` flags only `connector_contract.md`, `skill_contract.md`, and `src/noob_agent/settings.py`, all of which already fail on `main` and were deliberately left alone.

## Known limitations

- **Not durable.** Versions live in process. Persisting them through the SQLite source of truth would mean a new table and a `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump, which `AGENTS.md` requires explicit approval for, so it is left as a follow-up.
- **Depends on #5, which is not merged.** `SkillPackage.metadata` is deliberately an opaque JSON object. Typed `noob-agent.skill.v1` models, package checks, and AST static policy checks are #5's deliverables; this PR does not duplicate them and does not validate or interpret metadata.
- **No status history.** A version keeps its current status and reason, not the full trail of transitions it passed through.
- **One-repair-per-rejection is not enforced here.** `skill_contract.md` allows one repair; the registry only requires that a repair's parent is a rejected version, leaving the count to the Builder loop.
- No generated code is imported or executed, no model call, no connector edit, and no held-out logic — as the issue requires.

## Rollback

Revert the merge commit, or drop the branch — nothing else imports the new modules yet:

```sh
git revert -m 1 <merge-commit>
```

Reverting removes `src/noob_agent/domain/skills.py`, `src/noob_agent/skills/registry.py`, `src/noob_agent/skills/__init__.py`, `src/noob_agent/skills/communication.md`, and `tests/test_skill_registry.py`, and restores `CHANGELOG.md`. `src/noob_agent/skills/executor.py` is unaffected and remains importable either way.

body:
## 背景

ルート README 第5節「配布版の更新取り込み」は、採用側が差分を比較して必要な部分だけ反映することを求めています。しかし、版1から版2への変更は `template/` 全8ファイルに及ぶ一方でコミットメッセージは汎用的で、さらに版2のラベルのまま `template/` が2回改訂されていました（`cdb3e29` と `d0e4a88`）。採用側が「何が変わったか」を知る手段がなく、第5節の手順が成立していませんでした。

## 変更内容

**版管理（主目的）**

- ルート README に第7節「変更履歴」を追加し、版1〜3の変更点と採用側への影響を記載。第5節から参照するようにしました。
- ルート `AGENTS.md` に「版の更新」規則を追加。`template/` を変更したら配布版を上げ、標準の版は当該標準に変更があった場合のみ上げる、という運用を明文化しました。
- 本PR自身が `template/` を変更するため、この規則に従って配布版を **3** に上げています。標準2文書は未変更のため版2のままです。

**テンプレート側**

- `template/docs/document-policy.md`: 採用記録の「配布元・版」に本リポジトリへのリンクを追加。コピー後のプロジェクトから新版を辿れるようにしました。
- `template/AGENTS.md`: H1 直下に H3 があった「作業原則」を `##` に修正。

**リポジトリー整備**

- ルート README 第2節に bash の導入コマンドを1行追加（`mkdir` が既存ディレクトリーへの上書きを防ぎます）。
- `.gitattributes` に `* text=auto` を追加。インデックスは既に LF で、再正規化による差分はありません。
- ルート `AGENTS.md` に「変更時の確認」として、リンク・アンカーの解決確認と導入手順2種の実行確認を手動運用で明記しました。CI 化は現状の規模では見送っています。

## 確認したこと

- 相対リンク51件とアンカー（`<a id>` および見出し）がすべて解決すること、見出し階層に飛びがないことをスクリプトで確認。
- 外部リンク2件が GET で 200 を返すこと。
- PowerShell 版・bash 版の導入コマンドを一時ディレクトリーで実行し、`template/` の全ファイルと LICENSE が配置されること。
- 変更履歴の版2の記述は `git diff 7ca4857 d0e4a88` を読んで作成。

## レビューで見ていただきたい点

変更履歴の版2の項に「同じ版番号のまま2回改訂されている」旨を記載しています。事実ですが、公開文書に残すのが望ましくなければこの1行は削除できます。

あわせて、GitHub リポジトリーの description と topics（`project-template`, `ai-driven-development`, `mock-driven-development`, `agents-md`, `japanese`）を `gh repo edit` で設定済みです。これは本PRの差分には含まれません。

author: amirardekanian-crypto
body:
The exercise card could only ever offer an estimate off the set in front of it, which made a planned rep-max test impossible to record: the athlete does their 5RM on Saturday and there is nowhere to put it. Personal Records now has its own door.

## What's new

**`+ Log a max`** — pick a lift from the current cycle, enter what you actually lifted, optionally dated to the day you lifted it. Same three fields, same estimator, same Sharp/Good/Rough as the exercise card: `paintCeilingForm()` mirrors `paintFromFields()` deliberately, because a second copy of the maths is how the two screens start disagreeing.

The picker is the **current cycle only**, and **never free text**. An entry is filed under its display name, so a typed "Squat" beside a prescribed "Barbell Back Squat" splits an athlete's history in two with no way back.

It deliberately does **not** apply the reps-to-failure ceiling the card uses. That gate is about estimating off the set in front of you — a 3×12 leg press cannot produce an honest single, so the card offers nothing there. It says nothing about whether a 5RM test on the leg press is worth having. `estimateOneRM()` still refuses anything past the ceiling on save.

**The retest nudge, anchored to the cycle rather than the calendar.** A lift the programme marks `"test": "5RM"` shows in a *Due for a retest* strip when the cycle is in its closing week and the lift has gone 28 days without a number. Cycles run ~5 weeks and each chases one quality, so a test in the closing week measures the block that is ending; a rolling 30 days drifts into a deload sooner or later. Written by `/program-design` (`test_flag`) through `/program-assemble`; two or three lifts a cycle, because the nudge works by being rare.

## Three things this forced, all of which were already wrong

- **No delete existed.** Once athletes type numbers by hand somebody enters 150 for 15 and it is on their chart for ever. A delete is a **tombstone** (`{del: true}`), never a dropped row — the merge unions by `lift|date` across devices, so a row simply removed is handed straight back by the other phone. Which is also why every write now rebuilds from `loadCeilingRaw()`: rebuilding from `loadCeiling()` would silently drop every tombstone on the next save.
- **Renaming an exercise split the history.** `adoptRenamedExercises()` carries `setlog_`/`note_`/`cwlog_`/`wlog_` across a rename, but the lift name lives *inside* the shared `_1rm` array, so there is nothing to copy. Resolved at **read** time (`ceilAliasMap`) rather than rewritten: rewriting loses the race across devices and brings the split back doubled. Both sides share `matchRenamed()`.
- **The coach could not see any of it.** `coach.html` referenced `_1rm` nowhere, though the data has always ridden the progress blob. **The work** tab now carries a *Personal records* panel: latest estimate, movement, whether it came from a set or a test, how stale. It flags at the same 28 days but ignores the closing-week window — the athlete's strip waits so it does not nag, Amir is the one deciding when to ask. It runs a port of the same name matcher so the two never show one lift as two.

## Verification

Driven headless against a real programme fixture:

- the exercise card's own save path unchanged (5-arg call, no test flag)
- tombstones surviving the merge in **both** directions; a re-save beating a tombstone; a tombstone surviving the next write
- the rename folding two rows into one while leaving an unrelated lift alone, and refusing an ambiguous match
- a future date falling back to today; a 12-rep prescription opening the form blank rather than already refusing
- the retest window opening and closing with the cycle, and the 28-day floor deciding alone when a cycle has no `endDate`
- light and dark, at 390px

## Docs

`CODEBASE.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `MAP.md`, `SCHEMA.md` (the new `test` field), the design and assemble skills, `COACH_DASHBOARD.md`, `CEILING_HELP` and the app-guide card in place, and `privacy.html` §2.2 for the new entry and delete paths.
